102041.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a visit to City Museum in St. Louis, showing a spiral slide around a mosaic pillar, a treehouse made from branches and driftwood, a large bank vault door, a giant bronze ship propeller, and a frog sculpture.

1022105.abstract: Jamie shares a photo from the Tech Summit 2020 event, showing a packed conference hall with attendees at round tables watching a stage panel titled Technology Patterns and Trends, streamed live to all locations.

1033629.abstract: Jamie describes playing both sides of the new Ticket to Ride Japan expansion pack, including the flip-side Italy version.

1037722.abstract: Jamie describes an International Women's Day event at SPS Commerce featuring a keynote and exercise on vulnerability and bias led by Brave New Workshop's Margi Simmons, plus a panel of women leaders including Kara Boespflug, Jenny Nolan, Anna Picchetti, Nikki Riemersma, and Bre Taft.

1048936.abstract: Jamie shares sales data from Edina Liquor showing that after closing three retail stores on March 17 and shifting entirely to online ordering and home delivery, the business generated $8,300 on the first day and over $20,000 by day's end, matching typical revenue with stores open.

1049265.abstract: Jamie recounts a FaceTime conversation with emergency physician Michael Rock about the impact of Covid-19 on hospital operations.

1056741.abstract: Jamie redoes a candle making attempt after the first batch failed due to using roughly 20 times too much fragrance, which also caused nausea and headaches. Jamie cuts out the ruined wax, discards it, and pours new candles with a different fragrance at a much lower dose, reporting good early results.

1058111.abstract: Jamie marks Lucky the puppy's 3-month birthday and first week with the family. Jamie's wife Tammy works diligently on outdoor bathroom training, the kids adore Lucky, and the post notes crate training, playfulness, distractible walks, and a weight of 16 lbs.

1067583.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a customer appreciation parade organized by businesses in Warsaw, MN during the Pandemic lockdown, thanking Americas Mattress - Dundas, BFB Solutions, Channel Inn, D&L Real Estate, DGC, Doc's Dock Campground, Simple Strategies, Rick & Mary Tonjum, The Upper East Side, and Witte Bros.

1071109.abstract: Jamie describes buying Osmo's Hot Wheels MindRacers and Coding Duo during a sale, adding to an existing collection that includes Coding Awbie and Coding Jam.

1072935.abstract: Jamie asks the micro.blog community for advice on migrating about 8,000 Jekyll blog posts to micro.blog, weighing a Python API script against using Jekyll to generate RSS or JSONFeed for import, and cites Manton Reece's podcast migration as a similar precedent.

1074705.abstract: Jamie reviews the memoir "When Breath Becomes Air" by Paul Kalanithi, which covers Kalanithi's path to becoming a neurosurgeon and, after a stage IV lung cancer diagnosis, death within 18 months. Jamie connects it to Atul Gawande's "Being Mortal" and to the death of friend David Hussman, who had the same diagnosis.

1074706.abstract: Jamie writes about saying goodbye to family dog Chase, adopted in 2007, after complications from melanoma, other growths, and torn CCLs led to a vet visit at home for euthanasia. Jamie recounts Chase's personality and role in the family, including bonds with Mazie, Tyler, and Tammy, and shares photos of Chase over the years.

1074708.abstract: Jamie remembers friend David Hussman, an agile methods thought leader known as "The Dude," recalling a final evening together at Red Wagon Pizza and a 25-year mentoring relationship since meeting at MarketWatch.

1074709.abstract: Jamie recaps a DevOps Minneapolis Meetup session called "Changing the Enterprise" with Heather Mickman and Bridget Kromhout, sharing an embedded video and noting discussion of risk management, refactoring costs, and how Agile and DevOps intersect.

1074710.abstract: Jamie was recommended by Mike Carey, Chief HR Officer at SPS Commerce, for a Humble Leadership project led by Matt Norman, resulting in a 45-minute discussion and writeup on mattnorman.com describing how humble leaders avoid "blame and shame" under pressure.

1074711.abstract: Jamie recounts attending the 13th Minnebar, noting a blizzard for the first time and new Minnestar Executive Director Maria Ploessl leading the event. Jamie lists sessions attended, including talks by Bridget Kromhout, Chris Moffitt, and Leah Cunningham, with photos from several sessions.

1074712.abstract: Jamie explains the move of the Weekly Thing newsletter from TinyLetter to MailChimp, citing custom template control, automation via Workflow and the MailChimp API, and access to advanced subscriber segmentation, despite added complexity that Jamie has since streamlined back to iPhone-based production.

1074713.abstract: Jamie shares notes on Robert Wright's book "Why Buddhism Is True: The Science and Philosophy of Meditation and Enlightenment," praising how it connects Buddhist concepts like not-self and emptiness to modern psychology, and includes highlighted passages chapter by chapter covering meditation, mindfulness, and natural selection.

1074714.abstract: Jamie explores an idea from friend David Hussman, who describes age using version numbers (dividing by 10). Jamie extends this using Semantic Versioning concepts, mapping decades to MAJOR versions, years to MINOR versions, and days since birthday to PATCH versions, then shares a Workflow app script calculating this version number for address book…

1074715.abstract: Jamie describes weekend improvements to the Weekly Thing newsletter, including a new HTML template with better-styled quotes and hostnames on links, restored MailChimp API automation allowing publishing from an iPhone, and microblog posts now shown inline instead of as separate links.

1074716.abstract: Jamie identifies design patterns used in applications and websites to create addictive behavior, including pull-to-refresh, infinite scroll, and public and private feedback loops like likes and analytics, arguing that recognizing these patterns helps people avoid them.

1074717.abstract: Jamie tries Forestry.io as a content management tool for the Jekyll-based static blog hosted on Netlify, praising how it handles over 1,700 posts organized in year folders and image hosting without failing, unlike other tools tried. Jamie recommends Forestry.io to Jekyll or Hugo users.

1074718.abstract: Jamie analyzes a full year of calendar data from 2017, tracking 1,512 meetings across 223 days, averaging 6.8 per day.

1074720.abstract: Jamie reviews 913 links saved on Pinboard and Link Thing during 2017, breaking down patterns by hour, day, and month, noting Friday as the peak day tied to a Safari Reading List workflow and the Weekly Thing newsletter.

1074721.abstract: Jamie describes deliberately keeping a dedicated iPhone screen of apps meant to support personal improvement, avoiding social media and news apps with addictive patterns.

1074722.abstract: Jamie describes removing Google Analytics and all third-party resources from thingelstad.com, verifiable using Ghostery.

1074723.abstract: Jamie shares reactions to notable AWS re:Invent 2017 announcements, organized by compute, databases, machine learning, and other categories.

1074724.abstract: Jamie envisions a serverless, cloud-native wiki architecture built on AWS, storing pages in S3 as Markdown and HTML, with editing handled through Lambda functions and API Gateway, self-managed via IAM credentials.

1074725.abstract: Jamie describes a deer strike while driving to the cabin on highway 60 near Dairy Queen and I-35, after dinner at Smoqehouse. Jamie's wife Tammy was driving the Honda Pilot at 45 mph when the deer appeared; everyone was unhurt, the deer ran off, and the car sustained damage including a banged-up radiator, though it remained drivable.

1074726.abstract: Jamie appears as a guest on the Driving Change podcast hosted by Jeff Martin of Collective Genius, sharing an embedded episode along with links to other episodes featuring Bala Subramanian, Loren Brown, Nate Ober and Lisa Schlosser.

1074727.abstract: Jamie describes building the Weekly Thing newsletter using the Workflow app on iOS, pulling links from Pinboard's RSS feed and combining separate workflows for sections like photos, blog posts, and pins into one HTML draft, then finishing in TinyLetter before sending.

1074728.abstract: Jamie introduces the Weekly Thing, a new email newsletter built from earlier link blog posts that readers responded well to. Jamie cites newsletters like Club MacStories and Patrick Rhone's One More Thing as inspiration, chose TinyLetter for its simplicity, and shares the subscribe page with a goal of reaching 100 subscribers.

1074729.abstract: Jamie describes a technique for managing OmniFocus context notifications while keeping phone alerts minimal. Rather than enabling location notifications for the whole Office or Home context, which would be noisy, Jamie creates sub-contexts called "Office with notification" and "Home with notification" with location-based alerts attached, allowing…

1074730.abstract: Jamie describes deleting a Flickr account after Yahoo! changed its privacy policy following the sale to Verizon, having already deleted the associated Yahoo! account months earlier due to security breaches.

1074731.abstract: Jamie's mother sends a link to the Turing Tumble Kickstarter campaign, a game that teaches computing concepts using a mechanical computer with flippable bits. Jamie backs the project, hoping for November delivery as a Christmas gift, and notes the campaign nearly reached its funding goal within a day.

1074732.abstract: Jamie offers advice for technology speakers based on observations from presentations and demos. Jamie recommends avoiding words like "utilized" and "leveraged," skipping jokes about ending quickly or boring the audience, and not previewing demo highlights in bullet slides beforehand, arguing that showing the working product first is more…

1074734.abstract: Jamie describes adopting project templates in a task management system after long resisting them, valuing tools that support variable substitution and relative date calculations.

1074735.abstract: Jamie describes finishing horseshoe pits at the cabin, built using plans from horseshupit.com with help from Jamie's brother-in-law, after starting the project from a Christmas wishlist horseshoe set and completing digging once the ground thawed in spring.

1074736.abstract: Jamie links to a Minnesota Original feature on photographer Layne Kennedy, whom Jamie met through Kennedy's Wintergreen Dog Sledding workshop, and describes Kennedy as a skilled photographer, teacher and storyteller.

1074737.abstract: Jamie proposes a new ticketing process for Minnebar and Minnedemo, replacing the current rush-based system that causes unfair timing pressure, unclear demand data, and unused tickets.

1074739.abstract: Jamie recounts seeing Steve Wozniak speak at Augsburg College about early experiments with microchips leading to the Apple I and Apple II. Jamie highlights stories about Steve Jobs, Mike Markkula as Apple's "third founder," the Homebrew Computer Club's open culture, and Wozniak's focus on frugal design and user-centered technology.

1074740.abstract: Jamie recaps Minnedemo 25, covering seven demos: Talkative Chef, a hands-free voice-controlled cooking assistant built by an all-female Hack the Gap team; VennPT, a physical therapy program platform; Inkit, likened to Twilio for direct mail; EnduraData's data-transfer software (whose demo failed due to WiFi issues); the non-violent game Newt One…

1074741.abstract: Jamie describes a Microsoft Flow workflow for selectively sending flagged Office 365 emails to OmniFocus via Mail Drop, using a "when an email is flagged" trigger, an Active Directory lookup for sender name, and settings to avoid raw HTML. Jamie compares Flow to Zapier and IFTTT and recommends it for Office 365 users seeking automation.

1074742.abstract: Jamie describes playing in the 2017 Minnesota Kubb Winter Tournament with teammates Garrick and Jim as team Kubbchucks, marking their sixth year competing.

1074743.abstract: Jamie responds to a friend's question about using OmniFocus collaboratively by arguing that GTD, as defined by David Allen's Getting Things Done, is inherently personal rather than collaborative.

1074744.abstract: Jamie downloads Vibe, an open-source tool that generates visual stats from OmniFocus data, and shares a screenshot of the results. Jamie finds the visuals fun though not necessarily actionable, and suggests it would be valuable if OmniFocus offered an API for third parties to build similar tools.

1074745.abstract: Jamie describes stepping back from years of self-hosting, from a home server rack to VPS instances at Linode running Ubuntu, nginx, WordPress and MediaWiki, citing limited time for maintenance despite valuing the learning.

1074746.abstract: Jamie describes using TweetDelete, a free service from Memset, to automatically delete tweets after 90 days, viewing tweets as ephemeral unlike blog posts. Jamie notes TweetDelete's privacy policy confirms it never stores tweets, and relies on Pinboard to maintain a personal archive.

1074747.abstract: Jamie describes using an email rule to route action-required system emails (like Concur expense approvals) directly into OmniFocus Inbox, bypassing regular email, using the Omni Sync service's Maildrop feature to keep email clean.

1074748.abstract: Jamie describes a set of Office 365/Exchange email rules for managing meeting-related messages, sorting invitations into a "Meetings" folder and routing declines, new time proposals, and forwards into a "Review" folder while acceptances go to an "Affirmative" folder.

1074749.abstract: Jamie's daughter Mazie writes a short essay arguing against getting a phone for her birthday, describing electronics as "irresistible, eye widening, pass-time things" that make days disappear from memory. Jamie shares the essay and finds it captures more truth than most would like to admit.

1074750.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy and Jamie watch Spotlight as part of watching every Academy Award Best Picture nominee, and Jamie finds it a fabulous movie that highlights the critical role of journalism in exposing the Catholic church scandal. Comparing it to The Big Short, Jamie says Spotlight would get the vote for Best Picture for being "more serious."

1074751.abstract: After a week using Spillo, Jamie lists feature requests: handling 301 redirects on bookmarks, adding "not" conditions to Collection searches, regex-based title searches, creating collections from selected tags, dragging Community links into personal bookmarks, showing full descriptions, and date-part searches.

1074752.abstract: Jamie reviews Spillo, a Mac app for Pinboard discovered via a link in Brett Terpstra's 2015 Top Mac Apps post, after Thumbtack failed to satisfy. Jamie praises Spillo's three-column UI, Community features like Popular, and search-based Collections, using one for conference videos to watch.

1074753.abstract: Jamie reviews the film The Big Short, describing it as hilarious, suspenseful, and gripping, with strong acting and cinematography, while noting the terrifying reality behind the true story it depicts and urging reflection on how much of it is real.

1074754.abstract: Jamie and Tammy try curling for the first time at the St. Paul Curling Club, a fundraiser gift from Tammy, learning scoring, terminology and throwing technique before practicing on the ice. Jamie notes observations about stone speed, sweeping, strategy and sound, and expresses interest in returning and organizing a work team event there.

1074755.abstract: Jamie describes meeting brother Isaiah for the first time after receiving an email revealing their shared father, Michael Ringwall, whom Jamie had not seen since elementary school due to parents' divorce.

1074756.abstract: Jamie describes watching the documentary Barista, noting it appeals to coffee lovers through creative drinks and coffee culture, including distilled coffee, while also prompting self-recognition in overly enthusiastic coffee talk.

1074758.abstract: Jamie shares a video, sent by friends, of a European Pro RC Race, calling it amazing and highlighting the speed, passes and jumps. Jamie suggests additions like real-time telemetry, G-force data on turns, and POV streaming video from each car.

1074759.abstract: Jamie describes "Finding Winnie," a book Tyler received for Christmas, calling it well done and a good bedtime story, especially for kids who like Winnie-the-Pooh, and recommends it.

1074760.abstract: Jamie shares photos of the first big snowfall of 2015 at the cabin, describing staying inside by the fireplace while the snow accumulated outside. One photo shows a portable ice fishing house visible as a small dot on the lake.

1074761.abstract: Jamie describes replacing an aging LaCie 4big Quadra Firewire 800 RAID, which recently failed a drive, with a Synology DS416 NAS paired with four 4TB WD Red drives after weighing concerns about added SAN complexity.

1074762.abstract: Jamie tries Duet Display for the first time after seeing a recommendation from MacSparky, and comes away impressed, noting the app uses a Thunderbolt connection rather than WiFi and provides ample screen space when paired with an iPad Pro for travel setups.

1074763.abstract: Jamie reviews the movie The Martian, calling it entertaining and recommending it, while noting the book is better and the film omits a lot of material from it.

1074766.abstract: Jamie describes a long-standing goal of keeping a daily journal using the Day One app for iOS and Mac, noting past inconsistency. A recent change in approach produces a 13-day streak, shown in an accompanying bar chart of entries over 50 days.

1074767.abstract: Jamie reports that Namecheap's security notification emails included both old and new passwords in plaintext after a password change, exposing credentials via unencrypted email and suggesting Namecheap stores passwords in plaintext rather than as hashes.

1074768.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of the blood-red full moon captured during a total lunar eclipse, taken with a 70-200mm f2.8L lens and 2x doubler, while watching the event with neighbors.

1074769.abstract: Jamie shares a screenshot confirming successful deletion of a Google+ profile and associated social content, along with an exit survey option, noting the deletion was satisfying to complete.

1074774.abstract: Jamie describes attending the 2015 Minnesota Air Spectacular in Mankato, watching five hours of air performances despite hot, sunny conditions, and shares an embedded collection of photos from the event.

1074784.abstract: Jamie's Apple Watch, ordered on launch day in stainless steel with a link bracelet, arrives after a 4-6 week backorder.

1074786.abstract: Jamie shares a weekly report chart from SaneBox, an email management tool started a couple weeks earlier, showing daily personal email volume from Thursday to Wednesday, with important messages marked separately and total volume peaking near 70 on Tuesday.

1074789.abstract: Jamie orders the Apple Watch at 3:56am CT, choosing the 42mm Stainless Steel Case with Link Bracelet, and expresses anticipation for a new user experience and device category.

1074793.abstract: Jamie reports that a newly upgraded Comcast cable modem is now connecting via IPv6, noting the login address as evidence, and confirms the capability using the test-ipv6.com testing site.

1074794.abstract: Jamie highlights Software for Good, led by Casey Helbling, becoming one of the first companies to file as a benefit corporation under Minnesota's new Public Benefit Corporation Act.

1074795.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of a built LEGO City fire truck set (60002) with a white ladder, displayed on a play mat, and reflects on how modern LEGO pieces are more specialized and proprietary compared to the generic shapes Jamie remembers from childhood.

1074796.abstract: Jamie describes receiving Blokus as a Christmas gift in the Olson family brother-in-law swap, from Max. Jamie finds the game works best with four players, adapts gracefully to two, but suits three less well, and compares its blocking strategy loosely to Go.

1074797.abstract: Jamie links to Garry Kasparov's essay "The Chess Master and the Computer" at The New York Review of Books, quoting Kasparov's argument that chess computing abandoned innovation for incrementalism once brute-force search proved effective.

1074798.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a family outing to see Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer: The Musical at the Stages Theater in Hopkins, calling it the best production seen there, with praise for the costumes and the kids' enjoyment.

1074800.abstract: Jamie links to a Travis-CI post, "Minimum Vacation Policy," and agrees that unlimited vacation policies fail because uncertainty leads employees to take no time off, calling such policies a leadership punt. Jamie favors required annual vacation, or leaders modeling disconnecting.

1074801.abstract: Jamie describes submitting an account deletion request to Facebook, logging off, and erasing Facebook cookies, explaining this is why Jamie won't be reachable or reading posts there anymore.

1074802.abstract: Jamie describes using a Dropcam to monitor a garage and alley in South Minneapolis due to common garage theft, mounting it in a bay window with double-stick tape since no surface allowed the standard metal stand.

1074804.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Tyler smiling in an AC/DC t-shirt, standing in a bedroom with toys and a bunk bed ladder, noting AC/DC as one of Tyler's favorite bands.

1074805.abstract: Jamie complains about receiving identical Twitter promotional emails tied to a Thanksgiving NFL marketing campaign across 13 accounts, including several already deleted ones like @VeloTweets and @SenateTweets.

1074806.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Don and Kaye sitting among autumn leaves in a forest with their six grandkids: Tyler, Mazie, Lucas, Elsa, Nora, and Levi.

1074807.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the 2014 Olson Family Weekend, planned by Don and Kaye, which the extended family spent at Grand View Lodge.

1074808.abstract: Jamie encourages year-end donations to organizations defending an open Internet, quoting Dave Winer and recommending Tim Wu's book The Master Switch.

1074809.abstract: Jamie announces that Jamie's wife Tammy found a cabin, named Magic Pines, about 45 minutes from home on a lake with over an acre of land, closing in January for weekend getaways.

1074810.abstract: Jamie describes switching Question2Answer's anti-spam captcha, used on Ask Planet Kubb, from ReCaptcha to the Q2A Logical Captcha by amiyasahu, which uses Text Captcha but tripled spam registrations.

1074811.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of an "I Voted" sticker to mark participating in the 2014 election.

1074812.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy see the film Whiplash at the renovated Uptown Theater, praising its portrayal of the effort required to be great at music and its drumming and score. Jamie buys the soundtrack after the screening.

1074814.abstract: Jamie shares a photo from Titans of Tech 2014.

1074816.abstract: Jamie links to an MPR News report that United Properties is considering pro soccer for a site near the Minneapolis Farmers Market, potentially rivaling the Minnesota Vikings' Downtown East bid for an MLS stadium. Jamie hopes it happens and would consider season tickets.

1074817.abstract: Jamie describes an updated method for generating dynamic Questy Captchas for MediaWiki's ConfirmEdit extension, after spammers defeated the original character-based approach shared over a year earlier.

1074818.abstract: Jamie describes teaching a Kubb class alongside Garrick Van Buren, offered as an auction item at the annual SPS Charity Auction. A sales engineering team from SPS won the event, and 12 people attended a tournament-level session covering Kubb strategy and technique, accompanied by photos from the gathering.

1074823.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of a Mattel Classic Football handheld electronic game, noting the kids struggle to see it as a real game, while Jamie recalls loving it the year it was received for Christmas.

1074824.abstract: Jamie links to a two-part Charlie Rose interview with Apple CEO Tim Cook, noting it offers insight into how Apple works and how the company explores new products.

1074825.abstract: Jamie shares photos of Tyler catching a first fish over the weekend with help from Grandpa Don, noting Tyler's excitement and that Tyler released the fish back into the water alone.

1074826.abstract: Jamie describes restarting the Twin Cities Amazon Web Services User Group with Bridget Kromhout, renaming it AWS MN. The group meets monthly at SPS Commerce, using GitHub issues to coordinate, with David Federlein presenting on Automating AWS with Ansible next.

1074827.abstract: Jamie shares a fall poem written for Mazie's homework assignment, which asked parents to write a poem for their child to copy into a notebook. The poem describes bare trees, a chilly breeze, and the harvest moon.

1074828.abstract: Jamie describes a made-up word, "shingadooties," that Mazie invented to mean "everything," usable as any verb or noun. Jamie and Mazie define it here since it had no presence online, and a 2023 update notes it remains the only web reference and that OpenAI's GPT-4 doesn't recognize it.

1074831.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a first trip to Kyiv.

1074832.abstract: Jamie shares the LocalSettings configuration used to run a MediaWiki farm hosting about a dozen wikis at thingelstad.com, publishing the code to a GitHub repository (wiki-farm) for others to reference, with plans to later add the accompanying scripts.

1074833.abstract: Jamie describes starting to use Ansible for configuration management on hobby servers, after finding Chef too complex and never fully adopting SaltStack. Jamie manages some packages on Vagrant hosts with Ansible, with work shared on GitHub, and plans to convert build notes into Ansible playbooks.

1074834.abstract: Jamie shares a watercolor painting depicting a lone figure standing on a rocky cliff overlooking misty water, with trees in the background, evoking a scene along Lake Superior.

1074835.abstract: Jamie has clear vinyl stickers made for WikiApiary using a deal from StickerMule, and shares a photo of the bumblebee-themed stickers scattered on a sunflower background. Jamie offers to mail one to anyone who asks.

1074836.abstract: Jamie notes being one of over fifty-thousand backers of Mayday PAC, sharing a collage image celebrating the campaign reaching $5 million in donations on July 4th.

1074837.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a weekend trip on MetroTransit's new Green Line, riding from downtown Minneapolis to the end of the line in St. Paul with kids, stopping at a farmers market and passing a mural with math formulas and string-art sculptures.

1074838.abstract: Jamie sets up to watch stage 2 of the 2014 Tour de France, using a tablet propped on a kitchen counter with a Jawbone Mini Jambox speaker for sound, and wishes World Cup viewing were as easy without a cable subscription.

1074842.abstract: Jamie visits Ice Cream Riot, a new ice cream shop in Denver's Northeast neighborhood where the owner makes all the flavors, tasting Andes Mint, English Toffee and Fruit Loops. Jamie praises the creamy texture and relaxed vibe, and posts a Yelp review.

1074843.abstract: Jamie links to new Planet Kubb t-shirts available on Teespring, featuring a crown icon logo, and encourages readers to get one.

1074846.abstract: Jamie links to a Metafilter post about the CSS color "rebeccapurple," which highlights the human side of the technology community behind its creation, defined by a hue angle of 270 degrees, saturation of 50, and lightness of 40.

1074849.abstract: Jamie shares a graph tracking weekly IMAP message states for the jamie@thingelstad.com inbox, showing seen messages peaking near 100 before dropping to 23, with deleted messages averaging 463. Jamie notes the same tracking is done for an SPS inbox, though with larger numbers.

1074850.abstract: Jamie describes taking daughter Mazie to a New Standards show at The Dakota on Mazie's birthday, where Mazie enjoyed a Shirley Temple and cheeseburger while seated at a U-shaped table. Bandleader Chan Poling gave Mazie a birthday shoutout after Jamie emailed the band in advance.

1074851.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Mazie holding a tablet at a birthday party, with Tyler standing nearby, and describes Mazie receiving a personal iPad with own email and calendar accounts. Jamie notes Mazie already checks the calendar and plays games, while Tyler asks about getting one too.

1074852.abstract: Jamie shares a screenshot about a Facebook message on "improving ads" and "giving you control," arguing this really means Facebook collates data from every website with Like buttons to target ads more effectively, calling the framing bullshit.

1074853.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of a young girl making peace signs with both hands, wearing a navy graphic tee and purple leggings, and jokes that the shirt likely won't remain popular in a couple more years.

1074854.abstract: Jamie shares an aerial photo from 1938 found via the Minnesota Historical Aerial Photographs Online site, linked by friend Garrick, highlighting an undeveloped lot near Minnehaha Creek West Park where Jamie's current house, built in 1939, now stands. Jamie also notes a previous Minnetonka property was still farmland in 1937 and 1956.

1074856.abstract: Jamie describes stopping during a bike ride around Lake Harriet in Minneapolis and finding six women playing Kubb near the bandshell, using a Bex set on a somewhat small pitch and stacking field kubbs atop each other, unlike the players usually seen from Minnesota Kubb.

1074857.abstract: Jamie describes a family bike ride where Tyler tries a new Weehoo recumbent trailer bike, which Tammy also enjoys. Jamie compares it favorably to a Thule Chariot and a Novara trailer bike, citing its recumbent seat, low center of gravity, and secure seat-post attachment, though the pedal straps seem poorly designed.

1074859.abstract: Jamie describes helping Uncle Tim launch a website for Bike the Border, a North Dakota bicycle ride using WordPress as the CMS, and receiving a jersey in return. Uncle Tim plans to join Jamie for the Twin Cities Bicycling Club's Watermelon Ride on July 4th, wearing matching jerseys.

1074860.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Mazie smiling outside on the last day of school, marking the transition to becoming a 4th grader. Jamie notes the whole neighborhood celebrated as kids ran around to start summer.

1074861.abstract: Jamie describes ringing the NASDAQ market bell with the SPS team to open trading, an event covered on NASDAQ's market bell ceremonies page, and shares a photo of the group at the podium with the SPS Commerce logo displayed behind them.

1074862.abstract: Jamie and Tammy finish watching season 2 of House of Cards on Netflix, with Jamie praising the show and expressing particular enthusiasm for Kevin Spacey's performance.

1074864.abstract: Jamie explains why WikiApiary tracks pages rather than articles, responding to a question from Twitter user @Waldyrious and referencing an earlier answer on Jamie's WikiApiary talk page.

1074865.abstract: Jamie expresses a wish for a Dash docset for MediaWiki, noting that Kapeli's directions for creating docsets look straightforward and that pandoc could convert existing MediaWiki help pages into HTML for the docset, hoping someone else builds it.

1074868.abstract: Jamie links to an article by Rajiv Pant presenting a checklist memo for CTOs and technology managers covering culture, technology and operations. Jamie expresses respect for Rajiv and recommends the full piece to anyone in technology leadership.

1074873.abstract: Jamie shares a Keybase.io profile and describes Keybase as a product that uses public key cryptography in a decentralized way to establish identities through public proof rather than in-person meetings.

1074874.abstract: Jamie explores extending Keybase.io's cryptographic identity proofs to MediaWiki, proposing that users edit their User page and place proof text in the edit Summary field, since revision history provides a permanent, verifiable record via the MediaWiki API.

1074877.abstract: Jamie criticizes Twitter's Direct Messages "Mark all as read" button, which requires confirmation and displays in an alarming red color better suited to a delete-everything warning than a routine read-status action.

1074878.abstract: Jamie shares a new profile photo, a man in a dark blazer and blue plaid shirt outdoors with green foliage behind, adopted consistently across Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn and Google Plus, and posted here for easy future reference.

1074881.abstract: Jamie describes introducing Mazie to email and emoji characters, sharing a screenshot of one of Mazie's first emails, which fills the inbox with hundreds of rabbit face emoji followed by "ya" and dozens of exclamation marks.

1074882.abstract: Jamie mentions being a fan of Dropcam and pre-ordering two of the new Dropcam Tabs, expressing excitement to try them but wishing for a sooner shipping date.

1074883.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy and Jamie watch the PBS Frontline documentary "Generation Like," which examines how the social media ecosystem works, where revenue comes from, and what motivates users. Jamie finds it well done and wonders what impact such effort could have if directed toward something worthwhile instead of selling movie tickets.

1074884.abstract: Jamie describes migrating two personal Linode servers to Linode's newly announced cloud servers, which feature SSDs, double RAM, and a new chip architecture. Jamie notes an immediate performance improvement, illustrated by a graph showing faster API response times for the WikiApiary project.

1074885.abstract: Jamie contrasts Facebook's approach to scaling PHP, via HipHop (HHVM) and the newly announced Hack language, with Twitter's decision to re-engineer away from Ruby on Rails, and notes Wikipedia and WordPress instead rely on caching with tools like Varnish.

1074886.abstract: Jamie remembers Farhan Muhammad, CEO of ILM Professional Services, who died unexpectedly at age 41, recalling nearly a decade of collaborative technology projects across three companies. Jamie praises Muhammad's reliability, family devotion, and Pakistani heritage, and links to news coverage, an obituary, and tributes.

1074888.abstract: Jamie flags a Dropbox policy change automatically enrolling users into an arbitration agreement and points readers to Dropbox's opt-out page, noting it takes only a moment to opt out.

1074889.abstract: Jamie describes disabling a Google Plus and Gmail integration feature, noting frustration at needing to log into services only to turn off privacy-invading defaults, and includes a screenshot of the opt-out process.

1074890.abstract: Jamie marks WikiApiary's first anniversary, sharing statistics on the site's growth: 9,555 active wikis tracked, over 1.8 billion collected data samples, 5 million edits, and 32,416 visits.

1074892.abstract: Jamie shares the front and back images of a 2014 Christmas card.

1074893.abstract: Jamie describes neighbor Nicole's "Kids Running for Kid's" team, formed to raise money for Save the Children's World Marathon Challenge. Mazie and Tyler joined 50 other kids running marathon segments around the block, raising $1,526.

1074895.abstract: Jamie highlights photographer Layne Kennedy's book "Light Over Iceland," a collection of images from trips to Iceland, including one Jamie joined alongside Steve LeVahn and Dennys Bisogno. Jamie notes receiving special thanks on page 83 for a green laser and links to Jamie's own Iceland photos on photog.thingelstad.com.

1074897.abstract: Jamie shares scanned photos of an April 30, 1999 Star Tribune article about BigCharts being acquired by CBS MarketWatch, saved before recycling the old newspaper. Jamie notes Phil's hair at the time and that Phil later relocated to the San Francisco area, unrelated to BigCharts or MarketWatch.

1074898.abstract: Jamie lists productivity apps used on iPad, prompted by coworkers getting new devices. Highlights include OmniFocus for GTD-style tasks, OmniOutliner 2 for meeting notes and presentations, HipChat for team chat, MindNode for mind mapping, 1Password, Keynote, PCalc, OmniPlan 2, iA Writer, Dropbox, and Tweetbot, with brief notes on why each is…

1074899.abstract: Jamie describes a Twitter exchange between a wiki project's bot, which tweets random nutrition facts every 6 hours from a database of over 28,000 entries, and the account "theirctrout," which responded to a trout entry with an automated IRC-style trout slap.

1074901.abstract: Jamie shares photos from Mazie's first Minnesota Wild hockey game, attended along with Alone and Dylan. Mazie finds the game too loud at times but enjoys it overall, helped by chocolate ice cream and unusual hats.

1074903.abstract: Jamie describes the September 27th wedding of Jamie's sister Alona Thingelstad to Dylan Maas-Morgan at the Maple Grove Community Center, a Bahá'í ceremony with no officiant that Jamie opened with remarks, quoting from the Kitáb-i-Aqdas and 'Abdu'l-Bahá. Jamie shares wedding photos, also posted on Facebook.

1074904.abstract: Jamie describes a LinkedIn "People You May Know" prompt suggesting Jamie's 8-year-old daughter, despite there being no real LinkedIn account for her. Jamie speculates LinkedIn's iOS app pulled the name and email from contacts to encourage sending an invite.

1074905.abstract: Jamie shares a photo taken at the top of a high dune during the Saugatuck Dune Rides tour, where Lake Michigan is visible and the driver explains how the dunes formed, including that surrounding trees are actually six individual trees buried under over 100 feet of sand.

1074906.abstract: Jamie samples six hoppy beers at Saugatuck Brewing, including Pathfinder Pale Ale, Motueka's Revenge, Fortunate Events IPA, Not Messing Around Double IPA, Singapore IPA, and Continuum IPA, finding Continuum the favorite of the group.

1074907.abstract: Jamie shares panorama photos of beaches in the Saugatuck, Michigan area, expressing surprise at finding beaches like these in Michigan and describing relaxing, fun time spent in the sand and water there almost daily.

1074908.abstract: Jamie describes a beer flight at New Holland Brewing in Holland, Michigan, tried during a visit from nearby Saugatuck. Jamie lists six beers sampled clockwise, including Monkey King Saison, Imperial Hatter IPA, and Beerhive Tripel, noting all were very good.

1074909.abstract: Jamie links to an xkcd comic (xkcd.com/936) contrasting weak passwords with stronger passphrases, and notes using a long passphrase to unlock 1Password, previously described in a 2010 post, though many websites reject passwords longer than 20 characters.

1074910.abstract: Jamie describes problems paging through over 20,000 items in Semantic MediaWiki while exporting Wikinosh food data for use with Yaron Koren's Miga project.

1074911.abstract: Jamie links to NPR's story "The 40-Year-Old Photo That Gives Us A Reason To Smile," about a 1970s photograph of three Black and two white children laughing together in Mount Clemens. Jamie praises the photo but argues against tracking down and reporting on the children's current lives, feeling the moment should stand on its own.

1074912.abstract: Jamie shares photos taken over about an hour on Sunday at the 2013 US Nationals Kubb Championship, noting that Saturday was spent focused on the Kubbchucks team's bracket progress and Minnesota Kubb club results, while Sunday involved scoring games for Planet Kubb and running the Club Championship.

1074913.abstract: Jamie remembers John Riedl, a University of Minnesota computer science professor who died of melanoma after a three-year fight, tracing a friendship from a 1990 "hackers vs. crackers" letter to the Minnesota Daily, through GroupLens lab access, NetPerceptions, and a long-running book club.

1074914.abstract: Jamie describes using MediaWiki's QuestyCaptcha extension, part of ConfirmEdit, to stop wikispam on WikiApiary after Recaptcha and static questions failed.

1074915.abstract: Jamie describes the 10th Annual Olson Family Weekend, held in Lanesboro with Jamie's wife Tammy's family. Late season snow canceled biking plans, so the group played Kubb, celebrated Tammy's birthday, and marked Cinco de Mayo with margaritas made by the Daily family.

1074916.abstract: Jamie explains how to display the MediaWiki job queue size directly inside a wiki, developed for use on WikiApiary. The method uses the External Data extension to call the siteinfo API, retrieve the "jobs" value, and display it, combined with the MagicNoCache extension to prevent caching so the figure stays near real-time.

1074917.abstract: Jamie describes routinely unsubscribing from catalogs that arrive in the mailbox, noting some require detective work to opt out. Jamie contrasts this with email's legally required unsubscribe method under the CAN-SPAM Act and proposes catalogs print a plain unsubscribe URL, possibly as a QR code, near the mailing label.

1074919.abstract: Jamie reads Dave Winer's post about Google shutting down Google Reader while using Fever, a self-hosted RSS reader, and shares an accompanying photo.

1074920.abstract: Jamie reacts to Google's announcement that it will shut down Google Reader, noting a decision made years earlier to move away from it due to its social, Google Plus-integrated direction.

1074921.abstract: Jamie describes Tyler's third birthday, including bringing cupcakes to preschool, a family dinner at Yum! featuring mac-n-cheese and a cookie, opening presents, and watching the Thomas movie Misty Island Rescue at home. Photos show Tyler with a new worktable and Mazie demonstrating a new car toy.

1074922.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the 2013 Minnesota Kubb Tournament, held on Lake Calhoun, describing a 12-hour day outdoors that stayed cold despite dressing appropriately.

1074925.abstract: Jamie shares an email sent to DrawNames.com, a site the brother-in-laws on Tammy's side use to draw Christmas names, praising its smooth email confirmations and lack of ads or social logins, but proposing a small fee of $1-$2 per group to ensure the service's sustainability rather than relying on affiliate wishlist revenue.

1074926.abstract: Jamie shares a PHP snippet for the WordPress P2 theme, used on sites including team.minnestar.org, that adds email notifications when a user is @mentioned in a post or comment, since P2 normally only highlights the mention. Jamie notes it's based on code from trepmal.com and isn't heavily tested, but works well in practice.

1074927.abstract: Jamie describes attending Dads and Donuts day with Tyler at Berry Patch preschool, featuring a visit from Fireman Tom of the Edina Fire Department. Tyler tries on firefighter gear, poses by a ladder truck with Ms. Anita, sits in the driver's seat, and finishes with a donut.

1074928.abstract: Jamie describes fixing book title sorting on the Read/Write Book Club wiki (rwbookclub.com), where titles starting with "A," "An" or "The" were sorting incorrectly.

1074929.abstract: Jamie renames the home guest WiFi network from "Thingelstad Guest" to "openwireless.org" after Ry4an Brase posts about the EFF's Open Wireless project on Google+, and encourages others with router guest network support to do the same.

1074930.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a weekend visit to the National Eagle Center in Wabasha, Minnesota, including one with family posed beside a live bald eagle. Jamie and Mazie attend a workshop, learning about bald eagles and watching one eat lunch.

1074931.abstract: Jamie recounts attending a Robyn Hitchcock show at The Dakota with Tammy, who enjoyed Hitchcock's music in high school and college. Richard Lloyd opened but didn't impress either of them, while Hitchcock's nonsensical humor and performance made for an enjoyable night despite not knowing the songs well.

1074933.abstract: Jamie describes attending a performance by The New Standards at The Dakota jazz club, marking at least the sixth time seeing the group there. Jamie's friends Kent and Marilee joined to celebrate Kent's birthday, and the band mentioned a new album recording is finished and coming soon.

1074934.abstract: Jamie reports spotting AT&T LTE service for the first time while driving by the River Center in the Twin Cities, ahead of AT&T's announced year-end rollout, and finds the connection fast, comparable to WiFi.

1074936.abstract: Jamie shares photos taken between games at the 2012 Dallas Oktoberfest Kubb Tournament, where the Kubbchucks team competed.

1074937.abstract: Jamie marks Jamie's mom's 60th birthday, sharing a photo of her and noting the family gathered at the Minneapolis Photo Center, where Jamie took family photos to commemorate the occasion.

1074938.abstract: Jamie shares a video Dennys made from a recent Iceland trip taken with friends Steve, Dennys and Layne Kennedy, covering 1,200 miles of driving. Jamie likes how Dennys cut in driving segments for a road-trip feel and plans a recap blog post soon.

1074941.abstract: Jamie backs up photos from a trip to Iceland onto two separate 500G portable drives, connecting a MacBook Pro to the hard drives to ensure the photos aren't lost.

1074943.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of a packed camera backpack ahead of a week-long photography trip to Iceland, listing the full kit: a Canon 5D Mark II body, lenses including the 24-70mm, 70-200mm, 16-35mm, 15mm Fisheye and a 2X Extender, plus accessories like ND and gradient ND filters, a Rode video mic, Zoom H2 recorder, spare batteries, backup hard…

1074946.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Tyler at Choo Choo Bob's, watching a small electric train circle a track on a painted table during a visit together.

1074947.abstract: Jamie discovers that usakubb.com and usakubb.net redirect to Americoob's website rather than USA Kubb's official usakubb.org, the site for the US National Kubb Championship.

1074962.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the 2012 US National Kubb Championship in Eau Claire, where Jamie's team, the Kubbchucks, competed. The photos show teams like Kingpin, Wolfpack, Kubbsicles and Knuckleheads playing, posing in matching shirts, and celebrating with trophies and medals.

1074964.abstract: Jamie shares two iPhone screenshots from the PayPal mobile app: one showing an End User License Agreement prompt with Agree and View Privacy/Terms buttons, and another displaying the full lengthy license text, poking fun at how unreadable it is on a small screen.

1074967.abstract: Jamie shares photos of macchiatos from four coffee shops, Urban Bean Lyndale, Johnson Public House and Bradbury's Coffee in Madison, Wisconsin, presenting them as a reference standard and advising readers to pour out a macchiato that doesn't look like these.

1074968.abstract: Jamie announces a new photography website, Thingelstad Photography, built with WordPress using the AutoFocus 2.0 Pro theme by Allan Cole. Jamie plans to post an image weekly, often pulled from a Lightroom archive rather than recent shots.

1074970.abstract: Jamie describes building a personal bookmarking wiki called links_thing using MediaWiki and Semantic MediaWiki, defining bookmark properties like URL, Created at, and Has excerpt through Semantic Templates and Forms.

1074971.abstract: Jamie notes a longtime preference for real maple syrup over the corn-syrup blends common in stores, then shares a photo of an Our Family brand syrup bottle labeled "2% real maple syrup," questioning what makes up the other 98%.

1074973.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of the setup used to follow Apple's WWDC keynote: a MacBook Air and iPad side by side displaying live coverage, since Apple doesn't stream video live, relying on Mac Rumors Live for updates.

1074974.abstract: Jamie shares a photo from Terminal A, taken June 8 2012, showing a Windows Blue Screen of Death displayed on a monitor flanked by airport departure and arrival flight boards.

1074975.abstract: Jamie, a longtime OmniFocus user across Mac, iPhone and iPad, asks whether enough Twin Cities users would be interested in an informal meet up to share project structures, contexts and perspectives.

1074978.abstract: Jamie recaps two sessions from MinneBar 7: "Running a Virtual Server with Confidence," presented using build notes instead of slides, and "Every HTTP Status Code," co-presented with Garrick Van Buren, with both talks now available as embedded YouTube videos.

1074979.abstract: Jamie reports the start of another season of Men's Recreational E-League Softball, noting the B-Squad is playing well and a win seems within reach, and shares a photo of a Dusty's Bar sign advertising Dagos, burgers, soups and cocktails.

1074980.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Tyler seated in a large office chair, typing at a computer keyboard after wandering off alone upstairs at Tammy's parents' house, joking about it resembling Jamie's own habits.

1074983.abstract: Jamie links to a free iTunes photo book, "My Travels to Iceland," self-published by friend Dennys Bisogno documenting a trip taken with Steve LeVahn. Jamie hopes to join a future Iceland trip, possibly with photographer Layne Kennedy as well.

1074984.abstract: Jamie shares a MediaWiki template built with the Parser Functions extension that extracts a hostname from a given URL, using variable definitions for position and substring calculations. Jamie provides the template code, instructions for adding it as Template:Get hostname, and a usage example returning "www.thingelstad.com".

1074985.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a donut run with Tyler, who wears a green bucket hat throughout, pictured holding a Winnie the Pooh stuffed animal, sitting with a book at a coffee shop, and standing next to a cow statue outside a brick building.

1074986.abstract: Jamie considers switching from Gillette Mach 3 blades to the Dollar Shave Club's $6-a-month plan after running low on razors. Using Soulver to compare costs against Amazon's subscription price of $33.24 for a 15-pack, Jamie calculates a 32% savings and decides to sign up.

1074987.abstract: Jamie shares a security notice received from Slicehost, warning that an unauthorized party accessed the forum's login database containing emails, user IDs, and encrypted passwords.

1074988.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of a vinyl kubb decal, sold by Des Moines Kubb, applied to a yellow Mini Cooper, calling it well done and noting continued enthusiasm for the game Kubb.

1074989.abstract: Jamie describes receiving a second Kubb set purchased from Old Time Games, noting the kitchen smells like wood, and shares a photo of the pieces arranged on a kitchen counter. Jamie mentions plans to customize the set and post photos once finished.

1074992.abstract: Jamie describes playing three practice rounds of Kubb with friend Garrick at Minnehaha Creek West Park, with the first game going quickly to Garrick, the last quickly to Jamie, and a middle game lasting an hour. Photos show the wooden blocks and players on the winter lawn.

1074993.abstract: Jamie describes Typerighter, a minimal browser notepad built by friend Garrick Van Burden, and explains requesting a backup option.

1074994.abstract: Jamie describes Tyler turning two, with a birthday party held the prior weekend so Hector and Michelle could visit from New York, plus a smaller celebration on the actual birthday involving donuts from A Baker's Wife's, lunch at Yum!, and play at Edinborough Park. Jamie describes Tyler at two as active, playful, and not yet very verbal.

1074995.abstract: Jamie hosts a movie night with friends Jim, Tom and Tim to watch Stanley Kubrick's The Shining after wife Tammy declines to rewatch. Jamie reflects on the film's lasting impact since childhood and links to the Wikipedia page plus essays by Bill Blakemore and Rob Ager for deeper analysis.

1074996.abstract: Jamie recounts seeing Girlyman perform at 7th Street Entry in Minneapolis with friend Jim and wife Tammy, a show discovered through New York friend Hadar's blog about the band.

1074997.abstract: Jamie describes shutting down several websites, including Tammy's blog Smaller Than a Redwood, along with Road Sign Wordplay, Road Sign Bingo, MediaWiki Cookbook, Sandbox Wiki and thinglesBot, using nginx to serve proper "410 Gone" responses instead of "404" errors.

1074998.abstract: Jamie notes that the domain tylerthing.com came up for renewal and realizes its registration date, February 12, 2010, matches Tyler's birthday.

1074999.abstract: Jamie describes building a "Super Fort" in the living room with kids Mazie and Tyler, using OGOBILD Kit Pod sets and a 20-foot parachute from Amazon, after sheets proved too small and heavy for earlier fort attempts.

1075000.abstract: Jamie describes a morning smoothie routine built around a Vitamix 5200 blender used for about three months. Jamie explains a standard base of banana, apple and carrot, plus spinach, frozen berries or peaches, almond milk, chia seeds, and sometimes honey, noting the mix tastes good despite turning brown.

1075001.abstract: Jamie documents the January 18th SOPA blackout with screenshots from dozens of sites, including thingelstad.com, Tammy's Smaller Than A Redwood, and Mazie's site, all using Zach Johnson's protest template.

1075002.abstract: Jamie describes setting up crontab scripts to take all personal websites offline from 8 AM to 8 PM central time on January 18th, joining Wikipedia and Reddit in protesting the proposed SOPA and PIPA bills before Congress.

1075003.abstract: Jamie recounts turning 40, describing a birthday planned by wife Tammy that included breakfast at Original Pancake House, a visit to Como Park Conservatory with kids Mazie and Tyler, a chocolate cake baked by Mazie, Indian food from India Palace, and a surprise fire with friends.

1075004.abstract: Jamie links to Adobe's announcement of the Lightroom 4.0 beta, highlighting the new Map module that lets users add geographic coordinates to photos, a feature long wished for since earlier versions. Jamie notes face recognition remains absent, hoping for it in a future release.

1075006.abstract: Jamie describes a birthday dinner Tammy arranged at Heidi's Chef's Table in Minneapolis, featuring a 13-course vegetarian tasting menu designed by Chef Stewart Woodman (Shefzilla).

1075007.abstract: Jamie describes receiving a Yama cold brew drip tower as a birthday gift from Tammy, Mazie and Tyler, after seeing the design shared by Ry4an. The device takes three hours to brew 8 cups; Jamie's first attempt failed due to an inconsistent homemade grind, and Jamie links to a CoffeeGeek guide on iced coffee.

1075008.abstract: Jamie describes helping a friend from Dow Jones, known online as Armistral, plan a website called WeSolver, which uses MediaWiki and Semantic MediaWiki to let people collaborate on solving problems. Jamie recommended MediaWiki and notes the site is now live.

1075009.abstract: Jamie shares final photos and a walkthrough of a completed home remodel, covering the mudroom entry, office nook, family room with built-in media wall, home gym, fitness room, and storage areas, following an 18-week weekly update series on the project.

1075010.abstract: Jamie describes serving on the board of CaringBridge for three years, supporting the organization with both time and money, and encourages others to contribute during the holiday season through CaringBridge's Illuminate campaign.

1075011.abstract: Jamie recounts a visit to urgent care at Fairview Southdale after Tyler, 22 months old, fell into a kitchen door frame and cut his forehead. The doctor placed two stitches, with a follow-up in 5-7 days and no expected scarring.

1075013.abstract: Jamie shares a family photo from November 2011, taken by Angie, showing two adults and two young children posing outdoors on a lawn with evergreen trees in the background.

1075014.abstract: Jamie shares a Unix command pipeline for counting 404 errors across WordPress access logs stored per virtual host, combining zgrep, cut, sed, sort and uniq to rank the most frequent missing URLs, with sample output from thingelstad.com.

1075015.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy finds a favorite photo of Jamie while searching the Lightroom library for the exercise room, taken at the finish of the 2004 Chequamegon Fat 40 mountain bike race, showing Jamie mud-covered and seated among scattered bikes.

1075016.abstract: Jamie describes moving all websites, including this blog, from Slicehost to Linode, finding the new host 2-3 times faster for basic Linux tasks. The setup now runs nginx instead of Apache, uses php5-cgi over mod_php, and consolidates WordPress and MediaWiki under one PHP install, achieving 99.9% APC cache hits.

1075018.abstract: Jamie tests iTunes Match across a MacBook Pro, iPhone 4S, iPad 2, and Apple TVs, focusing on how it handles ratings, play counts, and Smart Playlists. Jamie finds ratings sync within 10-20 seconds and play counts update promptly, but last played dates don't update, and Smart Playlists referencing other Smart Playlists aren't supported.

1075019.abstract: Jamie shares high-resolution scans of album cover art for the band Good Commies, made up of friends from the B-Squad Softball team, after finding only thumbnails available online. The scans include covers for "Three Houses" and "Red Rug."

1075020.abstract: Jamie recommends creating an iOS 5 keyboard shortcut for iPhone owners with a Big Green Egg, setting up "bge" to expand into "Big Green Egg" via Settings - General - Keyboard - Shortcuts, saving typing effort.

1075021.abstract: Jamie describes reclaiming the garage after a summer remodel that filled the driveway with a dumpster, lumber, and a portable toilet, forcing cars onto the street. Jamie expresses excitement at parking both cars inside the garage again once it was cleared out.

1075022.abstract: Jamie describes the first snow of 2011 falling, with large flakes drifting down slowly, and expresses hope that the snow remains on the ground the next morning for Mazie.

1075025.abstract: Jamie recounts watching Margin Call, a movie depicting a 24-hour segment of the 2008 financial crisis, via iTunes rental, drawn in partly by star Kevin Spacey. Jamie finds the pacing uneven despite its 86% Rotten Tomatoes score, noting similarities to Glengarry Glen Ross in having no heroes, while praising the film's website.

1075026.abstract: Jamie prepares Chile Cornmeal-Crusted Tofu with Southwestern Corn Pudding from the Veganomicon cookbook, noting the tofu crust turned out too coarse but praising the corn pudding, and plans to try baking it on the Big Green Egg with New Mexican smoked chiles next time.

1075027.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy and Jamie watch Moneyball, starring Brad Pitt as Billy Beane, after having previously read the book. Jamie finds Pitt's casting surprising but effective, recommends the movie while still preferring the book, and notes the film references Bill James but never mentions sabermetrics.

1075028.abstract: Jamie describes cooking Hot-Sauce Glazed Tempeh from the Veganomicon cookbook during a month of eating vegan with Tammy, using a Big Green Egg grill at 450°F and serving it with Messy Rice, a vegan take on Dirty Rice.

1075029.abstract: During a month of eating vegan, Jamie adapts the Ratatouille's Ratatouille recipe from Smitten Kitchen by cooking it on a Big Green Egg set up for indirect heat instead of in the oven, then serves it over couscous. Jamie reports a light smoke flavor and finds the dish delicious, noting the Big Green Egg can replicate oven cooking.

1075030.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy and daughter Mazie see Dolphin Tale, finding it a heartwarming, family-friendly film, and Jamie links to See Winter for more on Winter the Dolphin. Jamie also mentions dinner beforehand at Big Bowl, enjoying a vegan Kung Pao Tofu dish, and a successful first attempt at leaving Tyler with a sitter.

1075031.abstract: Jamie describes Tammy making hot soup in a Vitamix blender by running it on high for several minutes, which heats the ingredients through blending friction alone. Jamie shares a photo showing an infrared thermometer reading 189.0 degrees Fahrenheit as proof.

1075032.abstract: Jamie shares photos of low voltage wiring work by Ben from Homelink Entertainment during a home remodel, highlighting a wall plate with labeled Cat 5 jacks, coax, and speaker terminations, calling the meticulous detail "awesome."

1075033.abstract: Jamie reports that a home remodel project reaches completion at 18 weeks, within the originally expected 16-to-20-week timeframe. This final week includes flooring installation, finished electrical work, network infrastructure, and security system setup; Jamie shares photos and plans a final wrap-up post once furniture is in place.

1075034.abstract: Jamie describes Whole Foods sparking Jamie's wife Tammy's interest in a Vitamix blender, despite Tammy's usual ambivalence toward gadgets, leading to a purchase tied to their 30 Day Vegan Challenge. Jamie compares it favorably to a longtime BlendTec, noting each has areas of specialization.

1075035.abstract: Jamie shares photos of Tyler playing with two Magna Doodles at once, carrying both around the house and occasionally pausing to scribble on them before moving on.

1075036.abstract: Jamie shares a photo from 8thBridge, where Apple-focused coworkers marked Steve Jobs's passing with a memorial sheet cake featuring a frosting iPhone and the inscription "Rest in peace Steve Jobs."

1075037.abstract: Jamie captures a detail spotted by friend Kent Tangen and shared on Facebook: Apple's website tribute to Steve Jobs used the file name "t_hero.png," visible in the page's inspector code, which Jamie preserves as a fitting label for the memorial image.

1075038.abstract: Jamie shares a gapingvoid cartoon featuring the character "Gloop," received in a daily email, linking to the piece on gapingvoidgallery.com. Jamie quotes the artist's description of Gloop as representing human dignity and self-belief amid hardship, calling it a fitting message for the day.

1075041.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Mazie playing in a soccer game on Saturday, kicking a ball through a muddy puddle on the field, noting the kids had no trouble playing through the wet conditions.

1075042.abstract: Jamie reports major progress on a home remodel: painting is mostly finished, the mudroom railing and both built-ins are complete, utility and electric rooms are usable again, and a fence is installed around egress window wells. Jamie anticipates the coming week will finish electrical work, cork flooring, carpet, and theatre and network wiring.

1075043.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of runners passing through a tree-lined street during the Twin Cities Marathon, taken while walking over to watch the race at Minnehaha Creek on a sunny autumn morning.

1075044.abstract: Jamie shares a shell script for monitoring Cacti polling times, designed to run hourly via cron. The script scans the Cacti log, averages the last 24 polling samples (about 2 hours), and emails an alert if the average exceeds a configurable threshold, catching slowdowns before they cause data gaps.

1075046.abstract: Jamie describes having an iPad snatched while waiting for the 4K bus at Lake and Lyndale in Minneapolis, after a day out with 8thBridge that included Bryant Lake Bowl, moto-i, and Muddy Waters.

1075048.abstract: Jamie describes buying a LoFerno fire pit made by local artist Jeff Lohaus, whose work was first seen at Art Attack in the Northrup King Building. Jamie compares it favorably to a Big Green Egg chiminea, praising its 120-pound weight, thick steel construction, and fire tower design.

1075049.abstract: Jamie shares photos of ad hoc signs Mazie and friend Gigi added to a playhouse while playing, including phonetically spelled messages like "Keep owt," "No MoMr," and "Privet Popry." Jamie enjoys the inventive spelling.

1075050.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of new built-in cabinetry installed in the family room, featuring a wood veneer panel, frosted glass TV niche, and white lower drawers, with a floating granite shelf and TV/speaker mounting still to come.

1075051.abstract: Jamie provides a week 16 update on a home remodel, noting the project has extended beyond the original timeline with about two more weeks remaining.

1075052.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy and Jamie have dinner at Kings Wine Bar in Minneapolis before watching the film Contagion. Jamie calls it a good movie, noting it may even underplay the chaos a real epidemic would cause, and jokes about feeling wary of other moviegoers afterward.

1075053.abstract: Jamie describes planting 32 plants purchased at 50% off from Wagners nursery, after landscapers improved the yard. Jamie handles most of the digging while Tammy and Mazie place plants in the ground, with hope they establish before winter.

1075054.abstract: Jamie shares a week 15 remodel update covering exterior painting of the new mudroom, installation of the bannister and family room hand railing, and progress finishing the utility and electrical rooms. Jamie notes upcoming plans for more painting, cabinetry, and landscaping to restore the yard.

1075055.abstract: Jamie recounts a first trip of the year to the Renaissance Festival on Labor Day, including the annual attempt at the strongman hammer game, ringing the bell 3 out of 5 times. A photo shows the strongman sign ranking titles from Kynge down to Pustule.

1075056.abstract: Jamie describes week 14 of a home remodel, noting the mudroom tile floor installation and finish carpenters completing doors, trim, and pocket doors. Upcoming work includes outdoor railing installation, final painting starting Wednesday, and delivery of two built-in cabinets.

1075058.abstract: Jamie describes week 13 of a home remodel as slow-moving, with work focused on installing the mudroom tile floor, which temporarily cut off basement access.

1075059.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy watch the movie Midnight in Paris at the Edina Cinema, a rare trip to see a film. Jamie finds it fun, interesting, and describes it as leaving them with a smile.

1075061.abstract: Jamie describes the document versioning feature in Mac OS X Lion, noting its appearance in updated applications like OmniGraffle. Jamie finds the ability to revert to previous document versions helpful, though notes discoverability may be a challenge, and shares a screenshot comparing two versions of a transit journal diagram.

1075062.abstract: Jamie describes troubleshooting why Google Reader stopped picking up thingelstad.com's RSS feed for days or weeks. Jamie determines the cause was uninstalling PubSubHubbub, and after reinstalling it, updates appear in Google Reader within seconds.

1075063.abstract: Jamie assembles a John Deere pedal tractor, a gift from Jamie's Mom given after Tyler was born, recalling a similar heavy metal pedal tractor at Jamie's Grandparents' farm. Photos show Tyler sitting on the tractor, still too small to pedal it, and Mazie trying it out too.

1075064.abstract: Jamie provides a week 12 update on a home remodel, noting drywall priming, ceiling painting, exterior siding reassembly, and new front trim replacing rotting pine. The temporary kitchen wall comes down, and railing replacement and mudroom tile installation are underway.

1075065.abstract: Jamie recounts Mazie's performance at the 2011 So Long Summer show, an annual neighborhood event hosted by the Miller family for five years running before school starts. Mazie sings "It's a Hard Knock Life" from Annie, and Jamie expresses pride while noting poor camera focus during filming.

1075066.abstract: Jamie describes building a playhouse for Mazie and Tyler after Jamie's wife Tammy noticed the kids enjoyed playhouses when visiting others. The project involved a Home Depot trip for cedar deck boards to build a floor platform, with Mazie helping assemble it and Tammy preparing the site.

1075067.abstract: Jamie shares a photo from an impromptu S'mores gathering at neighbors the Conley's, noting that Mazie enjoyed staying up until 11:30 pm around the fire pit.

1075070.abstract: Jamie provides an update on week 11 of a home remodel, describing progress on drywall mudding and taping while Jamie's family was out of town, and notes the walls looked smooth on return, signaling the project is nearing completion.

1075071.abstract: Jamie shares a week 10 update on a home remodel, describing drywall installation across the framed space, completed by one worker in two days using large 54-inch by 12-foot sheets, followed by application of joint compound. Photos from the week are included.

1075072.abstract: Jamie describes feeling saddened by the sight of orange-ringed trees marked for removal in the neighborhood, sharing photos of a removal crew and a mature street tree with major limbs cut. Jamie mentions a large ash tree at home kept on a treatment program from Rainbow Treecare, hoping to protect it from invasive pests.

1075073.abstract: Jamie describes selling used electronics on eBay by pricing low with no reserve and letting the market decide, then highlights an experiment with three identical first-generation Apple TVs listed simultaneously with wildly different bids (53, 31, and 10 dollars) despite equal watcher counts, questioning market efficiency.

1075074.abstract: Jamie describes putting Gypsie, a calico cat owned since college, to sleep after kidney failure at around 22 years old. Jamie recalls Gypsie's history, quirks like an inability to meow, tension with Tammy and the family's dogs, and describes the peaceful euthanasia process with Tammy and Mazie present.

1075076.abstract: Jamie provides a week nine update on a home remodel, noting exterior work on the new mudroom nearing completion aside from the roof, railing, paint and door. Inside, the electrician finishes most work except the doorbell, low voltage installers run Category 5E and speaker cable, and a radon system gets installed despite acceptable test levels.

1075078.abstract: Jamie links to U2's "gigapixel" Fan Cam from the U2 360° show, noting curiosity about how the high-detail crowd-capturing technology works. The Fan Cam caught Jamie and Tammy in the audience, with Jamie noting looking "dorky" while eating popcorn before the band came onstage.

1075079.abstract: Jamie provides a week eight update on a home remodel, describing completed framing, an electrical walk-through, security system pre-wiring, furnace ducts, and deck reassembly, plus plans for electrical inspection, low voltage work, and fencing restoration in the coming week.

1075080.abstract: Jamie recounts hearing an electrician nicknamed Sparky at two office build-outs, then overhearing framers at a remodel using the same name for the electrician on site, prompting the question of whether "Sparky" is a generic nickname for electricians on job sites.

1075087.abstract: Jamie provides a week seven update on a home remodel, noting the basement walls are now framed and windows installed in the mudroom and family room, giving a sense of light and flow. Most of the side lawn is restored, a temporary dust barrier is set up in the office, and an exterior wall is removed for new pocket doors.

1075089.abstract: Jamie contrasts an indoor temperature of 76°F with air conditioning against outdoor conditions of 91°F, 75% humidity, and an 81°F dew point, illustrating the difference with a photo of condensation fogging a window.

1075090.abstract: Jamie describes week six of a home remodel, noting the basement now has a cement floor and finished steps, and the old exterior wall was removed to open up the new mudroom. Egress windows are framed for installation, rebar-reinforced cinder block walls await cement pouring, and air conditioning is restored with a new furnace and condenser.

1075091.abstract: Jamie compares real versus perceived progress on a 12-week home remodel to patterns seen in software projects, noting how groundwork and framing feel fast while final details like edge cases and punch-list items drag on.

1075092.abstract: Jamie describes Tyler spending half an hour climbing in and out of a car seat brought inside from the van, treating it as a toy. An accompanying photo shows the blond toddler sitting in the gray car seat indoors, smiling and holding a pink sippy cup.

1075093.abstract: Jamie describes fitting Tyler's forward-facing car seat into a Mini Cooper, noting the infant seat never fit and rear-facing installation wasn't possible either. The forward-facing setup works, though the fit isn't spacious, and includes a photo of the seat installed in the yellow Mini's back seat.

1075094.abstract: Jamie shares photos of Minnehaha Creek running high, fast, and muddy after Friday's heavy rains, noting it looked more like a river. Jamie links to a February photo of the same spot for comparison.

1075095.abstract: Jamie describes using a Square credit card reader, originally bought for a planned garage sale, to collect funds for the B-Squad 2011 Bat Fund at Dusty's, swiping six Visa cards and finishing fundraising within a week.

1075096.abstract: Jamie describes concrete trucks arriving between 6:45 and 7:00am to pour a new basement floor for a home project, with one truck mixing concrete and pumping it through a hose into the basement. Jamie's child Tyler watches the trucks from the window while Jamie leaves for work.

1075097.abstract: Jamie describes a drinking fountain at the Minnesota Arboretum visitor center, made by Elkay, that includes a bottle-filling station and a digital counter tracking disposable bottles saved—46,060 at the time. Jamie praises the design and links to an earlier post, "Stop Drinking Bottled Water."

1075098.abstract: Jamie describes week five of a home remodel: the mudroom is framed in, steel reinforcement plates are installed in the basement, and the dirt is prepped for concrete pouring, delayed to the following week. Jamie anticipates a basement floor and windows soon, plus restored main-floor air conditioning.

1075099.abstract: Jamie describes setting up an email filter for Google Plus notifications, matching messages from "@plus.google.com" and routing them to a folder using Sieve mail filtering syntax.

1075102.abstract: Jamie shares photos of the 2011 B-Squad shirts, featuring a diamond-shaped logo reading "Every Stat For Itself" with "Dustys in our heart and stomach," and notes the design glows in the dark, crediting Keekley for the idea.

1075103.abstract: Jamie describes finishing Shel Silverstein's "Where the Sidewalk Ends" with daughter Mazie, who found the poems funny and goofy. Jamie recalls reading the same book as a child and hopes Mazie remembers it similarly in 30 years.

1075104.abstract: After a week trying a makeshift standing desk built from a copy paper box, Jamie reports worse lower back pain, sore feet, but more movement and interaction with coworkers, while noting the setup makes one-on-one office conversations harder and remains ergonomically imperfect.

1075105.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy attend a Black Keys concert at Roy Wilkins Auditorium, having recently discovered the band. Jamie describes Dan Auerbach and Patrick Carney's simple two-person stage setup, an oversized disco ball, and songs from Brothers played with added band members, sharing iPhone photos of the lighting and crowd.

1075106.abstract: Jamie describes Tyler climbing onto a chair and operating a computer keyboard unsupervised while the Tour de France streamed in the background, noting Tyler's persistence as a climber. A photo shows the toddler kneeling at a wooden desk typing on an Apple keyboard in front of an iMac.

1075107.abstract: Jamie recounts an Independence Day filled with activities for Mazie and Tyler, including a pancake breakfast, a trip to the Minnesota Zoo, swimming at the Edina Pool, Cheeseburger Pie for dinner, watching Mr. Popper's Penguins, and Minneapolis fireworks, plus a surprise visit from Grandma Rosalin.

1075108.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Tyler, a blond toddler in a blue high chair, biting into a glazed donut with both hands while wearing a green shirt, noting that Tyler likes donuts.

1075109.abstract: Jamie tries Rush River's Bubble Jack IPA at Cheeky Monkey Deli in St. Paul, having a second pint on the patio, and recommends it for a summer evening.

1075110.abstract: Jamie describes week four of a home remodel: egress window wells are poured and filled in the yard, and the mudroom foundation is complete, easing yard access.

1075111.abstract: Jamie describes using a portable conveyor belt to remove seven inches of dirt from a basement floor, noting the conveyor also appeared in a prior photo of the basement destruction posted two days earlier.

1075113.abstract: Jamie describes heavy equipment being brought inside to tear out the basement floor, and shares a photo showing the demolished space with the concrete broken into rubble piles, exposed dirt, and yellow-and-white cinder block walls.

1075114.abstract: Jamie shares an update on a home remodel project, noting that concrete forms have been poured for the foundation, including new egress window openings and a mudroom foundation, and includes photos of the excavated work site.

1075115.abstract: Jamie describes seeing Cars 2 in 3D with daughter Mazie, calling it a Daddy-Daughter outing with Gummy Bears. Jamie names Cars as a favorite kids' movie and finds Cars 2 fun but not as good, noting the original set a high bar.

1075116.abstract: Jamie complains about monthly AT&T autopay text notifications, illustrated with a screenshot showing a $153.63 charge. Jamie lists complaints: poorly timed interruptions (including one on Christmas Day), lack of human scheduling logic, and awkward, jargon-filled wording.

1075117.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Tyler pushing a neighbor's Honda lawn mower in the yard, holding a small red cup, taken while Jamie was photographing the remodel update for the week.

1075118.abstract: Jamie describes week three of a home remodel, marked by heavy equipment and large holes dug around the yard, making it hard to walk between front and back and confusing the dog, Chase. Jamie notes plans for framing and basement floor excavation ahead, enthusiasm for basement light and large windows, and about three lost workdays due to rain.

1075119.abstract: Jamie tries out a standing desk setup made from a box of paper and an upside-down recycling container supporting a monitor and keyboards, with plans to consider a proper standing desk if the trial works well.

1075120.abstract: Jamie recounts accompanying the kids to the Science Museum while Jamie's wife Tammy attends a second photography class, following a previous Saturday's trip to the Zoo, and shares photos from the visit in an embedded collection.

1075121.abstract: Jamie shares a video combining nine matches from a Ping Pong Tournament held at this year's Olson Family weekend, edited together using the newly purchased Final Cut Pro X.

1075122.abstract: Jamie shares photos of excavation work happening around the house, including a Takeuchi TB016 mini excavator and a CAT skid steer digging holes for concrete forms near egress windows and exposing the brick foundation wall. One photo shows Jamie sitting in the excavator.
