1075123.abstract: Jamie describes Mom rescuing Hostas and other plants from the side of the house before remodel excavation begins, with Mazie helping load them into Grandma's car. A photo shows the two hugging beside a potted plant in the backyard.

1075124.abstract: Jamie describes attending an outdoor puppet show in Garrick Van Buren's backyard with Mazie, the third year the Open Eye Figure Theatre has hosted its Driveway Tour there, drawing over 100 attendees.

1075125.abstract: Jamie receives an email from Google's Search Quality Team warning that a WordPress blog managed for a brother-in-law is running an outdated version, with links to the WordPress download page and a Google blog post explaining the notifications.

1075126.abstract: Jamie takes Mazie and Tyler to the Minnesota Zoo while Tammy attends a photo workshop at the Minneapolis Photo Center. The visit includes a dolphin show, a crowded shark feeding, and a monorail ride, with Mazie photographing the outing and posting 100 photos to a personal website.

1075127.abstract: Jamie describes issues with a two-year-old Mini Cooper S: it can't fit all four family members, Tammy can't drive its manual transmission, and its front-wheel drive causes torque steering. Jamie plans to test drive a Mini Countryman All4, hoping it solves these problems while keeping the Mini feel, and asks readers for experiences with the model.

1075128.abstract: Jamie describes long-term enrollment in Xcel Energy's Windsource program, which buys renewable wind energy to offset usage. Citing a blog post on The Deets, Jamie notes Windsource customers avoid the Fuel Cost Charge, making the program's net cost only $5.82, or $0.18 per day, on a recent bill covering 830 kWh.

1075129.abstract: Jamie describes Tyler briefly sitting in a small green safari-print rocking chair that Jamie's Mom gave Mazie, noting the novelty lasts only about five seconds since Tyler stays constantly on the move. Photos show Tyler in a red shirt seated among toys and books.

1075130.abstract: Jamie shares an update on a home remodel's second week, noting installation of a new furnace, new footings poured for central supports and replacement of a 1939 wooden foundation beam with a steel I-beam. Jamie notes excavation work is set to begin the following Monday.

1075131.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the first week of a remodel project, covering demolition of the deck to prepare for a new mudroom foundation and initial work removing a central support post in the basement to open up space for a family room.

1075132.abstract: Jamie recounts reading The Hunger Games trilogy by Suzanne Collins on Kindle after Jamie's wife Tammy recommended it, finishing all three books within a couple of weeks. Jamie calls the series enjoyable and recommended for summer reading, though finding the ending of Mockingjay wanting more story.

1075134.abstract: Jamie describes watching "The King's Speech" and finds the movie very good with incredible acting, calling it worthy of its awards. Jamie also recommends the film's Wikipedia page as a good read.

1075135.abstract: Jamie shares a team photo of the Spring 2011 Cyclones, taken after their last game, along with two coaches on a grassy lawn. Jamie notes the team played a great spring season and will return in Fall.

1075138.abstract: Jamie links to a Memorial Day video by photographer Dennys Bisogno, shot in River Falls, Wisconsin using a Canon 1D and edited in Final Cut. Jamie highlights the clip of an elderly soldier walking down a path at 3:40 as particularly notable.

1075139.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Mazie sprinting across the field in a Cyclones shirt during a second season of soccer with the Fuller Soccer Club, noting the team's improved ball handling and Mazie's enjoyment.

1075141.abstract: Jamie describes the start of a remodeling project on the house, lasting just under four months, covering lowering the basement floor, adding two egress windows, installing a new furnace and air conditioning unit, and adding a mud room.

1075143.abstract: Jamie shares photos of car dashboards posted on Facebook showing outside temperatures of 103, 100, and 103 degrees Fahrenheit, noting it was a hot day and that taking dashboard photos to prove it seemed to be a trend.

1075144.abstract: Jamie congratulates friend Jim Bernard on completing the Minneapolis Marathon, Jim's first marathon, noting Jim looked great even at the finish. A photo shows runners and spectators at the finish line on a sunny day.

1075145.abstract: Jamie describes using a Max Burton Pro Chef 1800 portable induction cooktop, bought from Kitchen Window, as an outdoor burner for tasks like simmering barbecue sauce while smoking a brisket on a Big Green Egg. Jamie values its durability, easy cleaning, and precise temperature control, noting it struggles only with boiling large volumes of water.

1075146.abstract: Jamie watches the documentary Inside Job about the financial collapse and finds it very good, noting the recap of CDOs and credit default swaps is somewhat redundant for those already familiar, while praising its pointed criticism of ratings agencies and the economics profession.

1075147.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Tyler wearing a Minnesota Twins jersey and cap, joking that the effort hasn't yet helped the last-place Twins.

1075148.abstract: Jamie describes grilling an entire Memorial Day meal outside, including burgers, asparagus, carrots, and grilled romaine hearts, using two Big Green Egg grills on a deck prep table.

1075149.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Mazie climbing a tree during a kindergarten class picnic at the Rose Garden by Lake Harriet.

1075151.abstract: Jamie recounts attending a Foo Fighters concert at the Mid-America Center in Council Bluffs with Kent, disappointed that opening act Motörhead cancelled due to travel problems but noting the Foo Fighters compensated with a 2.5-hour set.

1075152.abstract: Jamie describes trying to use the myTouchTunes iPhone app to remotely control the jukebox at Dusty's Bar and Dagos, home bar of Jamie's B-Squad softball team, but abandons it after the registration form demands email, zip code, birth date, and gender.

1075153.abstract: Jamie references Marco Arment's post on Twitter's API changes, quoting Arment's point that "Twitter is not Ours" and can do whatever it wants since it's a private, centralized service. Jamie extends this to other platforms, explaining it as the reason for running personal websites on self-administered servers using open source software.

1075154.abstract: Jamie highlights the term "technotarian," encountered in a Jason Calacanis article about Bitcoin, quoting its footnote definition describing internet advocates for individual freedom, free speech, and open technologies like Wikileaks, Anonymous, Linux, and Wikipedia. Jamie also links to a 1995 definition of Technological Libertarianism.

1075155.abstract: Jamie shares photos from MinneBar 6, taken mainly at the event's kick-off since Jamie presented during the first three sessions, showing registration, MinneBar MMXI t-shirts, speakers including Luke and Ben Edwards, and crowded conference rooms.

1075156.abstract: Jamie notes that the original Twilight Zone series is now available on Netflix streaming via Apple TV, and mentions watching season 1, episode 1, "Where is Everybody?"

1075160.abstract: Jamie reports spotting a Tesla Roadster parked outside Café Lurcat in Minneapolis, and guesses from the plates that the car belongs to someone from Z.Vex Effects. A photo shows the black Roadster parked at dusk among other vehicles.

1075161.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy finds a pot rack from Org Innovations that fits the kitchen in the new house, though mounting it proves difficult since the wall studs aren't spaced 16 inches on center. Jamie expects it to make cooking more pleasant.

1075162.abstract: Jamie describes adding LED tree lights to the backyard to create a nighttime outdoor living space, hiring Custom Christmas Lighting for the installation and noting satisfaction with the result. A photo shows trees wrapped in warm white lights on a deck at dusk.

1075165.abstract: Jamie describes a newly installed cabinet with a black granite countertop that now houses an espresso machine and coffee grinder, plumbed directly so the reservoir no longer needs filling, with only door pulls left to add.

1075166.abstract: Jamie asks for planting suggestions for a shaded backyard bed created during hardscaping the previous year, preferring native, low-light perennials with possibly a few annuals, and shares a photo of the stone bed alongside the garage.

1075167.abstract: Jamie describes an odd Facebook exchange spotted while following photographer Jim Brandenburg, who lives in Ely, Minnesota. Brandenburg posted about selling camera gear, but a commenter named "Ellen" replies repeatedly in all caps, seemingly missing the point.

1075168.abstract: Jamie describes ordering an Ergotron LX LCD Arm and Apple Cinema Display adapter, inspired by a friend Garrick van Buren's post about a similar ergonomic upgrade, after experiencing back fatigue from sitting improperly.

1075169.abstract: Jamie describes visiting Grandma Rose in North Dakota for a long weekend and seeing a needlework display, made by Jamie's mother, listing the names and birthdates of fifteen grandchildren. Jamie reflects on what the piece represents about family.

1075171.abstract: Jamie shares a passage from Edward Glaeser's book Triumph of the City, which is being read by Jamie's book club, highlighting Minneapolis's post-1950 population decline and later economic resurgence tied to University of Minnesota-educated leaders at Medtronic and Target. Jamie notes surprise at the city's high education ranking.

1075172.abstract: Jamie discusses the Epsilon data breach as an example of the downsides of Internet centralization, contrasting it with the decentralized design that lets independent blogs run on personal servers. Jamie shares notification emails from Marriott, Hilton HHonors, and TiVo, all informing customers their email addresses were exposed through Epsilon.

1075175.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of the newly arrived Fitbit Ultra activity tracker, describing an easy initial setup and appreciation for automatic wireless data uploads, and plans to report on results after using it to track daily activity and sleep.

1075178.abstract: Jamie describes a vacation week that includes a trip to North Dakota, a day spent with Tyler, and plans for a Daddy/Daughter day with Mazie. Jamie also shares a photo of a Chemex coffee break featuring an old Road Sign Math mug.

1075180.abstract: Jamie highlights lyrics from Eddie Vedder's song "Society," from the Into the Wild soundtrack, quoting the verse about "less is more" and how measuring it against "keeping score" undercuts the idea. Jamie finds the lines striking and thought-provoking.

1075183.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy gave Jamie a Lensbaby Composer lens for Christmas, inspired by pro photographer Layne Kennedy's enthusiasm for the lens during the Stone/Steel/People workshop. Jamie shares photos shot manually at f/4 during a trip to Grand Marais.

1075184.abstract: Jamie describes adding a Canon TS-E 24mm f/3.5L tilt-shift lens to the camera bag, noting it's the older version rather than the new Mark II. Jamie plans to use it mainly for creative effect and video shooting while still learning its operation.

1075185.abstract: Jamie shares early results from experimenting with a new tilt-shift lens while shooting in Grand Marais, including a snowy shoreline shot and a forest image where the tilt effect blurs the frame around a focused clearing. Jamie plans more experimenting, including video.

1075186.abstract: Jamie describes clicking an unsubscribe link that triggers several redirects, one of which briefly reveals a URL containing "leadCapture/save." Jamie takes this as confirmation the emails weren't needed, and wonders what cookies were dropped during the redirect chain.

1075187.abstract: Jamie describes upgrading to iOS 4.3 to enable Personal Hotspot on an iPhone 4, which required switching from AT&T's unlimited data plan to a metered one.

1075188.abstract: After a book club discussion with Dan and other members about writing a book, Jamie uses the WordPress Word Stats plugin to tally blog output: 226,235 words since February 2004, averaging 2,631 per month, with 2010 notably quiet.

1075189.abstract: Jamie describes Tyler's progress from crawling to walking, noting that Tyler passed the 1 year mark without much walking practice but now takes a dozen or more steps without falling. Jamie shares a Vimeo video of the milestone.

1075191.abstract: Jamie describes a photography weekend near Grand Marais with friends Steve and Dennys, where snowy, grey conditions made shooting difficult.

1075192.abstract: Jamie describes cooking lasagna and acorn squash on a Big Green Egg grill for a dinner with friends. Jamie notes the lasagna picked up a smoky, smoked-mozzarella-like flavor and offers lessons learned: use the grid rather than placing the pan directly on the plate setter, cover with tinfoil to reduce smokiness, and use a ceramic baking dish…

1075196.abstract: Preparing for a class presentation at the University of Minnesota for friend John, Jamie revisits an old Keynote slide predicting OpenID would become a social graph, hCard-based, browser-integrated customer gateway. Jamie admits being badly wrong, noting regret since OpenID was open and not owned by any single company.

1075197.abstract: Jamie recounts having dinner at friends the Rock's, where Mike made ristretto using a Gaggia espresso machine. Inspired, Jamie adjusts the grind on the Andreja machine at home and produces rich, delicious shots.

1075198.abstract: Jamie describes discovering The Black Keys through an interview on Fresh Air on MPR and picking up the band's new album, Brothers, recommending it and highlighting the track "Black Mud" as one to play loud.

1075199.abstract: Jamie notes that the 8thBridge office added prints by Michael Birawer to its hallways, including amusement park and urban cityscape artwork, and shares photos of the framed pieces displayed on the office's orange and yellow walls.

1075200.abstract: Jamie describes a frustrating experience buying an issue of Wired magazine (19.01) through its iPad app: the 368MB download required deleting a movie to free storage, took about 15 minutes, then needed a separate installation step before Jamie could view the content, mostly advertisements. Jamie doesn't plan to repeat the process.

1075202.abstract: Jamie describes limited options for clearing snow from a driveway, often blowing it over the fence or against a neighbor's garage, and considers building wood shelves next fall to act as a snow fence, allowing snow to be blown 10-12 feet high. A photo shows a collapsed snow pile against the garage wall.

1075204.abstract: Jamie shares a panoramic photo of the New Standards performing at the Lantern Festival gala, captured with the iPhone 4 app You Gotta See This!, showing a crowded venue with purple stage lighting and red lantern decorations.

1075205.abstract: Jamie recounts attending the Lantern Festival Gala for Yinghua Academy, a Chinese immersion school in Minneapolis, to see The New Standards perform. Jamie's wife Tammy secured tickets, and Jamie calls the intimate show really good.

1075206.abstract: Jamie praises Unix shell tools, sharing a bash one-liner using a while loop with date, netstat, grep, awk, sort, and uniq to monitor leaking network connections to a host every five minutes while debugging the problem.

1075210.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of a heart-shaped pancake cooking on a griddle, made for Valentine's Day dinner at Mazie's request, though Mazie ate little after eating too much chocolate.

1075211.abstract: Jamie shares a Valentine's Day drawing made by Mazie, a hand-drawn heart filled with colorful triangles, rectangles, and spiral shapes on a red and blue background, and wishes everyone a happy Valentine's Day.

1075212.abstract: Jamie describes building a custom double table for two Big Green Egg grills after finding the stock table's build quality disappointing.

1075213.abstract: Jamie describes making EGGfest Chili for the second time, a recipe from the new Big Green Egg Cookbook, smoked for hours in a Le Creuset Dutch oven on a Big Green Egg grill. Jamie calls it the best chili ever made.

1075214.abstract: Jamie highlights a quote from the OkCupid blog OkTrends, which states that "the basic currency of the Internet is human ignorance, and, frankly, our database holds a strong cash position," a sentiment Jamie finds often true.

1075215.abstract: Jamie criticizes iOS for lacking support for digitally signed and encrypted email, noting that an encrypted message arrives as an unreadable smime.p7m attachment. Jamie hopes Apple adds support, since Mac keychain data could easily enable it.

1075216.abstract: Jamie recounts a family sledding outing using the Mountain Boy sleds, with baby Tyler joining in on toboggan runs. A photo shows the baby bundled in the snow beside two wooden sleds, and a video from the afternoon is referenced.

1075217.abstract: Jamie shares a LinkedIn InMap visualization of a professional network, generated by LinkedIn's InMaps tool, showing Jamie at the center connected to clusters of contacts in blue, green, orange, red, and purple. Jamie calls the graphic "useless really" but visually appealing.

1075218.abstract: Jamie describes weekend updates to family websites: Tyler gets a new landing page with links, Mazie's site gets a new theme plus recently added photos, and Tammy's blog Smaller Than a Redwood receives a new theme as well.

1075219.abstract: Jamie provides a buyer's guide for the Big Green Egg grill, recommending the large size over medium or x-large, and naming required accessories like the plate setter, ash tool, paraffin fire starters, Big Green Egg charcoal, and heavy-duty hand protection.

1075220.abstract: Jamie describes doing a surprise photo shoot at a friend's 40th birthday party, requested by Jamie's sister. Jamie details the setup: a black backdrop, a Canon 580EX II flash fired wirelessly via an ST-E2 transmitter, a Canon 5D Mark II with a 24-70mm f/2.8L lens, and a bounce reflector, noting flash recharge issues from draining AA batteries…

1075221.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Mazie having fingernails painted to match butterfly face paint at Sunshine Montessori's Sunshine on a Stick festival, held at Burroughs.

1075222.abstract: Jamie shares a video of Tyler pushing a music table while learning to walk, filmed entirely on an iPhone. Jamie notes an attempt at embedding video without using an external video service.

1075223.abstract: Jamie shares a crayon drawing Mazie made showing two stick figures holding hands, labeled Mazie in a yellow top and purple skirt, and Dad in a blue outfit, made after Jamie returned from a trip.

1075226.abstract: Jamie notes surprise at finding two empty seats on an otherwise fully booked flight, sharing a photo of the unoccupied seats beside the row.

1075232.abstract: Jamie shares photos of Tyler flinging shoes around a coffee table, then hiding them underneath and giving a sly, coy look toward the camera.

1075238.abstract: Jamie critiques OmniFocus, used across Macs, iPhone and iPad, for displaying "Updating with synced data" during synchronization, noting that "synced" isn't an actual word per the OED. Jamie suggests Apple's "Sync in Progress" phrasing, used for iTunes, works better.

1075240.abstract: Jamie notes that Amazon released the Kindle application in the Mac App Store and updated the iOS Kindle app within a day of each other, but the iOS version got a new icon featuring the Kindle brand while the Mac App Store version kept the old reading-under-a-tree icon, leading Jamie to wonder if the mismatch was an oversight.

1075241.abstract: Jamie proposes an iPhone feature idea: showing all apps with outstanding badge notifications on the Spotlight search screen, using examples like Mail, OmniFocus, and Carcassonne, with icons disappearing once typing begins.

1075242.abstract: Jamie recounts Tyler learning to climb stairs over a weekend, quickly moving up and down repeatedly, around 30 times in one day, with a photo showing the baby crawling up carpeted stairs as a woman watches.

1075243.abstract: Jamie and Mazie snowshoe around Minnehaha Creek West Park and along Minnehaha Creek, stopping for photos on the way to see a nearby "Huge Snowman." Jamie notes Mazie enjoys the REI snowshoes.

1075244.abstract: Jamie describes spending nearly a record-setting hour cutting and bundling cardboard for recycling, noting the snow shelf from an earlier post remains mostly intact despite some warm days.

1075245.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Mazie standing beside a huge snowman built annually by neighbors in a Minneapolis park near Minnehaha Creek, complete with a top hat and a traffic-cone nose, visible at night from Penn Ave.

1075247.abstract: Jamie recounts watching the new TRON: Legacy movie as part of birthday celebrations, calling it great, and includes an IMAX promotional poster photo showing a glowing cyan light cycle with its rider.

1075248.abstract: Jamie receives an 11" MacBook Air as a birthday gift from Jamie's wife Tammy, Mom, Kurt, and sister Alona, and writes the post on the new laptop, noting it suits bus travel and couch blogging.

1075252.abstract: Jamie describes living near a sledding hill in a new house and finding that daughter Mazie's plastic sleds are neither steerable nor sized for two riders. Frustrated by cheap, flimsy sleds sold locally, Jamie orders a Mountain Boy Sledworks Ultimate Flyer 52" and a 6' Mountain Boggan from Amazon, along with sled pads.

1075255.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Mazie, wearing frog pajamas, smiling and hugging a large red Angry Birds plush toy in a kitchen.

1075256.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Mazie smiling while holding a pink Kodak EasyShare CD22 digital camera in its packaging, dressed in frog-print pajamas indoors.

1075260.abstract: Jamie shares a 2010 family holiday photo collage featuring six black-and-white and color snapshots, a monogram T, and the text "And I Think To Myself What A Wonderful World," with a holiday greeting for readers and their families.

1075261.abstract: Jamie describes an effort to become more nomadic in computing by moving away from a large 30" external monitor, trying a smaller desktop setup for a few weeks. A photo shows a MacBook Pro on a stand with an external keyboard, trackpad, speaker, and document scanner on a wood trestle desk.

1075262.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy takes Mazie and Tyler to see Santa Claus for their annual visit. Mazie is excited to share stocking requests, while Tyler seems less enthused about the man in the red suit.

1075263.abstract: Jamie shares photos of a young girl assembling a colorful jigsaw puzzle on a wood table during an afternoon break while celebrating Christmas that weekend with the Olson family.

1075264.abstract: Jamie describes Tyler improving at standing, though walking still seems far off, and notes a preference for being upright despite a rash on the face from thumb-sucking. A photo shows Tyler in overalls standing at a coffee table while a girl sits nearby on a rug.

1075265.abstract: Jamie reports receiving the Glif, an iPhone 4 tripod mount and stand backed via Kickstarter, and shares a photo of the small black plastic clip on its packaging. Jamie already used it to tilt an iPhone up for viewing a recipe on the kitchen counter.

1075266.abstract: Jamie describes attending a Spanish class program at Burroughs where Mazie and classmates demonstrated skills naming fruits, shapes and colors and playing games in Spanish. Jamie shares a photo of Mazie holding a "Hablemos Espanol 2011" bumper sticker and notes being impressed with how much the kids learned.

1075267.abstract: Jamie, a longtime OmniFocus user across Mac, iPhone and iPad, outlines wishes for Omni Group's Omni Sync Server: a browser-based web version of OmniFocus, real push notifications to fix inaccurate local alerts and badge counts, and a JSON-based web API for scripting tasks with cron, curl, Ruby or Perl.

1075268.abstract: Jamie describes learning to play Carcassonne, playing a game against Singapore-based friend Aaron via the Carcassonne app during a late-night session. Jamie loses badly after a city falls apart, shown in an accompanying photo of the tablet board with scores 62 to 32.

1075269.abstract: Jamie highlights how the My-Cast iPhone weather app uses sparklines effectively, calling out the small word-sized graphs next to data like temperature, wind, dewpoint, humidity, and pressure that convey information without extra effort.

1075270.abstract: Jamie critiques the iPad Remote app's use of a black square mask behind non-square cover art, contrasting it unfavorably with iTunes, which displays covers on white. Jamie illustrates the issue with a screenshot of a TV Shows library including M*A*S*H, and asks Apple to change the behavior.

1075271.abstract: Prompted by news of the Gawker password breach, Jamie describes switching from reused, weak passwords to 1Password, using a Smart Folder to find and replace insecure credentials with unique 20-character strings synced via Dropbox across Macs, iPhones and iPads.

1075272.abstract: Jamie describes clearing snow in an alley by flattening the top into a shelf for recycling bins and a trash cart, rather than removing the snow entirely, and shares a photo of the result.

1075273.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of a snow-covered backyard, showing a fence, swing set, and a roughly 3-foot-high plow line blocking the gate, and expects the snowblower to be working overtime.

1075274.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of dog Chase running energetically through deep snow during a neighborhood walk after finishing snow removal chores, describing Chase as a very happy dog.

1075280.abstract: Jamie describes receiving spam replies from fake Twitter accounts, apparently women's profiles, after posting a question seeking an ad-free weather app for iPad.

1075281.abstract: Jamie notices that the coffee shop Kavarna names its WiFi network something like "Free WiFi at Kavarna" rather than just the business name, inviting nearby people to come in and use it. Jamie suggests other businesses try similar tactics, like naming a network "Free Refills."

1075282.abstract: Jamie works out the correct water-to-oats ratio for Arrowhead Mills Organic Irish Style Oat Flakes after noticing the package's chart for 1, 2, and 6 servings doesn't scale linearly, then calculates water amounts for 3, 4, and 5 servings.

1075283.abstract: Jamie describes creating a first photo book, "Stone/Steel/People," after taking a workshop led by Layne Kennedy at the Minneapolis Photo Center focused on shooting a subject for 72 hours. Jamie shares lessons learned about editing and formatting, notes the book was made using Blurb, and links to related books by Layne Kennedy and Heidi Neumann.

1075284.abstract: Jamie recalls a plea posted a year earlier asking Canon to allow locking the mode dial on a Canon 5D Mark II, and notes Canon has now announced a $100 program to replace the dial with a locking one. An update reports National Camera hadn't heard of the program and questioned its appeal.

1075285.abstract: Jamie reflects on why sleeping from 10pm to 2am feels far worse than sleeping from 2am to 6am, even though both provide only four hours of sleep. Jamie mentions doing the less desirable schedule that night ahead of an office product release.

1075286.abstract: Jamie describes replacing an old Christmas tree stand after asking staff at Settergren's Ace Hardware for a recommendation, who suggested the Swivel Tree Stand from Amazon.

1075287.abstract: Jamie describes a strong enthusiasm for upgrading devices, especially firmware, and recounts an evening spent updating iOS on an iPhone 4, an iPhone 3GS, two iPads, and two second-generation Apple TVs.

1075288.abstract: Jamie shares a video link, sent by friends Dennys Bisogno and Layne Kennedy, of Iceland's Eyjafjallajökull volcano filmed by Sean Stiegemeier. Jamie notes Stiegemeier used the same Canon 5D Mark II camera Jamie owns, finding the footage both inspiring and intimidating.

1075289.abstract: Jamie notes The Beatles catalog is finally available on iTunes, linking to Apple's announcement page, and expresses relief that years of rumors about a Beatles-iTunes deal can now end.

1075290.abstract: Jamie describes creating a first photography book, noting the editing process is arduous but nearing completion, with the layout finished, photos selected and tweaked, and fonts chosen, leaving one final push to finish.

1075292.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of a five-foot section of coiled black rubber hose, the only item shipped inside a large cardboard box, calling the packaging wasteful.

1075293.abstract: Jamie shares a brief personal observation that riding the bus makes it hard to feel superior to others, framing public transit as a kind of social equalizer.

1075296.abstract: Jamie describes starting the process of removing a home name and address from junk mail lists after a recent move, noting the mail is piling up again, including catalogs addressed to 8-month-old Tyler.

1075297.abstract: Jamie quotes Bill Bryson's remark that Thomas Midgley Jr., who invented leaded gasoline, had "an instinct for the regrettable that was almost uncanny" for also inventing chlorofluorocarbons.

1075298.abstract: Jamie describes Mazie's first soccer game, playing center forward for the Cyclones in the Fuller Soccer Club, a league for 5-6 year olds where games run 8 periods of 5 minutes each. Jamie recorded video of the 8th period and shares a photo of Mazie in her uniform.

1075305.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of a large pork shoulder, coated in dry rub seasoning, cooking on a Big Green Egg smoker on the 4th of July.

1075307.abstract: Jamie links to a fresh strawberry tart with port glaze recipe from Minneapolis food blog Healthy and Gourmet, describing it as delicious and sharing a photo of the pastry tart topped with whole glazed strawberries.

1075310.abstract: Jamie recounts hearing an insurance company's automated phone tree offering options like pressing 9 for a death claim or 5 for a cancer policy, finding the menu of grim choices bleak.

1075312.abstract: Jamie describes watching the US v. Ghana World Cup match with brother-in-law Hector at the Riverview Theater, noting the packed crowd and the energy when Donovan scored a penalty kick to tie the game, despite the eventual US loss.

1075313.abstract: Jamie praises Flickr for making it easy to delete an entire photo collection, describing deleting 2,228 items through clearly labeled, accessible controls that leave the account fully in Jamie's control.

1075315.abstract: Jamie describes plans to add a swing set to the backyard of a new house for Mazie, noting the challenge of fitting one on a standard city lot. Jamie's wife Tammy orders a unit from CedarWorks, which sends rendered 3D models showing a wooden playset with swings, a blue slide, climbing wall, and covered tower.

1075316.abstract: Jamie describes how folders in the newly launched iOS 4 Springboard, though intended for grouping apps by function, work well for organizing apps by context instead, citing a "Reading" folder containing Kindle, iBooks, Reeder, Instapaper, ReadMore, and Goodreads as an example.

1075317.abstract: Jamie describes picking up the first CSA box of the season from Tangletown Gardens, a farm about a mile away in the city. Jamie signed up for a half-share on Tammy's suggestion and praises the refrigerated boxes, helpful contents printout, and fresh strawberries available for purchase.

1075318.abstract: Jamie asks why detached garages don't commonly include a tunnel connecting to the house's basement.

1075320.abstract: Jamie links to an NPR report by April Fulton suggesting coffee does not truly boost alertness but instead restores regular caffeine drinkers to a normal state after overnight withdrawal. Jamie responds with a single word: "Vindication!"

1075321.abstract: Jamie notices that the Facebook, Twitter, and LinkedIn iPhone app icons are all blue, and questions why these companies, supposedly thought leaders, settle for such similar, bland logo colors instead of something more distinctive like red.

1075326.abstract: Jamie wishes wife Tammy a happy Mother's Day, calling Tammy a great mom, alongside a photo showing a woman holding a baby outdoors with a young girl in a pink cardigan smiling beside them.

1075327.abstract: Jamie describes using the "Find My iPhone" feature to locate a misplaced iPhone by triggering its sound, avoiding a manual search.

1075330.abstract: Jamie criticizes the Groupon iOS app for using a popup that asks users to rate the app, calling it an annoying tactic designed to game AppStore ratings. The post includes a screenshot of the popup with its Rate, Remind Me Later, and No Thanks buttons.

1075332.abstract: Jamie describes starting a move to a new house at 53rd and Morgan in Minneapolis, closed on March 1st, after three weeks of painting and new carpet. Family helped move art first, with a moving company packing before the final move on Tuesday.

1075333.abstract: Jamie compares the 1987 cast photo from the TV series "thirtysomething" with a 2010 cast photo from NBC's "Parenthood," noting the similar group poses and matching typography in both shows' logos, calling both "decent shows."

1075335.abstract: Jamie describes trying a bottle of Bent Nail IPA from Red Lodge Ales in Montana, given by brother-in-law Denny after a trip there. Jamie finds the beer notably hoppy and enjoyable, calling it true to its IPA style.

1075336.abstract: Jamie links to HumbleFinance, which produces smooth, interactive HTML5 Canvas stock charts, discovered via Daring Fireball. Jamie notes MarketWatch attempted similar charts years earlier but found the user experience hard to achieve, and now believes browser technology has finally caught up.

1075338.abstract: Jamie orders two iPad Wi-Fi 32GB models along with two iPad Cases, choosing the middle storage tier due to uncertainty about needed space, and anticipates the devices arriving in early April.

1075350.abstract: Jamie describes closing on a new house and celebrating by moving in Mazie's play table and having dinner from Broder's Deli. The family plans to move in after painting and new carpet are completed.

1075355.abstract: Jamie announces the birth of Tyler Thingelstad, born at 8lb 3oz and 22 inches long, noting that Jamie's wife Tammy handled the delivery well and everyone is doing fine.

1075357.abstract: Jamie responds to a friend's question about introducing kids to programming by recommending BASIC and Logo, recalling learning BASIC at age six on a TI-99/4A. Jamie suggests the Chipmunk BASIC interpreter and ACSLogo for Mac as free tools, while dismissing other kid-focused languages as too simplistic or verbose.

1075358.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a tour of Surly Brewing, showing stainless steel fermentation tanks, a guide addressing a group in the brewery warehouse among stacked kegs, and a wall of stacked Surly Furious beer cans.

1075359.abstract: Jamie reviews the movie Moon, calling it interesting and noting comparisons to 2001 are inevitable, but finding it stands tall even in that film's shadow.

1075360.abstract: Jamie shares high-resolution album art for Chan Poling's "Calling All Stars," the Cities 97 Sampler Volume 8, and Dan Wilson's "Live at Pantages," intended for others who own these albums.

1075361.abstract: Jamie quotes a self-written line comparing each new blog's creation to an angel earning its wings, noting an intent not to make a habit of self-quotation despite liking this one.

1075362.abstract: Jamie describes a Smart Playlist created in iTunes called "Three Plays," designed to surface newly added tracks from a collection of 1,463 albums and 19,392 songs.

1075363.abstract: Jamie describes a bug in Mac OS X Address Book where contact images stored in ~/Library/Application Support/AddressBook/Images duplicate repeatedly, ballooning weekly backups from 16.4MB to 120.3MB over about six weeks.

1075365.abstract: Jamie describes a problem with the Canon 5D Mark II paired with the Canon 70-200mm f/2.8L IS USM lens: when slung over the shoulder "upside down" so the heavy lens hangs naturally, the mode dial rests against Jamie's side and can shift modes while walking, ruining shots. Jamie suggests the dial needs a flip-lock safety.

1075366.abstract: Jamie criticizes poorly designed web surveys, describing an encounter with one from Strategic Vision that presented a list of feature options so long it overflowed a 30" monitor. Jamie abandons the survey rather than continue.

1075367.abstract: Jamie describes using MindNode Pro for mind mapping and MindNode Touch for sketching on a phone, then explains adding Unicode symbols as metadata to nodes using TextExpander shortcuts like :star, :plane, :check, and :seven. Jamie shares a sample vacation-ranking map and offers a downloadable TextExpander definition file.

1075368.abstract: Jamie finds out by accident that paying the dentist on the same day of treatment gives a 5% discount, and expresses frustration that this discount isn't clearly advertised.

1075369.abstract: Jamie describes creating a second version of video stingers used to introduce personal video content, improving on ones made a year earlier by shortening them to 5 seconds, adding Creative Commons license information, increasing resolution for HD, and defaulting to widescreen aspect ratio.

1075370.abstract: Jamie explains that Unix's find command doesn't spawn a shell, so backticks fail inside an exec parameter. Jamie shares a workaround using sh -c to invoke a shell, with an example command converting DBF files to MySQL using dbf2mysql.

1075371.abstract: Jamie shares a video explaining, in plain language, why net neutrality matters, describing it as a clear explanation of the open internet concept.

1075372.abstract: Jamie mentions obtaining a bottle of Surly Darkness beer, noting it has not yet been tasted, and includes a photo of the bottle.

1075373.abstract: Jamie describes waking up to eleven PayPal emails showing 16 unauthorized charges, between $39 and $59 each, totaling nearly $1,000, sent to an unfamiliar company called NC Interactive, Inc. for online game credits.

1075376.abstract: Jamie shares a YouTube video of anvil shooting, linking to Wikipedia entries on model rockets and anvils and joking that anvils make a more exciting alternative.

1075378.abstract: Jamie expresses disappointment that Verisign, Thawte's new owner, is shutting down the free Thawte Web of Trust system, noting Verisign sells a competing paid product. Jamie, a recent Thawte notary, criticizes the Web of Trust website for still allowing sign-ups without mentioning the shutdown.

1075379.abstract: Jamie describes using Smart Mailboxes in Mail.app for the first time and finding them helpful, noting many people may not know they exist, and links to a 43 Folders post with hints on setting them up.

1075380.abstract: Jamie describes giving the keynote at the University of Minnesota Computer Science department's 2009 Open House, covering software's societal impact, the case for open source, and developers' responsibility to create inspired, elegant software rather than "codemonkey" code.

1075391.abstract: Jamie recounts a hike to Kawishiwi Falls near Ely and shares video shot with the Canon 5D Mark II and Canon 70-200mm f/2.8L IS lens, noting satisfaction with the footage quality despite web conversion. Jamie mentions previously photographing the same falls during winter on the Wintergreen Photography Dog Sledding trip.

1075393.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a drive between Duluth and Ely, including stops at Canal Park in Duluth and Gooseberry Falls State Park, marking the start of a weekend trip to Ely. Jamie especially likes a photo of violins.

1075394.abstract: During a full cleaning of a Big Green Egg grill, Jamie describes aligning the fire box to the right side of the draft door instead of centering it, making the ash tool easier to work as a right-handed user; left-handed users should align to the left.

1075398.abstract: After upgrading to iTunes 9, Jamie finds old iPhone IPSW restore images moved to the trash, including seven files from 2008-2009 totaling 1,793 MB, some for an iPhone model no longer owned.

1075399.abstract: Jamie describes trying freezer canning for the first time, using 20 pounds of organically grown tomatoes bought at the Mill City Farmers Market from a farm about 70 miles outside town. After processing and simmering the tomatoes for a few hours, Jamie yields 12 pints of unseasoned sauce to freeze for winter dishes.

1075400.abstract: Jamie describes trying to check Tejas Restaurant's hours on an iPhone, only to find the site's all-Flash design rendered as a blank orange screen with no readable content. Jamie argues websites built entirely in Flash fail on devices like the iPhone and recommends at least including basic HTML elements.

1075405.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the 2009 Minnesota State Fair, noting this was the first year Mazie really enjoyed the event. Highlights include the butterfly house, carousel ride, cookies, skyjump, and the butter heads, with Mazie especially enjoying the skyjump.

1075407.abstract: Jamie calls Julie & Julia a fun, light movie with a laugh or two, noting the cool context of cooking and blogging. The post includes the movie poster, showing two eggs with the tagline "Passion. Ambition. Butter."

1075409.abstract: Jamie relays a feature idea from friend Dave Oosterhuis: iTunes should support "song linking" to unify metadata like play count, last played date, and rating across duplicate or alternate versions of the same song.

1075410.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a day at the Minnesota State Fair in 2009, noting that Mazie had a blast.

1075412.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a birthday gathering for brother-in-law Max, who turned 30, held at Bayside Grill on Lake Minnetonka. Jamie notes the photos capture only a fraction of the attendees.

1075415.abstract: Jamie proposes a "Caps Lock Day" where everything is written in capital letters, joking that capital letters deserve more respect and that such a day would be maddening but worth trying.

1075416.abstract: Jamie describes having the 20-year-old deck resurfaced with new cedar boards after the original wood began rotting and nails kept loosening. Terry Owens of Como Lake Carpentry did the work, and Jamie shares photos of the finished deck with its new neutral stain, railings, and outdoor furniture.

1075419.abstract: Jamie argues Twitter functions more like a "micromessaging" tool than a microblogging platform and should have a retention policy rather than an indefinite archive.

1075421.abstract: Jamie highlights a TED talk by Hans Rosling that presents animated visualizations of 200 years of global economic data, calling the visuals impressive.

1075422.abstract: Jamie describes a "Daddy-Daughter" day with Mazie, including a shopping trip for new dresses and a photo shoot in the front yard using the tall grasses and native plants as a backdrop, then shares the resulting photo collection.

1075423.abstract: Jamie describes removing a mural that Tammy's friend Liane McMeen painted in 2003 around a Blue Dog sculpture from Denver, in the living room. After six years, Jamie and Tammy retired it with a dinner for Liane and husband Chris, replaced it with new art, and Jamie shares an updated time-lapse video with new photos.

1075424.abstract: Jamie describes an evening spent listening to the band Frankhouse at the 318 Club, calling it good jazz, and notes that a friend plays lead trumpet in the group.

1075428.abstract: Jamie describes rushing to Four Firkins after an email announcement of the store's first limited shipment of Surly Hell, buying the last four 4-packs alongside neighbor Mike before the beer sold out shortly after. Jamie finds the beer delicious.

1075429.abstract: Jamie describes using Spotlight search, added in iPhone 3.0 software, as a faster way to launch apps than swiping through multiple Springboard pages, comparing it to Quicksilver on the Mac.

1075430.abstract: Jamie notices repeated "All Things Twitter" posts while browsing RSS subscriptions in Google Reader and recalls kill files from the Usenet newsreader nn used nearly 20 years earlier, citing Wikipedia's definition, and asks why RSS readers lack this feature.

1075432.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of a water lily blossom taken at the Como Park Conservatory's Water Lily area, captured straight off a Canon 5D Mark II with a 70-200mm f/2.8L lens, needing only a slight crop.

1075433.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a visit to the off-leash dog park, showing a small white fluffy dog named Izzy running across a grassy field, at one point carrying a red ball.

1075434.abstract: Jamie describes switching to a Canon 5D Mark II camera and experimenting with its full HD video capability, sharing a video of a frog shot with a 50mm macro lens and life-size converter, giving about 1mm depth of field, filmed through a window from roughly two inches away.

1075448.abstract: Jamie describes how to add a custom "Send to..." destination in Google Reader for posting directly to WordPress using the built-in "Press this" function, since WordPress isn't among Reader's default sharing options like Facebook, Twitter, and Delicious.

1075449.abstract: Jamie reflects on the "asymptotic behavior" of packages shipped with signature-required delivery, sharing an image, and notes plans to pick up the package at the UPS office that evening.

1075453.abstract: Jamie announces removing the "www." prefix from thingelstad.com, redirecting visitors automatically. Jamie notes hesitation due to search engines treating www.thingelstad.com separately, but finds Google Webmaster Tools makes the change easy.

1075456.abstract: Responding to John Gruber's Daring Fireball post on Microsoft's declining hold on tech enthusiasts, Jamie proposes two changes: replacing the Windows NT kernel with an open-source Unix-based kernel, and swapping Internet Explorer's Trident rendering engine for an open-source alternative like WebKit or Gecko.

1075457.abstract: Jamie describes joining Split Rock Partners as an Entrepreneur in Residence, citing Wikipedia's definition of the EIR role and explaining it as a partnership rather than employment. The post includes Split Rock's press release detailing Jamie's prior CTO roles at BigCharts, MarketWatch, and Dow Jones's Wall Street Journal Digital Network.

1075459.abstract: Jamie links to a preview clip of the upcoming Tron Legacy, set for release in 2010, calling it a great clip. Jamie recalls watching the original Tron at age 10 and looks forward to the new film.

1075472.abstract: Jamie announces joining the board of directors at CaringBridge, a nonprofit offering free personalized websites that let people stay connected with family and friends during health crises, treatment and recovery. Jamie calls the organization a strong fit and expresses interest in hearing readers' CaringBridge stories.

1075473.abstract: Jamie describes redesigning an HTML email signature after friend Kent noted it wrapped oddly on the iPhone, tracing the issue to a fixed-width element.

1075474.abstract: Jamie describes a first visit to Burger Jones with Tammy, Mazie, sister-in-law Angie, Nora and Grandma Olson, finding the burger overcooked and unremarkable, the cheese curds inconsistent, and the sweet potato fries bland, concluding the food doesn't merit a quick return.

1075478.abstract: Jamie reflects on spending the night in the country, noting how the absence of sun, moonlight, and farmhouse light creates an unusually strange, complete darkness in the windows.

1075488.abstract: Jamie shares high-resolution front and back cover scans for three Peppa Pig DVDs: The Balloon Ride, Piggy in the Middle, and Bubbles, noting that Mazie loves Peppa Pig.

1075489.abstract: Jamie quotes E. F. Schumacher's "Small is Beautiful," on the idea that without wisdom, humanity builds a monster economy that destroys the world.

1075490.abstract: Jamie links to a visualization tool from Xefer that charts Twitter activity by day of week and hour of day, showing the results as a bubble chart grid with summary bar charts. Jamie notes the tool isn't especially important but finds the display appealing, and observes the results confirm no Twitter use during sleeping hours.

1075492.abstract: Jamie notes a small change in the iPhone 3.0 release: a new built-in "iPhone" label option now appears alongside existing phone type choices like mobile and home in Address Book. Jamie finds the addition odd, speculating it may relate to vanity or future MMS targeting of iPhone users specifically.

1075493.abstract: Jamie recommends "Flying Scotsman," a movie about cyclist Graeme Obree's pursuit of various cycling records, and shares an image of the film's poster.

1075495.abstract: Jamie recounts a coffee shop exchange in which a barista repeatedly assumes an order for a macchiato means caramel macchiato, before clarifying it's actually an espresso macchiato being requested.

1075497.abstract: Jamie describes making homemade vanilla ice cream for the first time using a Cuisinart electric ice cream maker, a Father's Day gift from Mazie, with Mazie assembling ingredients and Jamie measuring. Jamie notes lessons learned, including running the machine longer and freezing the serving bowl beforehand to prevent melting on contact.

1075498.abstract: Jamie describes finally watching the new Star Trek movie after hesitating for a long time, and finds it really good, sharing a black and white close-up movie poster image dated 05.08.09.

1075504.abstract: Jamie shares scanned cover art for two Peppa Pig DVDs, Cold Winter Day and Stars, after finding high-resolution copies unavailable online, offering the images for others to use.

1075505.abstract: Jamie describes taking a sausage-making class with Kent Tangen at the North House Folk School in Grand Marais, a trip arranged by Jamie's wife Tammy after both admired sausage made by friend Kevin Dotzenrod. A video, mostly featuring Kent since Jamie operated the camera, captures the experience.

1075508.abstract: Jamie describes using CSS to convert an unordered list of Tumblr tags into a grammatically correct comma-separated list, using a 2005 technique found at milov.nl as a starting point. The solution handles singular/plural labels, commas, and "and" without requiring loop logic in code, and Jamie plans to apply the same CSS to a WordPress site.

1075510.abstract: Jamie describes plans to video-interview Mazie, who is about to turn 4, using a consistent set of questions each birthday to capture how answers change over time. Sample questions include favorite color, favorite food, best friends, and favorite activity; Jamie asks readers for additional question suggestions.

1075514.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of the poster for the Pixar movie "Up" and describes Mazie's excitement heading to the theater to see it, noting everyone enjoyed the film.

1075524.abstract: Jamie describes attempting tandoor-style cooking on a Big Green Egg, inspired by blog posts from foodnotfiller.com, using uncooked Tandoori Chicken obtained through friend Senthil's connection to Taste of India.

1075526.abstract: Jamie attends a two-day photography workshop led by John Gregor of ColdSnap Photography, shooting at Lake Harriet's Peace Garden and Rose Garden with seminars at REI in Bloomington. Jamie praises Gregor's teaching and technical knowledge, especially of color spaces, and shares favorite photos from the sessions.

1075531.abstract: Jamie reflects on why professional cyclists use Twitter, following positive feedback on the VeloTweets project. Jamie highlights Lance Armstrong's tweets about frequent, unannounced anti-doping controls and posts showing constant training, arguing these two messages help combat doping's image problem and rebuild trust in cycling.

1075532.abstract: Jamie recounts speaking at an entrepreneurship class at the Carlson School of Management about a month earlier, describing a group with many good questions, and shares a photo of roughly 35 students and an instructor posing together in a classroom.

1075533.abstract: Jamie submits a first photo to JPG Magazine for its "Shoot Your Pet!" theme, showing a black Labrador mix with amber eyes and a red collar, and hopes it gets published.

1075535.abstract: Jamie reviews Theodore Rosendorf's "The Typographic Desk Reference," discovered through I Love Typography's coverage, praising its terminology, careful design, binding, and typeface choices, comparing its craftsmanship to Edward Tufte's books, and recommending purchase directly from publisher Oak Knoll.

1075537.abstract: Jamie introduces VeloTweets, a site built with Luke Francl, Norm Orstad, and Chris Hatch that aggregates professional cyclists' Twitter feeds, inspired by riders like Lance Armstrong tweeting during races such as the Giro d'Italia.

1075540.abstract: Jamie describes retiling a downstairs bathroom shower with a Tetris-inspired pattern, designed with Tammy's friend and using screenshots from the Mac game Quinn to keep the game logic correct. Terry Owens of Como Lake Carpentry installed the colorful mosaic tiles, shown in accompanying photos.

1075548.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy prepares for the first game of a brand new softball team, and Jamie shares a photo of Tammy wearing a Sea Monkeys team shirt while awaiting the recap.

1075551.abstract: Jamie watches the movie Role Models as a rental on Apple TV after a weekend of watching several movies, and finds it funnier than expected.

1075555.abstract: Jamie points to the Open Font Library, a site offering fonts under an Open Font License, noting that CSS3's upcoming @font-face support will finally allow real fonts on the web, and hopes the library's font selection grows over time.

1075558.abstract: Jamie announces the next Minnedemo event on May 7, 2009 at 6:00pm, noting it's free but requires registration, with 324 open tickets remaining. Jamie describes being a fan of Minnedemo as a place to connect with people and learn about new products and projects.

1075559.abstract: Jamie describes a first attempt at commercial photography, shooting equipment at Select Fitness, a local personal training studio previously photographed for the gym's own website.

1075563.abstract: Jamie notes that the temperature at home in Minnesota passed 70°F for the first time in months, an event Jamie welcomes as the start of the transition from winter to summer. A tweet from Jamie's robot, thinglesbot, records the exact reading as 70.025 degrees.

1075577.abstract: Jamie shares an account of Mazie practicing on a Skuut balance bike over the first weekend in April, despite overnight snow leaving an inch of wet snow. Mazie expresses excitement about eventually getting a bicycle without needing training wheels.

1075584.abstract: Jamie describes using DNS redirects through Namecheap to create friendly subdomain URLs for social profiles, listing examples like facebook.thingelstad.com, flickr.thingelstad.com, linkedin.thingelstad.com, reader.thingelstad.com and twitter.thingelstad.com that redirect to the actual profile addresses.

1075586.abstract: Jamie describes downloading Flight Control for iPhone, a top-down game where players draw flight paths to land different types of planes as they arrive faster over time. Jamie finds the game addictive, reaching a high score of 57.

1075588.abstract: Jamie describes setting up Cacti, the network graphing tool built on RRDtool, to track Twitter follower and friend counts every five minutes, after noticing increased followers following a guest appearance on Minnesota Public Radio's Midmorning.

1075589.abstract: Jamie links to a Current.com video mocking the "twittersphere," which Jamie finds funny, noting the irony of discovering it via mkortekaas on Twitter.

1075590.abstract: Jamie exchanges tweets with garrickvanburen about Cullect, who compares indexing, archiving, and ranking tweets to peeling an onion. Jamie jokes about it causing tears, and garrickvanburen admits that happens more often than preferred.

1075593.abstract: Jamie reacts to "The final reel," a story in the March 14th issue of The Economist reporting that Fisher-Price will no longer make the View-Master. Jamie recalls childhood fascination with the toy and notes Mazie's own enjoyment of it, expressing sadness that future reels will only feature licensed characters.

1075594.abstract: Jamie and Tammy watch the film Milk, based on the story of Harvey Milk, and Jamie calls it a great movie with great acting by Sean Penn. The post includes a photo of the DVD cover.

1075595.abstract: Jamie shares enthusiasm for the album "Willie and the Wheel," a Texas swing record by Willie Nelson enjoyed after about a week of listening, and includes an image of the album cover.

1075596.abstract: Jamie revives Thinglesbot, a Twitter robot that turned 2 on March 11 but had gone quiet after losing sensor connections.

1075598.abstract: Jamie links to Nick Potter's Lightroom Keyword Lists, questioning the need for standardized keyword lists and preferring folksonomy instead, but finds the idea of color keywords interesting and useful for generating ideas.

1075599.abstract: Jamie appears as a guest on Minnesota Public Radio's Midmorning, hosted by John Moe, discussing Twitter alongside Pioneer Press columnist Julio Ojeda-Zapata, with a call-in from John Hodgman.

1075601.abstract: Jamie describes discovering that the dome thermometer on the Big Green Egg was reading 60°F too low, causing overcooked ribs and inconsistent grilling results. After calibrating it using boiling water at 212°F, Jamie finds grilling results improve and recommends regularly checking thermometer accuracy this way.

1075605.abstract: Jamie links to WordPress.com's announcement of P2, a new iteration of the Prologue theme, and notes it looks even better than the original. Jamie suggests it could easily power a private Twitter-like service, especially as Twitter feels increasingly crowded and less interesting.

1075606.abstract: Jamie shares a link to a YouTube remix video called "Mother of All Funk Chords," calling it a cool watch worth passing along.

1075607.abstract: Following Apple's release of iTunes 8.1, Jamie argues iTunes should let one computer's iTunes library sync directly with another, just as it already syncs to iPods and Apple TV. Jamie notes copying files manually is painful and fails to sync metadata like play counts and ratings, undermining Smart Playlists across multiple Macs.

1075608.abstract: Jamie notes that Apple's new iPod Shuffle, released with a VoiceOver feature using recorded audio prompts to compensate for its lack of a screen, isn't a novel concept.

1075609.abstract: Jamie shares the newly published 2009 RAGBRAI bicycle route, which crosses southern Iowa, along with charts of daily mileage, climbing feet, and climbing feet per mile. Jamie notes friend Jim's claim that RAGBRAI aims to prove Iowa isn't flat, compares climbing totals to Texas Hellweek 2001, and observes the route grows gentler over the week.

1075610.abstract: Jamie recommends When Is Good (whenisgood.net), a web tool for scheduling group get-togethers that requires no registration and lets participants mark and filter available times to find a slot that works for everyone. Jamie praises its simplicity, contrasting it with the usual back-and-forth frustration of scheduling by email.

1075611.abstract: Jamie describes a first attempt at studio photography using a Manfrotto Background Support system, one continuous light, and wireless Canon flashes, shooting portraits of Mazie, cousin Nora, and neighbor kids.

1075613.abstract: Jamie announces registering for RAGBRAI 37, the Register's Annual Great Bike Ride Across Iowa, with wife Tammy, a 442.3-mile, seven-day ride from Council Bluffs to Burlington starting July 19th, and plans to log 1,000 training miles beforehand.

1075614.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of a dog named Chase, taken as a test shot while setting up camera equipment, using a white muslin background to help with exposure since black dogs are difficult to photograph. Jamie asks for caption ideas.

1075616.abstract: Jamie shares photos taken at Sierra Bravo's Overnight Website Challenge, capturing the start, middle, and end across three visits. Jamie notes the room and podium lighting made event photography difficult, favors a shot of the Ruby.MN 2.2 Team, and finds few sleeping participants to photograph.

1075620.abstract: Jamie links to a collection of OmniGraffle scripts by Peter McMaster that add capabilities like drawing arcs to the diagramming application from the Omni Group.

1075622.abstract: Jamie links to IndieBound, a resource for finding independent bookstores, after seeing a poster for it at Wild Rumpus in Linden Hills. Jamie finds it a useful way to highlight the value independent bookstores bring to communities.

1075623.abstract: Jamie photographs the first of three sessions at Sierra Bravo's Overnight Website Challenge, using a Canon 40D with lenses including a 70-200mm f/2.8L, 10-22mm ultrawide and 14mm fisheye. Jamie plans to return overnight and early morning to capture more of the event, noting the fluorescent-lit room is difficult to shoot.

1075626.abstract: Jamie reviews the movie Bottle Shock, describing it as a fun and happy film about the beginnings of the California wine valley, though noting the script isn't great, and calls it a fine choice for a snowy evening rental, rating it 4 stars.

1075629.abstract: Jamie recounts a family ski weekend at Giant's Ridge with the Tangen family, where Tammy already knew how to ski while Jamie and Kent took morning lessons before tackling the real hills. The kids enjoyed the bunny hill and magic carpet, and the retro feel of the weekend inspired a video Jamie put together.

1075645.abstract: Jamie shares photos of two pots from ceramics class that survived the kiln: a roughly 3-inch bowl with a carved geometric pattern and a smoother, smaller round bowl, both awaiting glazing next.

1075647.abstract: Jamie describes buying Wintergreen Designs' Plunge Mittens at their store in Ely before a dog sledding trip, having doubted existing gloves would handle severe cold. Jamie finds the mittens extremely warm, reporting hands rewarmed easily even at -27°F, and notes they are hand-made in Ely, MN.

1075648.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the Wintergreen Dog Sledding Photography Workshop led by Layne Kennedy, describing the trip as a chance to improve photography skills by focusing on the story behind each shot and its eventual use.

1075649.abstract: Jamie recounts advice from friend Jim Bernard before a dog sledding trip to Wintergreen: read Ely's two newspapers, the Echo and the Timberjay, and take the scenic Highway 1 route through Duluth home instead of the faster I-35 path. Jamie shares Flickr photos taken along the drive.

1075651.abstract: While emptying a filing cabinet during a hardwood floor conversion of the home office, Jamie finds a printed BigCharts Partnership Portfolio from 1997-1998 and scans it for others to see.

1075654.abstract: Jamie shares a blurry photo of a roadside billboard reading www.eatlamb.com, spotted along I-35 northbound leaving the Twin Cities, taken from a car traveling 75 mph, and remarks on it as evidence the Internet reaches everywhere.

1075657.abstract: Jamie shares GPS track data from a dog sledding trip during the Wintergreen 2009 Photography Workshop, pulled from a Garmin GPSmap 60CSx using GPS Babel and converted to KML for viewing in Google Earth or Google Maps.

1075660.abstract: Jamie describes upgrading to Google Earth 5.0 beta and encountering a dialog forcing installation of Google Software Update, with only options to accept and install or quit, no decline choice.

1075661.abstract: Jamie quotes a saying from Jason Zabokrtsky of the Boundary Waters Blogger: "You aren't cold and dead, until your warm and dead."

1075662.abstract: Jamie reads Winterdance: The Fine Madness of Running the Iditarod by Gary Paulsen during a dog sledding trip, a book recommended by Wintergreen. Jamie enjoys the training and race sections, finds it often funny, and gains new appreciation for the Iditarod, noting the 2009 race falls on March 7th.

1075663.abstract: Jamie shares a quote from Ansel Adams describing a scene that would not bend to visualization, offering it without further commentary.

1075667.abstract: Jamie recommends the Thermapen instant-read thermometer for grilling, describing its use during a 12-hour brisket session on a Big Green Egg with neighbor Mike. Jamie highlights its speed and ability to check multiple spots in a cut without overcooking.

1075668.abstract: Jamie visits Kopplin's Coffee in St. Paul, run by owner Andrew Kopplin, after Peter Vader's recommendation, driving 30 minutes with neighbor Mike to try it.

1075669.abstract: Jamie describes canceling DirecTV after 10 years as a customer, switching to over-the-air ATSC antennas (ChannelMaster 4221) and Apple TVs with expanded hard drives instead. Jamie recounts being charged an early-termination fee despite a supposedly free, non-extending MPEG-4 equipment upgrade, and links to Steve Borsch's similar cancellation story.

1075670.abstract: Jamie shares a video from C-Lazy-U, the dude ranch visited last summer with the Tangens, along with a video Jamie made of a horse run. Jamie notes the ranch's Shodeo video looks better than the "intrepid horsemanship" from Tammy and Bill during their week.

1075680.abstract: Jamie highlights Alocola, a new iPhone application by Dan Grigsby that lets web sites obtain location data from the iPhone by having Safari launch the helper app and return the info to the requesting site. Jamie notes Dan plans to release the source under GPL2.

1075681.abstract: Jamie explains switching the home network from a self-hosted DNS server to OpenDNS, replacing an earlier reliance on Comcast's DNS. Jamie highlights OpenDNS's phishing-site content filtering, DNS request statistics graphs for spotting unusual activity, and custom shortcuts, recommending the free service to anyone able to change DNS providers.

1075686.abstract: Jamie describes converting the bedroom floor from carpet to bamboo hardwood, part of a larger round of home projects including countertops and paint. Natural Built Home supplied options; bamboo was chosen over maple for environmental reasons and its fast regrowth. Jamie's office will get the same treatment soon.

1075687.abstract: Jamie asks for suggestions on Minneapolis photography spots beyond the Stone Arch Bridge, mentioning the Midtown Global Market as a dim indoor option, and invites readers to share favorite locations or join a photowalk.

1075691.abstract: Jamie explains a technique for managing a large iTunes library (18,439 items) using Smart Playlists: creating a "No Playlist" Playlist that excludes categories like Children's Music, Radio content (such as This American Life episodes), and Holiday music by matching "any" criteria, then referencing that playlist as an exclusion rule in other Smart…

1075692.abstract: Jamie drafts a mock congressional resolution demanding coffee shops preserve proper espresso traditions: serving espresso in thick-walled porcelain cups under 2 ounces, and requiring monthly employee certification tests for crema that lasts at least 60 seconds.

1075697.abstract: Jamie explains the decision to stop sending Twitter updates to a Facebook profile, prompted by a conversation with Jim Bernard about severing the Twitter-Facebook bridge and feedback from Facebook friends about excessive updates.

1075699.abstract: Jamie shares a screenshot of Mac Address Book showing about 14 duplicate "Apple, Inc." entries, a recurring MobileMe sync problem that persists after the 10.5.6 update. Jamie regularly merges the duplicates but they reappear within days, and asks whether others see this issue or know a fix.

1075703.abstract: Jamie shares a video of daughter Mazie singing "Santa Claus is Coming to Town" with a guitar shortly after Christmas, noting the excitement Mazie showed for the holiday that year made Christmas more enjoyable.

1075704.abstract: Jamie describes a Lightroom 2 Smart Collection workaround for finding photos missing IPTC location data. Since Lightroom lacks an "is blank" operator, Jamie creates a rule using "doesn't contain" for every letter of the alphabet in the Location field, successfully isolating photos with no location information.

1075705.abstract: Jamie highlights a video showing the personal impact of Kiva micro-loans, having used Kiva for over a year to make several loans. Jamie links to a lender page and credits Aaron Oliver for introducing Kiva as a gift.

1075706.abstract: Jamie links to adaptinstyle's post about a bottle cap adapter that turns a standard water bottle into a camera tripod for group photos or stable video. Jamie finds the idea appealing but wonders about a version compatible with SIGG bottles rather than plastic water bottles.

1075707.abstract: Jamie recounts sending a father-in-law's damaged Petzl Zipka Plus headlamp, cracked and broken after an outdoor fall, to Petzl's customer support though it was out of warranty. Petzl repaired and returned it within weeks, prompting Jamie to praise the company's service as living up to its premium price.

1075708.abstract: Jamie shares plans for a dog sledding photo workshop trip to Ely, MN, a birthday gift from Tammy through Wintergreen Dogsled Lodge, led by photographer Layne Kennedy, whose advice on storytelling through images Jamie quotes from a Nikon World piece.

1075709.abstract: Jamie describes upgrading the hard drives on Apple TV units, citing better local video playback, occasional iTunes server bottlenecks, and reliance issues when the server is offline as motivations.

1075712.abstract: Jamie describes a bug found in Apple TV 2.3 while swapping hard drives during a network outage caused by painting work: when set to play through an AirTunes destination, the device fails to play local music or audiobooks if disconnected from all networks, though video still works.

1075719.abstract: Jamie explains how to create a Smart Playlist in iTunes to track DRM-protected content by matching tracks whose Kind field contains "Protected." Jamie also shows how to combine this with a date-added rule to exclude DRM content, useful for syncing to devices that don't support FairPlay.

1075720.abstract: Jamie welcomes Apple's announcement that all iTunes music is shifting to DRM-free iTunes Plus, noting the change was long expected. Jamie describes upgrading a personal library of about 1,800 DRM items, paying $161.69 to upgrade 728 songs across 9 songs, 49 albums and 2 music videos, while DRM remains on movies and TV shows.

1075721.abstract: Jamie describes MobileMe duplicating every Address Book entry and group, despite Apple's claimed sync improvements in 10.5.6, and relies on Time Machine and weekly Address Book archives to recover. Jamie suggests Apple add Time Machine-style restore functionality directly to MobileMe.

1075722.abstract: Jamie explains how to hide a Facebook Wall by adjusting Profile Privacy settings rather than removing the Wall application itself, since Facebook does not allow deleting it entirely.

1075730.abstract: Jamie suggests that Airfoil should offer an SDK for the iPhone, noting background apps aren't yet possible, and imagines using it to stream Pandora audio to AirTunes speakers.

1075740.abstract: Jamie describes using YakTrax Walkers, a gift from Santa, for morning dog walks in snowy, slippery conditions, having been inspired by Robert Craig's blog post about the product. Jamie reports they provided excellent traction with no slipping, though Tammy mentioned online complaints about breakage, and Jamie recommends buying a pair.

1075741.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of the dog Chase taking a break in deep snow in the yard, after being shoveled multiple times, describing Chase as having fun running around while Jamie shovels the driveway.

1075742.abstract: Jamie wishes readers a Merry Christmas and describes traveling to North Dakota to spend Christmas Day with family. Jamie notes there's no Christmas letter or card this year, observing a pattern of sending one only every other year, citing 2007 and 2005 as letter years versus 2006 and 2004.

1075743.abstract: Jamie examines Last.fm's "Best of 2008" ranking, which named Coldplay's Viva La Vida the top album with over 12.5 million scrobbles, and questions Last.fm's claim that Coldplay may be the "biggest band in the world," a title Jamie associates with U2.

1075744.abstract: Jamie shares a bash script for tracking which SQL files have already been loaded into MySQL, using a tSQLVersions table to check and record loaded files.

1075746.abstract: While updating Tammy's original black MacBook to 10.5.6, Jamie finds the battery too worn to finish the process and uses CoconutBattery to check it, showing 513 mAh capacity, 10 percent health, and 184 load cycles after 31 months. Jamie buys a replacement battery at the Apple Store, restoring the MacBook to near-new condition.

1075749.abstract: Jamie discusses Violet's new Mir:ror product, an RFID reader designed for home use, following earlier work like the Nabaztag and Ambient Devices' Ambient Orb. Jamie suggests applications like using RFID-tagged keys to trigger home automation, such as turning off lights when leaving, and notes friend John Riedl also blogged about the product.

1075750.abstract: Jamie describes attending a holiday hay ride at Bunker Park Stables as part of a family gathering hosted by Jamie's mother's office. Despite cold temperatures and off-key singing during the hour-long ride, everyone has a good time, helped by a sleeping bag Jamie's sister brings to sit on.

1075751.abstract: Jamie analyzes annual household expenses and finds DirecTV service costs $1,079.88 a year, prompting a comparison against replacing it with iTunes and Apple TV.

1075752.abstract: Jamie shares another contribution of high resolution album art, following an earlier post on the same topic, including covers for Lola and the Red Hots' "Have Yourself a Red Little Christmas," The New Standards' "Candy Cane," and a black and white photo of a guitarist smoking on stage.

1075753.abstract: Jamie describes a Comcast broadband speed upgrade, referencing an earlier post about the DOCSIS rollout, and reports a notice claiming PowerBoost now allows downloads up to 15 Mbps. After power cycling the modem, Jamie's Speedtest.net results show over 20 Mbps download and up to 8 Mbps upload, prompting a compliment to Comcast.

1075754.abstract: Jamie describes using Back to My Mac to access files and screen-share with a home Mac Pro while working remotely, calling the feature useful. Jamie requests that Apple add support for shared iTunes libraries to Back to My Mac, arguing it would be simple to implement.

1075755.abstract: Jamie describes a refill station for Restore Products cleaning supplies encountered at Lakewinds co-op, where empty containers are scanned by barcode and automatically refilled, eliminating plastic waste.

1075756.abstract: Jamie describes converting a DVD library into iTunes using Handbrake on a Mac Pro for playback on three connected Apple TVs, and hits trouble joining M4V files that span two discs.

1075757.abstract: Jamie notes an unheralded improvement in iPhone 2.2: the "Update All" button now works reliably, letting Jamie update up to five apps at once without issues, and updated apps install in place rather than jumping locations.

1075758.abstract: Jamie describes Jamie's wife Tammy searching for a No VOC paint to repaint rooms in their color-filled house, eventually finding Safecoat, which avoids chemicals some other "No VOC" paints still contain.

1075759.abstract: Jamie reports reaching a fitness milestone by dropping below 300 pounds, about 25 pounds lost in under two months, well ahead of a year-end target. Jamie credits daily dog walks and two weekly spin classes, notes looser jeans, a smaller belt size, and being able to wear a wedding ring again, and sets a next goal of 280 pounds by January 31st.

1075760.abstract: Jamie notes Twitter has recently been more reliable, but finds it down for database maintenance at 10:22 am CT, questioning why maintenance would occur during peak daytime traffic instead of causing downtime at all.

1075761.abstract: Jamie describes having a row of shelves installed on the back wall of the garage, a project completed in about six hours including moving items and putting everything away. Jamie compares the earlier post about installing 6 inch rain gutters and shares a photo of the finished shelves.

1075763.abstract: Jamie recounts Mazie learning to identify starting letters of words, including a claim that "eyebrow" starts with an I. Tammy corrects the spelling, while Jamie jokes that Apple might actually name eyebrows "iBrow."

1075764.abstract: Jamie describes valuing high-resolution album art for use with Apple TV and iTunes cover flow, and shares 11 album covers scanned at 1,600 by 1,600 pixels that could not be found online, including works by Dan Wilson, Sugar, Trip Shakespeare, and Mike Hosty Trio.

1075765.abstract: Jamie shares Mazie's 2008 school picture, noting that the scowl from the previous year's photo seems entirely gone.

1075766.abstract: Jamie recounts a coffee shop visit where ordering a double espresso leads to confusion from the barista, who questions what the term means. Jamie also notes the shop's smallest ceramic mug holds 12 oz, calling the experience frustrating, and includes a photo of a small espresso in an oversized mug.

1075767.abstract: Jamie shares a photo from lunch at Yum showing Mazie hugging Jamie's wife Tammy at a restaurant table.

1075768.abstract: Jamie votes on Election Day 2008, casting ballot #382 with almost no wait, unlike Jamie's mother who stood in lines over a hundred people long. Jamie compares this to a longer 2006 line and shares a photo of an "I Voted" sticker.

1075769.abstract: Jamie shares a screenshot of a real-time Facebook widget from Election Day 2008 that counts users reporting they voted, taken at 9:44 am central time. Jamie finds the trend appealing, suggesting seeing others vote on Facebook could encourage more people to vote.

1075770.abstract: Jamie notices a Cathay Pacific ad in the Economist that uses media-player button icons (pause, pause, play) in its copy and argues the sequence is a mistake, since starting with "pause" makes no sense; Jamie proposes the correct order should be play, pause, play.

1075771.abstract: Jamie shares a baked oatmeal recipe that Jamie's wife Tammy found in the October 2003 issue of Cooking Light, originally attributed to Susan Baldwin of Eatontown, NJ. Jamie notes the dish reheats well for weekend breakfasts and adds cinnamon and fresh nutmeg to the original recipe, then lists the full ingredients and baking instructions.

1075772.abstract: Jamie shares photos of Mazie's third Halloween, describing excitement building for weeks beforehand, practicing "Trick or Treat" and "Thank You," and choosing a Train Conductor costume over a Princess outfit for a giddy, happy night out.
