1075773.abstract: Jamie explains a dislike of Twitter direct messages, preferring to keep all communication in a single email workflow, and suggests Facebook could improve its own messaging by making it IMAP-capable.

1075774.abstract: Jamie describes appearing in the background of a Star Tribune article photo taken at One on One, a coffee shop and bike shop near Jamie's former downtown office, and recommends the cold press coffee there.

1075775.abstract: Jamie posts a weight loss update, reporting a drop from 314.6 to 307.4 pounds over two weeks, a total loss of 14.8 pounds, and credits recent progress to focused high-quality food choices while staying on track for a sub-300 goal by year's end.

1075776.abstract: Jamie links to a TED talk on flow by Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi, noting a lifelong familiarity with the concept since early teenage programming. Jamie also references Kathy Sierra's writing on "flow killers" like Twitter, and mentions Csikszentmihalyi's book, Flow: The Psychology of Optimal Experience.

1075777.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy watch the documentary King Corn, about two Boston twenty-somethings with Iowa roots who return to grow an acre of Liberty Corn near Greene, Iowa.

1075778.abstract: Jamie links to a Break the Bottled Water Habit campaign found online, revisiting an earlier post about problems with bottled water. Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy had banned bottled water at home and mostly kept the commitment during a six-week trip, with Jamie breaking down twice while Tammy relied solely on tap water in a Sigg bottle.

1075779.abstract: Jamie drops off a Honda Odyssey for maintenance at Richfield Honda and notices a sign in the Parts Dept and Customer Lounge offering text or email alerts when a vehicle is ready, calling it a good alternative to a mid-day phone call.

1075780.abstract: Jamie recounts a fourth spin class at LA Fitness, noting the bikes remain far better than others used previously and that classes, especially the last two, have gone well despite being out of shape. Jamie wore a heart rate monitor for the first time, hitting a max of about 187, and shares a photo of sweat on the floor beneath the bike.

1075781.abstract: Jamie describes converting years of native Canon Raw files (CRW and CR2) into Adobe's DNG format after months of resisting, using the Adobe DNG Converter to process thousands of photos year-by-year. Jamie plans a follow-up post detailing the process, space savings, and reasoning, reversing prior advice against using DNG.

1075782.abstract: Jamie describes using the iPhone app My Diary to log food while losing weight, contrasting it with the gram-precise tracking Jamie used with Lifeform back in 2000.

1075783.abstract: Jamie discusses the newly announced Canon 5D Mark II, noting its lack of a focal length multiplier and its full 1080p HD video capability, and highlights Vincent Laforet's short film "Reverie," shot entirely on the camera, praising its technical quality and depth-of-field shots.

1075784.abstract: Jamie provides a two-week update on a fitness effort begun after committing to a diet change, reporting a loss of 4.4 pounds that week and 7.8 pounds total.

1075785.abstract: Jamie announces that a Minneapolis WordCamp, first proposed in a February 2008 post that drew about 75 interested people, will not move forward. Jamie cites weak sponsorship uptake amid the economic downturn, losing the keynote speaker, and event coordination being outside Jamie's skill set, while hoping someone else will take the lead.

1075786.abstract: Jamie requests an iPhone feature to block certain WiFi networks, citing a screenshot showing options like 2WIRE251, USI Wireless, and Minneapolis public WiFi that repeatedly prompt but are never useful. Jamie also suggests a "join once" checkbox and a captive-portal network type distinct from secured or open.

1075787.abstract: While traveling in the UK, Jamie finds that IP-based geo targeting causes Google services to misfire: Google Reader's login and interface appear in an unrecognized language, and Google Earth only offers a UK store priced in pounds despite a US-based account, prompting Jamie to caution against using geo targeting for account settings or commerce…

1075788.abstract: Jamie highlights independent Mac developers, describing a recent purchase of Timeline 3D from Bee Docs' and a postcard received from the author, citing it as an example of beautiful software paired with strong customer interaction.

1075789.abstract: Jamie describes making homemade applesauce for Mazie, inspired by a sister-in-law's homemade baby food, while eating better and cooking more with Tammy using ingredients from Lakewinds co-op. Jamie buys a Norpro apple peeler from Kitchen Window and a Bamix stick blender to smooth the sauce, then chills it with brown sugar, cinnamon and nutmeg.

1075790.abstract: Jamie tries to link to a sample video shot on the new Canon 5D Mark II from Canon USA's Digital Learning Center, but finds a page declaring Canon has "EXCEEDED [THEIR] DOWNLOAD CAPACITY," which Jamie finds embarrassing for a company promoting its imaging and video capabilities.

1075791.abstract: Jamie describes a printing problem in Lightroom 2 where Canon S900 quality and media settings disappear, replaced by an "incompatible architecture" error. Jamie traces the issue to running Lightroom in 64-bit mode and finds that switching to 32-bit mode restores normal printer settings.

1075792.abstract: Jamie links to a video, shared via friend Raanan's blog, depicting the reality of home foreclosures in southern California, including a man who paints abandoned lawns green. Jamie finds the video depressing.

1075793.abstract: Jamie describes a long struggle with weight, including a 100-pound loss in 2000 working with trainer Fiona Lockhart, followed by failed attempts in 2004 and 2006 to regain fitness.

1075794.abstract: Jamie and Tammy join a new LA Fitness location built near their house, after previously having an "under-leveraged" gym membership elsewhere. Jamie notes the new gym lacks spa amenities but has good equipment, and cuts both commute distance and monthly cost by 70%.

1075795.abstract: Jamie attends a first spin class in over four years at LA Fitness and describes the experience as a good workout, joking with Tammy beforehand about checking a life insurance policy.

1075796.abstract: Jamie uses the CoconutBattery app to check the MacBook Pro's battery health and finds it down to 39% of original capacity, holding only 2,187 mAh of a rated 5,500 mAh after 237 cycles over 20 months, compared to about 90% in January. Jamie plans to try battery conditioning cycles to restore capacity.

1075797.abstract: Jamie shares two Twitter posts about the iPhone OS 2.1 update's effect on battery life, one claiming it's worse and the other calling it much improved, noting how rarely such contradictory opinions appear side by side online.

1075798.abstract: Jamie shares a screenshot of a Mac OS X Trash dialog showing 74,959 items queued for deletion, remarking that the large number reflects bad computer housekeeping.

1075799.abstract: Jamie describes stacking a "fireplace cord" of firewood delivered from Firewood.com, which arrived about 20% larger than ordered. The wood is divided into a storage bin, a deck pile intended for an upcoming Big Green Egg Chiminea and possible wood cooking, and an outdoor stack for winter fires.

1075800.abstract: Jamie describes opening the Big Green Egg grill too quickly while cooking chicken breasts, without "burping" it to let oxygen in slowly, causing a burst of flame that singed a patch of arm hair. A photo shows the resulting burn mark.

1075801.abstract: Jamie joins an SEO challenge issued by Dan (unpossible.com) to test how PageRank affects search rankings for the invented term "Abalastow Compendium," noting an existing hit from blog.lib.umn.edu and no Wikipedia results. An update reports that someone later registered both the .com and .org domains for the phrase.

1075802.abstract: Jamie reacts to news that Lance Armstrong, the 7-time Tour de France winner, is returning to racing in 2009, linking to livestrong.com's announcement video and wondering what Armstrong's goal might be, doubting a Tour de France GC win is likely.

1075803.abstract: Jamie describes visiting the Royal Observatory in Greenwich, London, reached by boat up the Thames after fish and chips near Greenwich Pier. Jamie highlights standing at 0° longitude and seeing John Harrison's H1-H4 timekeepers in the Time Gallery, previously read about in Dava Sobel's book Longitude.

1075804.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy and Jamie prepare to leave by train for a three-day trip to Scotland, bringing only reading material and cameras, while Mazie and Grandma stay in Kensington, London.

1075805.abstract: During a London trip, Jamie's Mom offers to watch Mazie so Jamie and Tammy can attend Zorro the Musical. Jamie finds it more enjoyable than Wicked, while Tammy calls it a favorite, surpassing even Mama Mia.

1075806.abstract: Jamie spends a day in London alone with daughter Mazie while Tammy and Jamie's Mom travel to a Beatles festival in Liverpool.

1075807.abstract: Jamie describes searching London for Amy's Organic Frozen Macaroni and Cheese, a favorite of Jamie's daughter Mazie, after discovering English kids don't typically eat mac and cheese. A Tesco version fails, but Whole Foods in Kensington has it in stock, earning Jamie's gratitude.

1075808.abstract: Jamie describes Jamie's mom arriving in London to join the family for part of a month abroad, planning to explore the city with Mazie while Jamie and Tammy travel to Scotland.

1075809.abstract: Jamie describes visiting friends Alice & John in London, who moved there a little over a year ago, along with Jamie's wife Tammy and daughter Mazie. The visit includes Mazie playing with the girls after initial shyness, catching up on London adventures, and finishing with pizza and beer, with plans for more visits before leaving town.

1075810.abstract: Jamie describes upgrading to Lightroom 2 and highlights the Develop module's Localized Corrections feature, which allows masking and targeted exposure adjustments without round-tripping to Photoshop.

1075811.abstract: Jamie reviews the iPhone app Units, describing how it converts currencies, lengths, speeds and more using a fast calculator-style interface. Jamie notes an early complaint about switching modes was resolved in a newer release that also added conversions, calling it a handy mobile app.

1075812.abstract: Jamie describes a morning visit to Harrods, calling it the world's largest department store, and suggests treating it like an amusement park rather than a place to shop given high prices, such as £79.95 kids' shirts. Jamie's wife Tammy compares it to a casino without gambling, and Mazie picks a toy baby costing £14.95.

1075813.abstract: Jamie describes getting daily espresso while staying in an apartment in London that lacks a coffee pot, noting a double espresso at Harrods as great stuff, with a photo of a Morellis espresso cup and cookie on a cafe table.

1075814.abstract: Jamie describes the rented apartment at Philbeach Gardens in Kensington for a month-long London stay, contrasting it with the earlier Summer of Love road trip.

1075815.abstract: Jamie describes using a Huawei E220 3G USB modem from the provider "3" for internet access at the London Apartment, sharing the connection via OS X Internet Connection Sharing to a MacBook Pro and iPhones.

1075816.abstract: Jamie recounts flying overnight from the US to London for a month-long stay, with daughter Mazie taking a first-ever flight and Tammy managing a fear of flying. Mazie stays awake until 1:30 a.m. due to seatback screens, and the family later takes a £55 cab to Kensington before spending the first day recovering from jet lag.

1075817.abstract: Jamie shares a video from the 2008 Winnipeg Folk Festival showing the kids having fun, noting the family attends every year but the kids only go every other year, and links to a related post about the festival's music.

1075818.abstract: Jamie shares a video captured with a Canon HDV-30 of the horse run at C-Lazy-U, following an earlier audio-only recording of the same event, and notes preferring the audio version in many ways.

1075819.abstract: Jamie praises Quordy, a word game on the iPhone AppStore similar to a dice-based letter game, noting that Jamie and Tammy have become addicted to it. Jamie highlights the touch interface, shake-to-start board, and the asynchronous friend-challenge feature that tracks wins and missed words.

1075820.abstract: Jamie troubleshoots why the WordPress iPhone application stopped working on thingelstad.com after upgrading to version 1.1, tracing the issue to a missing RSD link needed for the XML-RPC endpoint. The cause is a remove_action('wp_head', 'rsd_link'); line in functions.php, which Jamie removes to fix the problem.

1075821.abstract: Jamie describes organizing iPhone Springboard panels into categories—main, info, media, games, and other—to manage a growing collection of apps, and notes frustration that app updates reset their placement, hoping Apple addresses this. Photos show each panel's arrangement, including apps like Twitterrific, Facebook, Pandora, and Trism.

1075823.abstract: Jamie and Tammy prepare for the second trip of the "Summer of Love," a four-week stay in London starting Sunday, renting a flat in Earls Court and planning day trips to Stonehenge and the Royal Observatory. The couple also plans a short trip to Scotland, during which Jamie's mother will watch Mazie before honeymooning with her new husband.

1075824.abstract: Watching the Beijing Olympics gymnastics coverage with Tammy, Jamie notes ongoing confusion over scores, including delays over Nastia Liukin's low vault score despite recent scoring system changes commentator Al Trautwig often discusses.

1075825.abstract: Jamie revisits cold press coffee, previously introduced in a 2007 post, after using a Toddy Cold Press Brewing System from Amazon.

1075826.abstract: Jamie tracks the US Dollar's exchange rate against the British Pound while preparing for a trip to London, sharing charts from BigCharts.com showing the dollar strengthening in August 2008 after a year of weakness. Jamie notes wiring an apartment payment and £1,000 security deposit at a favorable rate.

1075827.abstract: Jamie shares news of a new Minneapolis ALT.NET group, learned about via an email from Ira Mitchell, with help from Freemind.

1075828.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy hosted and produced the latest Iron Chef Minnetonka night, with video from that event to come in three months. Jamie shares the newly released video from the previous edition, themed around egg, also produced by Tammy, and links to a related post on Battle Yogurt.

1075829.abstract: Jamie reviews SleepOver, a $2.99 iPhone app that sends a Wake-on-LAN packet to wake sleeping computers over a network. Jamie describes using it with the Remote app to wake a Mac Pro, start a playlist, and route audio to an Apple TV, calling it a small, useful app worth having.

1075830.abstract: Jamie describes a surprise 70th birthday party for Don Olson, organized by Jamie's wife Tammy and sisters Corinne, Angie, and Michelle, with about 70 guests. Jamie made a video of interviews and photos plus an outtake reel, and links to Angie's blog post about the event.

1075831.abstract: Jamie describes an afternoon spent working intensively on a Mac Pro, running many applications at once. A CPU Monitor screenshot shows all four processor cores maxed out, prompting Jamie to conclude more cores are needed.

1075832.abstract: Jamie describes troubleshooting a non-working basement electrical outlet needed for a new mini-reef aquarium setup. Jamie's father-in-law Don Olson spends over two hours diagramming the switched wiring before fixing it in about ten minutes, a ratio Jamie compares to network debugging.

1075833.abstract: Jamie upgrades to Adobe Lightroom 2 immediately upon release and tests running it in 64-bit mode on a Mac Pro with 7 GB of RAM. Jamie finds 64-bit mode noticeably faster than 32-bit, with quicker catalog browsing and less hard disk activity, and notes Lightroom as the first regularly used application where 64-bit performance gains are significant.

1075834.abstract: Jamie installs the WordPress application on an iPhone and tests it, noting the ability to post and edit while traveling. The post includes a photo of a MacBook decorated with stickers, including a WordPress logo.

1075835.abstract: Jamie notes that cup plants in the yard are beginning to flower, with a couple hundred yellow blooms expected within a week along with bees collecting pollen. Jamie explains the original photo was lost after deleting a Flickr account and could not be recovered from any archive.

1075836.abstract: Jamie lists albums purchased digitally after returning from the 2008 Winnipeg Folk Festival, noting 19 were found online out of roughly 20 typically collected, with three unavailable titles requiring direct outreach to artists.

1075837.abstract: Jamie shares a time-elapsed video of a new asphalt driveway being installed, following the earlier driveway removal described in a previous post.

1075838.abstract: Jamie shares a time-lapse video of a contractor removing a driveway, filmed after noticing the work in progress on a Thursday.

1075839.abstract: Jamie describes coaching Mazie's first Tiny Tonka T-Ball game through Minnetonka Community Education, noting the program has no scores or strikes and is mainly for fun among 3- and 4-year-olds. Jamie recounts kids losing interest by the second inning, except one standout player, and notes the team voted itself the "Yellow Bees."

1075840.abstract: Jamie records a personal note detailing a haircut style: a #1 clipper guard on the sides, high, blending to a #2, finished with a #3 on top.

1075841.abstract: Jamie describes a stay at C-Lazy-U ranch, where wranglers send horses out to pasture each evening and retrieve them each morning. A photo shows a herd running down a dirt road past a red barn.

1075842.abstract: Jamie recounts reaching a milestone on the Summer of Love road trip: after 29 days and 4,541 miles, the Honda Odyssey signals it needs an oil change.

1075843.abstract: Jamie posts an updated statistical index for the "Summer of Love" road trip, including 29 days on the road, 4,541 total miles driven in a 2006 Honda Odyssey, $921.78 spent on fuel, 9 hotel stays, and 1,955 photographs taken, linking back to the first index for comparison.

1075844.abstract: Jamie shares a video of a lap around the Lazy River at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas, part of the Summer of Love collection, marking Mazie's first time in a lazy river.

1075845.abstract: Jamie reviews Tracy Kidder's Pulitzer-winning "Soul of a New Machine," recommended by John Riedl at a book club meeting, about Data General's development of the 32-bit Eclipse MV/8000 ("Eagle") computer in 1981.

1075846.abstract: Jamie marks Father's Day 2008 by noting it falls the day after daughter Mazie's birthday, a coincidence that won't recur until 2014 and then 2025. Jamie reflects on fatherhood as life's priority, quoting a passage from "The Soul of a New Machine" about work as a "bear trap" that distracts from family.

1075847.abstract: Jamie celebrates daughter Mazie's third birthday, noting new vocabulary, budding independence, and affectionate bedtime moments. The celebration takes place in Las Vegas as part of the "Summer of Love" trip, with a pool morning, chocolate cake, and presents.

1075848.abstract: Jamie describes driving through the Mojave Desert toward Las Vegas as the next stop on the Summer of Love trip, noting the temperature has reached 103°F, and shares a dashboard photo of the desert highway.

1075849.abstract: During a long road trip, Jamie encounters record-high gas prices, paying $5.499 per gallon near the Nevada border in San Bernardino County, and shares a photo of the pump display showing the total.

1075850.abstract: Jamie reflects on stops at three national parks during the "Summer of Love" road trip, a hotel-and-restaurant journey rather than a camping trip: Glacier National Park, Mount St. Helens and the Redwood Forest, describing each as expansive, powerful and majestic respectively.

1075851.abstract: Jamie shares a field recording made while walking among the Redwoods, noting brief wind noise and a faint distant truck but mostly capturing birds and the majesty of the setting, along with a photo from the visit.

1075852.abstract: Jamie recounts a visit to the Redwood Forest near Crescent City, sticking to kid-friendly, well-traveled areas rather than long hikes. Jamie describes the trees as majestic, comparing the site to the Valley of the Kings, and shares several photos from the visit.

1075853.abstract: Jamie shares a time-lapse video of a 40-minute drive on US-199, part of the Redwood Highway, from the Oregon/California border into Crescent City, CA, passing through the Redwood Forest about three minutes in.

1075854.abstract: Jamie describes checking into the Curly Redwood Lodge in Crescent City, CA, the 7th hotel on a road trip along the Redwood Highway, chosen after Tammy researched options using Trip Advisor. Jamie notes the motel is built entirely from a single Curly Redwood tree and praises its immaculate, 1960s-period character.

1075855.abstract: Jamie recounts a road trip moment during the "Summer of Love" travels when daughter Mazie, though fully potty trained, refuses normal toilets and insists on using a portable kids' potty, including during a stop in downtown Portland.

1075856.abstract: Jamie recaps attending RailsConf 2008 in Portland during a family road trip, listing sessions attended including keynotes by Joel Spolsky, David Heinemeier Hansson, and Jeremy Kemper, plus talks by Ryan Singer and Scott Chacon on Git.

1075857.abstract: Jamie describes bricking a Linksys WTR-54GS travel router while attempting to install DD-WRT firmware during a six-week road trip, running the hack from Windows inside Parallels on a MacBook Pro. The router fails after a new boot-loader flash, leaving Jamie without WiFi at a hotel during RailsConf, with a JTAG cable fix possibly needed later.

1075858.abstract: Jamie presents an index of statistics from the first 14 days of the "Summer of Love" road trip in a 2006 Honda Odyssey, covering mileage (2,599 miles), fuel cost ($481.13), CO2 footprint (963 lbs) and offset cost ($2.41), hotels stayed in (6), and photographs taken (944).

1075859.abstract: Jamie praises Flickr for its usability and extendability but notes it falls short at helping users find friends beyond Gmail or Yahoo Mail contacts. Jamie highlights Flickr Friends, a site that matches address book exports, including Leopard Address Book vCard dumps, to Flickr accounts, and reports connecting with several friends using it.

1075860.abstract: Jamie recaps a Seattle stop on the Summer of Love road trip, describing extensive walking near Seattle Center, visiting the Elliot Bay Trail, the Northwest Folklife Festival, Cascade Park, the REI flagship store, and the Experience Music Project's Jimi Hendrix exhibit, plus meals at Tutta Bella and Five Spot.

1075861.abstract: Jamie experiments with a new blog theme and asks visitors for feedback before investing further effort in setting it up fully.

1075862.abstract: Jamie describes visiting Mount St. Helens with Kent Tangen's family while their spouses, Tammy and Marilee, spend the day in Portland during RailsConf. Jamie notes the valley sits 100 feet higher than before the eruption 28 years earlier and recommends visiting the site.

1075863.abstract: Jamie describes the daily rhythm of traveling with daughter Mazie during the six-week "Summer of Love" trip, outlining a schedule of early mornings, a midday nap break around 2:00pm, and an 8:00pm bedtime that shapes when Jamie and Tammy handle email, website posts, and Twitter.

1075864.abstract: Jamie recommends musician Greg Merkle, known from working together at Dow Jones, noting the music isn't yet available for purchase but sharing a video Merkle recently posted online.

1075865.abstract: Jamie reports on the release of Delicious Library 2 by Wil Shipley and the Delicious Monster team, describing use of the original Delicious Library to catalog a 1,400+ item CD and DVD collection now stored in Slappa cases.

1075866.abstract: Jamie announces that Jamie's wife Tammy has revived the blog Smaller Than A Redwood, posting regularly during what Jamie calls the Summer of Love, and has given it a new theme. Jamie encourages readers to add the feed.

1075867.abstract: Jamie and Tammy stay at McMenamins Kennedy School, a converted school turned hotel in Portland, while daughter Mazie sleeps. With the baby monitor left in the hallway to catch its signal, Jamie notices passersby stopping to pick it up and listen, and jokes about broadcasting something like War of the Worlds or The Shadow over it.

1075869.abstract: Jamie describes being inspired by Dante Vono's Flickr photos, which paired images with audio recordings, and recounts trying a similar approach using a Zoom H2 recorder in Glacier National Park, pairing a photo of a moss-covered rock outcropping with recorded sounds of rapids and dripping water.

1075870.abstract: Jamie describes moving all sites from Dreamhost to Slicehost after months of slow MySQL and file I/O performance despite liking Dreamhost's interface and structure. Jamie sets up a Ubuntu 7.1 virtual private server, praises Slicehost's documentation, daily backups, and overall service.

1075871.abstract: Jamie shares a Google Webmaster Tools graph showing site response times before and after moving sites to Slicehost from Dreamhost, with erratic slow responses on Dreamhost giving way to consistently fast times on Slicehost.

1075872.abstract: Jamie shares photos from Glacier National Park.

1075873.abstract: Jamie recounts a day in Glacier National Park with Tammy and toddler Mazie, including breakfast at the West Glacier Restaurant and a hike along the wheelchair-accessible Trail of the Cedars.

1075874.abstract: Jamie finishes reading Into the Wild by Jon Krakauer while staying at Glacier National Park, having borrowed the book from a friend, Kent, after previously watching the film adaptation.

1075875.abstract: Jamie describes a first full day at Glacier National Park, staying in a cabin near McDonald Creek and Lake McDonald during cold, rainy weather with only one restaurant open for the season.

1075876.abstract: During a long driving day from Glendive, MT toward Glacier National Park, Jamie watches Dumbo on the new iPod with daughter Mazie and criticizes the film's treatment of otherness, alcohol, and racial stereotyping, recommending viewers skip most of it.

1075877.abstract: Jamie describes buying a 160GB iPod Classic before a 6-week family road trip called Summer of Love, fitting all 15,000 songs, a dozen movies for Mazie, and four rented films. Jamie notes the van's AV input plays the iPod directly, and mentions still using an older iPod Mini for kids' music with compact speakers.

1075878.abstract: Jamie describes an all-day drive on Interstate 94 in a Honda Odyssey, traveling about 635 miles with daughter Mazie, who watches Charlotte's Web and listens to Son Volt, Willie Nelson and Frank Sinatra on a new iPod Classic.

1075879.abstract: Jamie describes an early birthday party held for Mazie, ahead of an actual birthday that falls during an upcoming Las Vegas "Summer of Love" trip. Jamie shares a video of Mazie inventing words for the camera, joined by Uncle Max, after eating the frosting off the cake.

1075880.abstract: Jamie announces selection as a recipient of the Minneapolis St. Paul Business Journal's 40 Under Forty award, thanking Dan Grigsby for the nomination and John Riedl for quotes, and mentions a dinner at the Minneapolis Club to celebrate.

1075881.abstract: Jamie describes committing to walk dogs Izzy and Chase daily through the summer, noting three recent 60-90 minute walks and that the exercise benefits both the dogs and Jamie, with Chase notably calmer afterward while Izzy remains energetic.

1075882.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of daughter Mazie, dressed in a denim jacket, hugging a stuffed animal before school. Jamie notes Mazie's excitement about Jamie being home for the summer and repeatedly saying "Daddy-this and Daddy-that."

1075883.abstract: Jamie describes struggling to find a WordPress theme for Tammy's blog, Smaller Than a Redwood, criticizing themes lacking sidebar widget and tag support and citing one broken theme with missing images.

1075884.abstract: Jamie shares handout materials from the Power WordPress presentation given at Minnebar, delivered without slides. Links to three PDF handouts cover Performance, Plugin Review, and SEO Basics.

1075885.abstract: Jamie describes a farewell video made by colleagues at the Bernards' house, compiled from a year of Jamie's Twitter posts covering coffee, family moments with Mazie, work incidents and tech mishaps, with an unexpected cameo at the end. Jamie thanks everyone and links to the original tweets featured.

1075886.abstract: Jamie describes leaving Dow Jones/MarketWatch after 10+ years, wrapping up projects and helping hire a New York-based replacement CTO. Jamie plans a summer respite with family trips before starting something new.

1075887.abstract: Jamie describes preparing a home office setup while leaving Dow Jones, sharing photos of the current office workstation and the upgraded home workstation that will replace it as the primary computer.

1075888.abstract: Jamie recalls MarketWatch and BigCharts, built on the BigArchitecture COM infrastructure, being featured in Microsoft's Windows 2000 launch scalability demo after switching from unstable Windows NT 4.0 to a Windows 2000 Server beta.

1075889.abstract: Jamie announces plans to present a "Power WordPress" session at Minnebar on May 10th, covering must-have plugins and SEO tactics for driving traffic, and hopes to gather feedback on organizing a WordCamp in the fall.

1075890.abstract: Jamie shares Mazie's first preschool school picture, noting an expression that seems to convey Mazie's feelings about having the photo taken.

1075891.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of an older man playing saxophone on a rain-wet concrete ledge in downtown Minneapolis, taken while walking around the city. Jamie mentions considering a photoblog but instead plans to post individual photography on the site.

1075892.abstract: Jamie recounts an earlier mock Iron Chef competition against friend Dean Eichaker at the Bernard's house, with tomatoes as the secret ingredient. Jamie's wife Tammy later organized a real rematch in January using yogurt as the ingredient, documented in a 15-minute video Tammy produced, with a link to a follow-up post, Iron Chef Egg.

1075893.abstract: Jamie notes that Yum! Kitchen and Bakery, a regular favorite restaurant, now offers open WiFi named "Yum," discovered via iPhone, letting customers browse the internet while eating.

1075894.abstract: Jamie describes craving hash browns and deciding to visit Al's Breakfast, a Wikipedia-linked college mainstay in Minnesota, emailing Jim Bernard and Kent Tangen to join for breakfast before work.

1075895.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy finds Local Burger while researching Lawrence, Kansas restaurants; the spot serves grass-fed, locally raised beef, bison, and elk, and Jamie praises the taste while noting the absence of composting. Jamie also highlights Milton's breakfast, especially the french toast, as worth a repeat visit.

1075897.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy travel to Lawrence, Kansas to see Big Smith and Blue Mountain perform at The Bottleneck, fulfilling Tammy's New Year resolution. Jamie describes Blue Mountain's reunion set of older songs and Big Smith's two-hour-plus performance, noting the band members are all first cousins.

1075898.abstract: Jamie recommends the TED website and podcast, noting the difficulty of attending the conference in person but praising the large library of talk videos available online. Jamie highlights three 2008 TED talks by Karen Armstrong, Stephen Hawking, and Al Gore, describing them as worth watching in sequence.

1075899.abstract: Jamie links to a New York Times piece and a Comcast press release announcing new DOCSIS 3.0 high-speed internet service for Minneapolis and St. Paul, offering 50 megabit downloads at about 2.5 times the cost of current service. Jamie notes the option isn't yet available in Jamie's own service area.

1075900.abstract: Jamie's brother-in-law Hector competes in Ironman Arizona, a 2.4 mile swim, 112 mile bike, and 26.2 mile run, marking Hector's second Ironman after Ironman Wisconsin. Jamie notes Hector's bib number, 297, and reports Hector finished in 10:57:50, placing 191st overall.

1075902.abstract: Jamie describes a phone interview with Scott Swigart and Sean Campbell for their How Software Is Built series, focused on how open source is changing software development. A 2024 update notes the original site is gone but the interview remains accessible via the Wayback Machine.

1075904.abstract: Jamie previews an upcoming period of extended travel, dubbed the "Summer of Love" by Tammy, taken between leaving a current role and starting a new one. Jamie links to a wiki itinerary and a Google Earth preview, and shares a video tour of West Coast cities set to Son Volt's "Windfall."

1075905.abstract: Jamie recounts finding old video clips from February 4, 1998, when CNBC's Bill Griffeth featured BigCharts.com, overwhelming the startup's single Sparc 20 server running Perl/CGI on Apache.

1075906.abstract: Jamie describes being prompted for a zip code while paying for gas, noting the system accepted six zeros as valid input, which suggests the request serves marketing rather than credit-card authorization purposes. Jamie argues companies should respect customer privacy and suggests entering invalid data to undermine such practices.

1075907.abstract: Jamie describes screens now installed in most New York taxis that display weather, news, location and map information, finding the unsolicited activation intrusive but noting they can be turned off.

1075908.abstract: Jamie continues exploring FriendFeed, following up on an earlier post, and highlights an example showing Twitter and Flickr activity tied together within the service, calling it an open, mashable "Web 2.0" approach to life streaming.

1075909.abstract: Jamie describes noticing duplicate posts on FriendFeed caused by a followed user, loupaglia, feeding both Twitter and Tumblr into FriendFeed while also piping Twitter into Tumblr, creating duplicates. Jamie compares this to deduplication problems long seen in financial news and suggests FriendFeed will need to address it.

1075910.abstract: Jamie describes the "Air Bag" warning light appearing on an aging 1999 Audi A6 Avant and learning the issue stems from a controller card failing a checksum validation, the same problem previously encountered with the ABS controller.

1075911.abstract: Jamie describes attending a publisher event at Hearst Tower hosted by True Ventures, Automattic, Sphere, New York Times and Hearst Interactive, arranged by Raanan of Automattic.

1075912.abstract: Jamie describes setting up a profile on FriendFeed after previously building a Yahoo! Pipes-based "Thingelstad Superfeed" in September 2007 to consolidate personal content. Jamie finds FriendFeed easy to use for adding feeds and consolidating friends' information, and invites readers to connect.

1075913.abstract: Jamie recounts completing Rails Studio, a course taught by Mike Clark and Dave Thomas of Pragmatic Studio, with logistics handled by Nicole Clark.

1075914.abstract: Jamie suggests Nintendo add a Flickr channel to the Wii, comparing it to the Flickr channel on Apple TV Take 2. Jamie notes the Wii's existing Photo Channel is "imminently useless" and shares a mockup image of a Wii home screen with a Flickr channel included.

1075915.abstract: Jamie shares a focus tip from a two-day Rails training class: turning off Wi-Fi (Airport) on a laptop to remove internet access and reduce distractions, illustrated with a screenshot of the macOS menu bar Wi-Fi icon.

1075916.abstract: Jamie recaps the final day of Rails Studio, taught by Dave (pragdave.pragprog.com) and Mike (clarkware.com), covering ActiveRecord many-to-many relationships, filters, partials, and AJAX before deploying the event application via Capistrano.

1075917.abstract: Jamie describes creating an offline site-specific browser for Rails API documentation using Fluid, crediting the idea to friend Kent. Jamie downloads RailsBrain's zip file of API docs, uses its logo as the app icon, and finds the resulting local application fast and easily launchable via Quicksilver.

1075918.abstract: Jamie recaps day two of Rails Studio, taught by Dave Thomas and Mike Clark, covering custom forms, ActiveRecord, relational mappings, and routes. Jamie highlights Rails 2's built-in REST support and praises its handling of related data sets, calling it better than other frameworks used before.

1075919.abstract: Jamie describes returning to Twitter after quitting in November, following again at twitter.com/thingles via Twitterific on Mac and Hahlo on iPhone. Jamie outlines habits that make it work: avoiding SMS, not protecting updates, following more people, and following those far away for distance.

1075920.abstract: Jamie describes Fluid, a Mac app that creates site-specific browsers (SSBs), explaining benefits like protecting web apps such as GMail from browser crashes, keeping focus by locking navigation to one domain, and desktop integration with tools like Quicksilver and alt-tab.

1075921.abstract: Jamie shares a flashback about the day MarketWatch's sole publishing server, webfront, permanently died, halting all content publishing. Jamie recalls the editorial team's fake homepage and an all-night effort with Chris Tersteeg to build a replacement system within days.

1075922.abstract: Jamie reads Edward Tufte's book Beautiful Evidence as the newest member of a tech geek book club, after having attended Tufte's lecture twice previously without reading any of the books. Jamie particularly likes the chapters on labeling and sparklines, though finds other parts ramble, and notes the whole club had mixed reactions.

1075923.abstract: Jamie attends day one of Rails Studio in Denver, a Pragmatic Studio class taught by Dave Thomas and Mike Clark, with about 37 attendees. The day covers a Ruby overview, MVC concepts, and hands-on Rails coding, including updates on Rails 2.0.2 changes.

1075924.abstract: Jamie recommends Caffeine, a free menu bar utility from Lighthead Software that prevents a Mac from sleeping, dimming, or engaging the screen saver with a single click. Jamie finds it useful for watching videos, reading long posts, or focusing on problems, and uses it more than expected.

1075925.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy attend a friend's 40th birthday celebration at Fugaise, a Minneapolis restaurant, describing an impeccable salad, beef tenderloin, mashed potatoes, and Toffee Bread Pudding, plus a greeting from Chef Don Saunders. Jamie recommends the restaurant, noting its relaxed, casual atmosphere.

1075926.abstract: Jamie explains the recent lack of posts, citing a heavier travel schedule and time spent preparing to move websites to a new hosting provider, with more details promised later. The post links to a photo of an anechoic chamber at the University of Washington.

1075927.abstract: Jamie gauges interest in hosting a Minneapolis WordCamp, an unconference for WordPress users and developers covering blogging topics generally, and sets up a wiki sign-up page for anyone wanting the event to happen.

1075928.abstract: Jamie shares initial impressions of the Apple TV 2.0 software update, installed across three Apple TVs, noting a quick painless install and a redesigned interface. Jamie highlights Flickr integration and newly discovered AirTunes support for synchronized whole-house music as standout features.

1075929.abstract: Jamie announces the release of the Mac OS X 10.5.2 update, a 341MB download, and advises running Software Update again afterward to install the Leopard Graphics Update. Jamie notes the promised Apple TV update has not yet appeared.

1075931.abstract: Jamie reviews Michael Pollan's "In Defense of Food: An Eater's Manifesto," summarizing its argument against "nutritionism" (a term from Gyorgy Scrinis) and Pollan's core advice: "Eat food. Not too much.

1075932.abstract: Jamie links to an Atlassian case study on using the Confluence wiki at work, featuring quotes from Jamie, and notes it omits how wiki use began at MarketWatch before Dow Jones acquired the company. Jamie calls the writeup accurate and free of the errors such pieces often contain.

1075934.abstract: Jamie shares a voicemail recording from Jamie's daughter Mazie, calling it a "Proud Papa" moment that made Jamie melt.

1075936.abstract: Jamie shares an account of a post-swim class outing with Mazie, describing their usual bagel routine followed by a walk down the mall where Mazie discovers mirrored columns and enjoys playing with them.

1075937.abstract: Jamie expresses enthusiasm for Delicious Library, an application for cataloging books and media, praising its design as an example of software exceeding basic spreadsheet functionality, and notes Delicious Library 2 is a long-anticipated Leopard-only upgrade.

1075939.abstract: Jamie notes that Edward Tufte's seminar is returning to Minneapolis on June 23 and 24, linking to Tufte's site and course page. Jamie has attended twice before, recommends it highly, and mentions attendees receive copies of all four of Tufte's books.

1075940.abstract: Jamie describes using a Jumpnode network appliance for several months to monitor computers, network devices and other infrastructure at home. Jumpnode, a Minneapolis startup product, monitors systems via SNMP or WMI and sets up through a hosted Flash application after simple unboxing. Jamie finds it easy to use and simple to set up.

1075941.abstract: Jamie describes a solution for offsite backups using paired A-set and B-set bare hard drives swapped through a bank safe deposit box, with a USB drive adapter for connecting the disks instead of using bulkier USB or FireWire enclosures.

1075942.abstract: Jamie registers for RailsConf 2008 in Portland, Oregon, running May 29 through June 1, marking a first-time attendance at the conference, and shares an image of the event's "I'm Attending" badge graphic.

1075943.abstract: Jamie describes switching to greener bathroom products, prompted by Jamie's wife Tammy, after already adopting Tom's of Maine toothpaste. Jamie recommends Alba Botanica's moisturizing shave cream, noting its smooth, non-foamy texture and travel-friendly lotion format.

1075944.abstract: Jamie describes revamping the OS X desktop late at night, aiming for a clean, simple look with an abstract background and a minimized dock. Jamie highlights tools used: CoverSutra for music, WeatherDock for temperature, Quicksilver for launching apps, and Warp to improve Leopard's Spaces.

1075945.abstract: Jamie shares four technology resolutions for the new year: signing email with a digital certificate from Thawte, reducing reliance on Google by moving off GMail to Tuffmail and dropping Google Calendar, searching Wikipedia directly instead of via Google, and dropping unnecessary trailing slashes from URLs.

1075946.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Chase, a puppy who has lived with the family for a bit over a month, and notes the dog is old enough to be neutered the next day. Jamie says it's the right choice but admits the procedure makes Jamie uncomfortable.

1075947.abstract: Jamie describes spending an evening helping brother-in-law Hector Fernandez upgrade a Mac to Leopard and improve the WordPress blog I Will Tri, noting how enjoyable working with Mac and WordPress technology can be.

1075949.abstract: Jamie marks turning 36, describing the day spent with Jamie's wife and daughter along with a photo of the birthday cake, and mentions receiving well wishes and new camera equipment as gifts.

1075950.abstract: Jamie describes buying a Bogen-Manfrotto Pro Black Monopod with Swivel Tilt Head for Christmas and testing it with a Panasonic PV-GS400 camcorder, finding it dramatically reduces handheld shake compared to a tripod's limitations. Jamie also demonstrates flipping the camera screen to film self-shots with Mazie.

1075951.abstract: Jamie encourages blog commenters to set up a Gravatar, the globally recognized avatar service now owned by Automattic and integrated with WordPress, noting a plugin also lets Gravatars sync into the OS X Address Book.

1075952.abstract: Jamie describes purchasing thingelstad.com in April 1999, later adding thingelstad.net and thingelstad.name, plus jamiethingelstad.com/.net/.org/.name and misspelled variants like thinglestad.com that redirect to the main domain, all registered through GoDaddy.

1075953.abstract: Jamie buys a Western Digital 1TB My Book external drive at the Apple Store, paying a $30 premium over mail order after checking prices on an iPhone.

1075954.abstract: Jamie describes five Wii games received as Christmas gifts: Super Mario Galaxy, Wii Zapper with Link's Crossbow Training, Zack & Wiki Quest for Barbaros' Treasure, Super Paper Mario, and Tiger Woods PGA Tour 08, sharing first impressions and recommendations for each.

1075955.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of a thumbs-up and announces finishing Guitar Hero III on medium difficulty, deciding not to attempt hard, and includes a friend code, 5026 3031 4382, for others to play.

1075956.abstract: Jamie recaps Christmas 2007, noting that daughter Mazie began to understand the holiday and got excited about presents. Jamie shares a time-lapse video of assembling Mazie's new doll house together with Grandpa Don, continuing a family tradition.

1075957.abstract: Jamie shares a short video of brother-in-law Hector reacting with enthusiasm to a Bluetooth headset given to brother-in-law Denny as a Christmas gift, after Hector arrives from a required morning at the office.

1075958.abstract: Jamie shares thingelstad.com's 2007 holiday letter, written mostly by Tammy and printed via Kinkos, linking to the PDF alongside a curated list of the year's blog highlights.

1075959.abstract: Jamie describes switching to Vimeo after searching for a video hosting service comparable to Flickr for photos. Jamie tests a 13-minute fishing video from Canada that YouTube rejected for length, Google Video failed to transcode, and .Mac couldn't reliably receive, but Vimeo handles successfully.

1075960.abstract: Jamie reports hitting a 497-note streak on Kool Thing by Sonic Youth while playing Guitar Hero III on medium difficulty, ahead of a planned Christmas Day session with brother-in-laws, and links to a Guitar Hero profile page as proof.

1075962.abstract: Jamie visits the newly opened Apple Store on 14th Street in New York, describing it as more spacious than the Fifth Avenue store and noting its impressive glass spiral staircase and three-floor layout, and recommends visiting.

1075963.abstract: Jamie recaps the 2007 Dow Jones Disco Party, describing it as a hit with great food, costumes and the live 70s band Boogie Wonderland, and links to an earlier preview post along with a photo collection from the event.

1075964.abstract: Jamie shares a time-lapse video of setting up the 2007 Christmas tree, made after getting the tree later than usual that year. Mazie is mostly hidden behind a table throughout the footage.

1075965.abstract: Jamie's One Laptop Per Child XO-1 arrives, and initial impressions include a keyboard designed for children that feels very small and an overall "cute" design. Jamie shares photos of Mazie holding the new laptop.

1075966.abstract: Jamie describes recurring server overload problems at Nintendo whenever new Wii software updates or Wii Store titles are released, noting repeated failed attempts to update a system and download the Check Mii Out channel, and suggests Nintendo needs a content distribution network deal.

1075967.abstract: Jamie describes becoming absorbed in Guitar Hero III - Legends of Rock on the Wii, comparing it favorably to Dance Dance Revolution and calling it a must-have Wii game, while inviting readers to connect via a Guitar Hero profile link.

1075968.abstract: Jamie recommends the blog Dictionary Evangelist by lexicographer Erin McKean, discovered after watching McKean's TED talk "Redefining the Dictionary." Jamie places it in a new RSS reader group called "Interesting" and invites readers to share what's in theirs.

1075969.abstract: Jamie compiles a study guide for the Winnipeg Folk Festival finale tradition, in which all performers close the final night with three songs: The Mary Ellen Carter by Stan Rogers, Wild Mountain Thyme, and Amazing Grace.

1075970.abstract: Jamie and Tammy adopt a second dog, Chase, a five-month-old Border Collie/Black Lab mix born in South Dakota, joining their dog Izzy, who was added nine months earlier. Jamie describes Chase's appearance, energy, and quick learning of commands, expecting a weight of 40-50 lbs.

1075971.abstract: Jamie describes cracking an iPhone screen after fumbling the phone into a chair arm, with the fracture hitting near the speaker cutout, similar to a photo Jamie borrows from GeckoAndFly.com. Apple replaces the unit for $249, and iTunes restores it to match the previous device.

1075972.abstract: Jamie describes receiving Pleo, the first robot from Ugobe, part of a limited "First Hatch" edition of 2,000 units. Jamie finds Pleo impressively expressive, notes coworkers enjoyed interacting with it, and links to an Engadget write-up, promising a follow-up post with video.

1075973.abstract: Jamie describes rigging a way to mount an iPhone at headrest height during flights, using two rubber bands and two safety pins attached to the seat back, after finding it uncomfortable to hold the phone or prop it on the tray table for long video viewing.

1075974.abstract: Jamie announces an upcoming presentation, "Innovation in Product Development," at Code Freeze 2008 in January, describing the talk's focus on fostering innovation and creativity in development teams. Jamie invites readers to share their own views on what drives innovation.

1075975.abstract: Jamie reviews the Linksys WTR-54GS travel router, purchased on a recommendation from friend Chris, noting it lets multiple devices—a Dell laptop, MacBook Pro and iPhone—share hotel WiFi despite single-device restrictions, while its built-in firewall protects against other guests, such as exposed iTunes shares.

1075976.abstract: Jamie describes losing a Crash fountain pen owned for a few years, noting its graffiti-style design and having previously ordered replacement parts for it. Jamie plans to order a new one, noting that at least that option exists.

1075977.abstract: Jamie describes adding a Creative Commons license, a digital fingerprint, and the pulling machine's IP address to the thingelstad.com RSS feed, using the CopyFeed WordPress plug-in, to counter content theft by spammer websites, a practice Jamie notes Lorelle recently wrote about.

1075978.abstract: Jamie describes writing a blog post on a plane using MarsEdit, and highlights WriteRoom, a Mac application by Hog Bay Software that provides a full-screen, distraction-free writing environment resembling a retro terminal. Jamie praises its customizable, minimalist design, comparing its elegance to Quicksilver and other independent Mac software.

1075979.abstract: Jamie reviews MarsEdit, a desktop blogging client from Red Sweater Software, praising its WordPress 2.3 tagging support (which ecto lacked), flexible editing via tools like WriteRoom, draft management, live HTML preview, and multi-blog posting, including a mention of MinneLightroom.

1075980.abstract: Jamie describes a round of upgrades to thingelstad.com, including Gravatar support, tags and related links in the RSS feed via Simple Tags, 5-star post ratings from Lester Chan's WP-PostRatings, a new articles page using Alex King's Articles Plug-in, embedded polls via WP-Polls, an update to the blog.txt theme by Scott Wallick, and ongoing manual…

1075981.abstract: Jamie lists ten holiday wishes for Apple's iTunes ecosystem, including Front Row on iPhone, iTunes integration in cars, internet radio and star ratings on Apple TV, a display-equipped Apple TV, eBooks via iTunes, Flickr support, seamless multi-format video, social/P2P sharing features, and an open iPhone SDK.

1075983.abstract: Jamie previews an upcoming office holiday party with a 70's Disco theme, noting the event's tradition of annual themes like black & tie and favorite historical figures, and shares a photo of a silver holographic platform shoe planned for the outfit with Jamie's wife Tammy.

1075984.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy attend the first of two CPR certification sessions at the Twin Cities Red Cross, covering general emergency response practices including the "3 C's": Check, Call, Care. Jamie notes it has been about 20 years since a previous CPR class and the training had been planned since Mazie was born.

1075985.abstract: Jamie reflects on the maturity of Apple's iTunes ecosystem after extending Apple TV coverage into the family room, noting how one application now handles music, podcasts, home videos and soon DVDs across iPods, iPhones and TVs.

1075986.abstract: Jamie recounts a long-running office joke about problems in the men's bathroom, including flooding and broken fixtures, and shares a photo of a handwritten sign taped to a stall door telling coworkers to stop using hand towels because they don't flush.

1075987.abstract: Jamie describes making a pumpkin pie completely from scratch, including the crust, steamed pumpkin, and freshly ground nutmeg. Jamie recounts the difficulty of rolling out pie dough without tearing it, nearly ruining the crust before salvaging it.

1075988.abstract: Jamie describes stopping at SuperAmerica for gas and being subjected to on-pump marketing, including a video screen advertising 89 cent coffee with sound. Jamie complains about the unwanted marketing intrusion and considers switching gas stations.

1075989.abstract: Jamie proposes that Apple combine Apple TV's hard drive and iTunes syncing with the iPhone's touch, coverflow interface to create a car media system, replacing the Phatbox currently installed in a Audi A6. Jamie envisions a garage-synced, removable touch panel and dismisses simply docking an iPod as an inadequate workaround.

1075990.abstract: Jamie discusses One Laptop Per Child and its new XO-1 laptop, noting features like WiFi mesh networking, solar power compatibility, and built-in programming environments. Jamie links to David Pogue's review video and orders one through the "give one, get one" program, planning a follow-up review.

1075991.abstract: Jamie shares a video from a June fishing trip to Chipai, Canada, organized by Jamie's father-in-law for all the brother-in-laws.

1075992.abstract: Jamie and Tammy Thingelstad attend the Butterball charity event with the Tangens, invited by Dan Grigsby. Jamie describes winning a live graffiti painting by artist Chris Allen at the silent auction and watching a performance by Soul Asylum, then shares photos from the evening.

1075993.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy and friends attend the launch party for MinnPost.com, a non-profit news site founded by Joel Kramer applying a public-radio model to journalism. Jamie notes the site just passed 400 members and mentions the parody site MinnToast.com.

1075994.abstract: Jamie reviews Gmail's newly announced IMAP support after considering paid alternatives Fastmail and Tuffmail. Jamie notes problems including duplicate messages caused by the "All Mail" folder, non-standard Sent Items behavior via SMTP, and slow performance, but plans to try Gmail IMAP given its price and webmail client.

1075995.abstract: Jamie describes a San Francisco hotel stay with contradictory environmental practices: guests are encouraged to reuse towels and skip daily linen washing to save water and energy, yet the room's old CRT television runs unattended for hours playing soothing waterfall videos, wasting significant power.

1075996.abstract: Jamie describes becoming a major convert to iTunes after years of resisting it in favor of manual ID3 tag management and third-party iPod tools, but argues the software lacks real sharing features.

1075997.abstract: Jamie describes attending a Hold Steady show at the State Theater, calling it engaging and noting the Minneapolis band's roots in Lifter Puller. Jamie observes a crowd of devoted fans who knew every song, including some band members' parents.

1075998.abstract: Jamie announces quitting Twitter after posting 1,281 tweets, removing the Twitter section from the blog and disconnecting it from an iPhone.

1076000.abstract: Jamie recaps Minnedemo 3 at O'Garas Garage, noting around 300 attendees and demos including CrashPlan from Matthew Dornquast at Code42, Fanchatter, SOTAcomm, Wonderfile, Pokeware, and Adaptive Avenue, with a Christmas Edition announced for December 6th.

1076001.abstract: Jamie describes Mazie receiving and assembling a new toddler bed, transitioning from the crib after asking to sleep in it immediately upon setup. Mazie shows brief hesitation at bedtime but adjusts well, continuing to sleep in the new bed for naps and nights afterward.

1076002.abstract: Jamie describes installing Mac OS X 10.5 "Leopard" on four Macs the night it arrived, noting the iMac, MacBook Pro, and Mac Pro upgraded smoothly while the MacBook's install failed and required reformatting.

1076003.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy completes the Twin Cities Marathon, a first marathon attempt, finishing in around 5 hours 40 minutes using a run/walk strategy after training left Tammy disliking runs over two hours. Tammy currently says another marathon isn't planned, though Jamie senses possible future interest.

1076004.abstract: Jamie shares new caricature-based avatars from Iconize Me, a service created by Paul Sahner that Jamie learned about from a friend, Jim Bernard. Jamie orders vector avatars for the whole family, including Tammy, daughter Mazie, and a group image with the family dog, planning to use them for the website and as iTunes cover art for home movies.

1076005.abstract: Jamie describes moving thingelstad.com from TextDrive, after months of downtime and frustration, to Dreamhost, recommended by a friend, citing a $9 anniversary hosting deal, a fast admin interface, SSH access, and carbon-credit-based data centers.

1076006.abstract: Jamie reviews Michael Lewis's book Moneyball, recommended by a baseball-loving friend, and finds it enjoyable despite not particularly liking baseball. Jamie notes the book highlights how the sport resisted statistical analysis and describes Lewis's framing of "look and feel" versus "spreadsheet" camps as compelling storytelling.

1076007.abstract: Jamie describes attending Electric Arc Radio, a live show by a group of writers formerly known as the Lit6 Project, with Jamie's wife Tammy and friends from thetangens.net. Jamie finds the performance fresh and funny, notes Tammy loved it, and points to another show on September 29th.

1076008.abstract: Jamie describes participating in the first Minneapolis Bike Tour alongside Jamie's wife Tammy, riding the short route with an Ironman brother-in-law while Tammy and a sister rode the longer route. Jamie calls the event Minneapolis's answer to the St. Paul Classic and plans to ride again in 2008.

1076009.abstract: Jamie describes Jamie's wife Tammy's push toward environmentally conscious household changes, including shopping only at co-op Lakewinds, bamboo bedsheets, and a decision to stop buying bottled water after reading "Garbage Land," switching instead to Sigg bottles.

1076010.abstract: Jamie reviews Etymotic ER6i earbuds installed onto iPhone headphone cables by UltimateBuds, a service that swaps in Etymotic speakers while preserving the original microphone.

1076011.abstract: Jamie recounts taking Mazie to a first Renaissance Festival, bringing Izzy along as well. Jamie describes Mazie enjoying the event and Izzy showing interest upon noticing bones lying around, with photos from the outing.

1076012.abstract: Jamie describes getting Mario Strikers Charged for Wii, calling it a beginner at the game, and shares a friend code for others to play. Jamie questions why the game requires a separate 12-digit friend code rather than using existing Wii friend connections, comparing the system to old Compuserve addresses.

1076013.abstract: Jamie describes visiting the Uptown Art Fair in Minneapolis with Tammy, following the couple's usual routine of previewing on Friday and buying an anniversary piece on Saturday. Jamie names favorite artists including Gabe Lanza, whose painting "G0L147H vs.

1076014.abstract: Jamie recounts seeing Son Volt perform at the Minnesota Zoo, describing it as the most energetic show from Jay Farrar in 15 years of watching Farrar's music, from Uncle Tupelo through Son Volt's current lineup, with tracks from the new album The Search standing out live.

1076017.abstract: Jamie recounts attending the Beastie Boys' first-ever Brooklyn concert at McCarren Pool, part of a limited tour following the release of The Mix-Up, describing an outdoor show mixing old and new songs into mashups with heavy bass.

1076018.abstract: Jamie recounts a fishing trip where the goal is catching a large Northern, generally anything over 30 inches. Jamie catches a 35.5" Northern in a spot called the Ball Cap, while Don lands the trip's biggest fish at 46 inches.

1076019.abstract: Jamie reports that the Discovery Pro cycling team, formerly US Postal and tracing back to Subaru-Montgomery, will disband after the current season, unable to find a sponsor after Discovery Channel ended its support.

1076020.abstract: Jamie describes receiving a cryptic message while fishing at a remote Canadian camp run by George, a Native American camp operator with limited English, that turned out to contain only a phone number.

1076021.abstract: Jamie recaps a five-day fishing trip to Chipai Lake in Canada with three brother-in-laws, father-in-law Don, Don's brother Roger, and other extended family, catching Northern Pike and Walleye daily while staying off-grid without cell service. Jamie shares a collection of about 80 photos from the trip.

1076022.abstract: Jamie describes upgrading an HP LaserJet 1320 printer with a 128MB memory DIMM after experiencing slow printing on complex documents, noting the low cost and improved print speed, and shares a photo of the printer's system information panel showing 144MB total memory.

1076023.abstract: Jamie replaces the previous iMac G5, given to a sister five months earlier, with the newly released 24" iMac, purchased from the Apple Store the same day Apple announced it. Jamie praises the aluminum-and-glass design and thin new keyboard, and also buys iWork '08 and iLife '08, expressing interest in trying Numbers and the redesigned iMovie.

1076024.abstract: Jamie recommends two Mac puzzle games: Quinn, a free Tetris-style tile-dropping game by Simon Haertel with a standalone multiplayer server, and Frenzic, a paid pie-slice puzzle game with online rankings that Jamie finds more strategic and addictive.

1076025.abstract: Jamie discusses doping scandals disrupting the 2007 Tour de France, including Alexander Vinokourov's expulsion, Rabobank withdrawing after firing its leader, and Michael Rasmussen's ejection over missed tests rather than a positive result.

1076026.abstract: Jamie describes culling a CD collection and singling out "Only in America, Volume 2" from Arf! Arf! Records as possibly the worst CD ever made, quoting the label's own description of it as bewildering. Jamie notes a Volume 1 also exists and links to a related discussion at JasonHare.com.

1076027.abstract: Jamie recounts a roughly 17-mile bike ride to Yum with Jamie's wife Tammy and Mazie, wearing regular cargo shorts instead of cycling shorts. Jamie finds the experience uncomfortable due to heat, bagginess and restricted movement, and concludes cycling shorts are necessary for rides over 2 miles.

1076028.abstract: Jamie recaps a fourth visit to the Winnipeg Folk Festival, attended with wife Tammy, noting Mazie stayed with grandparents and marking a first year without Jamie's mother present.

1076029.abstract: Jamie shares a chronological log of SMS-based Twitter updates posted during the 2007 Winnipeg Folk Festival, covering performances by artists like Crooked Still, the Flatlanders, Spearhead, Leo Kottke, the Flecktones, and Los Lobos, plus camping, weather, and food notes.

1076030.abstract: Jamie describes switching from Waste Management to Randy's Sanitation, a locally owned company, after learning about its new Organics Recycling program in Minnetonka.

1076031.abstract: Jamie describes strategies for maximizing iPhone battery life while camping with limited electricity access at the Winnipeg Folk Festival. Recommendations include disabling WiFi and Bluetooth, switching email to manual checking, turning the phone off at night, lowering screen brightness while disabling auto-brightness, and muting sound and vibrate.

1076032.abstract: Jamie shares a series of Twitter updates chronicling the wait to buy an iPhone on its June 29, 2007 launch day, including being #53 in line, watching Christopher (first in line) get media attention, a Piper Jaffray survey passed down the queue, and ultimately obtaining two iPhones at 06:26 PM.

1076033.abstract: Jamie shares impressions after two weeks with the first-generation iPhone, comparing it to a BlackBerry 8800 and pointing to detailed reviews from Ars Technica and Engadget.

1076034.abstract: Jamie describes activating iPhones through iTunes, noting Tammy's activation went flawlessly but Jamie's own required nearly 90 minutes with AT&T, a new SIM card, and several account changes to move a business number to an individual plan.

1076035.abstract: Jamie describes waiting in line for a few hours at the Southdale Apple Store to buy an 8G iPhone, with a photo of the original 2007 iPhone's home screen, and promises further reactions soon.

1076036.abstract: Jamie recounts taking daughter Mazie to Mazie's first Minnesota Twins game over Memorial Day weekend, joined partway through by Tammy after Grandpa Bruce's visit, with the Twins winning and ice cream capping off the outing.

1076037.abstract: Jamie describes discovering cold press coffee at the local shop One on One, after asking the barista for an iced drink alternative to iced espresso or brewed iced coffee. The barista explains cold press involves brewing a pound of beans with 80 ounces of water for 12 hours, unheated, then pressing through a cloth filter.

1076038.abstract: Jamie previews an upcoming Canadian fishing trip departing with a father-in-law and brother-in-laws to fish for large fish. Jamie mentions packing Figamajigs snack bars, considering but skipping a Globalstar satellite phone due to cost, an 80-pound gear limit, and plans to journal offline and post upon return.

1076039.abstract: Jamie recaps the 4th annual Olson Family Weekend, planned by Angie and held at the Lundeen family's cabin, with 11 people and 3 dogs despite unpredictable weather. Jamie links to photos from the trip and notes that videos of Mazie originally posted to YouTube have since been removed.

1076040.abstract: Jamie argues JavaScript is a powerful, serious development environment despite common dismissals tied to its "script" name and early trivial uses like falling snowflakes.

1076041.abstract: Jamie tests Google Gears, released the previous night, using the offline mode it enables in Google Reader while on an airplane flight, finding the experience impressive despite missing features like marking all items read.

1076042.abstract: Jamie shares a screen capture, forwarded through a chain of friends including Jim Bernard and Lapoint, showing a Twitter moment where Jamie's robot and comedian Steven Wright post similar-sounding lines.

1076043.abstract: Jamie posts a second time-lapse video of a drive to work, an improvement over an earlier attempt that suffered from a poorly mounted, shaking camera.

1076044.abstract: Jamie describes a five-year-old directory structure for organizing digital photos, used with tools like Adobe Lightroom, built around root folder, year, month, day (with an added title like "Around House"), a timestamp-plus-serial-number filename format, and a catch-all "Other" folder, emphasizing consistency, unique filenames, and simple…

1076045.abstract: Jamie recounts a conversation with wife Tammy about whether to give up the Internet forever in exchange for a favorite food, mentioning chocolate brands Lindt and Vosges and joking about surviving on meal replacement shakes instead. Jamie asks readers what food would make them abandon the Internet.

1076046.abstract: Jamie describes installing a Solatube skylight system, discovered through Home Power magazine and Solar Midwest at the Living Green Expo, in a previously dim entryway.

1076047.abstract: Jamie shares a time-elapsed video of a morning drive to work, made with the time-elapse feature of a new Canon camera. Jamie notes sun glare and a weak mount, and plans to try again with a Joby Gorillapod, also linking to an earlier time-elapsed video of a flight take-off.

1076048.abstract: Jamie describes breaking out of a longtime habit of wearing only conservative, dark dress shoes, sparking a shoe-buying spree that includes two-tone Ecco dress shoes, bright orange Crocs, Campers, and Gola sneakers found while shopping on Zappos with Jamie's wife Tammy.

1076049.abstract: Jamie describes upgrading from a Canon S500, used for nearly three years, to the newly released Canon SD750, purchased at B&H Photo and Video in New York.

1076050.abstract: Jamie uses the time-lapse feature on a new Canon SD750 to record assembling a table and chairs set, a birthday present given early to Mazie, who is turning 2. The resulting video runs 48 seconds.

1076051.abstract: Jamie recounts attending Jon Stewart's stand-up show at the Orpheum in downtown Minneapolis with Tammy, after a friend of Tammy's invited them.

1076052.abstract: Jamie recounts being stranded in New York after a 6:00pm LaGuardia flight faces repeated delays, then cancellation, amid storms and a citywide hotel shortage. A friend from opticality.com, reached via Twitter, offers a couch after a $900 Four Seasons room falls through.

1076053.abstract: While stranded in New York, Jamie attends Frost/Nixon at the Jacobs Theatre after hearing about it on MPR. Jamie recounts the play's story of David Frost's interviews with Richard Nixon and praises performances by Michael Sheen and Frank Langella, recommending the show.

1076054.abstract: Jamie describes using OpenID for a few weeks and finding it impressive, noting an identity created on MyOpenID had little use until recently. Jamie cites a ReadWriteWeb excerpt explaining OpenID as a decentralized single sign-on framework, and points to Simon Willison's screencast for a demonstration.

1076055.abstract: Jamie describes a weekend getaway to Birdwing Spa for Tammy's birthday, arranged with relatives handling childcare for Mazie and Izzy.

1076057.abstract: Jamie shares dock icons for Adobe Lightroom, Photoshop, and Illustrator CS3, noting the new "iconography" sparked debate and inspired community-made alternatives, but states liking the simple, cohesive orange-and-red square designs once lined up together.

1076058.abstract: Jamie reflects on Minnebar 2007, praising organizers Ben Edwards, Luke Francl and Dan Grigsby, and notes attendance nearly tripled from the prior year. Jamie led a Q&A with Ruby on Rails creator David Heinemeier Hansson, sharing Tim Elliott's recording and full transcript of the session.

1076059.abstract: Jamie upgrades a Mac Pro to 7 GB of memory, sharing a screenshot of the About This Mac dialog showing OS X 10.4.9 with dual 2.66GHz Xeon processors, and notes the added memory lets Lightroom use as much as it wants.

1076060.abstract: Jamie switches the WordPress theme from K2 to blog.txt, finding K2 too heavy and not "stretchy." Jamie works to get Ultimate Tag Warrior and Extended Live Archive functioning with the new theme, re-enables the Share This plugin, adds WP-Cache for speed, and reduces the blog's main page to 5 posts.

1076061.abstract: Jamie announces the launch of MinneLightroom, a Twin Cities user group for Adobe Lightroom, inspired partly by encountering Lightroom developers at Adobe's Minneapolis office. Jamie plans to collaborate with Adobe and the Twin Cities Photoshop User Group to build interest among photographers.

1076063.abstract: Jamie and Tammy Thingelstad attend the American Craft Council Craft Show at the River Centre in St. Paul, noting strong attendance despite a $12 entry fee. Jamie highlights standout artists including Flinn Designs, Raymond Bock furniture, Stoner/Hatton Mobiles, and Amazing Wind Machines whirligigs.

1076064.abstract: Jamie recounts the final day of a five-day "Mr. Mom Weekend" spent solo with daughter Mazie, including a trip to the Minnesota Zoo with Aunt Alona, before Jamie's wife Tammy returns home early. Jamie calls the puppy's first-time care the most stressful part and welcomes Tammy's idea of an annual extended trip.

1076065.abstract: Jamie compiles a series of Twitter posts from a solo-parenting "Mr. Mom Weekend" spent caring for daughter Mazie and dog Izzy, covering tasks like school bus duty, naps, meals, cleaning up after the dog, an Apple Store visit, and organizing digital photos in Lightroom.

1076066.abstract: Jamie describes initial skepticism toward 37 Signals' Highrise, comparing it dismissively to Salesforce.com, but after trying it for personal use—tax preparation, house projects—finds it surprisingly useful even solo.

1076067.abstract: Jamie recounts a Sunday with Mazie and Izzy, including skipping swim class due to Mazie's congestion, a lunch at Good Day Cafe, and an energetic visit from Aunt Angie's dog Louie. Jamie notes forgetting Mazie's afternoon snack caused a difficult evening before an early bedtime.

1076068.abstract: Jamie shares best practices for using Keywords in Adobe Lightroom's Library module, distinguishing them from Collections and IPTC metadata fields.

1076069.abstract: Jamie describes buying a Griffin Technology PowerMate USB controller at the Apple Store after admiring it for a long time. Jamie calls it frivolous but praises its spin and click feel, noting its usefulness for tasks like selecting video ranges in Final Cut.

1076070.abstract: Jamie recounts a Saturday spent caring for daughter Mazie and puppy Izzy, including a playdate with friend Dan's son Henrik and lunch at Yum. Jamie concludes puppy chores are harder than parenting Mazie and finds the 5-7pm stretch especially difficult, while anticipating a visit from Grandma Rosalin and Aunt Alona.

1076071.abstract: Jamie recounts a day handling childcare duties for daughter Mazie and dog Izzy, describing morning scheduling mishaps, a visit with Grandpa Don, a grocery trip, and a chaotic moment juggling a business call, yogurt demands, and a dog mess. Friends later visit with dinner, Guinness, and cigars.

1076072.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy leaves for a 5-day trip to Heifer Ranch's Women's Lambing Weekend, helping deliver newborn lambs and planning to ride a water buffalo.

1076073.abstract: Jamie complains that most GPS units degrade saved tracks by discarding time and date stamps and removing points to reduce file size. Jamie discovers this while trying to geo-associate Switzerland photos, and concludes the only fix is writing a program to interpolate missing timestamps.

1076074.abstract: Jamie describes giving away the 20" iMac G5 to a sister two years after buying it as the first Mac in over a half-decade. Jamie notes Macs now outnumber PCs at home, with a Mac Pro, MacBook, and a Sony Vaio running Quicken, and plans to wait for a rumored redesigned iMac with Leopard, using the MacBook in the kitchen meanwhile.

1076076.abstract: Jamie announces the second annual Minnebar "unconference," scheduled for Saturday, April 21st, and encourages readers to sign up on the wikipage at barcamp.org/MinneBar. Jamie explains Minnebar is a full-day, topic-focused event related to Minnedemo, a twice-yearly evening demo event.

1076077.abstract: Jamie describes enthusiasm for Adobe Lightroom, having imported nearly 40,000 photos and using its Library module for organizing collections, keywords, and location metadata like country, state, city, and place.

1076078.abstract: Jamie describes receiving one of the first Apple TV units from the local Apple Store, comparing it to an iPod for the living room with a 40G hard drive and HDMI connection. Jamie finds setup simple and the interface elegant, but notes a short power cable and poor results encoding a DVD for playback.

1076079.abstract: Jamie announces the arrival of Izzy, a new dog joining the Thingelstad family, following an earlier post about getting a dog. Jamie's wife Tammy, daughter Mazie, and Grandma Kaye pick Izzy up from the foster home, with Izzy vomiting on Grandma Kaye three times during the nervous ride home before calming down and meeting neighbor kids.

1076080.abstract: Jamie announces that the family is adopting a dog, a terrier-poodle cross, found by Tammy through online adoption sites after other pups Tammy liked were adopted quickly. The dog arrives the following Wednesday; the post includes photos of puppies and notes daughter Mazie's fondness for dogs like Rusty and Louie, belonging to relatives.

1076081.abstract: Jamie reviews Albert-László Barabási's book Linked, discovered through a colleague's recommendation, which explores scale-free network theory and its application to the Internet, the Web, social circles, and human cells.

1076082.abstract: Jamie describes creating a Twitter bot, thinglesBot, to surface data from home monitoring scripts that previously went unnoticed via email or tools like cacti. The bot reports outdoor and indoor temperatures, solar panel activity, and end-of-day inbox email counts, and Jamie notes strangers have followed it.

1076085.abstract: Jamie describes a late-night AM radio listening session during a drive to Chicago with Tammy, sharing sarcastic "learnings" picked up from talk radio, including claims that minimum wage pushes are a union scheme, that arranged marriages and "disgrace" should return to American culture, and that poor bowel movements cause sluggishness.

1076087.abstract: Jamie recounts a Chicago weekend away with wife Tammy, their first without daughter Mazie, staying at the Peninsula Chicago and visiting the Field Museum, Wicked the musical, an Untouchables gangster bus tour, and the Apple Store's glass staircase, while comparing deep dish pizza spots and favoring Gino's East over Paisano's.

1076090.abstract: Jamie describes frustration with Tab key behavior in OS X when filling out web forms, since checkboxes are normally skipped. Jamie explains the fix: in Keyboard & Mouse settings, under Keyboard Shortcuts, switching Tab behavior to "All Controls."
