1076091.abstract: Jamie describes discovering Everyone Votes, a free Wii Ware download from Nintendo that appeared after a system update to 2.0U, letting players answer either/or questions, predict others' responses, and suggest new questions using Mii avatars. Jamie praises Nintendo's creativity and links to coverage at Wii Nation, Wii Nintendo, and Go Nintendo.

1076092.abstract: Jamie describes PackRat, a Mac OS X application from infinitenil.com that connects to Backpack using a username and API key, downloading content for offline access and syncing changes back. Jamie notes it handles tag navigation better than Backpack and often uses it even while online, wishing a Windows version existed.

1076093.abstract: Jamie notes that the 50th and France area of Minneapolis offers plenty of open WiFi access points, making it easy for anyone with a laptop to get online there.

1076094.abstract: Jamie notices that breaks at an offsite business training event are now called "Blackberry Breaks" rather than "Communication Breaks," suggesting Blackberry has become a generic brand like Kleenex, and wonders if future breaks will be called "iPhone Breaks" or "iBreaks."

1076095.abstract: Jamie announces giving up self-hosted email after years of running it, citing the burden of fighting spam and phishing and maintaining SMTP, IMAP, and antivirus software.

1076096.abstract: Jamie watches the Super Bowl and comments that rain beading up on players' helmets, viewed in HDTV, demonstrates the value of the technology.

1076097.abstract: Jamie describes testing different permalink structures for search engine optimization, moving from a /category/title format—frustrating since categories can change—to a more stable /year/month/title structure, noting some links may break temporarily but the sitemap stays updated.

1076099.abstract: Jamie and Tammy attend a Minnesota Rollergirls roller derby event with friends, finding it more enjoyable than expected. Tammy favors the Rockits and player Jawbreaker, while Jamie enjoys watching Rebel Stella of the Dagger Dolls. Jamie recommends attending but suggests reviewing the rules beforehand.

1076100.abstract: Jamie provides an update on a weight loss program using Traineo, reporting a drop from a high of 315 lbs to 21 pounds lost, with motivation from friends and a trainer at MySelectFitness.

1076101.abstract: Jamie reviews Google Analytics data showing which search terms bring visitors to thingelstad.com, noting one visitor who searched about coin jar distributions from the Change Game post and stayed for 41 more pages.

1076102.abstract: Jamie describes becoming a regular user of Backpack, a personal information management tool from 37 Signals, after searching for a "personal wiki" alternative to the abandoned OpenWiki project.

1076104.abstract: Jamie describes moving thingelstad.com from a server in the laundry room to a faster rented server at ValueWeb, gaining more bandwidth and friendlier URLs, while also upgrading WordPress, though some features remain broken and need fixing.

1076105.abstract: Jamie describes noticing that water tastes different out of new red handblown drinking glasses purchased to replace broken clear glasses, while Jamie's wife Tammy notices no difference. Jamie tests the theory by comparing water in old and new glasses and wonders whether glass color affects perceived taste or whether this is imagined.

1076106.abstract: Jamie describes celebrating a birthday as a family vacation day with wife Tammy and daughter Mazie, crediting Tammy for planning gifts and activities. Jamie shares an old photo with Jamie's mother from about 34 years earlier and references a prior post on "fractional life" theory about time passing faster with age.

1076108.abstract: Jamie describes frustration with the Sony NTM-910 baby monitor's poor range and random "out of range" beeping, then details switching to the Philips Digital SCD-589, a DECT-based monitor offering clear audio, room temperature readout, two-way talk, and remote music or light activation, noting Tammy tested its range successfully but found it…

1076109.abstract: Jamie links to a Twin Cities Business Journal article from January 1 covering Dow Jones's Minneapolis office and R&D work, noting the piece inaccurately frames the office as solely about Dow Jones Online rather than multiple divisions. Jamie welcomes the publicity to raise awareness and attract talent.

1076110.abstract: Jamie recommends Thunderbird add-ons for syncing address books across five computers: Addressbook Synchronizer copies the address book to a network or IMAP location, while Contacts Sidebar and Duplicate Contact Manager add a contacts pane and remove duplicates.

1076111.abstract: Jamie describes feeling overwhelmed by metadata needs across a 33,000-photo archive, 400GB of ripped music, and video files.

1076112.abstract: Jamie describes unseasonably warm, rainy weather on December 30th, 2006, with temperatures reaching 41°F, and notes a lack of snow throughout the month.

1076113.abstract: Jamie describes bringing a Nintendo Wii to North Dakota for Christmas, where cousins requested it and it saw over 9 hours of play on December 25th, with Wii Sports and Mii creation proving especially popular.

1076114.abstract: Jamie, Tammy, and Mazie send Christmas wishes and explain that the planned second annual Thingelstad Christmas letter never got finished, so it won't arrive by mail. Jamie promises to try again with a letter in 2007.

1076115.abstract: Jamie describes discovering Traineo, a community-based fitness tracking site, via a TechCrunch post, and signing up after reading about it. Jamie plans to use Traineo instead of the Lifeform software for tracking progress, citing its motivator system and community features as advantages, while still praising Lifeform's food logging.

1076116.abstract: Jamie discovers Cha-Ching, a Mac personal finance application from Midnight Apps, while browsing RSS feeds in Google Reader. Jamie compares it to Firefox challenging Internet Explorer, and though only at version 0.4 and not yet a rival to Quicken, finds it sleek and enjoyable, hoping it develops into a simple yet powerful tool.

1076117.abstract: Jamie describes a personal campaign against unwanted mail order catalogs, prompted by receiving as many as ten a day during the holiday season. Jamie contacts each company's customer service to request removal, tracks the requests for potential escalation, and reports prompt responses so far.

1076118.abstract: Jamie tests newly arrived component cables for the Wii, comparing the composite 480i connection against the component 480p setup using close-up photos of the Disc Channel logo, Mii Channel screen, and the settings button.

1076119.abstract: Jamie reviews three OCZ USB drives bought after losing an OCZ Rally2 2G: the Rally2 4G, Mini-Kart 2G, and Roadster 1G, comparing write/read speeds via ATTO benchmarks. Jamie plans to use the Mini-Kart for mobile work and the Rally2 for large file transfers, citing the Roadster's slow performance despite its compact design.

1076120.abstract: Jamie assembles a wooden play kitchen as an early Christmas present for 18-month-old daughter Mazie, insisting on doing the assembly personally rather than letting wife Tammy build it while Jamie was away in NY. Jamie reinforces every joint with wood glue and notes relatives are coordinating gifts of matching accessories.

1076121.abstract: Jamie describes replacing a failing home-built workstation with a new Mac Pro, ordered with 2.66Ghz CPUs, an ATI Radeon X1900 XT card, Bluetooth, and expanded to 3G of RAM, plus three added SATA drives.

1076122.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy visit Butter Bakery, a new restaurant in south Minneapolis offering brunch, baked goods, and coffee, eating lunch there Saturday and returning for breakfast Sunday. Jamie praises the bakery items overall but singles out the pancakes as especially gooey and flavorful.

1076123.abstract: Jamie describes Mazie's progress learning new words and recounts Mazie navigating both flights of stairs in the house without help, bracing against the wall and taking one step at a time while Mom and Dad stay close by in case of a fall.

1076124.abstract: Jamie highlights singing the ABC song backwards, a skill credited to Ralph's World, linking to an audio clip and noting the third verse is where it gets difficult to perform.

1076126.abstract: Jamie describes bringing a newly released Nintendo Wii to the Olson family Thanksgiving gathering, where three hours of Wii Sports play appealed to relatives in their 20s through 60s. Jamie predicts the Wii will outsell its nearest rival console by a factor of two.

1076127.abstract: Jamie describes migrating an old DotText (.Text) blog to WordPress instead of Community Server, detailing the process: exporting all posts via RSS using a PinkJoint DLL fix, editing image URLs with regex, and importing through WordPress's RSS tool despite losing categories.

1076129.abstract: Jamie describes getting a Nintendo Wii and becoming enthusiastic about it, praising the motion-sensitive controller for tennis, boxing, bowling in Wii Sports and for passing and kicking in Madden 07. Jamie also owns Zelda and Rayman, and notes Tammy's separate order for a Wii was canceled due to insufficient units.

1076130.abstract: Jamie describes getting a Wii on release day at Target after Tammy accepts an extra ticket, numbered 9, offered by a stranger who had waited in line overnight. Jamie reflects on the moral dilemma of accepting the unearned ticket and wonders how the stranger came to have a spare.

1076131.abstract: Jamie describes dealing with a new wave of spam at home after previously solving the problem by switching email addresses. Jamie has used Postini at work for years, and after finding Postini doesn't offer individual accounts, locates a reseller charging $2.50/month per address that provides quick setup.

1076132.abstract: Jamie describes trying friend Chad's new Playstation 3, praising its graphics on a high-end HDTV but finding the launch games underwhelming and the system too focused on first-person shooters. Jamie's wife Tammy orders a Wii after noticing Jamie's enthusiasm, hoped to arrive before Thanksgiving.

1076133.abstract: Jamie describes returning from a business trip and encountering an electronic "Threat Level Orange" sign at the airport, questioning what practical value such alerts provide.

1076134.abstract: Jamie announces that Jamie's wife Tammy launches a website called Smaller Than a Redwood, featuring early content of varied thoughts and comments rather than a diary-style format, with plans to include contributions from friends.

1076135.abstract: Jamie, not typically a console gamer, expresses fascination with the upcoming Nintendo Wii, citing an Economist article on its unconventional approach compared to Sony and Microsoft. Jamie notes positive experience with a Nintendo DS shared with wife Tammy and hopes to receive a Wii as a Christmas gift.

1076138.abstract: Jamie describes video chatting with Jamie's wife despite each being on a computer in the same house, one upstairs and one downstairs, and shares a photo captioned "Local Videoconference."

1076139.abstract: Jamie announces the new website is live after configuring port-forwarding on a Zywall 10 router, noting the manual's example configurations solved the setup. Jamie plans further additions and is seeking a WordPress-compatible replacement for the removed photo galleries.

1076140.abstract: Jamie announces plans to relaunch thingelstad.com using WordPress, with the new site expected by the end of the week. Jamie notes plans to redirect links, especially RSS feeds, and advises readers to check feed links if updates stop appearing.

1076141.abstract: Jamie recounts being the 37th voter at a polling station on election day, sharing a photo of the line before polls opened. Jamie notes wariness of the vote-scanning machine after watching the documentary Hacking Democracy, and suggests voting is well suited for the internet.

1076142.abstract: Jamie reviews the redesigned Google Reader, noting the update fixed usability issues that earlier versions had. Jamie recommends it as a web-based, mobile-friendly alternative to using Thunderbird's RSS functions.

1076143.abstract: Jamie describes attending a first Ruby Users of Minnesota (RUM) meeting, highlighting friend Dan's presentation using rex and racc to build a LaTeX math parser for Road Sign Math, plus a laptop count showing 11 Macs versus 2 Windows machines.

1076144.abstract: Jamie describes ordering a DeLonghi Magnifica fully-automatic espresso machine to recreate the coffee shop experience at home, noting the regular order of iced triple espresso that inspired the post's title. Jamie reports relying on Amazon user reviews before buying and finds the machine easy to use, producing consistent shots with good crema.

1076145.abstract: Jamie tries How Many of Me?, a site using census data to rank name popularity, finding 49,535 John Smiths, no Thingelstads, and that "Jamie" is 182nd most popular with 69.86% female, prompting teasing from Tammy.

1076146.abstract: Jamie describes recurring thumb pain from frequent BlackBerry ("CrackBerry") use, noting past success avoiding hand problems through ergonomic tools like a trackball and split keyboard after a bout with Carpal Tunnel Syndrome in the early 90s.

1076147.abstract: Jamie announces the second MinneDemo, a shorter, more social BarCamp-style event featuring quick demos, scheduled for December 11th at Acadia Cafe in Minneapolis, following the earlier Minnebar unconference. Jamie missed the first MinneDemo but plans to attend this one, noting Road Sign Math as a sponsor.

1076148.abstract: Jamie describes commissioning a painting from local artist Erik Sletten of Slettenstudios.com, after being struck by a sketch while flipping through Sletten's sketchbook at a neighbor's gathering months earlier. Jamie and Tammy visit the studio to watch Sletten begin adding color to the 5.5-foot-square canvas.

1076149.abstract: Jamie recounts a detour to Atlanta to visit the Georgia Aquarium at Pemberton Place, calling it the largest aquarium in the world and a must-see.

1076150.abstract: Jamie recounts the final day of the Great East Coast Adventure, arriving home after 37 days, 5,890 miles and 8 beds, noting 15-month-old Mazie's relaxed reaction to being back. Jamie also updates a Google Earth file documenting the trip's stops.

1076151.abstract: Jamie describes a rained-out visit to Boone Hall Plantation in Charleston, noting its 300-year-old oak-lined drive, then walking partway across the Ravenel Bridge to Mt. Pleasant, calling it "my bridge" and wishing Minneapolis had one like it.

1076152.abstract: Jamie recounts a car-free day in Charleston, taking the water taxi to lunch at Jim n' Nicks barbecue and visiting the South Carolina Aquarium, home to a two-story, 20-foot reef tank. Mazie, initially scared on her first boat ride, later rides the water taxi calmly.

1076153.abstract: Jamie describes Mazie's improved sleep after a difficult stretch that reached a breaking point in Asheville, exhausting Jamie's wife Tammy. After a hotel change and time at Ed & Nancy's, Mazie sleeps through the night for five days in Charleston.

1076154.abstract: Jamie recounts a day trip from Charleston to Savannah, Georgia, including lunch at Paula Deen's restaurant The Lady & Sons, which Jamie calls a "Temple to Butter," and an afternoon spent taking photos in Forsyth Park.

1076155.abstract: Jamie describes walking Charleston's historic downtown with Tammy and Mazie, shopping along King Street, and eating at Sermets Corner, recommending the sweet potato french fries. Jamie also reflects on Market Street's history as a former slave market, finding the legacy of slavery unsettling.

1076156.abstract: Jamie recounts a weekend in Charlotte with Tammy's biological father Ed, wife Nancy, half-brother Christopher, aunts Betty Lou and Sandi, and Sandi's husband Bob, before continuing to Charleston, SC and checking into the Belvidere Club Resort.

1076157.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy track the words Mazie uses independently, compiling a list that includes "help," "please," "credit card," "kitty," "all done," and "oh jhez," noting the list grows daily and will quickly become outdated.

1076158.abstract: Jamie reports successfully installing Windows Vista RC 1 (Build 5600) on a MacBook using Parallels Desktop (Build 1898), noting the setup works without special tricks and delivers Aero, though not Aero Glass.

1076159.abstract: Jamie describes a car accident while driving back to a hotel with Mazie, where another driver ran a red light and struck the passenger-side rear bumper of Jamie's minivan. The other driver was uninsured, leaving Jamie facing repair costs or a rate increase, and photos show scrape damage and paint transfer near the rear wheel.

1076160.abstract: Jamie recounts visiting Chimney Rock Park near Asheville, hiking to a 400-foot waterfall with Mazie, then touring the North Carolina Arboretum's bonsai exhibit before switching hotels and updating the trip's Google Earth KMZ file.

1076161.abstract: Jamie describes driving from Asheville to Hot Springs, NC, to hike a short stretch of the Appalachian Trail with toddler Mazie in a carrier. Photos show the AT blazes, forest trail, water breaks, and Mazie walking parts of the path.

1076162.abstract: Jamie describes trouble getting daughter Mazie to sleep in Asheville, where she wakes screaming and ends up in bed with Jamie and Tammy. Jamie covers the windows with tinfoil to darken the room, which helps her fall asleep alone but doesn't stop a 3:30am waking.

1076163.abstract: Jamie describes 25 days into a family road trip and the challenges of traveling with one-year-old Mazie, who struggles to sleep away from home, screams at bedtime, and refuses naps outside her car seat. Jamie notes toll roads disrupt her sleep and mentions a hotel meltdown prompting Jamie's wife Tammy to consider other lodging.

1076165.abstract: Jamie describes arriving in Asheville and touring the Biltmore Estate, calling the 8,000-acre grounds and mansion amazing and recommending a visit. The family checks into the historic Princess Anne Hotel, noting its small elevator and spacious rooms with kitchens.

1076166.abstract: Jamie reflects on finishing three weeks in the New Jersey/New York area before heading on vacation and eventually back home. Jamie notes feeling eager to leave, citing constant checkout lines and jammed traffic, and concludes the density of people in the region is overwhelming despite generally enjoying city life.

1076167.abstract: Jamie describes a six-hour drive to Roanoke, Virginia, marked by heavy traffic, daughter Mazie's crying, and wife Tammy's ear infection. Referencing Bryson's "A Walk in the Woods," Jamie detours onto Skyline Drive in Shenandoah National Park before dinner at Macado's, ahead of plans to reach Asheville and the Biltmore Estate.

1076168.abstract: Jamie recounts the final week in New Jersey before vacation continues, noting visits from Grandma Kaye and Aunt Angie, who took around 230 photos, and describes a calmer schedule with fewer meetings and more evenings with Tammy before leaving the 800 square foot apartment.

1076169.abstract: Jamie shares a Google Earth map letting readers explore locations from the Great Adventure series of updates, noting the original KMZ file the post linked to has since been lost.

1076170.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the first two weeks of the Great Adventure, edited by Tammy. Updates include a dead MacBook memory DIMM fixed with a Radio Shack screwdriver, Mazie learning new words like "please," settling into a small apartment, and losing 5 pounds. Day 17 begins with Grandma Kaye and Aunt Angie visiting before a trip to the Bronx Zoo.

1076171.abstract: Jamie recounts day 17 of the East Coast Adventure, visiting the Bronx Zoo's Congo Gorilla Forest with Mazie, Tammy, Grandma Kaye and Aunt Angie, then traveling to Philadelphia to see American Pie furniture store and dine at El Vez.

1076172.abstract: Jamie recounts day 16 of the East Coast Adventure, including breakfast at PJ's Pancake House in Princeton, a visit to the New Jersey Grounds for Sculpture with a boss and family, and dinner at Main Street Bistro before picking up Grandma Kaye and Aunt Angie at Newark airport.

1076173.abstract: Jamie reflects on a hectic Friday during the "East Coast Adventure '06" trip, noting that overscheduling three weeks of in-office plans left no room for unexpected fire drills. Jamie's lesson: leave unstructured time for handling people and surprises. Links to other days in the series follow.

1076174.abstract: Jamie describes commuting into New York City for a 9:00am meeting via Princeton Junction and Penn Station, taking three hours and arriving 15 minutes late. Jamie notes commuters mostly sleep rather than work, and finds it surprising people accept 2-hour commutes daily.

1076175.abstract: Jamie recounts Day 10 of the East Coast Adventure in Washington DC, visiting the White House, Washington Monument, Holocaust Museum, WWII Memorial, Korean War Memorial, Lincoln Memorial and Vietnam Memorial with Tammy, Mazie, and visiting Grandma Chrest and Aunt Alona.

1076176.abstract: Jamie recaps a busy week of early mornings and evening business events before preparing to head to Washington DC for the long weekend, where Jamie's mom and sister will join Jamie, Tammy, and Mazie.

1076177.abstract: Jamie describes daughter Mazie struggling to sleep during day four of the East Coast Adventure trip, screaming when placed in the crib despite normally being an easy sleeper. Jamie's wife Tammy spends 90 minutes settling Mazie the previous night, and Jamie attributes the trouble to exhaustion from driving and the time change.

1076178.abstract: Jamie describes wanting to run an application directly from a USB flash drive instead of just storing files, and finds existing 1G drives too slow using ATTO Disk Benchmark tests. Jamie orders an OCZ Rally2 2G accelerated drive from Newegg, which shows much better benchmark performance and comes in a compact metal enclosure.

1076179.abstract: Jamie describes buying a Linksys WRT300N wireless router and WPC300N PCMCIA card from Best Buy while on the Great Adventure, choosing 802.11n over a WRT54GS since a WRT54G is already owned at home. Jamie notes easy setup but regrets not finding an affordable router supporting IPsec VPN back to the Minneapolis network via ZyWall.

1076180.abstract: Jamie describes an effort to lose weight after weight gain over the past couple of years, having logged food for two weeks and dropped about 3 pounds.

1076181.abstract: Jamie recaps the first days of a five-week family trip east, including three weeks working from a New Jersey office followed by two weeks vacationing in North Carolina. Jamie describes the drive from Minneapolis with Jamie's wife Tammy and dog Mazie, stops in Rockford, Illinois and Toledo, Ohio, and settling into an apartment in Lawrenceville, NJ.

1076182.abstract: Jamie describes daughter Mazie giving an unprompted kiss on the cheek, calling it exciting, and notes Mazie's progress navigating stairs, walking alongside a parent for longer stretches, and learning words like "help," "dog," and "cat."

1076183.abstract: Jamie recounts a weekend trip to Iowa City to visit friends Lisa and Eric and their new baby Rachel, staying at the Hotel Vetro. Jamie's wife Tammy recognizes actor Doug Savant from Desperate Housewives in the hallway, and Jamie notes online that Savant's wife is from Iowa City.

1076184.abstract: Jamie recounts winning the "Change Game" at Starbucks, a personal challenge Jamie previously described on the blog, noting this marks only the third or fourth win in over four years.

1076185.abstract: During a Best Buy visit, Jamie and Tammy try a Nintendo DS demo after Jamie reads about "brain games" in Scientific American Mind, then buy a Nintendo DS Lite with Brain Age, Big Brain Academy, and Super Mario Bros, noting plans to research hacking the device.

1076186.abstract: Jamie describes touring six rural properties with Tammy in the Red Wing/Zumbrota, Minnesota area and across the river in Wisconsin, seeking 15-25 wooded acres within one to two hours of the Twin Cities.

1076187.abstract: Jamie reviews two Nintendo DS brain-training games, Brain Age and Big Brain Academy, describing Brain Age's voice recognition, research grounding, and comparison of scores against Tammy's, plus Big Brain Academy's more game-like puzzles. Jamie concludes Brain Age is superior overall, though recommends both for puzzle fans.

1076188.abstract: Jamie recounts going with Tammy to see the documentary Wordplay at the Edina Theater while Mazie's aunt babysits, describing it as a fun look at competitive crossword puzzle solving, including a tournament and solvers finishing in just over two minutes.

1076189.abstract: Jamie describes a first visit to the Mill City Farmers Market in its second weekend of operation, noting it differs from the larger Minneapolis farmers market.

1076190.abstract: Jamie describes receiving a black Apple MacBook as a Father's Day gift from wife Tammy, after years using Windows following an early Mac upbringing and a return to the platform via an iMac in 2004.

1076191.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy and Jamie donate to PAX (paxusa.org), a national organization working to reduce gun violence among children and teenagers, on daughter Mazie's birthday.

1076192.abstract: Jamie reflects on celebrating a second Father's Day shortly after daughter Mazie's birthday. Jamie describes Mazie's development—walking well, growing vocabulary, strong-willed food preferences, and playful games—and credits wife Tammy with handling most of the harder parenting tasks.

1076195.abstract: Jamie's solar heat project is completed, with Innovative Power Systems turning on the collectors and starting to bring heat to the storage tank. Jamie uses Cacti to monitor the system, recording a peak return water temperature of 138 degrees and panel temperatures around 145 degrees, and plans a detailed follow-up post on the solar experience.

1076196.abstract: Jamie describes applying Window Alert decals to the house's windows after noticing frequent, sometimes fatal, bird strikes caused by increased songbird activity from landscaping.

1076197.abstract: Jamie criticizes Xcel Energy for its handling of wind power, noting years of voluntary payments into the WindSource program while a separate, mandatory "curtailment payment" also funds wind energy.

1076198.abstract: Jamie recounts attending the opening showing of An Inconvenient Truth, noting the timing coincided with finishing a solar heat installation. Jamie describes it as more like Al Gore's long-running presentation on global warming than a typical movie and urges everyone, regardless of political affiliation, to see it.

1076199.abstract: Jamie describes getting pulled over on the MnPASS lane leaving downtown, clocked at 71 in a 55, and receiving a citation for Unacceptable Acceleration rather than a full speeding ticket, the first stop in about 10 years.

1076200.abstract: Jamie provides an update on a home solar project, noting the roof and attic work is finished with only utility room plumbing remaining before a contractor team activates the system.

1076201.abstract: Jamie describes finding a child safety gate to fit an awkward stairway space where one connecting wall is only 30.5 inches high. The gate came from USA Baby and Jamie recommends it for similarly challenging spots, expressing relief now that Mazie can move around the upper level safely.

1076202.abstract: Jamie describes revamping a home network after a gigabit connection dropped to 100 mbit during solar project cabling changes, and shares a photo of switches and a small rack mounted on plywood. Jamie plans to rewire ethernet runs into a patch panel and set up color zones for security, referencing a linked article on securing home networks.

1076203.abstract: Jamie describes Mazie beginning to walk during the Olson Family trip to Lanesboro, then becoming confident on her own over the following two weeks. Jamie shares a shaky video, shot on a Canon S500, of Mazie walking at the Minnesota Landscape Arboretum.

1076204.abstract: Jamie describes learning to fly an Align T-Rex RC helicopter, getting help from Rudy at Hobby Warehouse in Richfield before practicing at home and at a father-in-law's garage over Easter weekend, and details a series of crashes damaging servos, the tail, canopy and bottom plate, requiring repeated trips to the hobby shop for parts.

1076205.abstract: Jamie provides an update on a home solar project, explaining a decision made after meeting with the contractor to relocate the panel array from its original spot to the front roof, near the skylights.

1076206.abstract: Jamie shares first impressions of new Sony noise canceling headphones after trying them on a recent trip to New York, noting mixed but generally positive results. Jamie describes a noticeable pressure sensation, inconsistent cancellation when sound hits at an angle, some impact on sound quality, and comfortable wear over a couple of hours.

1076207.abstract: Jamie shares an update on daughter Mazie at 9 months old, noting recovery from a second cold, emerging teeth, babbling, and a preference for walking while held rather than crawling.

1076208.abstract: Jamie provides an update on a home solar project, noting that the collectors were installed on the roof's north side, angled for full southern exposure. Jamie has mixed feelings about their appearance, especially the view from the deck, and plans to discuss alternatives with the contractor before the hot water and heating integration proceeds.

1076209.abstract: Jamie describes a miserable Dallas-to-Minneapolis flight spent in a loud, narrow last-row seat near the engines after losing an "empty middle seat bet." Jamie buys Sony MDR-NC50 noise canceling headphones from Best Buy and plans to test them on upcoming flights.

1076210.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of a white-tailed deer eating spilled seed at a backyard bird feeder on a gray winter morning, noting that unlike squirrels, this visitor is not something Jamie can do much about.

1076211.abstract: Jamie describes buying a Britax Marathon car seat for Mazie, choosing a neutral, washable version over a pink floral option. Mazie tries it at the store and seems to like it, prompting Jamie to think Mazie was ready to move up from the infant seat to see more while riding.

1076212.abstract: Jamie describes spending four hours assembling an Align T-Rex 450SE remote-control helicopter, noting the high-end kit arrives 80% pre-assembled. Jamie still needs to wire the electronics and mentions using Reflex XTR training software, where repeated crashes occurred, plus a new video solution for testing.

1076213.abstract: Jamie describes Mazie's first serious cold, worse than a milder one experienced as an infant, with heavy congestion and coughing. Jamie recounts giving Mazie a bath while Tammy was at the gym and comforting Mazie afterward, noting visible discomfort and hoping for a quick recovery.

1076214.abstract: Jamie describes receiving an iPod Nano as a Valentine's Day gift from Jamie's wife and daughter, after previously dismissing interest in it until trying one at Best Buy. Jamie updates the firmware, sets it up in iTunes, and loads photos, noting no further need for a "big" iPod unless rumored widescreen models materialize.

1076215.abstract: Jamie tests a wireless video camera from Helidirect mounted on an E-Sky Llama helicopter and a nitro RC car, sharing two videos of the results.

1076216.abstract: Jamie describes upgrading digital video audio after finding built-in camcorder microphone quality poor, citing a shotgun microphone comparison review. Jamie chooses the Røde Electronics VideoMic over an unavailable Panasonic hot-shoe option, reporting excellent audio quality despite its size and increased background noise pickup.

1076218.abstract: Jamie recounts hiring Minnesota Statewide Roofing & Remodeling to replace shingles ahead of a solar heating installation, describing repeated no-shows, unreturned calls, a weather-damaged tarp job, and a roof that initially failed inspection.

1076219.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy gives Jamie a Canon EF-S 10-22mm f/3.5-4.5 USM ultra-wide zoom lens as a birthday gift. Jamie compares it to the EF-S 17-85mm lens using side-by-side toaster shots, noting the wider field of view and some corner distortion, and looks forward to using it for outdoor photography in summer.

1076220.abstract: Jamie recommends Yum Kitchen and Bakery, a new restaurant mentioned at The Rake, noting it lacks a website. Jamie describes the cafeteria-style ordering setup and praises the chicken chili, macaroni and cheese, and dessert counter.

1076221.abstract: Jamie revisits Harry Middleton's book "The Earth Is Enough," which recounts Middleton's boyhood living with uncles in the mountains and celebrates simple living. Jamie compares Middleton's writing style to Norman MacLean's and recommends reading slowly, alongside other Middleton titles like "Bright Country" and "On the Spine of Time."

1076222.abstract: Jamie describes buying Canon 12x36 IS II binoculars as a delayed Christmas gift, chosen for wildlife and bird watching around the house, with secondary use for astronomical viewing alongside a telescope.

1076223.abstract: Jamie describes trying Sudoku, a puzzle recommended by Jamie's mother, noting it involves numbers but little actual math and compares it to Minesweeper. Jamie finds it enjoyable and time-consuming, good for flights, but limits playing due to a backlog of other tasks.

1076224.abstract: Jamie tries desktop blogging clients BlogJet and Post2Blog after typically writing posts directly into a web page, noting features like automatic image uploads to a hosting provider and offline writing. Jamie also considered w.bloggar but finds it less polished than the other two.

1076225.abstract: Jamie announces a switch to shooting all digital photos in RAW format starting in 2006, comparing RAW files to negatives versus JPEG's Polaroid-like limitations, with an exception for the Canon S500.

1076226.abstract: Jamie reflects on turning 34, noting plans to spend the day with wife Tammy and daughter. Jamie introduces the idea of an age "set point," a stable age people feel they belong to, mentioning Tammy's set point of 27 and linking the idea to an earlier "Fractional Life" theory post, while noting this birthday feels different as a first one as a…

1076227.abstract: Jamie shares an open letter sent to the Hopkins School Board after being notified the district finished the year in statutory operating debt.

1076228.abstract: Jamie describes visiting two new restaurants: Salut, a French bistro at 50th and France in Minneapolis owned by the same group behind Manny's, Chino Latino, and Good Earth, praising the steak frites and steak sandwich, and Ravello in Long Lake, recommended by a coworker, where Jamie dines with friends Jim and Suzie and enjoys the lamb shank.

1076229.abstract: Jamie describes a visit from Brian Broughten, founder of Advanced Aquarium, to discuss a bid for a custom saltwater tank: 8 feet long, 2 feet deep, 30 inches tall, totaling 300 gallons, with dual pumps moving 3,000 gallons per hour and metal halide lighting.

1076231.abstract: Jamie's friend Chris gets into RC helicopters, prompting Jamie to buy an E-Sky Lama 2 electric helicopter from eBay.

1076232.abstract: Jamie describes turning the earlier blog post "Digital Photography Storage Explosion" into a shorter article for MarketWatch, published with a byline under the title "Digital Photography Presents Huge Storage Challenge." Jamie notes the piece is abbreviated compared to the original unabridged version.

1076233.abstract: Jamie reports that Mazie slept through the night for the first time in 196 days, resting from 7:00 pm to 6:10 am with minimal disturbances. Mazie's mother is excited but doubts a pattern has formed, while Mazie's father thought this was already routine.

1076234.abstract: Jamie reports that Mazie turned 6 months old on Dec. 14th and had a checkup showing 75th percentile for weight, height and head circumference. Mazie now sits up, plays with toys, and has started oatmeal and carrots, though bananas prompt a funny face.

1076235.abstract: Jamie describes revisiting several hobbies, including getting an equatorial wedge for a telescope to try astrophotography, becoming interested in image-stabilized Canon binoculars for birding, and considering shortwave radio after trying a Yaesu VR-5000 at Radio City.

1076236.abstract: Jamie describes seeing Al Franken outside Barnes & Noble at the Galleria in Edina while shopping with Tammy and Mazie, apparently for a book signing. Jamie notes the group avoided gawking and includes a photo of Franken speaking.

1076237.abstract: Jamie describes buying a Linksys WRT54G wireless router at Radio Shack, drawn by its Linux-based open firmware platform that enabled third-party firmware like Sveasoft and DD-WRT. Jamie finds that Linksys, now owned by Cisco, switched the WRT54G v5 to VxWorks, blocking third-party firmware, though the WRT54GL model retains Linux.

1076238.abstract: Jamie describes taking a week of vacation at home with Tammy and Mazie rather than traveling, planning some projects alongside relaxing, with babysitting arranged for outings. Jamie notes feeling energized by work but expects the break to bring more focus.

1076239.abstract: Jamie recounts a visit to Southdale where Mazie gets a first photo with Santa, joking that Santa mentioned the Teletubbies. Jamie also complains that the "Hi-Res Digital Photo" CD, shot on a Canon Digital Rebel, turned out to be only 3.15 megapixels for $26.

1076240.abstract: Jamie recounts having to watch a TV show live with commercials after a roof replacement required removing the DirecTV satellite dish, breaking a six-year TiVo habit. Jamie describes checking TVGuide.com for the show's schedule and looks forward to TiVo returning once the dish is reinstalled.

1076241.abstract: Jamie describes a first movie outing since Mazie was born, seeing Walk the Line with Tammy and calling it very good, followed by lunch at the newly opened Naar Grille. Jamie notes concerns about the restaurant's location but finds the Mediterranean food, including the gyros, very good, and recommends trying it.

1076242.abstract: Jamie describes trying Google Analytics after finding Weblog Expert inadequate and nearly purchasing Visistat before Google's free tool appeared. Jamie notes Google Analytics is overwhelmed by demand, with reports delayed since Thursday despite a promised 24-hour turnaround, and warns of a potential PR problem if the issue persists.

1076243.abstract: Jamie links to an article, "Digital Photography Storage Explosion," inspired by watching visitors use digital cameras at Disneyworld with Jamie's wife Tammy, which analyzes personal photo-taking habits to estimate how much digital storage Disneyworld generates daily.

1076244.abstract: Jamie analyzes personal digital photo storage growth since getting a Fuji MX-700 in 1999, tracking over 20,000 photos and nearly 50GB against Moore's and Kryder's Laws.

1076245.abstract: Jamie describes several home projects underway at once: the third phase of a landscaping project adding a stone path and stairs, a new high-efficiency furnace and air conditioner, new glass shower doors in the master bathroom, a roof replacement complicated by poor contractor communication, and roof prep for a solar heat installation planned for…

1076246.abstract: Jamie recounts attending friend Scott's wedding to Cara near San Jose, including go-kart racing at Lemans Karting in Fremont, dinner at City Beach, driving a rented Ferrari 308GTSi from Club Sportiva along Skyline Drive, lunch at Alice's Restaurant, and the ceremony in Half Moon Bay.

1076247.abstract: Jamie, Tammy, and Maze visit friends Dan and Melanie in Iowa City to see their newborn, Henrik, while another couple, Lisa and Eric, expect their first child after buying a house. Jamie reflects on becoming comfortable as a parent after four months and mentions reading Dan's new blog about the experience.

1076248.abstract: Jamie describes buying two Roku M500 MP3 players after previously praising the Roku M1000, purchased for Mazie's room, during a sale. Jamie places the new units in the bedroom and another location, finding installation easy but expressing frustration with UPnP servers.

1076249.abstract: Jamie describes moving Mazie's crib from the parents' bedroom to Mazie's own bedroom, noting the first night alone went well and Mazie seemed to sleep better in the quieter space. Mazie also discovered how to trigger the crib's music toy by kicking it.

1076250.abstract: Jamie reviews Corteo, a traveling Cirque du Soleil production in Minneapolis, marking a seventh Cirque show after "O," Dralion, Alegria, La Nouba, Varekai and Mystere.

1076251.abstract: Jamie recounts the second annual Olson family weekend, a yearly mini-vacation tradition on Tammy's side of the family, this year organized by Corinne in Wisconsin Dells. The group stayed at Wilderness Resort cabins, hiked, geocached, and played Xbox, marking dog Mazie's first trip to Wisconsin.

1076252.abstract: Jamie recounts taking Mazie to a Ralph's World concert on a neighbor's suggestion, describing the show as surprisingly loud but full-band and kid-friendly, with Mazie enjoying it until getting tired. Jamie recommends Ralph's World concerts to other parents.

1076253.abstract: Jamie reflects on a demanding work week culminating in a launch of streaming stock quotes on MarketWatch, calling it one of the most significant projects completed.

1076254.abstract: Jamie recounts a lunch at Rix Bar & Grill in north Minneapolis, chosen for Jamie's mother's birthday, describing the relaxed atmosphere and praising the sweet potato french fries with chipotle dipping sauce, the green bean appetizer, and the Sunday-only huevos rancheros. An update notes repeat visits confirming it as a good neighborhood spot.

1076255.abstract: Jamie shares follow-up impressions of the 2006 Honda Odyssey after two weeks, praising the ECO cylinder-management system and thoughtful storage features, but criticizing the driver-memory mirrors not syncing with seat memory and finding XM Radio's programming boring, noting Sirius carries NPR while XM does not.

1076256.abstract: Jamie describes daughter Maze's developing personality at nearly four months old, including distinct cries and reactions to being held by dad, plus giggling from tickling.

1076257.abstract: Jamie describes a "purple haze" HDMI display problem on a DirecTV HD TiVo (HR 10-250) that had worked fine since January, where true blacks appear purple. After a 33-minute call, DirecTV support claims the HDMI port is known to fail and recommends component video instead, agreeing to send a replacement unit.

1076258.abstract: Jamie describes buying a 2006 Honda Odyssey Touring edition in silver pearl metallic from Richfield Bloomington Honda, prompted by difficulty using a car seat in a station wagon and plans to get Tammy a new car.

1076259.abstract: Jamie recounts a coffee purchase totaling $4.58, paid with a $10 bill and three pennies, expecting a $5 bill, a quarter and two dimes back. Instead the cashier gives nine nickels, which Jamie says sets back progress in the "change game" described in an earlier post.

1076260.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of baby Mazie wearing a "Hello World" onesie printed with C code, linking to the Jinx.com product page for the shirt, and wonders whether Mazie will later find the picture cool or embarrassing given Jamie's geekiness.

1076261.abstract: Jamie shares parenting tips based on early experience with baby Mazie, covering diaper-changing position, moving the crib into the parents' room before her own, and dealing with evening fussiness.

1076262.abstract: Jamie reflects on Mazie approaching a 3-month milestone on the 14th, describing new developments like tracking movement, giggling, and playing games, alongside a recently emerged full-bore crying pattern that has Jamie and Tammy wondering about colic.

1076263.abstract: Jamie describes experimenting with LDAP to unify address books across webmail and Thunderbird, installing OpenLDAP for Windows and phpLDAPAdmin, and upgrading to PHP5, which required patching SquirrelMail with an unreleased 1.4.6cvs build.

1076264.abstract: Jamie reflects on the family farm in northwest North Dakota where Jamie's mother grew up and where grandparents still live, describing childhood summers there and the surrounding wheat and barley country.

1076265.abstract: Jamie describes an ongoing battle with raccoons tearing up newly laid backyard sod to get at worms and grubs underneath. Attempts to stop them—tent stakes, fifty lawn staples, and eventually a landscaper-installed deer fence—all fail as the raccoons keep returning nightly.

1076266.abstract: Jamie describes weekend work on a home network following a "security incident" about 10 days earlier that caused no significant damage.

1076267.abstract: Jamie describes spending four hours attempting to configure a new network topology using pfSense 0.79.4 on a firewall box with four ethernet ports, trying to set up WAN, LAN, DMZ and WIRELESS networks without success, and plans to try again later.

1076268.abstract: Jamie describes a busy wedding weekend: Jamie's wife Tammy's sister Michelle marries with both Jamie and Tammy in the wedding party, and the next morning Jamie flies to New York for friend Greg's Central Park wedding, timed tightly against a possible Northwest mechanics strike.

1076269.abstract: Jamie describes Mazie's 2-month checkup with a pediatrician recommended by neighbors, noting measurements of 97th percentile height and weight, 75th percentile head circumference, 24 inches, and 13 lbs 1 oz. Mazie receives four single-dose, mercury-free vaccines and cries briefly before calming.

1076270.abstract: Jamie shares a note sent to Minneapolis Mayor R.T. Rybak suggesting the city pursue Bicycle Friendly Community designation from the League of American Bicyclists, noting Chicago recently received this status and Minnetonka's Mayor Anderson previously declined to pursue it. Jamie invites readers to send their own notes to Rybak.

1076271.abstract: Jamie describes daughter Mazie approaching the 8-week mark and an upcoming 2-month appointment, noting weight gain over 12 pounds, increased smiling and interaction, spit-up, and Mazie's strength standing while supported. The post includes a linked photo collection, including two pictures of Jamie asleep with Mazie.

1076272.abstract: Jamie describes having front-yard landscaping redone by native plant firm Go Native, noting native plants are lower maintenance though the first year focuses on root establishment. Jamie shares photos of bees, an American Goldfinch, and a swallowtail butterfly visiting the new native flowers.

1076273.abstract: Jamie finishes reading J.K. Rowling's "Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince," moving through it faster than "Order of the Phoenix." Jamie considers it a favorite in the series, noting it sets up the anticipated final book rather than following the previous finite story structure.

1076274.abstract: Jamie and Tammy Thingelstad, with dog Mazie, return to the Uptown Art Fair after a preview visit, noting favorite artists including John Sumner, Edward Holland, Liang Wei, and Jay Long, plus a purse by Laura Maclay and an annual painting purchase from Keith Grace.

1076276.abstract: Jamie describes upgrading from a Canon Digital Rebel (300D) to a Canon 20D with the 17-85mm USM IS lens, purchased at National Camera despite earlier insistence on waiting for a camera without a focal length multiplier like the Canon 1Ds Mark II.

1076277.abstract: Jamie and Tammy Thingelstad attend the Uptown Art Fair in Minneapolis, a longtime anniversary tradition, and note more vendors and food (including an Avon tent and Court TV) crowding out art this year, worrying it could follow Taste of Minnesota's decline.

1076278.abstract: Jamie describes breaking the .Text blogging platform after heavily customizing its open-source code, causing an exception when editing published posts. An update narrows the bug: posts created in Firefox rather than Internet Explorer can't be reopened for editing, a problem Jamie decides to tolerate for now.

1076279.abstract: Jamie discovers del.icio.us, a social bookmark manager that uses a tagging system similar to Flickr and lets users see bookmarks tagged by others with similar interests. Jamie adds the last ten items tagged on del.icio.us to the website's right-hand navigation bar.

1076280.abstract: Jamie and Tammy's wife Tammy celebrate an anniversary dinner at 20-21, the new asian-fusion restaurant in the Walker Art Center with a menu by chef Wolfgang Puck. Jamie describes attentive staff, family-style dishes including a marinated iron steak, and a chocolate dessert inspired by the sculpture garden's cherry sculpture.

1076281.abstract: Jamie reflects on the Space Shuttle Discovery's Return to Flight launch, recalling childhood dreams of becoming an astronaut, memories of the Challenger disaster, and a visit to Cape Canaveral after the Columbia disaster. Jamie praises NASA while noting spaceflight remains inherently risky, not risk-free.

1076282.abstract: Jamie describes Mazie approaching six weeks old, noting the milestone of a developing immune system after weeks of breast milk, improving head control, inconsistent sleep patterns with loud grunting, and a new bout of spitting up.

1076283.abstract: Jamie reflects on the 2005 Tour de France, praising Lance Armstrong's dominant, strategic win and the unprecedented gesture of letting Armstrong speak at the podium ceremony, while announcing plans to retire a Livestrong bracelet.

1076284.abstract: Jamie describes bicycle commuting to work for about a month, motivated partly by losing weight gained while Tammy was pregnant with Mazie. Jamie details the bike path route, the satisfaction of passing stalled traffic on highway 100, and benefits including mood, money saved on gas and tolls, and exercise.

1076285.abstract: Jamie describes finding BabyCenter.com content aimed at dads that highlights hiking as a baby activity, leading to a mention of Grateful Dads, a San Francisco group where fathers hike monthly with young children. Jamie expresses interest in organizing similar dad/baby hikes once Mazie is a bit older.

1076287.abstract: Jamie describes getting into remote control cars about five years earlier, buying an HPI Racing RS4 MT electric model and an HPI RTR Nitro RS4 gas model, then setting the unfinished gas car aside for over four years.

1076288.abstract: Jamie shares a discovery that Creedence Clearwater Revival's "Chronicle I" makes the best music for mowing the lawn, recommending it as a weekly companion for the task via iPod.

1076289.abstract: Jamie celebrates George Hincapie's first Tour de France stage win, achieved on the demanding "Queen's Stage" after a long breakaway that came down to Hincapie and Oscar Pereiro. Jamie notes Hincapie's friendship with Lance Armstrong and hopes Hincapie will someday also win Paris-Roubaix.

1076290.abstract: Jamie reviews Bill Bryson's "A Walk in the Woods," describing it as an account of Bryson's attempt to hike the 2,175-mile Appalachian Trail with friend Katz. Jamie calls Bryson very funny and highly recommends the book, admitting to rereading it despite a long unread list, and expresses interest in someday hiking the trail.

1076291.abstract: Jamie describes discovering that Windows Media Player visualizations, set to random rotation with Mozart playing, captivate 1-month-old daughter Mazie, who watches intently and reacts to screen changes and flute passages while sitting on the couch during an evening feeding.

1076292.abstract: Jamie describes the EarthRoamer, an off-road RV built on a Ford F-450 turbo diesel, noting solar and engine-based power with no generator and BioDiesel capability. Jamie's wife Tammy found it in a magazine, and Jamie emails the company asking about Internet access, imagining trips to Moab or Alaska.

1076293.abstract: Jamie describes upgrading the blog, which runs on the discontinued .Text engine rather than its successor Community Server, citing a converter tool by Kevin Harder but deciding to wait for a possible 2.0 release.

1076294.abstract: Jamie marks Mazie's one-month birthday, noting growth since coming home from the hospital, easing panic, and new milestones like babysitting solo while Jamie's wife Tammy shops. Jamie describes struggles introducing a bottle and pacifier and shares photos from the past three weeks.

1076295.abstract: Jamie describes Mazie's first three weeks, noting increased crying "exercise," good sleep helped by swaddling and a "heartbeat" CD, and jokes about lulling her to sleep by talking about computers, telescopes, and Road Sign Math.

1076296.abstract: Jamie comments on the early stages of the Tour de France, noting that Lance Armstrong's Discovery team (formerly US Postal) looks like one of the best ever assembled, highlighting Armstrong's strong individual time trial performance and recent sprint finishes.

1076297.abstract: Jamie describes a quiet Independence Day at home with a barbecue of bison burgers and baked beans, opting out of fireworks since Mazie is just under three weeks old, and mentions Stillwater's fireworks. The post includes two photos: an American flag near a highway exit sign and a woman in a stars-and-stripes skirt shopping.

1076298.abstract: Jamie reflects on the eve of the 92nd Tour de France, describing cycling as a favorite sport and Lance Armstrong as a major reason for that fandom.

1076299.abstract: Jamie recounts another power outage, this one starting at 4:04 pm and returning fitfully around 6:30 pm, and expresses frustration at not understanding why these outages happen so often.

1076300.abstract: Jamie describes installing an add-on requiring a validation code before comments can be submitted, aiming to block spammers, and acknowledges the code can be inconvenient or hard to read.

1076301.abstract: Jamie recounts early parenting worries with newborn Mazie, noting basic crises have passed as she gains weight and her belly button heals, replaced by concerns over her being too hot or too cold.

1076302.abstract: Jamie describes a surge in trackback spam reaching hundreds per day from many unique IP addresses, likely spread via spyware, which prevents blocking at the router level.

1076303.abstract: Jamie recounts the first week with newborn Mazie, describing early worries with Jamie's wife Tammy over dirty diapers, warmth, and the umbilical stump, followed by a first "crisis free" day.

1076304.abstract: Jamie reflects on the first four days of new daughter Mazie's life, describing feeding and sleep patterns and sharing observations on becoming a father, including how easy tasks prove simple while comforting a crying baby at night proves difficult, and how protective instincts and fragility fears quickly give way to comfort holding the newborn.

1076305.abstract: Jamie describes commissioning a painting titled "New Addition" from artist Amy Lynn Stevenson to celebrate the birth of a baby, choosing art over the traditional post-delivery gift of jewelry. The 5-foot by 3-foot piece depicts a man and woman with a newborn, and Jamie's wife Tammy is pleased with it; Jamie hopes to someday give it to Mazie.

1076306.abstract: Jamie announces the birth of Mazie Kaye Thingelstad on June 14th at 3:17 pm, weighing 7 lbs 11 oz and measuring 21 inches long, noting both baby and mom are doing well after delivery.

1076307.abstract: Jamie describes setting up Snort for network intrusion detection on a Fedora box, logging alerts to MySQL and reviewing them with BASE, and notes persistent SQL Slammer and Code Red traffic plus repeated ICMP pings from hammurabi.acc.umu.se.

1076308.abstract: Jamie explains that thingelstad.com was down for 21 hours and 26 minutes after a severe storm with winds exceeding 70 mph knocked out power. Jamie shares a graph of the outage and mentions considering buying a generator to keep essentials, including internet service, running during future outages.

1076309.abstract: Jamie reports a midwife check-up showing the baby healthy but overdue, four days past the due date. A follow-up visit and ultrasound are planned for Monday, with induction set for Thursday if labor hasn't started.

1076310.abstract: Jamie sets up a Roku M1000 wireless music player, from rokulabs.com, in the baby's room to stream digitally stored music for both parents and the kid. Jamie calls setup nearly instant, rates it among the best products ever purchased, and considers replacing an existing Audiotron with another unit.

1076311.abstract: Jamie describes installing a PhatNoise PhatBox digital media player into an Audi A6 wagon, with help from friend Chris, despite the unit being designed for Volkswagen and requiring a custom cable connector, a blown fuse, and cutting into the steel frame.

1076312.abstract: Jamie reports that a poll on thingelstad.com predicting the baby's delivery date proved inaccurate, with 58% expecting arrival by the due date. Jamie's wife Tammy is eager for the pregnancy to end, and Jamie describes rushing to finish projects while planning only day by day.

1076313.abstract: Jamie recounts attempting to repair "the Christmas Bell," a battery-powered musical decoration that had been a fixture at Jamie's grandparents' farm for years, surviving falls, taping, and a soldering repair by an uncle.

1076314.abstract: Jamie describes wife Tammy's largest mosaic project yet, a 32" by 50" tree design created to cover a hole left after Jamie's mother removed a kitchen window during a remodel. The piece took about 50 hours over two weeks, and Jamie helped install and grout it since Tammy is pregnant.

1076315.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy see Star Wars Episode III at the DLP digital theater at Eden Prairie AMC, finding the movie better than expected despite minor complaints about the droid general. Jamie hopes George Lucas eventually makes episodes seven through nine, and mentions anticipating War of the Worlds and Chronicles of Narnia.

1076316.abstract: Jamie describes spending weeks setting up SNMP monitoring on a home network using MRTG, calling it harder than expected but useful for tracking gateway traffic. Jamie notes an oddity where different CPUs appear under different OIDs across separate Windows Server 2003 installations.

1076317.abstract: Jamie attends a New Dads Class (still preferring the name Daddy Boot Camp) at North Memorial, joining other expectant fathers to learn baby swaddling, diaper changing, and watch a video on Shaken Baby Syndrome.

1076318.abstract: Jamie describes getting a MnPASS transponder and using it for the first time on the "sane-lane" on Highway 100 into downtown, paying $0.25 and noting the account was debited almost instantly.

1076319.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy and Jamie attend a breastfeeding class at North Memorial, which Jamie initially questioned attending but finds informative. Jamie also plans to take the Baby Boot Camp class for dads that weekend.

1076320.abstract: Jamie describes building out a home server rack, an APC NetShelter VX 25U, installed in the basement laundry room to house growing server capacity.

1076321.abstract: Jamie highlights National Bike-to-Work Week, linking to bike-to-work.com, and encourages readers to dust off their bikes and ride to the office, noting plans to bike to work most of that week.

1076322.abstract: Jamie recounts a frantic morning in Manhattan after discovering the only dress slacks packed for a business meeting no longer fit. After failed attempts at Macy's and Banana Republic, a hotel concierge locates a store that opens early, letting Jamie buy Dockers and a belt and reach the meeting on time.

1076323.abstract: Jamie describes struggling to finish Bad Leadership by Barbara Kellerman, published by Harvard Business School Press, finding the book's premise sound but padded with excessive examples, and eventually decides to abandon it unfinished.

1076324.abstract: Jamie describes flying Northwest Airlines from Minneapolis (MSP) to New York's LaGuardia (LGA) on an Airbus 320, missing an upgrade despite full fare due to platinum elite frequent flyer priority on the popular route.

1076325.abstract: Jamie describes enabling HTTP compression on ASPX pages, achieving roughly 4:1 compression, and links to instructions for editing the IIS6 metabase to make it work. Jamie also moves Road Sign Math to its own server and enables compression there.

1076326.abstract: Jamie expresses concern about Google Web Accelerator, a Google Labs product that routes all web browsing through Google's servers to speed up page loading via compression and prefetching.

1076327.abstract: Jamie recounts seeing the new Broadway production of Glengarry Glen Ross at the Royale Theatre, starring Alan Alda as Shelley Levine, after dinner at Carmine's with coworkers.

1076328.abstract: Jamie reviews Mac OS 10.4 (Tiger) after upgrading an iMac G5, calling the installation easy but the upgrade underwhelming, comparing its search feature unfavorably to X1 on Windows. Jamie criticizes Apple's annual paid-upgrade model and marketing hype, questioning whether $100 is justified given minimal visible changes.

1076329.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy attend the Living Green Expo at the Minnesota State Fairgrounds, marking their third visit to the event's fourth year. Jamie notes the expo moved into the grandstand this year, expanded substantially, and drew record attendance, with exhibitors running out of materials.

1076330.abstract: Jamie recounts upgrading a DirecTV satellite setup to a triple-LNB dish after adding an HD TiVo, describing three separate technician visits and repeated rescheduling problems, including a botched installation that knocked out satellite C entirely.

1076331.abstract: Jamie marks Jamie's wife Tammy's birthday, noting that Tammy treats birthdays as a much bigger occasion than Jamie does, and closes with an original birthday haiku.

1076332.abstract: Jamie attends the one-day course "Presenting Data and Information" taught by Edward Tufte, after colleagues recommended it, and comes away impressed by both Tufte's expertise on data visualization and speaking style, recommending the session to anyone who gives presentations.

1076333.abstract: Jamie describes taking mosaic classes with Jamie's wife Tammy and visiting Mosaic On A Stick, a shop that opened about six months earlier selling mosaic supplies, teaching classes, and offering open workspace time for a fixed fee. Jamie recommends trying mosaics.

1076334.abstract: Jamie shares an email from a former coworker who launched a baby-carrier business and website, Attached to Baby, where the coworker also models products. Jamie praises the entrepreneurial effort and mentions needing to choose a baby carrier before the couple's own baby arrives.

1076335.abstract: Jamie describes being in week 35 of Jamie's wife Tammy's pregnancy, noting visible movement from the baby including reaching, punching and kicking, and remarks that the due date is approaching.

1076336.abstract: Jamie describes deploying a home intranet application using OpenWiki, restricted to household access with authentication, to organize scattered notes like cable modem details, network information, trip reminders, and service contract numbers. Jamie names the site Spiral, likening it to a shared spiral notebook for the household.

1076337.abstract: Jamie and Tammy work through choosing a name for a child and Jamie finds the responsibility significant. A friend points Jamie to NameVoyager, a Java application at babynamewizard.com that visualizes how names' popularity has changed over time, which Jamie recommends trying.

1076338.abstract: Jamie describes setting up a Windows Scheduled Task using blat.exe to send monthly email reminders, prompted by trouble remembering to change heater filters. A screenshot shows tasks for both a heater filter and sprinkler system reminder, next scheduled for 5/1/2005.

1076339.abstract: Jamie shares selected photos from a trip to New Mexico and Colorado, originally hosted in an nGallery album now archived on archive.org.

1076340.abstract: Jamie buys a Sony VAIO VGN-S360 laptop at a Ballio's electronics store during a trip, drawn by rebate pricing despite reservations about Sony's software-based controls for brightness and volume. Jamie plans to use the 80GB drive for astronomy software and Photoshop work, replacing a four-year-old Fujitsu S-4542.

1076341.abstract: Jamie recaps a vacation with wife Tammy through Santa Fe, Albuquerque, and Denver, mentioning a dinner at NoRTH restaurant, the Albuquerque Aquarium and Botanic Garden, Great Sand Dunes National Park, Cherry Creek galleries including Art Z!, and the Denver Zoo, while battling cold weather and a bad cold before the drive home.

1076342.abstract: Jamie describes a final night of stargazing at Star Hill, marked by erratic weather including snow, sun, and wind gusts over 40 mph that made CCD imaging with Phil impossible.

1076343.abstract: Jamie describes a night of stargazing at Star Hill Inn near Las Vegas, NM, with owner Phil, using a Meade LX200GPS 12" telescope to view Saturn, Jupiter, the Orion Nebulae, binary stars and galaxies before ending the evening with Boggle at the cabin with Tammy.

1076344.abstract: Jamie recounts a day trip through northern New Mexico from Las Vegas, NM to Taos and Santa Fe, noting worries about altitude given Tammy's pregnancy and dealing with caked mud on the car's wheels from the previous day's incident.

1076345.abstract: Jamie describes a road trip taking nearly 14 hours to reach Denver's Cherry Creek North area, en route to the Star Hill Inn in New Mexico, with plans to stop for breakfast at Eggshell before continuing. Jamie also mentions playing Road Sign Math during the drive, finding it harder than expected.

1076346.abstract: Jamie reviews David Laskin's book The Children's Blizzard, about the January 12, 1888 storm that killed hundreds of schoolchildren across the plains. Jamie compares it favorably to Norman MacLean's Young Men and Fire, noting both authors' skill at making weather details gripping, and recommends reading it in winter.

1076347.abstract: Jamie shares a haiku about spotting numerical patterns while driving, linking to the site Road Sign Math as an example of enjoying math found on road signs.

1076348.abstract: Jamie describes a kitchen iMac G5 that suddenly stopped turning on, even after bypassing a recently installed UPS. After using Apple's diagnostic instructions, Jamie takes it to FirstTech, which confirms a dead power supply, but Apple has no replacement parts in stock and no ETA, prompting Jamie to criticize Apple's recurring supply chain problems.

1076349.abstract: Jamie describes receiving a flier from the League of American Bicyclists (LAB) about its Bicycling Friendly Community program and shares a letter sent to Minnetonka's Mayor Anderson.

1076350.abstract: Jamie describes upgrading home power backup after recurring under-voltage events and outages, replacing an undersized APC Back-UPS Pro 650 with a Smart-UPS 1500VA RM rackmount unit for the terabyte server, planning a future half-rack setup.

1076351.abstract: Jamie describes resolving a bank error with USBank after noticing a plumber's check cleared for $158.95 instead of the $138.95 entered in Quicken.

1076352.abstract: Jamie replaces a failing SMC 8508T gigabit switch, detailed in an earlier post about "trouble in gig," with a NetGear GS716T after evaluating options for price and manageability.

1076353.abstract: Jamie describes attending the first session of a 6-week Introduction to Child Birth class with Tammy's wife Tammy at North Memorial, covering the Empathy Belly exercise, a birth video, group question lists, and the realization that most couples aren't using a midwife or know what a doula is.

1076354.abstract: Jamie criticizes a "Dad Tip" from the book Your Pregnancy Week by Week, which suggests fathers "may" want to take time off after a baby's birth, calling the advice outdated for a 2004, fifth-edition publication.

1076355.abstract: Jamie describes spending a day with Tammy registering for a baby shower, first at USA Baby then at Babies-R-Us, where scanning items proves fun but choosing among bottles, bassinets, and other gear leaves both overwhelmed. A friend recommends the book Baby Bargains, which Jamie and Tammy buy at Barnes & Noble for guidance.

1076356.abstract: Jamie recounts attempting to fix a clogged kitchen sink shortly before dinner guests arrived, using a clothes hanger and a miniature plumber's snake before loosening a bolt that turned out to hold the drain onto the sink, causing water to gush onto the floor and seep downstairs onto a desk and iPod.

1076357.abstract: Jamie recounts frustrations from a coach flight during a business trip, including a cramped laptop nearly crushed by a reclining seat, being hit twice by the beverage cart, and a neighbor's laptop damaged the same way. Jamie argues airlines should ban reclining in coach and criticizes the industry for poor customer comfort despite full flights.

1076358.abstract: Jamie writes an informal update covering the launch of Road Sign Math, an upcoming road trip to Colorado and New Mexico that includes a stargazing-focused B&B stay, a viewing of the movie Hitch starring Kevin James, and new CD purchases from Green Day and Willie Nelson, praising both albums.

1076359.abstract: Jamie highlights TV-B-Gone, a keychain remote that broadcasts over 200 shutoff codes covering hundreds of TV manufacturers, priced at $14.99, and jokes about using it in sports bars to turn off annoying televisions.

1076360.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy declares herself "officially pregnant" at 26 weeks, and Jamie describes a midwife checkup that includes a gestational diabetes test, which comes back normal. Measurements are on track, a late-March trip gets approval, and childbirth classes begin in two weeks.

1076361.abstract: Jamie recounts an overnight trip to Iowa City with Jamie's wife Tammy to visit friends over a long weekend. Jamie describes disliking college towns generally, noise from other guests at the Fairfield Inn, dinner with Lisa and Eric at One Twenty Six, and breakfast at Lou Henri's with Dan and Mel, praising the 7-grain pancakes and bike discount.

1076362.abstract: Jamie announces the launch of Road Sign Math, a driving game website developed after long deliberation, describing the project as pure geek joy and predicting it will spread nationwide.

1076363.abstract: Jamie presents a theory that the feeling of time speeding up with age is mathematically explainable: since each year represents an ever-smaller fraction of total life lived, later years feel shorter than earlier ones, and a decade at 40-50 equals the same percentage of life as the single year from age 4 to 5.

1076364.abstract: Jamie reacts to Lance Armstrong's appearance with Sheryl Crow on Oprah, covering topics like Armstrong's record Tour de France wins, the popularity of LIVESTRONG bracelets (46 million sold), a wish for Armstrong to retire from Tour racing in favor of events like the spring classics or hour record, criticism of OLN's declining non-Tour coverage…

1076365.abstract: Jamie announces a domain transfer of thingelstad.com away from Register.com, citing high prices, a slow interface, and inability to create an SPF record. Jamie moves the domain to GoDaddy, praising its low cost, speed, and technical capability.

1076366.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy see the late matinee of Million Dollar Baby, a film Jamie describes as the story of a woman's persistent pursuit of a dream to become a boxer. Jamie calls the movie a tear jerker, noting Tammy nearly cried and warns pregnant women should beware.

1076367.abstract: Jamie compares how Microsoft and Apple communicate security patches, noting Microsoft's monthly releases use scary, detailed language like "malicious" while Apple's MacOS X 10.3.8 update is vague, omitting mention of the dozens of security fixes it contains.

1076369.abstract: Jamie switches to SquirrelMail after trying hMailServer the previous day, despite a general belief that PHP and Windows don't mix well. Jamie reports an easy installation with several working plugins and finds SquirrelMail a solid webmail client.

1076370.abstract: Jamie switches home email service from Xmail to hMailServer, citing hMail's easier configuration and IMAP support, which Xmail lacked. Jamie reports a smooth transition and recommends hMail for anyone needing an easy-to-setup Windows mail server.

1076371.abstract: Jamie describes taking advantage of unseasonably warm February weather in Minnesota for a 17-mile bike ride down to the lakes and back, noting many other cyclists were out too, though the lower body got cold without leg warmers or booties.

1076372.abstract: Jamie describes feeling the baby kick for the first time, after Jamie's wife Tammy had noticed flutters for a couple of weeks. Tammy calls this kick strong, though Jamie only senses a slight movement.

1076373.abstract: Jamie describes rebuilding the thingelstad.com terabyte server after it went down over the weekend, restructuring the RAID setup on the 3ware Escalade 8506-8 card into a RAID1 mirror for boot, app and data volumes plus an 800G RAID5 export volume, adding two more drives and a hard-mounted hot spare.

1076374.abstract: Jamie criticizes books aimed at expectant fathers, calling much of their advice obvious or condescending and noting they're often reduced to list formats like "101 things" rather than real prose. Jamie recommends blogs instead, naming Daddy Types and Laid-Off Dad, and singles out "The Baby Owner's Manual" as a worthwhile book.

1076375.abstract: Jamie compares two HD OTA antennas, the Terk HDTVs and the ChannelMaster 4221, using signal readings from a DirecTV TiVo HR10-250 in the Minneapolis area near highways 494 and 62. Jamie finds the cheaper Terk performs comparably to the $35 CM4221, even outperforming it on weaker stations like KMWB and KPXM, though the CM4221 is more directional.

1076376.abstract: Jamie describes a second ultrasound appointment showing significant growth over eight weeks, with the baby moving actively and appearing healthy, including visible individual heart chambers.

1076377.abstract: Jamie describes setting up a new Sharp Aquos LC-45GD4U flat-panel LCD TV, pairing it with a DirecTV HD TiVo unit and a Terk HTDVs outdoor antenna for over-the-air HD channels. Jamie lists signal strength readings for ten local stations and notes readiness to watch the Vikings/Packers game in HD.

1076378.abstract: Jamie withdraws an earlier endorsement of the MacMice 2-button wheel mouse for Mac, citing slow wake-up from sleep mode and occasional choppy, unpredictable movement, and now keeps both it and the Apple mouse on the desk.

1076379.abstract: Jamie describes celebrating a birthday with a trip to Spider Lake Lodge near Hayward, WI, where lack of snow led to Boggle and watching the Lemony Snicket movie instead of skiing. Jamie's wife Tammy gave a Meade LX200GPS 8" telescope with UHTC coating, prompting renewed interest in astronomy and plans to observe Saturn at opposition.

1076380.abstract: Jamie recounts a two-day Fargo visit with Tammy, split between a suburban day and a downtown day. Suburban activities include West Acres Mall, lunch at a struggling Taste of India, dinner at Happy Joes, and browsing Barnes & Noble; downtown activities include the Plains Art Museum, Babb's coffee shop, a haircut, and watching The Machinist at the…

1076381.abstract: Jamie provides a pregnancy update on Jamie's wife Tammy, describing a midwife appointment where the baby's heartbeat was heard for the first time. Jamie and Tammy are skipping most screening tests due to high false positive rates and plan an ultrasound in a couple weeks to learn the baby's sex.

1076382.abstract: Jamie notes the earthquake and tsunami's scale feels hard to grasp, then highlights Amazon's one-click donation feature for the Red Cross, which has raised $7.6 million. Jamie contrasts this with the $35 million pledged by the US government, hoping that figure increases.

1076383.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy gives Jamie a Panasonic PV-GS400 digital camcorder for Christmas, a 3CCD unit that also shoots 4 megapixel stills. Jamie calls it a first "Dad Gift" and lists other presents including Logitech wireless Xbox controllers, a poker chip set, and Six Feet Under Season 2.

1076384.abstract: Jamie describes taking time off after the holidays and traveling with Tammy to Fargo, North Dakota, building the trip around the Hotel Donaldson downtown. Jamie details the "Big Dog" suite's amenities, including 17-foot ceilings, hardwood floors, a separate living room, and WiFi, calling the cost less than typical business travel lodging.

1076385.abstract: Jamie describes trying to win a 25% discount coupon for the Dell 2005FPW monitor through Dell's coupon game, only ever winning printer discounts instead. Jamie finds Dell coupon codes for sale on eBay, buys one for $2, and orders the monitor, saving over $200.

1076386.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy and Jamie begin a Christmas trip, driving to Minot, ND, then continuing to Jamie's grandparents' farm outside Lignite, ND, for a family visit. Jamie notes another year without holiday cards or a letter but hopes to send them next year.

1076387.abstract: Jamie describes finishing "In Code" by Sarah Flannery, a book about Flannery's love of mathematics and the public key cryptography algorithm she built as a high school student, which challenged RSA before being found vulnerable to attack. Jamie recommends it for girls interested in math.

1076389.abstract: Jamie describes buying a two-button Bluetooth mouse with a scroll wheel from MacMice to use with a recently purchased iMac G5, calling Apple's single-button mouse a serious shortcoming despite otherwise strong hardware and OS.

1076390.abstract: Jamie describes a failure of the SMC 8508-T gigabit switch at home, installed after a February upgrade to Gig E, which stopped working for all gigabit devices one night.

1076391.abstract: Jamie describes rediscovering the googol (1.0 × 10^100) while reading about natural numbers and primes, including Sierpinski numbers, which Jamie is helping search for via seventeenorbust.com.

1076392.abstract: Jamie mentions reading a book on cryptography and searching online about prime numbers, leading to discovery of the Seventeen or Bust project, which allows participation by running a client.

1076393.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy and Tammy's two sisters with their significant others see Ocean's Twelve. Jamie, having enjoyed Ocean's Eleven, finds the sequel fine but not as good, noting the soundtrack and cinematography stand out more than the story, and plans to check out the soundtrack once available.

1076394.abstract: Jamie describes reading Dan Brown's novel The Da Vinci Code with intense speed, comparing the experience only to reading the Dune series, though not ranking it as highly. Jamie calls it a page-turner and an enjoyable read, deliberately withholding story details to preserve surprise for others.
