1076395.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a weekend of Christmas decorating, including a house lit with white lights along the roofline and red and green ground lights, plus a decorated tree indoors with red ornaments and a Santa figurine.

1076396.abstract: Jamie recounts learning about Thomas Frank's book What's the Matter With Kansas? from The Daily Show after the presidential election, then reading it and finding it a great read.

1076397.abstract: Jamie recommends the movie Finding Neverland, seen at a packed matinee, praising Johnny Depp's performance in this story about the making of Peter Pan. Jamie notes a sad, heartfelt ending that left few dry eyes in the theater.

1076398.abstract: Jamie recounts a computer history starting with the TI-99/4A and Apple //c through Fat Mac, Macintosh IIc, Unix and Windows NT, then describes buying a 20-inch iMac G5 during a one-day sale, noting Mac OS X interest and plans to share re-acquaintance experiences.

1076399.abstract: Jamie and Tammy Thingelstad announce, in mock press-release style, that they are expecting their first child in June 2005. The post describes an ultrasound at 13 weeks showing a healthy fetus, and includes reactions from both sets of first-time grandparents, including Kaye Olson, Rosalin Chrest and Don Olson.

1076400.abstract: Jamie describes a "change game" invented with wife Tammy, where the goal is to use spare change so a cash transaction leaves no coins in pocket.

1076401.abstract: Jamie shares photos and notes from an Xbox modding session involving circuit boards and soldering work, crediting Chris for the soldering and thanking Chris and Chad for help. The hardware operation succeeds on the first try, leaving software work still to come.

1076402.abstract: Jamie reviews Mary Roach's book Stiff: The Curious Lives of Human Cadavers, describing it as strange but engaging once past the initial unsettling detail. Jamie highlights the chapters on ecological burial and cross-cultural treatment of human remains as most interesting, and notes finding pre-1900 cadaver practices alarming.

1076403.abstract: Jamie links to breaking news that Dow Jones is acquiring MarketWatch, noting the deal is still very early with many open questions, but calls it great news on multiple fronts.

1076404.abstract: Jamie recounts seeing Jay Farrar perform at the Cedar Cultural Center after the show was moved from First Avenue following its shutdown, noting the smaller venue's smoke-free, intimate atmosphere.

1076405.abstract: Jamie describes a chaotic incident at home when Jamie's wife Tammy tied the wrist strap of a Canon Digital Elph camera around their cat Gypsie's neck, causing Gypsie to panic and drag the camera through the house, ripping blinds off a window before breaking free; the camera survives with only dents.

1076406.abstract: Jamie reports progress on returning to a healthier weight, noting fewer sugar headaches and adjustment to eating four meals a day without logging food. Starting at 271.2 lbs and 29.7% body fat, Jamie aims for 232 lbs, sharing a four-and-a-half-year weight graph that peaked near 340 lbs.

1076407.abstract: Jamie describes restarting a weight-loss effort, recalling a previous goal set in 2000 to lose 100 lbs, which took about ten months and succeeded.

1076408.abstract: Jamie recounts seeing The Incredibles on opening night, choosing a later showtime to avoid crowds, though Tammy fell asleep. Jamie praises Pixar's animation progress since Toy Story and finds the story fun, longer than expected at 105 minutes, and recommends it.

1076409.abstract: Jamie describes driving 360 miles from home to Milwaukee with Tammy to see Ira Glass of This American Life perform at the Pabst Theater, staying at the Wyndham hotel and having dinner with Tammy's family friend Jennifer McDaniel.

1076410.abstract: Jamie reviews Bill Bryson's "A Short History of Nearly Everything," noting it's less funny than Bryson's other books but still interesting, covering topics from Earth's formation to cellular biology. Jamie highlights facts about Yellowstone's volcano, sudden plane drops, and the inventor of both CFCs and leaded gasoline.

1076411.abstract: Jamie reports that First Avenue, the Minneapolis music venue, has closed its doors, recalling fun evenings spent there in the 90s and expressing hope it returns.

1076412.abstract: Jamie shares a recipe for Wassail Tea, listing ingredients including cinnamon sticks, allspice berries, cloves, sugar, apple cider, orange juice and lemon juice, along with directions for boiling, cooling and combining them, noting the tea tastes better with repeated reheating.

1076413.abstract: Jamie reviews the movie Friday Night Lights, comparing it to a mix of Hoosiers and Any Given Sunday, citing the unrealistic but fun action shots and a familiar alcoholic-father subplot, while finding the film entertaining overall.

1076414.abstract: Jamie recounts changing 15 household clocks for Daylight Savings Time, including digital cameras, two Philips Pronto remote controls, a Polar wristwatch, microwave, oven, phones and roughly 10 standard clocks. Jamie notes only computers and the TiVo adjust automatically, and dislikes DST mainly for disrupting sleep.

1076415.abstract: Jamie and Tammy volunteer at the Circus Juventas Boo Ball, an adult event, ending up directing arrivals into will-call, cash, or credit-card lines. Jamie notes costumes ranged from unthemed for men to revealing for women, and describes later guests struggling to answer simple questions after drinking.

1076416.abstract: Jamie buys an Xbox after previously vowing not to purchase another game console following costly experiences with the Dreamcast and 3DO. Jamie explains the appeal is modifiability, citing mod chips, a 200G hard drive upgrade, and the Xbox Media Center for streaming files, and plans to install a mod chip soon.

1076417.abstract: Jamie watches a 60 Minutes segment on electronic voting and argues the software these systems run sounds insecure and poorly built. Jamie suggests open source would make sense for such systems and calls the companies behind them pathetic.

1076418.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy see an advance screening of I Heart Huckabees at the Uptown Theatre before its general release, calling the existential-detective comedy odd but highly recommended, and mention receiving free promotional t-shirts.

1076419.abstract: Jamie describes a weekend at Grand Superior Lodge near Two Harbors, MN, marking the first Olson family vacation with Tammy's family.

1076420.abstract: Jamie reviews David Lebedoff's book "The Uncivil War: How a New Elite Is Destroying Our Democracy," received via a law firm's invitation to a discussion group.

1076421.abstract: Jamie describes seeing a sneak preview of Team America, the puppet-filmed movie from the creators of South Park, thanks to Chad. Jamie finds the puppet fight scenes funny and the political overtones humorous, but suggests waiting to catch it on video rather than paying for theater tickets.

1076422.abstract: Jamie and Tammy attend Rob Becker's show "Defending the Caveman," which Jamie had heard was funny and found made for 100 minutes of hard laughter, recommending it to others with the chance to see it.

1076424.abstract: Jamie describes watching Jamie's wife Tammy complete the TC10 (Shortcut to the Capital), the sister race to the Twin Cities Marathon, as the longest run Tammy had attempted, finishing despite knee pain that started a few miles in and averaging just under 10-minute miles.

1076425.abstract: Jamie describes buying a Dyson DC07 Animal upright vacuum, a bagless turbine model, and reports that three passes in one room removed enough cat hair to fill a half-gallon milk jug. Jamie recommends the Animal to anyone with pets, praising its purple design and easy dirt-canister emptying.

1076426.abstract: Jamie recounts seeing Napoleon Dynamite with Tammy, finding the movie stupid with dull characters and few laughs, comparing it to a Ween album but less interesting. Jamie also complains about teenagers using cell phones during the film, while noting Tammy and critics rated the movie more favorably.

1076427.abstract: Jamie recounts catching the Harry Potter series three years earlier and reading the first four books quickly, then pre-ordering Order of the Phoenix on Amazon.com. Despite a six-month pause partway through the nearly 900-page book, Jamie finishes it, calls it a great read, and looks forward to the next installment, Half Blood Prince.

1076428.abstract: Jamie follows up on an earlier "Expose of the Hot Air Balloon Industry" post, reporting that Aamodt's Hot Air Balloons has gone out of business after repeatedly postponing scheduled flights.

1076429.abstract: Jamie links to a Minot Daily News profile of grandfather Chet (Chester) Ringwall, an 80-year-old farmer near Columbus, North Dakota, covering decades raising turkeys and sheep, Prohibition-era liquor-running stories, and changes in farming. Jamie recalls childhood memories of the farm and reflects on a disappearing rural way of life.

1076430.abstract: Jamie and Tammy watch the movie The Forgotten, finding it moderately entertaining but not worth a big effort to see, comparing its theme to Dark City and noting several shocking, jump-inducing scenes.

1076431.abstract: Jamie analyzes spider activity logs on thingelstad.com and finds MSN Robot hitting the site over 20,000 times, roughly four times more than Googlebot, the next most frequent spider at around 5,000 hits. Jamie questions why MSN's crawler is so excessive.

1076432.abstract: Jamie notes that Thunderbird, the email client Jamie switched to from Microsoft Outlook, has released version 0.8 with newly added RSS support, providing an integrated RSS reader for home use.

1076433.abstract: Jamie shares an official announcement from JayFarrar.net that Son Volt—Jay Farrar, Dave Boquist, Jim Boquist and Mike Heidorn—is reuniting after a five-year hiatus to record a fourth album at Farrar's St. Louis studio, with a webcam offering glimpses of the sessions starting October 1. Jamie calls it unexpected, exciting music news.

1076434.abstract: Jamie recaps the 2004 Fat 40 mountain bike race in Wisconsin, finishing in 4:41:32 after bonking from under-eating on the muddy, difficult course. Jamie praises the new Specialized M4 Stumpjumper FSR Elite and notes brother-in-law Dennis Daily beat Jamie's time by over seven minutes in Dennis's rookie ride.

1076435.abstract: Jamie describes signing up with Jamie's wife Tammy for an eight-week introduction to meditation class at the Yoga Center of Minneapolis, finding the first session left a relaxed feeling despite difficulty quieting the mind, and mentions learning a mental chant, huang-sah.

1076436.abstract: Jamie describes winning an iPod Mini after months of deliberating over the purchase, noting a longstanding fondness for Apple dating back to the Apple //c and Macintosh. Jamie praises the packaging, simplicity, and iTunes, calling the experience "sweet" while worrying about eventually buying a 40G iPod too.

1076437.abstract: Jamie reviews The Metabolic Plan by Stephen Cherniske, recommended by friend Phil Hotchkiss, finding early chapters "overzealous" but ultimately valuable for understanding aging's catabolic effects and improving quality of life in later decades.

1076438.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy attend a Norah Jones concert at the Xcel Energy Center in St. Paul, with opener Amos Lee. Jamie finds Norah Jones better suited to studio recording or intimate venues than large arenas.

1076439.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy, along with John Murphy from Jamie's office, rides the Jesse James Century ride, part of Northfield's Defeat of Jesse James Days, marking Tammy's first-ever century ride and John's improved performance after training and losing weight.

1076440.abstract: Jamie notes that National Public Radio and Minnesota Public Radio both offer content through RSS feeds, linking to NPR's feed page and encouraging readers to subscribe to the news feeds.

1076441.abstract: Jamie describes a Labor Day weekend spent with Tammy in Lanesboro, cycling over 130 miles on the Root River & Harmony-Preston Valley State Trail, staying at Habberstad House Bed & Breakfast, and buying art by Erik Pearson at Cornucopia Art Center.

1076442.abstract: Jamie describes ongoing work tuning up the site, drawing on open source code and cut-and-paste hacking. The newest addition links to photo albums with picture highlights, using code posted by Edo van Vliet on swiftalpha.com.

1076443.abstract: Jamie researches satellite radio providers XM and Sirius ahead of an upcoming road trip, comparing them to the Dish Network versus DirecTV rivalry.

1076444.abstract: Jamie recounts a second trip of the year to the Minnesota Renaissance Festival, this time with Tracy and Jeff, describing the outing as a relaxing afternoon with cheap wine. The post includes an embedded photo collection from the visit.

1076445.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy watch the new version of The Manchurian Candidate, finding it more suspenseful than the original but missing Frank Sinatra, and notes the movie's premise feels uncomfortably close to current politics.

1076446.abstract: Jamie describes flying frequently for work without much concern until Jamie's wife Tammy, who fears flying, expressed anxiety about turbulence and crashes during a flight together. Jamie now notices wing flex and cabin movement, wondering if Tammy's phobia has become contagious.

1076447.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy watch Garden State and Jamie likes it, comparing it to Lost in Translation, Niagara, Niagara, and The Graduate. Jamie notes gaining respect for writer-director-star Zach Braff and considers buying the soundtrack.

1076448.abstract: Jamie recaps a trip to Europe in 2004, describing over 2,200 photos sorted into albums covering the Tour de France, Paris, and a hiking trip, the last captioned by Jamie's wife Tammy. Jamie also added GPS-derived maps of each hiking day, though the original photo albums and captions are no longer available online.

1076449.abstract: Jamie tries out Mozilla Thunderbird as an alternative to Outlook Express, noting adjustments needed for keyboard shortcuts and finding the news reader an improvement over Outlook's, though the overall verdict remains pending.

1076450.abstract: Jamie mentions recording heart rate data on every ride and run out of interest rather than necessity, and links to a Polar webpage showing heart rate data from riders in this year's Tour de France, noting surprise at how low their heart rates stay even on hard climbs.

1076451.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy see The Bourne Supremacy, finding it fun but less exciting than The Bourne Identity since the sequel offers fewer surprises. Jamie notes much of the film appears handheld, warning viewers prone to motion sickness.

1076452.abstract: Jamie recounts finishing a trip with Tammy, traveling from Soglio to Zurich via Zuoz to retrieve a goat sculpture, then encountering Zurich's Street Parade before flying through Amsterdam to Minneapolis and attending the Uptown Art Fair with Tammy's mother.

1076453.abstract: Jamie reviews Patrick Lencioni's business fable Death by Meeting, read during vacation, which argues most meetings lack clear purpose and proposes four distinct meeting types on different schedules.

1076454.abstract: Jamie recounts hiking from Casaccia to Soglio, Switzerland, the final day of a six-day, 63-mile trip covering 9.2 miles and 1,656 feet of ascent. Jamie describes an unattended honesty-system preserve stand, an ancient Roman road section, and Soglio's narrow medieval alleyways near the Italian border.

1076455.abstract: Jamie recounts a hiking day in Switzerland's Engadine region with a Ryder Walker group, describing group member Shirley's departure, cold and low-visibility conditions above the tree line, and an unplanned summit of Piz Lunghin with guide Annica and Jamie's wife Tammy after weather cleared.

1076456.abstract: Jamie describes a 4h58m, 11.9-mile hike from Pontresina to Sils Maria in Switzerland's Engadin valley, passing Lake Hahnensee, St. Moritz, and Lake Silvaplana. Jamie notes Tammy's photo of an edelweiss flower and mentions Switzerland's ban on picking it.

1076457.abstract: Jamie recounts hiking from Zuoz to Pontresina in Switzerland, covering 8.5 miles with 2,526 feet of ascent, riding a funicular, lunching at a crowded hut where fruchtkugen recalls childhood memories from Napoleon, North Dakota, and finishing with a long descent into Pontresina.

1076458.abstract: Jamie describes a loop hike from Zuoz to the Chamanna Des-Cha Hut in Switzerland's Engadine region, covering 9.6 miles with nearly 3,000 feet of ascent.

1076459.abstract: Jamie recounts the first day of a Ryder Walker guided hiking trip in Switzerland, hiking from a Scuol gondola through Alp Laret to Guarda, covering nearly 13 miles with 2,250' ascent. Jamie describes stunning scenery, a picnic lunch, Swiss National Day bonfires seen from the trail, and plans to ship excess luggage ahead to Zurich.

1076460.abstract: Jamie describes traveling from Zurich to Scuol, Switzerland, contrasting Zurich's multilingual, orderly feel with the mountains' German-only, less English-friendly atmosphere.

1076462.abstract: Jamie describes taking a high-speed first-class train from Paris to Zurich, praising the smooth ride, reclining seats, power connectors, and onboard breakfast, though noting no WiFi. Jamie contrasts this favorably with train travel in the U.S. and recounts brief confusion boarding with luggage, resolved with Tammy's help.

1076463.abstract: Jamie describes reading "Heft on Wheels" by Mike Magnuson, a memoir about shifting an obsession with drinking and smoking into cycling. Jamie relates personally, having lost significant weight, and notes shared experiences with Magnuson despite differing cycling abilities, expressing interest in meeting the author someday.

1076465.abstract: Jamie describes final days in Paris before heading to Switzerland, including night photography of the illuminated Eiffel Tower and Arc de Triomphe using long exposures, and buying an anniversary painting called "Allez Saute!" by artist Corniere at Art Club gallery near the Louvre.

1076466.abstract: Jamie recounts seeing "The Stepford Wives" at a movie theater in Paris, noting the theater had air conditioning this time. Jamie calls it a fun movie but suggests it's probably better to rent.

1076467.abstract: Jamie recounts a second wedding anniversary spent exploring Paris with Tammy, walking through several arrondissements, visiting La Sainte-Chapelle, Notre Dame, and the Louvre to see the Mona Lisa. The pair also stay at the Hyatt Regency Paris-Madeleine, eat at Latina Cafe and the Hard Rock Cafe, and climb the Eiffel Tower's lower level.

1076468.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy see Spiderman 2 in Paris while on vacation, finding it better than the first film. Jamie notes the English showing had French subtitles, no air conditioning, a run-down theater, and €9.50 tickets, remarking on Paris's high costs.

1076469.abstract: Jamie reflects on watching the Tour de France in person, describing the "Fin de Course" truck marking the race's end and comparing it to a movie's closing title card.

1076470.abstract: Jamie describes watching Lance Armstrong finish the 2004 Tour de France on the Champs Elysees, becoming the first cyclist to win six titles. Jamie and Tammy traveled from Beaune to Paris, struggled to find a good viewing spot in the large crowds, and watched the peloton catch a breakaway.

1076471.abstract: Jamie describes a 125km bike ride with Tammy from Beaune to Besancon during the Tour de France, riding with a fast group before dropping back to enjoy villages and a bakery stop. Jamie notes Tammy's new distance record and mentions watching Lance Armstrong win the time trial over Ullrich amid audience booing over doping suspicions.

1076472.abstract: Jamie describes riding a bus back to Paris after early mornings spent following the Tour de France, anticipating Lance Armstrong winning a record sixth title, and looks forward to more relaxed days in Paris after an exhausting travel schedule.

1076473.abstract: Jamie recounts leaving Grenoble for a two-night stay in Beaune during the 2004 Tour de France, riding bikes from the Stage 18 finish toward the 20km banner and back over a steep category climb near Annemasse and Lons-le-Saunier.

1076474.abstract: Jamie describes attempting the Col de la Madeleine climb during the 2004 Tour de France, riding about 7 km and 600 vertical meters (roughly a third of the 19.8 km ascent) before running low on water.

1076475.abstract: Jamie describes a search for cold drinks while traveling in France, noting that refrigeration seems weak there since neither water nor vending machine soda gets truly cold. Jamie tries not to seem like an "ugly American" but wishes for more ice, and mentions Jamie's wife Tammy is obsessed with water.

1076476.abstract: Jamie recounts watching Tour de France 2004 Stage 16 from Bourg d'Oisans as Lance Armstrong wins the climb to L'Alpe d'Huez, after skipping the ride due to crowds and Tammy's cold.

1076477.abstract: Jamie recounts riding stage 15 of the Tour de France near Grenoble, cycling part of the actual course including the Col de Chalimont with Tammy before watching Lance Armstrong's lead group and yellow jersey holder Thomas Voeckler pass through a village roundabout, then finishing with a difficult descent back to Grenoble.

1076478.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy arrive in Grenoble and post from a smoky Internet cafe, noting the difficulty of using a French AZERTY keyboard. Jamie mentions plans to ride the next day before signing off.

1076479.abstract: Jamie describes feeling better after a cold and preparing to fly overnight to Paris with Tammy, who is anxious about flying, bringing gear for both cycling and hiking. Jamie mentions excitement about seeing the Tour de France in person after Lance Armstrong's recent strong performances.

1076480.abstract: Jamie describes getting a cold the day before departing for Europe, blaming Chris Tersteeg for it, and details taking vitamins and medicine to recover. Bikes are boxed, bags are nearly packed, and the plan is to sleep near the Eiffel Tower the next day.

1076481.abstract: Jamie recounts entering the Chequamegon Fat Tire Festival's "Fat 40" race, a 42-mile ride Jamie has completed for three prior years, missing the lottery this time but winning entry through the "50 Ways to Ride the Chequamegon" essay contest, joining a brother-in-law also competing.

1076482.abstract: Jamie and Tammy's wife Tammy drop bikes off at Erik's Bike Shop to be packed in Trico Iron Cases for an upcoming trip to France, switching to a 12-27T cog set for climbs like Alpe d'Huez.

1076483.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy help Jamie's mother demolish the kitchen in a new house Jamie's mother has been renovating over the past year, gutting the room down to the studs. Jamie shares photos of the dusty work and the stripped-out space.

1076484.abstract: Jamie shares photos taken from a motor boat with rowing coach Lauren during a Learn to Row session, and links to related posts "All 8 Row!" and "Learn to Row."

1076485.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy run the ALARC Legends 5k, with Tammy finishing in 25:13 and Jamie around 26:30, followed by a pancake breakfast. Jamie notes the race honors Minnesota running legends, including marathon record holders and a 90-year-old participant.

1076486.abstract: Jamie describes a second Learn to Row class session at the Minneapolis Rowing Club (MRC), including drills rowing four and six at a time before the class rows all eight together for the first time. Jamie sat in seat 6 while Tammy rowed stroke seat, and Jamie mentions interest in continuing into MRC's novice program for the season.

1076487.abstract: Jamie and Tammy attend the "Learn to Row" class at the Minneapolis Rowing Club, taking their first session on the water in a sweep eight with ten classmates and planning a sculling day. Jamie feels uneasy when the boat wobbles but finds rowing enjoyable overall.

1076488.abstract: Jamie describes joining TCBC's annual Watermelon Ride for the 4th of July, an event named for the watermelon lunch served afterward. Jamie and Tammy chose the 55-mile option over the 25-mile route, finding the flat course manageable and the weather ideal for cycling.

1076489.abstract: Jamie and Tammy plan a Fourth of July weekend visit to the Taste of Minnesota with friends Tracy and Jeff, their first since 2002 when it was held at the state capitol.

1076490.abstract: Jamie describes watching the fireworks display in Stillwater, calling it on par with the best seen, and notes the roughly 30-minute show set to music, boats gathered on the water, crowds along the shore, and concession vendors.

1076491.abstract: Jamie describes purchasing a Canon PowerShot S500 to complement an existing Canon EOS Digital Rebel and Tammy's Canon PowerShot G3, wanting a light, portable camera for an upcoming Europe trip, including bike rides in France.

1076492.abstract: Jamie celebrates the improved American television coverage of the Tour de France, now available through OLN, compared to sparse coverage a few years earlier.

1076493.abstract: Jamie links to a page documenting a homemade Tron costume at ibiblio.org, describing a reaction of being stunned, confused and frightened, and shares the find as an internet oddity.

1076494.abstract: Jamie describes the Race Across America (RAAM), calling it the hardest sporting event in the world, and notes this year's edition included close competition and alleged espionage between teams. Jamie links to an animated progress map from caida.org showing the race's route.

1076495.abstract: Jamie calls TimeWarner about cable modem service and, while checking for a better deal, upgrades at no extra cost to 3 mbps download and 768 kbps upload, a 4x increase, activated within about an hour and confirmed with speed tests.

1076496.abstract: Jamie recounts riding the Tour of Saints, a bike event starting in St. Joseph, MN, with wife Tammy despite cold, rainy weather that cut the planned 50-mile route to 35 miles. Jamie describes forgetting proper rain gear, a lackluster food stop, and spotting another rider in blue jeans, concluding the miserable conditions made for a good story.

1076497.abstract: Jamie completes a project to move all family music to a home media server called Teraserver, a 1.4 terabyte system, after ripping and tagging nearly 1,000 CDs and finally finishing the vinyl record collection.

1076498.abstract: Jamie describes running the Minnetonka Summer Festival 8k for the first time, having previously done the event's 2 mile fun run two years earlier. Jamie finds the hilly course challenging but enjoyable, and calls the pancake breakfast afterward cheesey but good and cheap.

1076499.abstract: Jamie explains the yellow wristband as a Live Strong band from the Wear Yellow fundraising campaign run by the Lance Armstrong Foundation to raise money for cancer research, noting an interest in professional cycling and being a fan of Lance Armstrong.

1076500.abstract: Jamie links to a Star Tribune article about a hit-and-run against a cyclist, expressing dismay at driver hostility toward bicyclists. Jamie suggests reporting unsafe driving online to police and supporting pedestrian and bicycle safety advocacy groups like bikeped.org.

1076501.abstract: Jamie notes that a privately funded spacecraft, referencing Scaled Composites' Tier One project, successfully reached suborbital space that day, linking to a CNN report on the flight.

1076502.abstract: Jamie notes a brief power blip affecting home electronics, with sensitive systems resetting despite UPS backup on some devices. Jamie records the incident mainly for reference in dealing with XcelEnergy about persistent, unreliable power.

1076503.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy try paintball for the first time at Combat Zone, near St. Croix State Park, playing seven or eight games; Tammy captures the flag twice. Jamie notes Rambo-style tactics fail in practice and credits Kristina Mauersberger for organizing the outing.

1076504.abstract: Jamie recounts seeing the movie Dodgeball and calls it a stupid but genuinely funny film, describing it as undemanding entertainment—"chewing gum for the brain"—rather than anything intellectual.

1076505.abstract: Jamie links to a PC Magazine article noting the average American appears in at least 50 corporate databases, expressing concern about personal information becoming a commodity online. Jamie recommends refusing unnecessary data requests, supporting groups like the EFF, and tracking related legislative action.

1076506.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy attend a Prince concert at the Xcel Center as guests of Trizec, a property management firm being considered for a new office location. Jamie finds the two-hour show impressive, with strong staging and lighting, and notes the Xcel Center suites are nicer than the Target Center's.

1076507.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the annual MarketWatch golf outing, describing the day as a great one.

1076508.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy and Tammy's mom pick fresh strawberries, and Jamie eats about a pound and a half. Jamie calls strawberries a favorite fruit and finds vine-ripened ones far better than store-bought versions from the megamart or co-op.

1076509.abstract: Jamie links to a three-part article series called "Beyond Megapixels" on thetechlounge.com, covering issues surrounding digital photography and the direction of the technology and industry.

1076510.abstract: Jamie recounts an overnight car camping trip to St. Croix State Park with Tammy, describing a 9.6-mile hike plagued by mosquitos so severe that Tammy used DEET-based Jungle Juice for the first time. Jamie also mentions cooking breakfast on a new Coleman camp stove and biking the Willard-Munger State Trail near Hinckley afterward.

1076511.abstract: Jamie describes stopping in Stillwater while returning from a camping trip to watch the final stage of the Great River Energy Bicycle Festival, a criterium through historic downtown with a climb over 25% grade. Jamie finds the race fast and competitive, and hopes Minnesota's pro-level event continues improving.

1076512.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy complete the Easy Does It 5-mile run in Plymouth, choosing it over the Rally for the Refuge 5k after friends Alice and John recommend it. Jamie finishes in 46:38 and Tammy around 43:30.

1076513.abstract: Jamie shares a recipe for grilled tandoori chicken, listing ingredients including a whole chicken, yogurt, ginger, garlic, and spices like paprika, cumin, turmeric, and garam masala, with instructions for marinating and grilling or baking.

1076514.abstract: Jamie describes watching Stage 3, the Minneapolis downtown criterium, of the Great River Energy Bicycle Festival, which was delayed about 45 minutes by heavy rain. Jamie describes the excitement of watching the peloton and plans to attend the final stage in Stillwater on Sunday.

1076516.abstract: Jamie describes commuting home by bike along favorite trails, cruising at 22 mph with unusual ease. Jamie recalls advice from an older cyclist at Hellweek in 2001, that enjoyable riding means a tailwind, and confirms it by noticing grass bent in the same direction as the ride.

1076517.abstract: Jamie describes having rain gutters installed at home, part of several ongoing small and medium house projects. Jamie worried the gutters would ruin the house's modern, overhang-free 1980s design but finds the 6 inch gutters look fine and help keep moisture away.

1076518.abstract: Jamie describes a MarketWatch New York colleague, Rowan Hajaj, traveling to the North Col of Everest and links to Hajaj's trip blog, praising the writing. Jamie mentions repeatedly considering visiting the Everest region but changing course after learning the details involved.

1076519.abstract: Jamie mentions a growing interest in professional cycling over the past four years, starting with US Postal and Lance Armstrong. Jamie links to a Nike commercial featuring Armstrong, seen often on OLN, calling it cool enough to inspire a ride.

1076520.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy attend the Edina Art Fair, noting it's larger than in recent years with art quality both better and worse. Jamie mentions seeing Yardbirds, buying a local artist's picture, and spotting stuffed snakes from Taiwan among some questionable vendors.

1076521.abstract: Jamie reports that the exterior painting of the house is complete, with everything back in place afterward.

1076522.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy complete their first multi-sport event, the Apple Duathlon in Sartell, MN, a USAT-certified 5k run, 20-mile bike, 5k run race that is Minnesota's longest-running multi-sport event.

1076523.abstract: Jamie describes the near-completion of house painting, noting relief as painters remove plastic window coverings that had made the house feel like a sensory deprivation chamber. Jamie also mentions the garage door suddenly struggling to open.

1076524.abstract: Jamie highlights California's resistance to corporate influence, noting communities fighting off Walmart expansion and California's Senate Bill 19, which mandates nutritional standards for food served in public schools, joking about how few McDonald's items would qualify.

1076525.abstract: Jamie describes repeated attempts to schedule a hot air balloon ride, only to have flights canceled due to weather conditions required for launch. Jamie frames the pattern jokingly as a scam, arguing the hot air balloon industry collects payment upfront while leaving customers unable to verify weather claims or get a flight.

1076527.abstract: Jamie recounts building a terabyte home storage server using a 3ware Escalade 8506-8 RAID card and six Western Digital 200GB SATA drives, hitting successive obstacles: incompatible PCI slots forcing a dual-Xeon Asus PU-DL server motherboard, case incompatibility requiring a SuperMicro SC742T-550 chassis, difficult CPU cooling assembly, and…

1076528.abstract: Jamie describes upgrading a home network to gigabit ethernet, using an SMC 8508T switch and Intel Pro/1000MT cards with jumbo frame support, based on advice from Chris Tersteeg.

1076529.abstract: Jamie recounts a weekend kayak trip with Jamie's wife Tammy through the Apostle Islands, taken with Trek & Trail's Paddle Through Time tour out of Bayfield, WI, covering camps, two lighthouses, and a hike over three days totaling about 25.8 miles.

1076530.abstract: Jamie recounts a Florida-to-Minnesota road trip while writing from a Bob Evans counter in Marion, IL, describing Animal Kingdom, Epcot, Discovery Cove, Seaworld and the Cirque du Soleil show La Nouba, plus Tammy's illness during the drive.

1076531.abstract: Jamie recounts a Florida vacation with wife Tammy, covering a rainy first day at the Kennedy Space Center and WonderWorks in Orlando, followed by a sunny day at Disney World's Magic Kingdom using FastPass strategy for rides like Space Mountain and Splash Mountain.

1076532.abstract: Jamie recounts how Jamie's wife Tammy fell in love with a hanging VW-door sculpture featuring a blue dog seen at a Denver gallery during the honeymoon, describing it as reminiscent of George Rodrigue's work.

1076533.abstract: Jamie describes riding "the Rollercoaster" route through canyons and Majestic Rock state park during Texas Hellweek 2001, following the previous day's "death ride." Despite headwinds and cold, Jamie finds the 102-mile route scenic and less punishing than expected, averaging 15 mph, and considers either a short loop or a rest day with a massage in…

1076534.abstract: Jamie recounts day 6 of Texas Hellweek 2001, the "Leakey Death Ride," a 109-mile, over 7-hour ride from Fredericksburg to Bandera with six major climbs, including a nearly 1,000-foot ascent. Jamie hits 50 mph on descents, discovers loose spokes mid-ride, and completes the toughest day of the week with two remaining.

1076535.abstract: Jamie recounts day five of Texas Hellweek 2001, a 102-mile ride through Texas Hill Country near Fredericksburg and Boerne, completed in nearly seven hours through cold rain and about 5,000 feet of climbing, with speed and heart rate charts showing a slow, low-effort pace ahead of the next day's Death Ride.

1076536.abstract: On day four of Hellweek, Jamie describes riding Fred's Ride, a memorial route named for a friend of organizer Nick who died a couple years earlier, then suffering a rear tire blowout at 35 mph after climbing Eagles Nest Mountain, ending the ride early at about 40 miles despite hitting a fastest-yet pace of 16.1 mph average and 42 mph max.

1076537.abstract: Jamie recounts day three of Texas Hellweek, a 96.6-mile ride rerouted due to a flooded bridge, passing through Fredericksburg, Kerrville, Center Point and Comfort. A rider named Bill from Oklahoma City is hit by a truck and airlifted to San Antonio with a fractured vertebra.

1076538.abstract: Jamie recounts Day 2 of Texas Hellweek 2001, a long ride called "The Harper Image" featuring rolling hills, serious climbs, a headwind, and a route looping through Harper, Texas three times.

1076539.abstract: Jamie recounts the first day of Texas Hellweek 2001, starting with a damaged spoke fixed thanks to fellow rider Tom, then completing the 99-mile LBJ Ramble near Fredericksburg in 6 hours 15 minutes.

1076540.abstract: Jamie shares results from a second gear test during Texas Hellweek 2001, including a GPS-tracked 15.9-mile bike ride through Minneapolis lakes like Cedar Lake, Lake Calhoun, and Lake Harriet, plus elevation, speed, and heart rate data from the ride.

1076541.abstract: Jamie tests GPS gear on a 29.8-mile bike ride through Minneapolis ahead of a trip to Texas, sharing the route map and an elevation profile showing 933 feet of climbing, noting a heart rate monitor failed to get signal.

1076542.abstract: Jamie describes the second day of a Caribbean cruise, noting how much boats rock and joking that rum, gin and tequila don't help. Jamie mentions an upcoming wedding on St. Thomas the next day and a late-night buffet snack bar aboard the ship.

1076543.abstract: Jamie recounts arriving in San Juan, being mistakenly sent to the El San Juan Hotel instead of the Old San Juan Hotel, then walking the area near the cruise dock and noting the city's traffic and old war-era walls. Jamie also describes losing money playing blackjack, dropping from $100 up to $170 and back down to $35.

1077238.abstract: Jamie considers switching to Blot, a blogging platform gaining popularity on micro.blog, after learning it now supports Git as an alternative to Dropbox, eliminating any GitHub dependency. Jamie notes pairing it with the iOS app Working Copy enables robust mobile editing, and plans to try Blot, particularly for a photography site.

1077239.abstract: Jamie describes assembling the UGears Steam Locomotive model over the holidays, a 443-piece kit compared to the earlier 107-piece Chronograph build. Jamie notes improved manuals, a side-panel assembly mistake, and difficulty getting the rubber-band-driven gears to move smoothly despite using candle wax lubricant.

1077240.abstract: Jamie describes movers arriving to relocate the family to a new house, the first move in nearly nine years and the first time Jamie's kids experience the moving process. Jamie reflects on watching Netflix's Tidying Up with Marie Kondo and offers a thank-you message to the Morgan Ave. home.

1077241.abstract: Jamie describes a method for managing API tokens in iOS Shortcuts by creating dedicated "Secret" shortcuts that return credentials, rather than embedding them as text variables.

1077249.abstract: Jamie attends the demo day for Hack the Gap 2019, a hackathon for women and non-binary participants held at the Glen Nelson Center, and describes projects including Securiosity, whenIneedU, Ready Play, Hack the Bra, Make Friends Minnesota, Seshat Swap, Cat Flat, Little Free Library, Sweat Connect, and Planet.

1077252.abstract: Jamie recounts the 8th annual Minnesota Kubb Winter Tournament, played by team Kubbchucks against Team Dondante, the Free Agents, and The Four Old Guys in round robin before losing to Skol, featuring Evan Fitzgerald, in the Round of 16; the Free Agents go on to win the tournament.

1077253.abstract: Jamie describes moving websites to Blot and wanting JSONFeed support alongside its automatic RSS, but hitting a wall with Mustache templates that couldn't safely encode HTML into JSON.

1077255.abstract: Jamie's book club reads Scale: The Universal Laws of Growth, Innovation, Sustainability, and the Pace of Life in Organisms, Cities, Economies, and Companies by Geoffrey B. West, which examines scaling patterns across animals, cities, and companies. Jamie finds the book profound and important but is uncertain how to apply its ideas.

1077261.abstract: Jamie describes using gitwatch to automatically commit and push changes to a website managed with Blot.im, which now supports git alongside Dropbox for content management, eliminating the need for manual git commands while editing.

1077263.abstract: Jamie tries Tesla's new "Come to me" feature, shipped in v10, on a Model 3 at a busy South Minneapolis parking lot. The car backs out and starts approaching but gets confused by pedestrians and other cars, prompting Jamie to run over and take control, concluding the feature works best in calm, empty lots.

1077264.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a Sunday night photowalk in Kyiv, Ukraine, taken while visiting the SPS team with three colleagues. Images include Saint Sophia Cathedral, the Opera House, Golden Gate, St. Michael's Cathedral, the People's Friendship Arch, walking bridges and a Ferris wheel.

1078766.abstract: Jamie describes visiting the deserted herring factory in Djúpavík, Iceland, closed since 1954 and left with much of its original equipment intact. Jamie finds the dark interior with shafts of light an ideal setting for HDR photography, and shares photos of the abandoned machinery and structure.

1078769.abstract: Jamie shares photos of waves crashing onto a beach in Iceland, paired with audio capturing the sound of pebbles being tossed by the surf.

1078813.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of a red, white and blue wooden Kubb king piece standing in grass at an outdoor tournament, with players and a white canopy tent visible in the background.

1078814.abstract: Jamie shares a black-and-white photo of a small numbered steam locomotive emitting steam on a narrow-gauge track at the Riverside & Great Northern Railway in Wisconsin Dells, calling the steam engines there awesome.

1078824.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a photography workshop in Grand Marais taken with Layne Kennedy, alongside Jamie's wife Tammy, including images of dragon boat racing, a lakeside sunset, a rustic cabin filled with taxidermy, a sawmill, and a canoe near a lighthouse.

1078836.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Horseshoe Falls at Niagara, showing a red tour boat navigating the churning turquoise water below the massive curved waterfall.

1078838.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of four sailboats on the Hudson River, with the Lower Manhattan skyline and One World Trade Center visible in the background under overcast skies.

1078854.abstract: Jamie shares a nighttime panoramic photo of a packed baseball stadium at Target Field, showing the lit green field, dirt infield, and players positioned during a game.

1078857.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of Cascade Falls, showing a wide waterfall spilling over a sandstone ledge into a rocky pool, framed by autumn forest.

1078922.abstract: Jamie describes SPS Commerce celebrating the 10th anniversary of going public on NASDAQ, with #TeamSPS members sharing photos of themselves wearing SPS gear, compiled into videos posted on LinkedIn and Twitter, alongside several of the shared photos.

1079576.abstract: Jamie describes seeing Michael Moore's Fahrenheit 9/11 on opening day with Tammy, noting the charged political atmosphere and full, enthusiastic theater. Despite disagreeing with Moore's politics, Jamie calls the film essential viewing and says it prompts Jamie and Tammy to become more politically active.

1079577.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy and Jamie see The Terminal and Jamie admits liking it more than expected, despite mixed enthusiasm for stars Tom Hanks and director Steven Spielberg. Jamie finds the airport-set plot, though it sounds boring, enjoyable and leaves the movie feeling happy.

1079585.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy watch the film Room while attempting to see all the best picture nominees. Jamie describes the movie as having two distinct halves, before and after "the room," and praises the acting of the child actor playing Jack.

1079588.abstract: Jamie shares notes on reading Elon Musk: Tesla, SpaceX, and the Quest for a Fantastic Future by Ashlee Vance, including a photo of the book's cover.

1079597.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy finds The Lab by Alchemy Coffee, a coffee shop Jamie visits for a macchiato and a pour-over to go. Jamie praises the ambiance but finds the macchiato's espresso a bit thin and the pour-over's roast lighter than preferred.

1079598.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy finds Two Drummer's Smokehouse, a remote roadside BBQ spot, while researching Williamsburg, and the couple stops there for dinner. Jamie describes the ribs, pulled pork, and brisket as delicious, with the cornbread being the weakest part of the meal.

1079608.abstract: Jamie recounts eating pizza at Big River Pizza with Monique and Dave before a Mumford & Sons show, praising the crust and bright sauce but noting a lacking beer menu, and says Jamie will return.

1079612.abstract: Jamie watches Straight Outta Compton on a flight back from Ukraine, calling it a pretty good movie and noting interest in learning the back story behind N.W.A.

1079641.abstract: Jamie mentions watching the film Hell or High Water, which follows two men carrying duffel bags and weapons through a Texas prairie under a stormy sky.

1079642.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of the retro interior at Hi-Lo Diner, noting teal vinyl chairs and a chrome counter with liquor bottles and beer taps, and mentions the food was good, especially the banana cream pie.

1080163.abstract: Jamie attends the first online Minnebar, hosted by Minnestar using Crowdcast, and describes sessions by Dan Lew on tech's role in climate change, Joe Karlsson on an IoT kitty litter box, and SPS Commerce's Kisha Delain on pair programming with junior developers.

1080516.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a first visit to the Anderson Center Sculpture Garden in Red Wing, describing it as an enjoyable way to spend a nice day, with images of large steel sculptures including a rusted seesaw and red angular and looped forms set on grassy lawns.

1080526.abstract: Jamie joins Jamie's sister and family for the Extreme Sandbox Heavy Metal Drive-Thru, watching heavy equipment perform while excited children in attendance honk their horns.

1083873.abstract: Jamie describes getting Tammy a Numskull Quarter Arcade Ms. PAC-MAN cabinet as a birthday gift, calling it a well-built, battery-powered replica with a surprisingly responsive joystick that the whole family enjoys playing.

1084819.abstract: Jamie describes migrating a Jekyll blog archive to micro.blog, following an approach from Manton Reece's Timetable migration post, and shares Python code and a Jekyll JSONFeed template used for the process.

1088967.abstract: Jamie reflects on unexpected benefits of shifting interactions online during the pandemic, covering work, community events, and mourning rituals. At work, video calls equalize geography and give introverted or remote team members more voice, plus Q&A works better than in-person all-hands meetings.

1088986.abstract: Jamie describes using the Ate app to track meals and creates a custom scale for rating pre-meal and post-meal hunger levels, pairing numbers 0 through 6 with emoji labels like Irritable, Hungry, Satisfied, and Stuffed. The aim is to stay within the middle "thumbs up" range of Hungry, Satisfied, or Full.

1090833.abstract: Jamie completes a first Functional Threshold Power (FTP) test on Peloton, noting the bike's built-in power measurement features that customize a real-time power meter after such a test.

1097416.abstract: Jamie shares notes from an Economic Club of Minnesota webinar, "Our Economy and Health in Crisis," moderated by Margaret Brennan with panelists Neel Kashkari and Dr. Michael Osterholm, who discussed real unemployment near 25%, herd immunity thresholds, vaccine tradeoffs, and risk tolerance for reopening.

1098230.abstract: Jamie celebrates the 23rd anniversary of launching BigCharts.com, recalling personally backloading Dow Jones Industrial Average data to 1970, the "Big" chart size name, and the historical quote and up2.aspx load-balancer pages. Jamie includes a 1999 team dinner photo from Buca di Beppo and links to a related LinkedIn post.

1102209.abstract: Jamie recounts attending the online 2020 Minnesota Aspirations in Computing Award Ceremony, noting SPS Commerce's sponsorship and internship program, and credits Amy Patton's contributions, alongside photos of Erin Mitchell, John Bartucz, Afiya Ward, Stuti Arora, and Russell Fraenkel.

1109638.abstract: Jamie watches the SpaceX Dragon capsule approach the International Space Station, noting the station launched in 1998 with a communications system, C2V2, upgraded in 2016 to support such arrivals. Jamie remarks on the extensive long-term planning the docking requires.

1111191.abstract: Jamie recaps sessions attended at Minnebar 12, including Zen and the Art of Agility, Blockchains are Coming, Introduction to Functional Reactive Programming, a discussion on hiring junior developers, Privacy for Everyone, and Communicating When Stuff Is Going Wrong, with photos and brief notes on each talk.

1111192.abstract: Jamie recaps demos from Minnedemo 24, covering Raisable's Facebook Messenger fundraising chatbot, Binary Bride/CrossCare's offline-capable EMR intake tool, and Civic Eagle's civic engagement platform with voter registration and video debate features.

1111197.abstract: Jamie notes recurring references in "Leadership Pipeline" to reviewing one's calendar and time spent as a tool for assessing whether someone focuses on the right work, and highlights the Alignment Triangle concept for reviewing business and organizational health, sharing photos of the diagram and a related sample-questions table.

1111585.abstract: Jamie reflects on the killing of George Floyd in Minneapolis and the unrest that followed locally, nationally, and globally.

1111660.abstract: Jamie argues that Twitter's decision to tag and limit distribution of some of President Trump's tweets, while Facebook left similar content untouched, does not amount to censorship.

1117745.abstract: Jamie participates in an early run-through of a new Distribution Center Simulation at SPS, describing a hands-on experience using real products, staged distribution center scenarios, and truck and forklift sound effects, adapted for in-person use during the pandemic.

1117746.abstract: Jamie lists the books kept stocked on an office shelf, prompted by a friend's question after seeing a selfie, noting copies are given away freely and the selection changes over time.

1126751.abstract: Jamie recounts a late visit to the 2019 Edina Art Fair, noting it seemed fuller and higher quality than in previous years. Jamie highlights artists including Brendan Kramp, Straight Up Chess, Matthew Rucker, Jamie Heiden, Greta Sandquist, Dogfish Media, and Kate Whisler, whose laser-cut scenes stood out.

1136492.abstract: Jamie announces the start of TeamSPS TechJam 2020, an all-remote event featuring 31 presenters running sessions across global teams, bookended by a Hackathon and a Deep Racer competition.

1137283.abstract: Jamie and Tammy Thingelstad watch Minnesota Experience's "Jim Crow of the North" and describe learning about racist real estate covenants that barred non-white residents, including one found on Jamie's former Morgan Avenue home.

1142016.abstract: Jamie and Tammy Thingelstad attend opening night of Travail Kitchen and Amusements' Rooftop Patio Cantina, describing a southwest tasting menu with dishes like ceviche, Pescado ala Talla, and Mexican chocolate mousse, plus cocktails including a Paloma and El Valiente margarita.

1142523.abstract: Jamie recounts an early mishap while preparing for a Yellowstone Road Trip in the RV: a nighttime downpour caused minor water intrusion through roof vents, but a bigger problem arose when Mazie accidentally switched off the RV's main power while turning off lights, shutting down the refrigerator overnight.

1143246.abstract: Jamie describes a brief stop at Theodore Roosevelt National Park after staying overnight in Medora, en route to Bozeman, driving the Scenic Loop with stops at Wind Canyon, Boicourt Overlook, Buck Hill, and the Prairie Dog town, and shares photos from the visit.

1149695.abstract: Jamie describes picking up an RV from Hilltop Rental and loading it with supplies, noting that some items will likely go unused while other important things are probably forgotten, marking the start of a Yellowstone trip.

1149697.abstract: Jamie logs day one of a Yellowstone road trip, driving from Minneapolis after a grocery stop to replace food lost in an earlier RV fridge incident.

1149698.abstract: Jamie recounts day two of a Yellowstone trip: breakfast in the RV, three hours exploring highlights of Theodore Roosevelt National Park, a drive to Bozeman, dinner at a brewery restaurant, and arrival at an RV park outside Bozeman around 9pm.

1149700.abstract: Jamie logs day three of a Yellowstone trip: breakfast in the RV, a morning hike with llamas, lunch on the trail, and ice cream at Sweet Peaks. The day includes shopping in Bozeman, dinner at MAP Brewing, spotting an EarthRoamer, and a stop at Bozeman Hot Springs.

1149701.abstract: Jamie logs day four of a Yellowstone trip, noting breakfast at Wild Crumb, a return visit to Schnee's, lunch in the RV, tubing down the Madison River, and a drive to West Yellowstone on a beautiful day.

1149702.abstract: Jamie logs day five of a Yellowstone trip, noting lovely weather and visits to the Lower Geyser Basin, Grand Prismatic Spring, Biscuit Basin, Mammoth Springs and Roosevelt Arch, with a link to Hell's A-Roarin' Outfitters.

1149703.abstract: Jamie recounts day six of a Yellowstone trip: early morning fly fishing, lunch at a golf course restaurant, and a return to the park.

1149705.abstract: Jamie logs day seven of a Yellowstone trip, visiting Gibbon Falls, the North and South Rims of the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone River, Hayden Valley, and Yellowstone Lake, including ice cream and a shirt for Tyler at the General Store, plus a bison traffic jam.

1149706.abstract: Jamie logs day 8 of a Yellowstone trip: leaving West Yellowstone KOA, returning a rental car, stopping at Lewis Falls, and driving through Grand Tetons, including an accidental exit and detour along Teton Road, before reaching Jackson for groceries and dinner at Miazgas, then settling into a tight, less-favored spot at Snake River KOA amid road…

1149707.abstract: Jamie recounts a day in Yellowstone/Jackson: an early wildlife tour with Bush Buck spotting elk, black bear, moose, and a Great Blue Heron with a chick, then meeting Kendra, David, and Dawson for pastries and a Snake River walk, exploring Jackson shops, whitewater rafting with Dave Hansen, and pizza at Handfire Pizza.

1149709.abstract: Jamie recounts day 10 of a Yellowstone trip, where Tyler and Mazie meet up with Nola and Sebastian, and the group bikes from Dornan's to Jenny Lake, takes a boat, and hikes to Hidden Falls.

1149710.abstract: Jamie logs day 11 of a Yellowstone trip, noting rainy weather that clears into pleasant driving conditions, breakfast at Persephone bakery, a visit to the Teton Park visitor center, and a drive to Mount Rushmore KOA with scenic early scenery.

1149711.abstract: Jamie logs day 12 of a Yellowstone trip, noting a cool, rain-like morning and visits to Mt. Rushmore and Crazy Horse, followed by a chuck wagon dinner.

1149712.abstract: Jamie logs the final day of a Yellowstone trip: a long drive home, a stop for pizza at Dino's Pizzeria in Mankato, arriving home by 7:00pm, then spending two hours unloading and cleaning the RV before returning it the next morning.

1149713.abstract: Jamie shares photos from Mazie's Pirate Party.

1149714.abstract: Jamie shares photos from Mazie's birthday.

1150364.abstract: Jamie shares statistics from a Yellowstone trip in 2020, including 2,721 miles driven, 1,313 pictures taken, three national parks and one national monument visited, four fish caught, and one bear sighted, with a link to the full Yellowstone 2020 Collection.

1157629.abstract: Jamie describes trying Oddball, a new VR laser tag arena experience at REM5VR, with wireless headsets that let players walk around and see teammates in VR space. Jamie's wife Tammy and their kids played several rounds, and REM5 shared video of a round the kids won.

1165623.abstract: Jamie describes a morning kayaking trip starting at Tioga Beach on Pokegama Lake, through Big Jay Goulde Lake and Little Jay Goulde Lake into the Mississippi River, portaging around the Corps of Engineers Pokegama Dam and ending at Paddle Hoppers after 2 hours 35 minutes, noting lily pads and wild rice along the way.

1173007.abstract: Jamie shares photos and impressions from the Minnesota State Fair, mentioning a cherry wine slushy, the "Butterheads" butter sculptures, and a crowded fairgrounds scene. Jamie suggests there should be a wiki dedicated to the fair.

1173009.abstract: Jamie shares photos of a Brandi Carlile concert at the Minnesota State Fair, describing an outdoor stage packed with fans and fireworks bursting overhead. Jamie calls the show amazing and links to a list of Brandi Carlile shows attended.

1173010.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a Brandi Carlile performance at Big Top Chautauqua, describing the crowd's excitement and calling the show magical. Jamie links to a list of Brandi Carlile shows attended.

1173080.abstract: Jamie and Tammy visit Martina restaurant's new outdoor patio, praising its design with multiple levels, trees, and lighting, along with the food, drinks, and distancing precautions. Jamie notes the Panqueque dessert remains a favorite for sharing.

1174581.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the 2007 Minneapolis office picnic.

1174585.abstract: Jamie shares photos from an annual neighborhood block gathering to carve Halloween pumpkins, noting that this year's group produced a great pumpkin carving result.

1174586.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a weekend spent in Eastern Iowa staying with friends at Sous Les Sapins Guesthouse.

1174591.abstract: Jamie shares a photo collection from the days following Christmas 2007.

1174606.abstract: Jamie shares photos from Ardell & Rose Chrest's 50th wedding anniversary celebration.

1174704.abstract: Jamie and Tammy spend a day biking the Dakota Rail Regional Trail, starting with breakfast at The Grocer's Table in Wayzata and riding 33 miles out and back to Lake Waconia. Stops include Big Stone Mini Golf and its sculpture garden, plus lunch at Dakota Junction in Mound.

1174707.abstract: Jamie and Tammy Thingelstad kayak five miles down the Crow River from Hanover to Saint Michael, Minnesota, renting equipment through River Dragon Kayak Rental, with the trip taking about 90 minutes and ending with dinner at Main Street Farmer.

1175795.abstract: Jamie visits Mighty Fine Coffee, a new coffee roaster in Faribault, meeting the two owners and buying a bag of freshly roasted beans. Jamie shares a photo of the roasting facility and its red commercial roaster, and expresses enthusiasm for the new business.

1176117.abstract: Jamie shares photos and updates from a Minnesota United FC match against Tampa Bay, noting a full stadium, Atomic Data's sponsorship of the team, a Minnesota United goal, and Tampa Bay's equalizer to make it 1-1.

1176278.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of nine carved jack-o-lanterns on a deck table and notes that candy ran out by 7:30pm after more than 100 trick-or-treaters visited, calling it a "crazy night" on Halloween 2011.

1176715.abstract: Jamie shares photos and updates from a U2 Joshua Tree tour show at US Bank Stadium, with Beck opening. Jamie notes the large crowds for both acts and captures moments including "Elevation" and "One," plus a stadium ceiling wireless antenna unit spotted before the show.

1176720.abstract: Jamie shares first impressions of Apple's Game Center, joining under the username "thingles" and expressing being impressed despite not being much of a gamer. Jamie speculates about non-game uses, wondering what apps like Reeder or MindNode could do with it, such as multiuser mind mapping.

1176874.abstract: Jamie watches Mulan (2020) at home via Disney+ Premier Access, finding the film and its action impressive despite no prior exposure to the animated original. Jamie welcomes the ability to watch new movies immediately on digital platforms rather than waiting for theaters.

1176877.abstract: Jamie describes the first day of distance-learning school for Mazie and Tyler during the pandemic, keeping the tradition of chocolate chip pancakes and front-of-house photos. Both kids connect via Google Classroom and use Flipgrid, with Jamie's wife Tammy troubleshooting tech issues; Jamie calls the day a success.

1179386.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy spend the weekend in Lanesboro staying at the Habberstad House Bed & Breakfast, booking the Carriage House. Jamie notes Lanesboro is a good destination for cycling and offers unique lodging options, and shares photos of the Victorian house and its gardens.

1179392.abstract: Jamie and Tammy's wife Tammy ride 28 miles out-and-back on the Root River Trail from Lanesboro to Peterson, finding Aroma Pie Shoppe in Whalan closed for the season due to Covid-19 but stopping at Burdey's Cafe in Peterson instead.

1179531.abstract: Jamie attends a live recording by The Cactus Blossoms at the Turf Club, describing a packed, sweltering venue (around 98°F with the AC off for the recording), a friendly group of visitors from Texas, and the band playing Hank Williams Sr. classics.

1179672.abstract: Jamie describes stopping at Eagle Bluff Environmental Learning Center near Lanesboro for a casual hike down to the Root River on a forested loop trail, encountering bugs, two snakes, frogs and toads, and shares photos of the river, woodland canopy, and the trail.

1180434.abstract: Jamie shares photos and updates from an MN United v Real Salt Lake match at Allianz Field, describing goals from Quintero and Finlay leading to a 3-1 MNUFC win, with images of the crowd, flares, scarves, and a family selfie in the stands.

1180882.abstract: Jamie attends Marc Benioff's keynote at Dreamforce, describing a 2½ hour session in a huge, packed convention hall and the long lines throughout the event, plus a jab at attendees force-quitting iOS apps.

1181819.abstract: Jamie describes coining the "Two Second Test" while working in media and publishing on the web: a news website's front page should convey what's happening in just two seconds.

1181821.abstract: Jamie thanks Slalom Consulting for the "Slalom Presents: Realizing Racial Equality" program, which featured Ruby Bridges on desegregating schools, Dr. Condoleezza Rice on race and education, and a closing performance by Leon Bridges, calling it a backgrounder on addressing racism.

1182561.abstract: Jamie describes watching the Netflix documentary My Octopus Teacher, about the year Craig Foster spent visiting an octopus daily. Jamie highlights a favorite scene showing the octopus playing with a school of fish and praises the underwater filming.

1182562.abstract: Jamie describes an opening-night visit to Rosalia, a new counter-service pizza restaurant from Daniel del Prada located behind Martina. Jamie finds the Pepperoni and Margherita pizzas excellent and the Bianca pleasantly spicy, though a Tomato Fugazza slice was underheated, possibly due to the opening.

1182809.abstract: Jamie recaps Saturday morning soccer viewing, praising Harry Kane's goal against Leicester City and linking to an NBC Sports video, but Spurs still lose 1-2. Jamie also questions whether Premier League VAR offside rulings improve the game, then notes Lewandowski's early goal for Bayern against Köln.

1182810.abstract: Jamie describes attending a Minnesota United match against Sporting KC at Allianz Field, noting a rough first half before United rallies for a 2-1 come-from-behind win that clinches a spot in the 2019 playoffs.

1182811.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the 2019 #TeamSPS Kubb Tournament, where 20 teams played a round robin followed by bracket play tracked on handwritten paper brackets divided by job level. Jamie mentions possibly adding Mölkky next year and links to posts from other tournament years.

1182812.abstract: Jamie recaps day one of DevOpsDays MSP 2019, where SPS Commerce sponsored and staffed a booth. Jamie highlights talks and takeaways from Bridget Kromhout's opening, Liz Fong-Jones on observability and sustainable heroism, Yolonda Smith on perspectives on security, Jessica Kerr on collaborative automation and "symmathesy," and Nivia Sedai on AI/ML…

1182813.abstract: Jamie recaps day two of DevOpsDays MSP, covering John Engelman's keynote on cascading failure, a team overview from SPS Commerce's Nate Anderson, Sanjesh Kumar, and Olivia Alberts, talks by Martez Reed and Serena Tiede, and Alice Goldfuss's closing keynote on container operations.

1182814.abstract: Jamie shares photos and updates from a Minnesota United match against FC Dallas at Allianz Field, describing a 0-0 first half and goalkeeper Mannone saving a VAR-ruled penalty in stoppage time to preserve a 1-0 win.

1182815.abstract: Jamie shares photos and updates from a Minnesota United v FC Cincinnati match at Allianz Field, tracking the score from 4-0 to a 7-1 final, along with a stadium beer, sunny weather, the crowd, and a link to Wonderwall.

1182816.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a CONCACAF Gold Cup doubleheader at Allianz Field, attending with Tyler to watch Panama v. Trinidad and Tobago (which finishes 4-0) and USA v. Guyana, including a USA goal making it 1-0.

1182817.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a Minnesota United match against the Houston Dynamo at Allianz Field, including the opening lineup, a Minnesota goal, a Darwin Quintero sideline check, halftime field maintenance, and celebrations after the Loons win 1-0.

1182818.abstract: Jamie shares photos and impressions from Minnebar 14, hosted by Minnestar, noting record registrations and SPS Commerce's sponsorship. Jamie highlights a Session 0 talk by Sharon Kennedy Vickers on diversity in technology and a Product Management session with Adrienne Peirce, Shawn Heller, and Jeremy Moede.

1183680.abstract: Jamie shares updates from a Minnesota United FC match against the Portland Timbers at Allianz Field, describing goals building a 3-0 lead and celebrating the eventual Loons win while attending with family.

1189359.abstract: Jamie tries a Sous Vide brisket recipe from Serious Eats, trimming and seasoning a flat with salt and pepper Texas style before vacuum sealing and cooking in a 155°F water bath for 37 hours. After cooling, Jamie applies a second rub and finishes the brisket with 3-4 hours of smoke on a Big Green Egg.

1190345.abstract: Jamie shares photos and results from the #TeamSPS Technology Kubb Tournament, an outdoor game played on grass lawns among city buildings. Skubby Doo wins first place, followed by King Kubbas and Kubbernetes, while "Bring Back Kubbicles Plz" takes best team name. Links to tournament posts from 2019, 2021, 2022, and 2023 are also included.

1198211.abstract: Jamie attends and presents at Open Source North, sharing photos of the venue, SPS Commerce recruiters staffing a booth, and Jeff Urban's opening remarks.

1198215.abstract: Jamie upgrades three Apple TVs to version 2.2 and iTunes to 8.0.1, finding the Genius feature useful on Apple TV. Jamie also notes a possible bug causing black video with playing audio, fixed by restarting, and questions whether the new "Standby" menu differs from the existing 5-second play-button hold.

1198643.abstract: Jamie proposes using three-emoji combinations to represent cocktails, starting with an Old Fashioned (🥃🍊🍒) capturing bourbon, orange, and cherry. Jamie extends the idea to a Gin & Tonic, Mojito, and Moscow Mule, choosing emoji for each drink's key ingredients or associations.

1198726.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a first visit to Dancing Bear Chocolate to buy treats for Jamie's Mom's birthday, including a custom carrot cake Jamie finds delicious and filling.

1198827.abstract: Jamie streams Brandi Carlile's Campfire Singalong, a live performance featuring Carlile and "The Twins" playing songs including Simon & Garfunkel's "Homeward Bound," a cover of Radiohead's "Creep," "The Eye," and "The Mother," and links to a list of Brandi Carlile shows.

1199212.abstract: Jamie criticizes the State of Minnesota's COVID-19 resource page (mn.gov/covid19) for breaking entirely when tracker-blocking software is enabled.

1199460.abstract: Jamie attends Day 1 of AWS re:Invent, sharing photos and impressions from the keynote, dining hall, and sessions including Big Data: State of the Union with Paul Duffy, Amazon Redshift, and Netflix's development patterns talk, plus encounters with SPS Commerce colleagues like Rob Krystyniak.

1199461.abstract: Jamie recaps day two of AWS re:Invent, attending Werner Vogels' keynote and noting the announcement of Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, new i2 and c3 EC2 instances, and the EC2 spot market. Jamie highlights Amazon Kinesis for streaming data as especially promising for a current #TeamSPS project.

1199464.abstract: Jamie describes flying out at night to join other #teamsps colleagues for AWS re:Invent, noting a slight sadness about the nighttime flight, and finds the event's iOS app underwhelming and not as useful as it should be.

1199465.abstract: Jamie attends the first keynote of AWS re:Invent, given by Andy Jassy, and shares reactions to announcements including Amazon Snowball and MariaDB support in Amazon RDS, noting personal experience running MariaDB for years.

1199466.abstract: Jamie attends the AWS re:Invent tech keynote by Werner Vogels, sharing a photo of the packed conference hall and noting excitement over new announcements, including an X1 instance with 2TB of RAM and 100 cores.

1199467.abstract: Jamie shares photos from AWS re:Play, an outdoor concert event featuring DJ Zedd, describing losing and recovering a re:Invent badge while dancing and noting Zedd kept the volume high throughout the show.

1199468.abstract: Jamie shares photos and notes from Day 0 of AWS re:Invent, including a hotel corridor, a busy Amazon Web Services booth, and a crowded expo floor with TIBCO and Datapipe banners. Jamie describes discussing Mesos with attendees and talking tech details with SumoLogic cofounders, including Christian Beedgen.

1199469.abstract: Jamie shares photos and short updates from arriving in Las Vegas for AWS re:Invent, mentioning connecting with #TeamSPS, the 68°F weather, and a hotel suite upgrade with a photo of the room.

1199470.abstract: Jamie recounts attending AWS re:Invent, including the keynote by Andy Jassy on cloud computing becoming "the new normal" and Amazon Aurora, plus a security keynote noting AWS runs 5,000-7,000 instances continually testing internal system security.

1199472.abstract: Jamie recaps day two of AWS re:Invent, highlighting Werner Vogels's keynote, the launch of AWS Lambda and AWS's container service (with Docker), and packed sessions on containers and ECS. Jamie also notes a Skrillex re:Play performance and muses on "fleet" replacing "farm" as container terminology.

1199473.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the AWS re:Invent re:Play event, showing illuminated cube structures, attendees under stage lights, and a concert with a DJ performer, LED screens, and colorful stage lighting.

1199995.abstract: Jamie shares photos from attending a Minnesota Twins versus New York Yankees game at Target Field, including a selfie in the packed stadium and shots of Max Kepler and Nelson Cruz batting during the night game.

1199996.abstract: Jamie shares photos and updates from Minnesota United's sold-out home finale against Sporting KC at TCF Bank Stadium, attending with Mazie. The Minnesota Lynx are honored at halftime, and the match ends in a 1-1 tie, closing out MNUFC's inaugural MLS season.

1200054.abstract: Jamie links to a Star Tribune article on the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers lowering the Mississippi River by 12 feet to inspect locks and dams, then describes visiting the exposed riverbed near the Stone Arch Bridge at sunset, sharing photos of the dry areas and crowds.

1200265.abstract: Jamie attends the premiere of "Solid State: Minnesota's High Tech History," a documentary hosted by MHTA and aired on TPT, and shares photos of the packed theater audience and the reaction panel discussion following the screening.

1200811.abstract: Jamie recaps Minnedemo 15, noting SPS Commerce sponsored the event, Lou Abramowski demoed Unbenchable, and a polished Dash demo impressed. Jamie shares photos of the SPS Commerce logo onstage and the event's theater marquee.

1201537.abstract: Jamie attends Minnedemo, sharing brief updates including open WiFi access at O'Gara's, and demos from Crashplan and FanChatter, closing with a note that it was a great night.

1201611.abstract: Jamie discusses two New York Times stories from October 7 and 9, 2020, on Facebook widening its political ad ban and Twitter disabling features to fight election misinformation, arguing both companies now admit they can't control platform misuse.

1204835.abstract: Jamie shares impressions from a Bob Mould concert at The Dakota, noting the show opens with "Wishing Well" and describing Mould switching from acoustic to electric guitar partway through the performance.

1207350.abstract: Jamie attends a Michael Franti and Spearhead concert with Mom, sister, and family, sharing photos from the theater show featuring "Stay Human" and "Power to the Peaceful" banners. Jamie describes the music as inspirational, notes the show ends with everyone singing "Imagine," and mentions Mazie danced onstage with Franti.

1208192.abstract: Jamie describes returning from a walk to find a large gathering of birds in the pine trees.

1208553.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a Minnesota United FC match against the San Antonio Scorpions, including tailgating with Mazie, the teams lined up pregame, and an Atomic Data sponsorship shoutout, while criticizing Scorpions players for flopping.

1211083.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the TeamSPS Platform offsite event, showing a large conference ballroom and speakers including Peter Zaballos introducing Tyler Hamilton, Chuck Mallott discussing UX design, and Luke Samaha presenting on network math.

1211399.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the first day on TeamSPS's new office floor, showing the open-plan workspace with writable surfaces, 140+ lockers, two dev teams, scrum rooms, move-in day donuts, and a game room with a Pac-Man arcade table and bubble hockey.

1213321.abstract: Jamie attends the Wits Reunion show at the Fitzgerald Theater, sharing photos of the stage and performers beneath the Wits logo backdrop. Jamie enjoys Open Mike Eagle's performance and recommends checking out the music.

1213510.abstract: Jamie takes stock of compounding stresses eight months into the pandemic: widespread Covid-19 impact reaching rural North Dakota, business closures and job losses, reckoning with systemic racism after George Floyd's murder, and anxiety on the eve of the US election, worsened by social media's rage cycle.

1214448.abstract: Jamie shares a Peter Drucker quote passed along by a coach, in which Drucker advises a young person seeking managerial excellence to "learn to play the violin." Jamie links to a Time.com article referencing the quote and expresses agreement with valuing broad, cross-disciplinary knowledge.

1215109.abstract: Jamie shares updates and photos from SPS TechJam 2016, featuring talks by Ian Malpass of Etsy on planning for failure, an AppDynamics presentation on graphs referencing Tufte on color, and PagerDuty's Ophir Ronen on finding signal in noise.

1216499.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a Timberwolves versus Golden State Warriors game at Target Center, including a family selfie, pre-game warmups, and tip-off. Jamie notes the Wolves trailed 60-61 at halftime before tying 110-110 to force overtime.

1216698.abstract: Jamie announces the relaunch of the Link Blog, giving links shared in the Weekly Thing a permanent home. Jamie adds the Commento commenting system as an experiment, creates per-site Index pages (citing the EFF site), and plans future Annum pages showing yearly statistics.

1217856.abstract: Jamie shares impressions from attending Chaos Community Day, a conference sponsored by Netflix, DevJam, SPS Commerce, and Studio 2 Cafe, featuring talks by Andy Fleener of Sports Engine, Kent Beck, and Casey Rosenthal, and asks whether Chaos Engineering relates to DevOps as Extreme Programming does to Agile.

1217917.abstract: Jamie shares photos and impressions from Growth Summit 2021, an SPS event broadcast live from the Minneapolis Convention Center with pandemic safety precautions in place. Highlights include a keynote by Greg Bell on the question "What is Going Well?" and behind-the-scenes glimpses of production and makeup crews.

1218094.abstract: Jamie shares live updates and photos from SPS TechJam 2015's DevOps@SPS event, featuring talks by Bridget Kromhout on distributed teams and Jeff Sussna on Design Thinking, plus notes on AWS Lambda, API Gateway, and embedded tweets from colleagues attending in person and remotely.

1218755.abstract: Jamie shares photos and updates from SPS Commerce's 2020 Growth Summit, including a #TeamSPS selfie, a keynote by John Sweeney on innovative mindset, and recognition of four employees with over twenty years at the company.

1218758.abstract: Jamie shares photos and notes from a two-day #TeamSPS product platform event, covering Amy Patton's review of new tooling including Ansible, AppDynamics, Sumo Logic, Catchpoint, and Mesos, plus talks by David Hussman and Peter Zaballos on digital retail design.

1219424.abstract: Jamie shares photos and impressions from Dan Wilson's "3-Ring Binder" all-request show at Icehouse, performed solo on piano and guitar. Jamie finds the small, intimate venue and chaotic song-selection process made for a unique, enjoyable performance with crowd sing-alongs.

1220821.abstract: Jamie recounts a flight delay from KBP (Kyiv) that threatens a connection in AMS to MSP, then describes making the tight 17-minute transfer between gates E4 and E8, arriving back in Minneapolis with luggage intact.

1220823.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a cold, tailgate-style TeamSPS "Hop To It" Brew Off event, including a courtyard gathering with patio heaters and a photo posing with Pat Backen while raising beer glasses.
