1737049.abstract: Jamie reports the Things 4 Good 2022 Fall Fundraiser raised $5,217, up $460 from 2021, drawing about 100 visitors plus email orders. Proceeds were split among United Help Ukraine, Agate Housing + Services, Save the Snakes, and Free Guitars 4 Kids.

1737055.abstract: Jamie shares results from the Things 4 Good 2022 Fall Fundraiser, which raised $5,217 for four causes by selling 172 of 180 candles (in scents including new additions Tea Time, Red Hot and True North), 50 bottles of Sweet Thing Honey, and 10 Jiggy Thing Puzzles.

1744458.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy watch Ticket to Paradise at the newly renovated Edina Theatre. Jamie describes the movie as funny, enjoyable and predictable, calling it exactly what viewers would expect and reporting that both enjoyed it.

1752642.abstract: Jamie responds to Vitalik Buterin's essay on what excites Buterin about Ethereum, listing Money, DeFi, Identity, DAOs, and Hybrid Apps. Jamie reorders the list to put Identity first and adds commentary on stablecoins, Kiva lending, Endaoment, POAPs, Reddit's crypto identity efforts, Rainbow wallet, and governance flaws in DAOs like LilNouns.

1752935.abstract: Jamie recounts a conversation with a daughter who challenges Jamie to describe crypto in three words, arriving at "Common Digital Ownership." Jamie explains why digital life matters, why true ownership is hard to achieve digitally, and why decentralized, commons-based infrastructure—rather than corporations or governments—should guarantee that…

1753565.abstract: Jamie records votes on four LilNouns DAO proposals: for lowering the reserve price to 0.10 ETH, for Dot as engineering resident, against the Marketing Outreach Pilot, and for Brook as DAO Operator, noting opposition to any reserve price at all.

1754499.abstract: Jamie explains how to compile a unique list of addresses that claimed any of several POAP events, using CSV files downloaded from POAP. Jamie describes combining the CSVs with a shell loop, extracting the address column with awk, then using sort and uniq to produce a deduplicated address list.

1756613.abstract: Jamie draws a comparison to the crypto saying "not your keys, not your crypto," highlighted by the FTX fraud, to argue for a similar rule in social media: "not your domain, not your words." Jamie advises getting a personal domain and website to truly own one's writing.

1760028.abstract: Jamie quotes Sam Harris's Waking Up Daily Meditation for December 21, 2022, which asks readers to treat both a thought and the feeling of being the thinker as objects of consciousness, questioning whether a true source of attention exists or whether there is only experience.

1764763.abstract: Jamie shares five personal practices for improving online security and privacy: using 1Password for Families to manage passwords and secrets, creating unique email addresses per service via Fastmail's Masked Email feature, blocking trackers with 1Blocker, using paid search through Neeva (or DuckDuckGo as a free alternative to Google), and reading…

1764994.abstract: Jamie draws parallels between encryption and crypto as polarizing technologies that shift power from governments and corporations to individuals, citing Phil Zimmerman's PGP, the Bernstein v. United States ruling, the Apple-FBI dispute, and Bitcoin's whitepaper and Ethereum's launch.

1766224.abstract: Jamie explores "audience capture," the idea that creators gradually shape themselves to match audience feedback signals like analytics, likes, and click data.

1766447.abstract: Jamie recounts volunteering in high school for Minot Public School District's Craig Nansen, which led to involvement in Brøderbund's rare 1988 game "Where in North Dakota is Carmen Sandiego?" Jamie did page layout for the accompanying Carmen's North Dakota Almanac and links to the Screenland episode, Video Game History Foundation writeup…

1766729.abstract: Jamie describes working with style coach Nancy Dilts, arranged by Jamie's wife Tammy, spending 12 hours filtering roughly 70% of an outdated wardrobe and shopping at DXL to develop a "Tech Forward" personal style.

1767340.abstract: Jamie introduces the concept of "organizational dissonance," defined as the gap between where an organization is and where it wants to be, divided by available time. Jamie argues that culture, especially trust and integrity, determines how much dissonance an organization can handle, with faster-growing companies needing more capacity for it.

1767706.abstract: Jamie reviews goals set for the week between Christmas and New Years, including writing a daily blog post covering topics like security, encryption, audience capture, and organizational dissonance.

1767713.abstract: Jamie describes Mazie's talent for writing, noting the vivid, engaging quality of a short story shared with the family for Christmas. Jamie quotes the opening lines, about a character named Izzy Baltimore and the movement of water, and shares a photo of the printed manuscript's first chapter.

1775016.abstract: Jamie responds to a request from the December 30th POAPathon Community Call for feedback on the platform's direction in 2023, drawing on experience using POAPathon for events like a 51st birthday and a Kubb tournament.

1777722.abstract: Jamie shares a family outing to Chatime in the Mall of America for bubble tea, listing drink orders for Jamie, Tammy, Mazie, Nora, and Tyler, alongside a photo of the group holding their drinks by the Chatime sign.

1783935.abstract: Jamie outlines wishlist items for POAP, the crypto badge platform: adding RSS feeds and webhooks for event integrations, letting organizers sign events with their wallet for authenticity, supporting location-based (not just time-based) POAPs, and offering non-custodial wallets akin to Reddit's to simplify onboarding.

1786740.abstract: Jamie responds to a POAP issuer feedback survey that lacked comment fields by writing a blog post evaluating proposed premium features.

1786743.abstract: Jamie proposes three feature ideas for POAPs: adding a second image so POAPs have a front and back like challenge coins, creating official POAP collections (citing the Ethereum Merge and POAPathon Krampus POAPs as examples) that unlock bonus POAPs when completed, and allowing issuers to attach unique metadata to individual claim codes, such as…

1786750.abstract: Jamie outlines a potential tiered business model for POAP, the crypto collectible product, proposing paid plans for both collectors and issuers.

1788585.abstract: Jamie shares photos of the nearly completed remodel of the TeamSPS 5th floor, noting the team moved back to the floor this week and finds many improvements to the space.

1792770.abstract: Jamie describes falling back into compulsively checking the Twitter timeline after previously breaking the habit, and criticizes social media broadly as an addictive, reductive system built around engagement metrics rather than substance. Jamie responds by unfollowing every account on Twitter.

1800638.abstract: Jamie recaps a keynote by David Horsager of Trust Edge at the #TeamSPS 2023 Sales Kickoff, highlighting Horsager's Eight Pillars of Trust: clarity, compassion, character, competency, commitment, connection, contribution, and consistency.

1801541.abstract: Jamie describes the new POAP Family feature, which reveals overlapping POAP holders between events. Checking a 50th Birthday POAP, Jamie finds 7 shared holders with "Cryptog's HODLER" and 13 of 34 holders also share a 51st Birthday POAP, noting graph analysis like this builds connection.

1801555.abstract: Jamie describes an evening at The Great Northern's K'óoben pop-up at Glass House, a collaboration among chefs Gustavo Romero, José Alarcón, and Noe Lara with mixologists and guest chefs exploring Latin cuisine in Minnesota winter. Jamie calls every dish and drink amazing and recommends the featured restaurants.

1801626.abstract: Jamie marks the launch of Echo Forest, an NFT project with Minneapolis ties led by Brooks Clifford and Matt Benesch, by minting two Wolf Healers (numbers 18 and 19). Jamie likes the artwork, is curious how the utility develops, and values supporting a local project.

1802521.abstract: Jamie recommends the film Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris, describing it as a delightful, fun story enjoyed by the whole family, alongside the movie's poster showing a cheerful woman striding before the Eiffel Tower.

1802527.abstract: Jamie describes a first visit to Art Shanty Projects on Lake Harriet with Tammy, who has attended many times before. Jamie highlights shanties including re(center)ed, Archive of Collective Memory, Blankets of Ice, Chapsicle of Love, and Techno From the Sun, and suggests a future shanty could distribute a POAP and record memories.

1802746.abstract: Jamie criticizes the Indieweb POSSE (publish on your own site, syndicate everywhere) approach, arguing that syndication platforms like Twitter and micro.blog distort writing choices—limiting photos, prioritizing certain links, and dropping titles.

1804603.abstract: Jamie attends the Minneapolis Downtown Council Annual Meeting, held back in the Armory for the first time since 2020. Outgoing chair Mike Ryan welcomes new chair Karin Lucas from SPS Commerce, and Jamie notes SPS is downtown's 10th largest employer with 1,346 people.

1804608.abstract: Jamie highlights three kinds of listening described by Carolyn Coughlin in the "Become a Better Listener" episode (157) of the Knowledge Project Podcast: Listening to Win, Listening to Learn, and Listening to Fix.

1806186.abstract: Jamie discusses growth in Minnestar's Community Supporter program, following a conversation with Executive Director Maria Boland Ploessl, and proposes expansions beyond guaranteed event tickets.

1809073.abstract: Jamie describes a visit to the Ice Palace at Fountain Hills Winery, including dinner with wood fired pizza, walking through ice tunnels, watching fire performers, and eating mini donuts, with Jamie suspecting the visit will become a family tradition.

1809079.abstract: Jamie recounts a birthday escape room outing for Tyler at Mission Manor, playing the Countdown room with three others. The group escapes in 45m 55s with no clues used, earning a score of 2,240 points and the top "Escape Gods" rating, just 60 points short of the room record.

1813588.abstract: Jamie donates to the Unicode Consortium's Adopt a Character campaign, choosing the Thinking Face emoji, and shares a bronze sponsor badge received in return. Jamie suggests the program would be more compelling if it issued NFTs, with limited Gold and Silver tiers and open-edition Bronze levels.

1813622.abstract: Jamie sees To Kill a Mockingbird at the Orpheum Theatre, featuring a new screenplay by Aaron Sorkin and direction by Bartlett Sher. Jamie calls the performance incredible and powerful, praising Richard Thomas, known for playing "John-Boy" on The Waltons, as Atticus Finch.

1813627.abstract: Jamie and Tammy drive to Buffalo, MN for a macaron class at Abundant Kitchen taught by owner Becki Melvie, using a recipe learned from Nikkolette's Macarons. Jamie describes the process as fussy but not overly complicated, and shares photos of the blue shells made in class and orange shells filled with lemon curd and cream.

1818507.abstract: Jamie shares a movie night watching Netflix's Dog Gone, prompted by Tammy's watchlist and a recommendation after seeing the Walker family's blog post about it. Jamie calls it a good movie about growing up, parent-child relationships, and a great dog.

1818511.abstract: Jamie describes continuing a "snowpocalypse" movie series after over a foot of fresh snow, watching "Who Invited Charlie?," a film revisiting COVID-19 lockdowns as a wealthy family flees New York City for the Hamptons and is joined by visitor Charlie.

1818512.abstract: Jamie's family watches The Bad Guys to close out a three-night "snowpocalypse" movie series, an unusually rare feat for the Thingelstad household. Jamie notes the animated film's callbacks to heist movies like Oceans 11, admitting to nodding off a couple of times.

1818519.abstract: Jamie describes receiving three Ukrainian postage stamps as a gift from a team member visiting Minneapolis. The stamps commemorate the Russian Warship on Snake Island, the Crimean Bridge blast, and "Kherson is Ukraine!"

1818520.abstract: Jamie describes hosting the MnTech Q1 2023 Tech Leadership Forum on "Generative AI: Harnessing Disruption into Innovation," joined by Todd Van Nurden (Microsoft), Sam Pierson (Talend), and Tammylynne Jonas (Donaldson), discussing why generative AI is emerging now, its effect on software development, organizational opportunities and risks, and its…

1824880.abstract: Jamie recounts attending a Mason Jennings show at The Dakota, noting familiarity with the songs from Jennings's first album, and shares photos of Jennings performing on acoustic guitar and piano on the dimly lit stage.

1824886.abstract: Jamie and Tammy Thingelstad's wife Tammy dine at Nordic Village on Riva Terrace, sampling a 7-course meal including a cheese and charcuterie board, onion soup, rösti potatoes with smoked salmon, cheese fondue, and chicken cooked three ways after requesting an alternative to the clams dish, finishing with house-made s'mores in an outdoor cabin…

1825186.abstract: Jamie describes creating multiple Ethereum addresses to isolate crypto activity, moving beyond the single thingelstad.eth identity.

1825217.abstract: Jamie describes moving NFT assets to newly organized Ethereum addresses following an earlier post on isolating crypto assets.

1825280.abstract: Jamie announces that all Minnebar 17 attendees, presenters, and organizers will receive a POAP (Proof of Attendance Protocol) token via claim code, in addition to POAP holders being eligible for a raffle.

1825291.abstract: Jamie announces a planned Minnebar 17 session, "How to Newsletter: Lessons from 250 Issues of The Weekly Thing," but notes an update that it was cancelled due to travel plans, though a separate POAP session will still happen.

1825294.abstract: Jamie announces hosting a session at Minnebar 17 titled "Creating Digital Community with POAPs," listed on the Minnestar Sessionizer, marking a return to hosting after several years.

1830115.abstract: Jamie marks 20 years of Olson Family Vacations, a tradition started in 2004 by Tammy's side of the family, with hosting duties rotating among families. Jamie shares photos of a commemorative t-shirt listing all 20 vacation locations from Grand Superior Lodge in 2004 to Fergus Falls in 2023, and notes the milestone was also celebrated with a POAP.

1837257.abstract: Jamie recounts a day in New York City covering 19,922 steps and 10.01 miles, including bagels at Liberty Bagel, ferry visits to the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island to research Josef Gins on the manifest, the 9/11 Memorial & Museum, dinner at Shake Shack, and seeing Harry Potter and the Cursed Child.

1837770.abstract: Jamie recounts a day in New York covering 21,964 steps, with stops including Andrew's NYC, Paris Baguette, Angelina for macarons, the Nintendo Store, Apple's Fifth Avenue store, Milk Bar, and the Museum of Mathematics. The day also includes dinner with Hadar and Lois at El Rio Grande and completing the Sugar Rush room at Exit Escape Room NYC.

1838833.abstract: Jamie recounts a partial final day in New York, logging 10,069 steps and 4.6 miles: checking out of Arlo Midtown, breakfast at Andrews NYC, walking the Highline, a closed Milk Bar, macarons from Angelo's Paris, and lunch at Sunday Supper before flying home on DL1529.

1842626.abstract: Jamie and Tyler visit Nintendo New York on a Sunday at opening time, spending 90 minutes exploring the store's Nintendo history displays, character statues, and merchandise, including selfies with Link and Bowser.

1845281.abstract: Jamie announces a POAP raffle for Minnebar 17 (April 22nd), run in partnership with StayNftyMpls, founded by Erik Halaas, giving away 32 NFTs from the 612 Series depicting Twin Cities landmarks like the Foshay Tower, Stone Arch Bridge, and Al's Breakfast to attendees who collect event POAPs.

1845949.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy attend the 10th Annual Building on Dreams fundraiser for Avenues for Youth, emceed by Shayla Reaves, with remarks from Katherine Meerse and Princess Titus of Appetite for Change, plus performances by Known MPLS.

1850640.abstract: Jamie describes assembling a complete collection of all 32 landmarks from the 612 Series, an NFT project by local artist Erik Halaas of StayNftyMpls, noting Al's Breakfast as the rarest piece with only 2 minted.

238104.abstract: Jamie describes a first visit to Martina Restaurant, praising the space and a seat near the woodfire grill. Jamie highlights the Crab Cakes, Pork Chop Pizzaiola, Fusilli with Lamb Shoulder, and Panqueque dessert, and notes reasonable prices plus a kids menu and mocktails for future family visits.

2569270.abstract: Jamie describes attending the Aspirations in Computing annual award ceremony celebrating young women's achievements, and notes that four award winners will join TeamSPS internships at SPS Commerce this summer. Jamie links to accounts of similar events from 2016, 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2024.

2845246.abstract: Jamie describes ringing the Nasdaq closing bell with the SPS Commerce executive team and spouses, including Tammy, marking the 13th listing anniversary and Jamie's approaching ten-year anniversary with SPS.

2912222.abstract: Jamie recaps day one of a New York City birthday trip for Tammy, covering the flight from MSP to EWR, checking into the Hyatt Centric Times Square, and stops including Dough donuts, the Nintendo Store, St Patrick's Cathedral, the LEGO Store, Central Park, and Levain Bakery.

2912223.abstract: Jamie logs a rainy day two of Tammy's NYC birthday trip, covering 17,823 steps: Angelina bakery, brunch with Greg and Annique at Frankies, a wet Brooklyn Bridge walk, MOMA amid crowds, Harry Potter, and late-night Joe's Pizza after long lines elsewhere.

2912224.abstract: Jamie recounts a rainy day-three itinerary of Tammy's NYC birthday trip, covering 18,065 steps through Liberty Bagels, B&H, Whole Foods, the High Line, Chelsea Market, the Apple Store, Milk Bar, a movie at Regal Battery Park, dinner at El Vez, and an escape room.

2912225.abstract: Jamie recounts the fourth day of Tammy's NYC birthday trip, including a hotel work meeting, breakfast at Ole & Steen, visits to Bryant Park and the NY Public Library, Blue Bottle coffee, and a return to Angelina bakery before flying Delta 2589 from Newark to Minneapolis.

2926109.abstract: Jamie attends the MnTech Tech Connect 2023 event, describing sessions on AI, cybersecurity, and innovation featuring speakers including Matt Versaggi, Dr. Jayshree Seth, Aaron Warner, and Charles Betz, plus a panel on business success moderated by Jeff Tollefson.

2943892.abstract: Jamie shares excitement about attending Brandi Carlile's Mothership Weekend in Miramar Beach, Florida, listing the festival lineup: Carlile, Nathaniel Rateliff & The Night Sweats, Danielle Ponder, Hozier, Mavis Staples, The Milk Carton Kids, Katie Pruitt, Emmylou Harris, and Fancy Hagood across three days.

2961441.abstract: Jamie shares photos of a tiny 3D-printed Bitcoin ATM seen at Bitcoin 2023, which accepted pennies and dispensed 99 sats via Lightning Network.

2962453.abstract: Jamie describes creating a Shortcuts app called My QR Codes, inspired by someone at Bitcoin 2023 sharing a LinkedIn QR code. Jamie shares a link to the shortcut, explains customizing its Dictionary with personal links, and notes it can be added to the Home Screen for easy sharing.

2964305.abstract: Jamie describes first-hand experience with Bitcoin Lightning at the Bitcoin 2023 conference in Miami Beach, using Wallet of Satoshi funded via Strike to pay for coffee and empanadas through an IBEX terminal.

3065485.abstract: Jamie describes coming up with the name "Bison & Bitcoin" for a fictional newsletter and, for fun, asks GPT-4 to write a description and DALL-E to generate a cover image, both of which are quoted and shown, tying bison and Bitcoin together through themes of resilience, innovation, and self-reliance.

3065491.abstract: Jamie shares photos of TeamSPS coworkers in Ukraine celebrating Vyshyvanka Day, an international holiday honoring traditional embroidered vyshyvanka clothing, with more images linked on Instagram. Jamie plans to find a vyshyvanka to wear for the next celebration.

3065512.abstract: After gaining hands-on experience with Bitcoin Lightning, Jamie outlines six micropayment use cases: home allowance economies for kids, spam-deterring email payments, Little Free Library tip QR codes, automated creator tips, private subscriptions via invoices, and fridges that self-fund a year of electricity.

3065517.abstract: Jamie shares Board Search Criteria used by Constellation Software, highlighted in the company's 2017 President's Letter, recreating the primary points of the table covering three categories: The Role, The Candidate, and Experience, spanning traits like long-term orientation, cultural fit, and prior experience building large organizations.

3095012.abstract: Jamie marks 19 years of blogging at thingelstad.com, noting 8,186 posts totaling 493,751 words, and observes the site predates the iPhone, Bitcoin, and Instagram. A chart shows annual post counts peaking near 820 in 2008 and around 250 in 2023.

3098324.abstract: Jamie recounts visiting the Edina Art Fair with Tammy despite hot weather, highlighting standout artists including Mark Eliason, Faith Mebli's large wood carvings, Carla Bank's Blackbird piece, and Andrew Carson's kinetic sculptures, noting Carson's upcoming retirement.

3107122.abstract: Jamie shares family reactions to the Apple Vision Pro after watching its WWDC segment together. Tammy expresses excitement mixed with concern about where it leads, Mazie calls it exciting but destructive to humankind, Tyler wants to try it, and Jamie asks when one can be purchased.

3136557.abstract: Jamie quotes two Economist Espresso dispatches (June 7 and 8, 2023) on the destruction of Ukraine's Kakhovka dam, noting tens of thousands evacuated, mutual Russia-Ukraine blame, and UN warnings.

3160722.abstract: Jamie argues that URLs routinely embed hidden surveillance and tracking data, citing an Instagram link with 302 characters of tracking parameters like utm_campaign and fbclid attached to a 28-character link.

3160741.abstract: Jamie highlights a Kickstarter campaign by photographer Layne Kennedy for a new book, Beyond the Light: The Stories Behind The Photographs, a collection drawn from 40 years of work. Jamie recalls meeting Kennedy through a 2009 dog sledding photography workshop arranged by Tammy and quotes Kennedy's advice: "Every photo tells a story.

3193857.abstract: Jamie quotes an Economist Espresso item from June 12, 2023, noting that Andreessen Horowitz will open its first international office in London to focus on crypto and blockchain investments, viewing Britain as more hospitable than American regulators.

3259062.abstract: Jamie describes celebrating Mazie's 18th birthday, highlighting Tammy's idea of revisiting all 17 previous birthdays with photos and gift memories, plus a visit to Shady Oak Beach, lunch at Yum!, and a return to Zero Hour Escape Rooms.

3259078.abstract: Jamie describes a surprise carnival Jamie's wife Tammy organized to celebrate Mazie's 18th birthday and high school graduation, featuring games like Ring Toss, Bean Bags, Musical Chairs and Duck Pick, plus raffles, a bouncy house, photo booth, ice cream truck, airbrush tattoos and a balloon artist.

3263769.abstract: Jamie describes a Juneteenth celebration for TeamSPS featuring snacks, beverages, ice cream, games, and a raffle. The post names Black-owned businesses involved, including 3 Leche Kombucha, Michael Lavelle Wine, Montgomery Brewing, The Dripping Root, Old Southern Smokehouse, Symphony Potato Chips, 2 Scoops Ice Cream Eatery, Candy with a Twist…

3304569.abstract: Jamie describes a last-minute decision to attend Taylor Swift's Eras Tour after brother-in-law Hector's glowing report from the night before. Jamie's wife Tammy suggests checking for tickets, and floor seats are secured on SeatGeek at 6:24pm, transferred via Ticketmaster minutes later, in time for the 7:50pm show.

3304571.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the Taylor Swift Eras Tour show at US Bank Stadium, including a family selfie taken while leaving the floor and a shot of the stage teardown crew clearing the venue just 28 minutes and 39 seconds later. Jamie notes finding a merch table and remarks on how fast the teardown crew works.

3307181.abstract: Jamie shares a video short titled "Betwixt" by Minneapolis artist Matt Semke, who works under the name catswilleatyou, and finds the accompanying music haunting.

3315441.abstract: Jamie praises Matt Langford's Tiny Theme for Micro.blog and its integration of Vincent Ritter's Tinylytics service, then proposes a $50/year Micro.blog Community Fund that would distribute money to theme and plugin developers, tagging creator Manton with the idea.

3319930.abstract: Jamie and Tammy hike 5.3 miles with about 900 ft of elevation gain at Murphy-Hanrehan Park Reserve, finishing in 2h 8m, as preparation for an upcoming Switzerland hiking trip. Jamie links to the Strava activity and shares photos from the trail.

3328723.abstract: Jamie outlines steps taken to preserve online writing indefinitely, including publishing with micro.blog and Buttondown, avoiding corporate platforms, and regularly exporting archives from micro.blog, Buttondown, and Pinboard.

3399479.abstract: Jamie logs the first day of a Switzerland and Italy trip: a Lyft to MSP, Shake Shack cheeseburgers, Mazie getting a quesadilla, and Delta flight DL162 departing for Amsterdam at 7:50pm, switching to Central European Time.

3400623.abstract: Jamie logs the first day of a Switzerland and Italy trip: flights through Amsterdam to Zurich, checking into Motel One Zurich, a Tuk Tuk fondue tour, and a walk around the old city before an early night.

3401509.abstract: Jamie logs day two of a Switzerland & Italy trip: visiting Lindt Home of Chocolate in Kilchberg, training through Zurich HB to Scuol, and meeting hiking guides Dave and Erik for a four course dinner at Hotel Guardaval. Jamie's wife Tammy publishes a first blog post in over 11 years.

3405111.abstract: Jamie logs day three of a Switzerland and Italy trip: breakfast at Hotel Guardaval, a hike from Scuol toward Guarda ending at Ardez, train and bus travel to Hotel Meisser in Guarda, and dinner there, with warm sunny weather cooling in the evening.

3405116.abstract: Jamie describes hiking 10.7 miles from Scuol to Guarda in 5 hours 25 minutes, arriving at the Messier Lodge, and shares photos from the trip as part of the Switzerland & Italy 2023 collection, noting an earlier 2004 hike of the same route.

3407876.abstract: Jamie describes day two of the Engadine hiking trip, an out-and-back hike from Guarda toward Piz Buin to Chamonna Tuoi, featuring a steep 1,600-foot climb in the first 90 minutes and a lunch of rösti and grilled cheese. The post is part of the Switzerland & Italy 2023 collection and links to an earlier hike from the Europe 2004 collection.

3407891.abstract: Jamie logs day four of a Switzerland and Italy trip, describing a lost wallet that guide Dave fails to recover, a hike up Piz Buin, a mountain scooter descent, cold-water foot therapy, and dinner at Meisser Hotel.

3407893.abstract: Jamie describes stopping at one of the many water fountains found throughout the Engadine Valley, known for delicious, ice-cold drinking water, and soaking sore feet in it after hiking, finding the cold immersion painful but effective for relief. A photo shows a young woman in a Sunshine t-shirt soaking her feet in a stone fountain.

3408358.abstract: Jamie recounts losing a wallet in Ardez while hiking, likely misplaced near a train station after giving Tyler cash for ice cream. Despite guide Dave retracing the route and the hotel calling around, the wallet isn't found; Jamie notes 1Password's "Wallet" tag made inventorying lost items easy, with spending money the main loss.

3410111.abstract: Jamie describes a hike taken via train and funicular up to Segantini Hütte, followed by a mountain traverse and a cold, rainy descent by chair lift into Pontresina. The post is part of the Switzerland & Italy 2023 collection and links back to a 2004 hike from Zuoz to Pontresina.

3410145.abstract: Jamie logs day 5 of a Switzerland and Italy trip, hiking from Guarda via funicular to Segantini Hütte for lunch, then rushing down to a chair lift ahead of an approaching mountain storm before a rainy walk back to the hotel.

3411447.abstract: Jamie recounts recovering a wallet lost in Guarda, Switzerland, after Martin Lienhard commented on LinkedIn saying it was found. Martin's wife discovered it near a fountain the group had dipped feet in, and Jamie retrieved it from the local Volg store.

3412594.abstract: Jamie logs day six of a Switzerland and Italy trip, describing a split itinerary: family hikes from Pontresina to Lake Hahnensee and Silvaplana, while Jamie recovers a lost wallet in Guarda, walks to Nietzsche's Rock in Sils Maria, then reunites with family for art viewing and dinner at Hotel Edelweiss.

3412629.abstract: Jamie shares photos the family took while hiking from Pontresina to Sils Maria, passing Lake Hahnensee, while Jamie stayed behind to handle a wallet recovery mission. The post is part of the Switzerland & Italy 2023 collection and links to a similar 2004 hike from the Europe 2004 collection.

3414558.abstract: Jamie logs day 7 of a Switzerland and Italy trip: a hike above the treeline past Grevasalvas village and around a lake, followed by shopping and coffee in Sils Maria and dinner with Tammy, Mazie and Tyler, capped by apple strudel.

3414562.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a hike through the village of Grevasalvas in Switzerland, noting the small cluster of houses was used in the production of "Heidi" and describing the visit as like stepping backwards in time.

3414581.abstract: Jamie describes a hike from the Hotel Edelweiss out of Sils Maria on a gradual ascent above the tree line, passing through Grevasalvas, resting at the top, then returning along the lake, covering just over 9.5 miles.

3416425.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a sixth and final day of hiking into the town of Soglio, part of the Switzerland & Italy 2023 collection, also linking to a similar 2004 hike from Casaccia to Soglio.

3421758.abstract: Jamie logs day 8 of a Switzerland and Italy trip: hiking from Vicosoprano to Soglio through a thunderstorm, waterfalls, and a Roman road, with Tyler falling twice and Jamie once on slippery rocks. The group explores Soglio, shops at Soglio Products, waits out rain at Palazzo Salis, and shares a final group dinner.

3421760.abstract: Jamie logs day nine of the Switzerland & Italy trip: leaving Soglio, taking buses and trains through Promontogna, Chiavenna, Colico and Varenna to Milan, then doing an escape room at Mad Machines before returning to the iQ Motel.

3427282.abstract: Jamie recounts day ten of the Switzerland and Italy trip, spent on "Ferrari Day" touring the Enzo Ferrari Museum in Modena and the museum in Maranello, followed by a factory tour, an escape room called Time Machine, and pizza at Pizzeria Fabrico in Milan.

3427283.abstract: Jamie logs day 11 of a Switzerland and Italy trip: touring Milan's Duomo and Galleria Vittorio Emanuele, coffee at Marchesi, dodging a thunderstorm, then training to Venice, checking into Combo hotel, and walking the city at golden hour.

3430830.abstract: Jamie logs day 12 of a Switzerland and Italy trip, describing a Venice in a Day tour with a gondola ride, lunch at Ristorante Chianti, the Doge Palace, and an evening Pastry Tour with guide Maria despite an injured leg.

3441175.abstract: Jamie logs day 13 of a Switzerland and Italy trip, describing a lagoon excursion to Burano and Murano with guide Christiano, including lace-making, colorful houses, wine tasting, and glass blowing, followed by exploring Venice's alleys and dinner at Birraria La Corte.

3444793.abstract: Jamie logs day 14 of a Switzerland and Italy trip, traveling by water taxi and train from Venice to Florence, checking into Arté Boutique Hotel, and recreating a wedding photo for a 21st anniversary. The day ends with a Tuscan hills pizza and gelato cooking class with Tammy, Mazie, and Tyler.

3444815.abstract: Jamie logs day fifteen in Florence: viewing Michelangelo's David, touring the Duomo, and Mazie's solo climb to the dome's top. The family also takes an e-bike Tuscany tour, tastes olive oil at Chalet Fontana, and dines at Ristorante Natalino.

3448091.abstract: Jamie logs a hot, sunny day in Florence: a pasta cooking class with Accidental Tourist, an unsuccessful search for honey at Chalet Fontana, gelato at Venchi, shopping, and pizza dinner before strolling near the Duomo at night.

3450080.abstract: Jamie recalls the final evening of the Switzerland & Italy trip, walking around the Duomo in Florence with daughter Mazie and "breathing it all in," a ritual that began with waterfalls in Iceland. Jamie notes this marks the last family vacation before Mazie leaves for college.

3450281.abstract: Jamie recounts the final travel day home from Florence, including Tyler briefly forgetting Pokémon gifts at the airport, a delayed KLM CityHopper flight to Amsterdam, and a sprint to catch the connecting Delta flight to Minneapolis before arriving home.

3492102.abstract: Jamie describes attending Farmhilly 8, an annual event hosted by friend and fellow Minnestar Catalyzer Adrienne Peirce on an eight-acre property, featuring live bands, yard games, food, and kids' activities. Jamie notes finally attending after years of missing it, including a long cornhole game the boys won 21-20.

3502489.abstract: Jamie shares a photo of a handwritten journal entry, written on a reMarkable 2 paper tablet, describing first impressions of the device shortly after getting one.

3502821.abstract: Jamie describes bringing Tyler to work for a lunch meeting with Archie Black, CEO, after Tyler expressed interest in a 1:1 conversation. Archie and Tyler exchanged questions over lunch at the Minneapolis Club, and Archie gave Tyler a Chelsea FC soccer ball from an office collection.

3505551.abstract: Jamie links to the Making Sense podcast episode "Health & Longevity," where Sam Harris interviews Peter Attia about the book Outlive: The Science and Art of Longevity, covering topics like healthspan, diet, exercise, heart disease, and cancer.

3508103.abstract: Jamie marks Ukraine's 32nd year of independence and the 547th day of fighting Russia's invasion, recommending a Kyiv Independent membership for English-language news and linking to its article "Everything you didn't know about Ukraine's flag." Jamie shares a photo wearing a Kyiv Archangel shirt and a Ukraine-colored heart pin from a team in Kyiv.

3509300.abstract: Jamie describes a Mason Jennings album release show at the Parkway Theater, featuring a mix of new and old songs and performances by Dan Lawonn on bass and cello. The crowd's enthusiasm brought Jennings back for two encores.

3513261.abstract: Jamie describes a family visit to the Minnesota Renaissance Festival, revisiting favorite activities like Jacob's Ladder, cheese curds, Turtles on a stick, and a beef stick.

3514513.abstract: Jamie describes a fast-paced Minnesota State Fair visit squeezed into two hours before a Brandi Carlile concert at the Grandstand, checking off stops including Sweet Martha's Cookies, Baba's, the Fine Arts and Dairy Buildings, crop art, and the Giant Slide.

3520739.abstract: Jamie recounts seeing Brandi Carlile perform at the Minnesota State Fair, calling it the best fair concert attended and one of Carlile's best shows.

3521563.abstract: Jamie describes a daily practice of "blog gardening," using an OmniFocus routine to curate the archive from nearly 20 years of blogging. Each day Jamie visits the On This Day page to fix typos, repair broken links and images, add context, merge short posts, and link entries to Collections or Lists.

3522052.abstract: Jamie reacts to WordPress.com's newly announced 100-Year Plan for hosting websites, calling it the most significant offering of its kind from a trustworthy organization, and breaks down the $38,000 cost into domain and WordPress VIP hosting fees to argue it's reasonably priced.

3528641.abstract: Jamie reflects on a 17-year relationship with Twitter, joined in 2006 as user #82,903, recalling early SMS tweeting and a temperature-reporting bot. Jamie credits Elon Musk's transformation of Twitter into X with finally ending the addiction, noting no interest in the new platform, and thanks Musk separately for Tesla and SpaceX.

3561318.abstract: Jamie announces the Weekly Thing Forum, a new space to extend discussion beyond the Weekly Thing newsletter after six years of publishing it.

3561329.abstract: Jamie recaps TeamSPS's 5th Annual Kubb Tournament, with 96 players across 16 teams competing in round-robin play and four brackets. Jamie notes custom SPS-branded Kubb sets from JP's Backyard Games, a POAP for attendees, and lists bracket winners including EDI Emperors and Simply the Best.

3561901.abstract: Jamie describes building an Apple Shortcuts automation using S3 Files to shrink blog images before they appear in the Weekly Thing newsletter's Journal section, resizing them to 1,200 pixels and uploading them to files.thingelstad.com.

3562215.abstract: Jamie details a revamped Shortcuts-based automation system for producing the Weekly Thing newsletter, using Drafts, Data Jar, S3 App, and the Pinboard API to assemble sections into Markdown. The rebuild made the process cross-platform, Python-free, more durable with error handling, and automated the previously manual photo section.

3572213.abstract: Jamie shares a Mac Shortcut called "Launch Apps" that opens a preferred set of applications, like Mail, Calendar, and Drafts, from the menubar. Jamie provides the shortcut file as a starting point for building custom automations, part of the Shortcuts Collection.

3573157.abstract: Jamie describes the project management system behind the Weekly Thing newsletter, built in OmniFocus using Getting Things Done principles.

3599939.abstract: Jamie discusses the common gap between purchasing a physical product, like a Tesla, and being able to use its companion app before the item arrives. Jamie praises Eight Sleep for handling this well, letting customers set up accounts early, track order status, and see a checklist of items needed before delivery.

3599972.abstract: Jamie describes an evening at Squash Blossom Farm near Oronoco, Minnesota, attending a Farm-to-Table dinner hosted with Sod House Theater, featuring comedic skits, an accordion player, mead tastings, and simple, well-prepared dishes like spinach salad and crepes.

3601042.abstract: Jamie explains the process for finding links included in the Weekly Thing newsletter, describing three stages: collecting via Safari Reading List, Feedbin RSS feeds, Pinboard Popular, and newsletters; reading and filtering during free moments; and curating selected links into Pinboard descriptions using markdown, tagged _feature or _brief for use…

3612357.abstract: Jamie compares sleep stage data from the Oura Ring and a newly set up Eight Sleep device over three nights, finding the two sources correlate more than expected.

3612361.abstract: Jamie attends the 2023 Youth in Music Show at US Bank Stadium to watch a nephew perform with Grand Rapids High School's marching band, viewing all AAA and AAAA competition performances from schools including Papillion-La Vista South, Farmington, Irondale, Eden Prairie, and Eastview.

3612366.abstract: Jamie describes trying Agave's Savings xDai on Gnosis Chain, connected to MakerDAO's Dai stablecoin and DAI Savings Rate. Jamie deposits 100 xDai to receive Agave sDai tokens earning 7.521% APY, noting limited prior DeFi experimentation.

3619157.abstract: Jamie recounts the history of Road Sign Math, a site started in 2005 after spotting a mathematically significant I-94 sign (3×33=99), which grew to include contributors, scoring, and a wiki before shutting down in 2016. Jamie announces a simpler reboot at roadsignmath.xyz using MathJax, without the old scoring system.

3650507.abstract: Jamie orders two new iMacs to replace an aging 27" Intel iMac from 2019 and one from 2017, the latter unable to upgrade to macOS Sonoma. Following Apple's "Scary Fast" event announcing M3 chips, Jamie chooses blue and orange models, each with 24GB unified memory and 2TB SSD storage.

3690288.abstract: Jamie describes attending SPS Growth Summit 2024 with over 1,500 North American team members at the Minneapolis Convention Center, marking Chad Collins's first Growth Summit as CEO and featuring a keynote from Mike Walsh, alongside photos of the stage and event production.

3691389.abstract: Jamie describes switching the cabin's camera setup from Nest to Ubiquiti UniFi Protect after installing a UniFi network and Dream Router, replacing an unsatisfactory HomeKit attempt.

3691458.abstract: Jamie reports the Things 4 Good 2023 fall candle sale raised $5,755 from 52 donors, a 10% increase over 2022, split among Oceanites ($1,675), Food Recovery Network ($1,462.50), Heart to Care Tanzania ($1,367.50) and American Prairie ($1,250), each championed by a family member.

3705992.abstract: Jamie attends a Good Leadership Breakfast featuring Archie Black, marking a first visit to the event. Jamie highlights Archie's success habits: putting people first through training and education, staying focused on core priorities, and staying calm under pressure.

3708469.abstract: Jamie predicts Microsoft will acquire OpenAI following Sam Altman's firing by the OpenAI board and subsequent hiring by Satya Nadella at Microsoft.

3709430.abstract: Jamie collects tweets from OpenAI, Sam Altman, and Satya Nadella announcing Altman's return as CEO under a new board chaired by Bret Taylor, alongside Larry Summers and Adam D'Angelo, plus a DALL-E image and links to coverage from Om Malik, Ars Technica, Daring Fireball, The Verge, The Atlantic, and Stratechery.

3714350.abstract: Jamie analyzes data from the 3rd annual Things 4 Good Fall Fundraiser, which raised nearly $6,000 across 55 candle purchases with eight scents, up from six and four in prior years.

3714714.abstract: Prompted by a question from Alex, Jamie names three favorite iPhones: the original for being first in line at Southdale Mall, the iPhone 4 for its design and retina display, and the iPhone Xs for removing the home button. Jamie also lists every iPhone owned, from the original through the iPhone 14 Pro.

3781865.abstract: Jamie describes attending the 2023 New Standards Holiday Show, a yearly tradition, noting returning and new special guests and a closing performance of "Christmastime Next Year." Jamie shares photos of the ensemble, costumed performers, and links to past holiday show recaps.

3782725.abstract: Jamie describes a first visit to Heimie's Haberdashery in St. Paul, recommended by style coach Nancy Dilts as follow-up homework from a 2022 style coaching experience. Jamie's wife Tammy scheduled the appointment, and Richard Shallbetter took measurements for a custom suit, letting Jamie choose the fabric combinations. Jamie plans to return.

3782730.abstract: Jamie describes signing up for Ridwell, a service noticed on white boxes around the neighborhood, after Jamie's wife Tammy identified it as a way to properly recycle plastics and other items that normally end up in the trash.

3785490.abstract: Jamie upgrades three Macs, an iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch to OmniFocus 4.0 the day it releases, calling it central to a GTD system. Jamie notes a streamlined interface, improved perspectives, and a newly independent, usable Apple Watch app.

3787307.abstract: Jamie announces participation in Manuel Moreale's People and Blogs project, with issue 16 featuring Jamie Thingelstad published at manuelmoreale.com. Jamie lists the 15 previous interviewees and links to sign-up and RSS options for the newsletter.

3793752.abstract: Jamie shares a Strava "2023 Year in Sport" summary, linking to the recap and including an embedded photo collection highlighting the year's athletic activity.

3797529.abstract: Jamie describes a first visit to Sam's Christmas Village and Light Show, featuring 12 million lights, music, concessions, hot cocoa, and Santa visits, calling it a favorite holiday light display. Photos show illuminated Santa sculptures, a LOVE sign, snowmen, a globe, and an LED tank display.

3800653.abstract: Jamie watches Wonka, the origin story of Willy Wonka starring Timothée Chalamet, and finds the movie great, praising Chalamet's performance. Jamie criticizes the chosen theater for dirty seats, debris, and noisy patrons, and imagines an ideal screening paired with chocolates timed to match scenes and flavors from the film.

3800827.abstract: Jamie describes winning the eBay auction for a "10 of 10" museum quality brass plaque, one of items Jeff Atwood auctioned in the blog post "I Fight For The Users." The plaque features the famous @Horse_ebooks tweet "Everything happens so much," with proceeds benefiting The Trevor Project.

3800916.abstract: Jamie describes collecting 35 pieces from Erik Halaas's 612 Series NFT project (StayNftyMpls) and being the only person to own one of every landmark. To celebrate, Erik created a physical block painting of 612 Series #134, Cherry and Spoon, which Jamie plans to frame alongside a print of the NFT.

3814627.abstract: Jamie finishes reading Notes on Complexity by Neil Theise, a short book connecting complexity theory to consciousness, and finds parallels with Buddhism and Sam Harris's Waking Up. Jamie highlights Theise's idealism argument and the claim that AI may achieve intelligence without true consciousness.

3819388.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy watch the film Ferrari, directed by Michael Mann and starring Adam Driver, Penelope Cruz and Shailene Woodley. Jamie notes recognizing Modena filming locations from a prior Italy trip and finds the Mille Miglia crash scene highlights the dangers of early motor racing.

3821206.abstract: Jamie describes a tradition, started at 50th birthday, of issuing a POAP token each year as a gift to others, now done three years running with a different artist commissioned via a POAPathon bounty each time.

3829707.abstract: Jamie links to a Wall Street Journal article reporting the SEC's approval of Bitcoin ETFs for everyday investors, noting Bitcoin trading at $46,611. Jamie calls the move a credibility boost, and raises questions about its effect on Bitcoin demand, MicroStrategy (MSTR), and Ethereum and other blockchains.

3837972.abstract: Jamie describes testing POAP's new beta onboarding process, activated for a 52nd Birthday drop, which lets people reserve a token via email and then either mint to an existing wallet or "Create an account" to get a new non-custodial wallet powered by Privy, complete with an ENS name.

3838191.abstract: Jamie describes using Wallet of Satoshi as a Bitcoin Lightning wallet since a first purchase at Bitcoin Miami, including onboarding about 20 people by gifting 1,000 sats each.

3841154.abstract: Jamie interviews Erik Halaas, creator of the 612 Series NFT collection depicting Minneapolis landmarks like the Witches Tower and Stone Arch Bridge, covering the project's inspiration from Bright Moments' CryptoCitizens, landmark selection, Excel-based creation process, and the Hewing Hotel gallery show blending digital and physical art.

3849714.abstract: Jamie shares and archives the obituary of Tammy's father, Don Olson, who died January 17, 2024 at age 85 after a long battle with COPD. The obituary details Don's life running Mel-O Honey, coaching softball, and family, plus visitation and memorial service information; Jamie also includes a memorial video created by Angie Lundeen.

3856929.abstract: Jamie describes starting a serious investigation of Obsidian, prompted by a post from Daniel Tan calling it "indispensable," after previously dismissing the app in a 2022 post.

3859378.abstract: Jamie responds to Jim Nielsen's blog post "Online Handles" by sharing personal handle history: currently using jthingelstad for clarity, but previously going by thingles, a truncated, misspelled version of the surname from a first Unix account at the University of Minnesota.

3860431.abstract: Jamie backs Iconfactory's Kickstarter campaign for Project Tapestry, an open timeline app aggregating content from multiple services. Jamie cites Iconfactory's track record with Linea, Frenzic, and Twitterific, and expresses interest in the project's focus on open systems.

3864633.abstract: Jamie recaps a keynote by Diana Kander at the #TeamSPS Sales Kickoff 2024, where Kander discusses how expertise can hinder innovation and outlines becoming "curious experts." Jamie lists Kander's four guiding questions for evaluating tasks, including identifying the real problem, ranking importance, spotting "zombie" tasks, and reimagining work.

3869531.abstract: Jamie attends the 2024 Minneapolis Downtown Council annual meeting at the Armory, where board chair Karin Lucas speaks and Amelia Santaniello emcees, with appearances by Mayor Jacob Frey and Governor Tim Walz. Jamie notes SPS Commerce rose to become downtown's 9th largest employer with 1,465 people, up from 10th in 2023.

3878556.abstract: Jamie and Tyler visit five Twin Cities gaming stores in one day, following recommendations from brother-in-law Dylan: Tower Games, Level Up Games, Gamezenter (formerly Fantasy Flight), Source Comics & Games, and Dreamers Vault.

3878598.abstract: Jamie highlights the ENS DAO's February 13th update, noting that in January 2024 the ENS Protocol registered 39.8k new .eth domains (totaling 2.1 million) and generated $1.3 million in revenue for the DAO, projecting a $15.6M run rate.

3895468.abstract: Jamie recounts burning 394,305,096 BONK tokens received as an airdrop tied to Famous Fox NFT ownership, having no interest in meme coins. The tokens, once worth as little as $70, would be worth about $10,000 at BONK's price when Jamie writes the post.

3895475.abstract: Jamie recounts attending Bryan Hansel's Winter Along the Gunflint Photography Workshop near Grand Marais, a birthday gift from Tammy, shooting sunsets, sunrises, and Lake Superior waves despite minimal snow, and praises Hansel's Lightroom techniques and composition guidance.

3900021.abstract: Jamie describes purchasing a 2024 Tesla Model Y to replace a Mazda CX-9, after test driving the Model Y, Model S, and Model X and finding the Model X too expensive and likely too large for the garage.

3900036.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy gets tickets for the family to see Dune: Part Two at a sold-out showing at Edina 4. Jamie, a longtime Dune fan who read all six books in college, finds the film breathtaking and can't wait for Dune: Part Three, though Tammy, Tyler, and Mazie find it too long, slow, or violent and don't plan to see another one.

3901657.abstract: Jamie describes a multi-day home electric upgrade by Advantage Electric, covering panel replacement, meter remounting, LED conversions, new receptacles with USB C power, and Lutron Caseta switch installation, noting satisfaction with unifying lighting under the Caseta system.

3907286.abstract: Jamie describes visiting the Bee Lab at the University of Minnesota with Jamie's wife Tammy, an organization that Tammy's late father supported. The visit includes meeting Dr. Marla Spivak and touring the facility, with links to Spivak's TED Talk on bee disappearance and an interview on propolis research.

3907764.abstract: Jamie, a Micro.blog user, lists wanted improvements for the service's Uploads feature: search by filename, folder navigation by date, replacing an upload without changing its URL, and finding orphaned uploads for deletion.

3907773.abstract: Jamie recalls Grandpa Ardell and Grandma Rose Chrest, prompted by time spent with Cousin Josh reminiscing about the farm, and shares a photo of Grandpa eating lunch by a pickup with Uncle Tim near a John Deere 4440 tractor. Jamie quotes Banksy on dying twice and links to a 2001 post about Ardell and Rose's 50th anniversary.

3909771.abstract: Jamie reviews Matt Norman's book "Lead With Influence," read early at Norman's invitation, which walks readers through building influence in cross-functional teams via checklists and mental models organized around Position, Probe, Propose, and Persuade.

3936025.abstract: Jamie logs a Milwaukee spring break day: lunch at Archie's Flat Top, ice cream from Scratch, treats from Carrie's Crispies, a visit to the Milwaukee Public Museum's Old Streets exhibit, check-in at Saint Kate Art Hotel, and dinner at SafeHouse.

3936026.abstract: Jamie recounts day two of a Milwaukee spring break trip: breakfast at Toast, visiting the Milwaukee Art Museum, Tyler flying at Extreme Flight Simulation, seeing Brett Goldstein at the Riverside Theater, dinner at Tupelo Honey, and duckpin bowling at Koz's Mini Bowl.

3937026.abstract: Jamie recounts a Milwaukee spring break day including coffee at Discourse Coffee, brunch at Blue's Egg, a rainy visit to Milwaukee Zoo, mini golf at Big Putt's, a closed Oriental Theatre, dinner from Milwaukee Public Market vendors, and laser tag at Battle House with Tyler's Blue Team winning most games.

3937047.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a visit to the Milwaukee Art Museum, calling it one of the best art museums visited, with incredible art housed in an incredible building. The post is part of Jamie's Milwaukee Spring Break collection.

3937773.abstract: Jamie recounts day four of Milwaukee spring break: coffee at Discourse Coffee with Mazie, brunch at Uncle Wolfie's Breakfast Tavern, the Harley-Davidson Museum, a closed Milwaukee Domes, Historic Third Ward, the film Call Me Dancer, an escape room at 60 to Escape, and pizza at San Giorgio Pizzeria.

3938786.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a last-minute visit to the Milwaukee Domes, describing the tropical and desert domes as relaxing and pretty, part of the Milwaukee Spring Break collection.

3938789.abstract: Jamie recounts the final day of a Milwaukee spring break trip: coffee at Pilcrow Coffee, a visit to the Milwaukee Domes, a stop at Culver's in Tomah, Wisconsin, and arrival home at 3:14pm after departing Milwaukee at 9:37am.

3947112.abstract: Jamie visits the Harley-Davidson Museum in Milwaukee, noting that despite not being huge motorcycle fans, the group enjoys seeing the history and progression of the bikes over the years. The post is part of Jamie's Milwaukee Spring Break collection.

3947126.abstract: During Milwaukee Spring Break, Jamie describes a visit to Extreme Flight Simulation in Gurnee, Illinois, where Tyler flies a 737-800 simulator with a co-pilot, landing at Chicago O'Hare and taking off from Tokyo Narita, part of the Milwaukee Spring Break collection.

3947151.abstract: Jamie describes troubleshooting a Fastmail mail routing problem where ad hoc addresses at jamie.thingelstad.com stopped working. Fastmail support helped identify that adding a TXT record broke the wildcard MX entry, since any record on a name overrides wildcard DNS; Jamie fixes it by adding specific MX entries.

3947157.abstract: Jamie describes quitting coffee after cutting back to two cups a day for months, experiencing fuzziness, tiredness and a mild headache during the first two days. The goal is to observe effects on blood pressure, sleep and anxiety.

3951320.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy see Semisonic at the Palace Theatre in St. Paul, with Laamar (Geoffrey Lamar Wilson) opening. The post covers the setlist, homages to Mississippi River conservation, and Dan Wilson's co-written song "White Horse" performed in tribute to Chris Stapleton.

3951610.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy attend Gabe Mollica's "Solo: A Show About Friendship" at the Parkway Theater, opening act Ben Katzner. Jamie compares Mollica's style to Mike Birbiglia and notes part of the story appeared on This American Life episode 810, "Say It To My Face."

3983149.abstract: Jamie recounts the first day of a Turks & Caicos trip: a Landline shuttle to the airport, dinner at Barrio in MSP Terminal 2, a flight delayed 2.5 hours by Florida storms, arrival in Providenciales, and picking up a White Villas rental car before reaching the villa after 10pm.

3983150.abstract: Jamie recounts day two of a Turks & Caicos trip: breakfast at Shay Cafe, shopping near resorts including a hat from Goldsmith's, a grocery run to Graceway IGA, exploring White Villas, swimming, Long Bay Beach, and dinner at Mango Reef.

3983151.abstract: Jamie recaps day three of a Turks & Caicos trip: a morning massage, lunch and pina coladas at Hemingway's, shopping, swimming, sunset on Long Bay Beach, and pizza at Bella Luna, with Tammy and Mazie taking a separate walk.

3983152.abstract: Jamie recounts a Captain Jack full-day tour with Grace Bay Adventures in Turks & Caicos, including snorkeling at Coral Gardens with turtles, Half Moon Bay, Iguana Island, lunch at Fort George Cay, shark sightings at the Barrier Reef, and dinner at Indigo.

3983153.abstract: Jamie recounts day five of a Turks & Caicos trip: breakfast at Shay Cafe, pool time, Tyler's homework, Pina Coladas, and a Tammy conference call, followed by kite surfing at Long Bay Beach and dinner redirected from Da Conch Shack to Bella Luna.

3983154.abstract: Jamie recounts day six of a Turks & Caicos trip, including breakfast at Somewhere Cafe, snorkeling and playing at Coral Gardens, ice cream at Patty's Place, shopping with Tyler, dinner at Coco Van, and a movie night watching "The Adam Project" at White Villas with Max and other families.

3983156.abstract: Jamie recounts day seven of a Turks & Caicos trip, including jet skiing and coconut water at Sapodilla Beach, lunch at Omar's Beach Hut, an E-Foil lesson with Fly TCI on Grace Bay, and dinner at Bay Bistro.

3983157.abstract: Jamie recounts the last day of a Turks & Caicos trip: packing out of White Villa 1, COVID testing at Seven Stars, churros at Coco Van, relaxing at White Villas Villa 2, a late lunch at Da Conch Shack, then flying home.

4035547.abstract: Jamie recaps the 2024 Minnesota Aspirations in Computing awards ceremony, held for the first time at the Metropolitan Ballroom under the new MnTech Foundation. Jamie notes SPS Commerce's eighth year sponsoring the program, credits Amy Patton's involvement, shares event photos, and links to a GiveMN fundraiser for scholarships.

4036198.abstract: Jamie recaps attending Minnebar 18 at Best Buy Headquarters with Tyler, describing sessions on topics including community investing, LLM optimization, Google Sheets AI, retro-computing, and DevSecOps, plus photos and a list of community members greeted at the event.

4036488.abstract: Jamie describes a "blog gardening" session revisiting old posts, discovering that visits to New York's High Line happened exactly 11 years apart (2012 and 2013), and revisiting a one-year SPS team milestone and 2018 Kyiv cherry blossom photos.

4045378.abstract: Jamie watches Hard Miles at Edina 4, a film based on a true story about a counselor leading four young men from a correctional school on a bicycle ride to the Grand Canyon. Jamie notes a fondness for cycling movies, praises Matthew Modine's performance, and recommends the film.

4045380.abstract: Jamie recounts a chaotic early morning: a low-battery chirp from a CO detector wakes Jamie at 5:30a, letting the dog Lucky out leads to barking chaos over a neighbor's dogs, and grabbing keys accidentally sets off the car alarm.

4052139.abstract: Jamie and Tammy attend Constellation Fund's Bright Night 2024 at the renovated Uptown Theater, an event supporting the organization's data-driven approach to fighting poverty in the Twin Cities, similar to Robin Hood and Tipping Point.

4052690.abstract: Jamie reflects on abstaining from coffee and caffeine since April 1st, citing high blood pressure, poor sleep, and anxiousness as reasons.

4053622.abstract: Jamie orders two pounds of Turtles and salted caramel chocolates from Freese's Candy for Tammy's Mother's Day gift, only to have squirrels raid the delivered package on the front porch.

4059612.abstract: Jamie recaps attending MnTech's Tech Connect 2024 at the Saint Paul RiverCentre, with over 600 attendees, covering sessions on generative AI, quantum computing, AI product development, baseball technology, cloud governance, and a CIO leadership panel featuring speakers like Jennifer Hartsock and Cris Ross.

4059639.abstract: Jamie attends the first UnGala fundraiser for Cristo Rey Jesuit High School, noting the school's record of getting every student accepted into college programs. Jamie mentions Alberto Vergara, a former Cristo Rey student on TeamSPS now working as a full-time Account Executive, and shares a team photo from the event.

4076289.abstract: Jamie describes celebrating Vyshyvanka Day at a Minneapolis office, an event previously held only in the Kyiv office, led by Alexander Ivakhnenko and Valentin Kornukh with pierogi, Medovik, Kyiv cake, Napoleon cake, kvas, and a Ukrainian trivia challenge.

4121858.abstract: Jamie describes drinking coffee for the first time since April 1st, using beans from Fika Coffee, after 54 days without it. The initial sip feels unremarkable, but a strong caffeine rush hits later while driving to Crack of Dawn in Faribault, which Jamie finds disconcerting rather than enjoyable.

4135401.abstract: Jamie logs departure day for an Ireland trip: packing, visiting the Edina Art Fair, a Lyft to the airport, suitcase weights for Tammy, Jamie, Mazie and Tyler, and meeting a Seattle family rerouted through Minneapolis before the Delta flight to Dublin takes off.

4135406.abstract: Jamie and Tammy make a quick stop at the Edina Art Fair before heading to the airport for a trip to Ireland. Jamie names favorite artists including Tiny People Big Laughs, Chuck U Art, Brian Schmidt, Shantina Hatfield, Raelyn Larson and Tim Pahs, and Todd Voss, and notes Tammy's purchase of a sculpture called "Willie Fly."

4135506.abstract: Jamie logs arrival in Dublin, picking up a SEAT Leon from NewWay rental, and the drive to Killarney with stops at Barrack Obama Plaza and Killarney Brewing & Distilling, followed by exploring shops and dinner at Hilliard's.

4136628.abstract: Jamie logs a day biking through Killarney National Park, visiting Torc Waterfall, Muckross House, and Muckross Abbey, then dinner at Kitty O'Se's and a Guinness with live music at O'Connors Pub in Killarney.

4136633.abstract: Jamie appears as a guest on episode 136 of the Omni Show podcast, recorded with Andrew Mason, discussing how Jamie uses OmniFocus, with both audio and a new YouTube video version.

4137700.abstract: Jamie describes hiking the Gap of Dunloe in Ireland, starting at Lord Brandon's Cottage and finishing a 7.00-mile route at Kate Kearney's Cottage, noting steady climbing, strong wind at the summit, and sharing photos of family, scenery, and lambs along the way.

4137705.abstract: Jamie logs day four of an Ireland trip: a rainy boat tour from Ross Castle to Lord Brandon's Cottage, then a 7-mile hike over the Gap of Dunloe, followed by drinks at Kate Kearney's Cottage and a drive to Ballybunion.

4138604.abstract: Jamie describes a day spent exploring Ballybunion Beach in cool, windy weather around 55°F, examining rock walls, tide pools, jellyfish and crabs, and watching the tide separate the former Men's and Women's beaches.

4138617.abstract: Jamie recounts a barbershop connection: Gene, who has cut Jamie's hair for a decade at Dick's Sports Barbers, recommended McMunn's of Ballybunion, owned by former client Tony McMunn, an "Edina guy" now living in Florida. Jamie's family stops for Guinness and dessert, confirms the connection with a waitress, and brings golf tees back to Gene.

4138632.abstract: Jamie logs an unscheduled family vacation day in Ballybunion, Ireland, covering breakfast at Marine Bakery & Cafe, beach exploration, a failed surf school booking, dinner at Namir's, the Cliff Walk, and a barber-recommended stop at McMunn's.

4147248.abstract: Jamie describes an Afternoon Tea in the Great Hall at Adare Manor with Tammy, Mazie, and Tyler, noting it was Tyler's first such experience. The post details the 1832 Blend tea, Earl Grey Bellinis, sandwich and dessert courses, and various tea choices for each family member, concluding it was the family's favorite tea experience so far.

4147259.abstract: Jamie logs day six of an Ireland trip: a walk on Ballybunion Beach, afternoon tea at Adare Manor, shopping in Adare, and a drive to Doolin for dinner and traditional music at McGann's Pub before staying at a cottage near Doonagore Castle.

4148184.abstract: Jamie describes taking the Doolin Ferry to Inis Mór in the Aran Islands, noting rough seas and sizable swells during the first 10-20 minutes, with Tyler feeling unwell but managing to hold it together by the trip's end.

4149961.abstract: Jamie recounts a day exploring Inis Mór by e-bike rented from Aran Bike Rental, visiting the Seal Colony, roadside cairns, Dún Aonghasa, the Aran Sweater Market, Seven Churches, and Kilmurvey Beach with Mazie and Tammy, ending with a pub lunch of beef stew and Guinness at Joe Watty's Bar & Restaurant after fixing a dropped bike chain.

4149981.abstract: Jamie recounts a day traveling entirely on foot, walking from the cottage to Doolin pier for breakfast at Rocket House, then taking the Doolin Ferry to Inis Mór to explore. The day ends with shopping, including sweaters for Tammy at Irish Crafts, and fish and chips at The Ivy Cottage.

4150702.abstract: Jamie logs day 8 of an Ireland trip in Doolin, including breakfast at Irish Craft, the Doolin Cliff Hike led by Pat Sweeney, shopping at Village Crafts, ice cream, pitch and putt, pizza at Stonewall, and music with Guinness at Gus O'Connors Pub.

4150864.abstract: Jamie describes hiking the Cliffs of Moher with guide Pat Sweeney of Doolin Cliff Walks, who spent 14 years working with local farmers to establish the route.

4150865.abstract: Jamie describes trying pitch and putt golf at the Doolin Pitch & Putt in Ireland despite not being a golfing family, noting the ocean-side scenery and admittedly poor performance, with photos of the group playing on the coastal course.

4151709.abstract: Jamie logs a rainy travel day from Doolin to Ballyshannon, including breakfast and shopping in Galway, a stop at Ashford Castle for a hawk walk, dinner in Bundoran, and checking into Cria Lodge to try its hot tub.

4152007.abstract: Jamie describes a Hawk Walk at Ashford Castle, once owned by the Guinness family, with the Ireland School of Falconry. The family flies Harris Hawks named Walnut and Chestnut, birds Jamie notes hunt cooperatively and can reach 60 miles an hour, and includes photos of family members holding the hawks.

4152739.abstract: Jamie logs day 10 of the Ireland trip, covering County Donegal with stops at the Bakery Shack, Teelin Pier, a Sliabh League boat tour with Paddy, lunch at The Rusty Mackerel, a hike up Sliabh Liag Cliffs, and Silver Strand Beach before feeding alpacas back at the Airbnb.

4153062.abstract: Jamie describes taking Paddy's Sliabh League Boat Trip from Teelin Pier in County Donegal to view the Sliabh Liag cliffs, noting they are Ireland's highest, three times taller than the Cliffs of Moher, with rock formations resembling mountains.

4153407.abstract: Jamie describes a visit to Silver Strand Beach in Ireland, reached after Sliabh Liag via a remote drive filled with sheep. Jamie calls the crescent-shaped harbor beach nearly undisturbed, with fewer than 10 people present, and describes dolphins jumping in the bay toward the end of the visit.

4153613.abstract: Jamie logs day 11 of an Ireland trip: brunch in Donegal, shopping at The Donegal Diamond, and a drive to Rossnowlagh Beach where Tyler and Mazie finally get a surf lesson after two prior attempts fell through. The day ends with dinner at La Bella Donna and a Guinness at Whoriskey's Pub near Cria Lodge.

4154366.abstract: Jamie describes a detour from Ballyshannon to Belfast to visit Giants Causeway, comparing its columnar basalt geology to similar formations seen in Iceland, and shares photos of the hexagonal rock columns, coastal cliffs and visitors exploring the site.

4154370.abstract: Jamie logs day 12 of the Ireland trip: hiking Giants Causeway's Red and Blue Paths, then driving to Belfast to stay at the Titanic Hotel, with dinner at Little Wing Pizzeria and the Titanic-themed Timescape escape room.

4155165.abstract: Jamie logs day 13 of an Ireland trip: visiting the Titanic Museum and S.S. Nomadic in Belfast, driving to Kilkenny through rush-hour Dublin traffic, dinner at Brewery Corner, and checking into Tubbrid Castle for the night.

4155193.abstract: Jamie describes staying at Tubbrid Castle, a 600-year-old restored castle rented as an Airbnb with six-foot-thick walls and heat installed for the first time in its history. Jamie shares photos of the exterior tower, kitchen and dining area, bedrooms, stone staircase, bathroom, and a group selfie in front of the castle.

4155957.abstract: Jamie logs day 14 of the Ireland trip, spent celebrating Mazie's birthday in Kilkenny with visits to the Medieval Mile Museum, Kilkenny Castle, Smithwick's Experience, and Rothe House, ending with a birthday dinner at Ristorante Rinuccini.

4159459.abstract: During a Dublin visit, Jamie and family attend Experience Gaelic Games to learn Hurling, Gaelic Football, and Handball. Jamie notes hurling players stay with their birthplace clubs, teams lack sponsorships, and players remain unpaid, and shares photos from the session.

4159463.abstract: Jamie describes visiting EPIC: The Irish Emigration Museum in Dublin, opened in 2016, which chronicles Irish emigration worldwide and its impact, alongside Irish history. Jamie praises its multimedia experiences as the best ever seen, and shares photos of exhibits including a touch table, ship sculpture, and GAA jerseys.

4159468.abstract: Jamie logs day 15 of the Ireland trip: leaving Tubbrid Castle for Dublin, taking a Gaelic Games class, visiting the EPIC Irish Emigration Museum, and returning the rental car undamaged before settling into the Hard Rock Hotel Dublin and eating at Pi Pizza and Bunsen in Temple Bar.

4159479.abstract: Jamie recounts driving a manual, right-hand-drive SEAT Leon rented from New Way during a 2024 Ireland trip, covering 1,907 kilometers over 15 days using Google Maps with Tammy navigating. Jamie describes adjusting to opposite-side driving and narrow, shoulderless roads, then shares the family's rated feedback on the driving.

4160091.abstract: Jamie logs Father's Day in Dublin: touring Kilmainham Gaol, the Guinness Storehouse, Windmill Lane Studios and Trinity College's Book of Kells, then a steak dinner at F. X. Buckley and traditional music at Darkey Kelly's.

4160356.abstract: Jamie describes a tour of Windmill Lane Studios, noting U2 recorded "Boy" there and the Rolling Stones booked all three studios for six months during "Voodoo Lounge," with recent clients including Bruce Springsteen, Foo Fighters, P!nk, and Hozier.

4160371.abstract: Jamie describes visiting the Kilmainham Gaol Museum in Ireland, noting Tammy secured hard-to-get tickets online. Jamie recounts the prison's history since opening in 1796, its overcrowding during the famine, and its role holding political prisoners in the early 1900s, calling the tour sobering.

4160375.abstract: Jamie visits the Guinness Storehouse in Dublin on Father's Day, describing it as a history of Guinness rather than a brewery tour, highlighting the advertisement archive and a personalized "Stoutie" pint. Jamie finishes with beef stew at 1837 Bar & Brasserie, calling it a trip favorite.

4161195.abstract: Jamie logs the last full day in Ireland, spent in Dalkey with Tammy and Mazie: touring Dalkey Castle, visiting shops and Thyme Out, taking a ferry to Dalkey Island with Ken the Ferryman, then returning to Dublin for burgers at Bunsen and traditional music at O'Donoghues and Temple Bar.

4162228.abstract: Jamie logs the final day of an Ireland trip: a taxi ride with driver John's stories, checking luggage weights against day one, a Butler's Chocolates stop for Caramel Squares, clearing US Customs, and flying DL115 from Dublin to Minneapolis.

4165676.abstract: Jamie describes visiting the Titanic Museum in Belfast, built at the site of Harland & Wolff Slip 3. The post covers the shipbuilding history, the Titanic's 1909 construction and 1911 launch, the disaster's timeline, and the wreckage discovery display, which Jamie calls a moving experience worth the trip.

4165678.abstract: Jamie describes afternoon tea at the Titanic Hotel following a museum visit, comparing it to a previous experience at Adare Manor. Jamie finds it less fancy overall but notes the desserts were slightly tastier, while the tea and scones fell short of Adare Manor's standard.

4165680.abstract: Jamie describes a tour of Dalkey Castle featuring actors playing a Barber/Surgeon, Archer, and Cook from medieval times, explaining the origins of the barber pole, the "murder hole" defense, and the term "humble pie." The tour clarifies features Jamie also saw at Tubbrid Castle in Kilkenny.

4165681.abstract: Jamie describes a trip to Dalkey Island via ferry with Ken the Ferryman, noting the island is now uninhabited despite records of habitation over 1,000 years ago. Jamie mentions ruins of a church, a military cannon station, and a radar structure, along with goats (unseen) and seagulls, and shares photos of the ruins, coastline, and ferry crossing.

4165682.abstract: Jamie describes an evening in Dublin visiting O'Donoghue's Pub for traditional Irish music, recommended by cousin Josh, followed by The Temple Bar for a livelier sing-along set, marking a final night in the city.

4165685.abstract: Jamie describes visiting Sliabh League in Ireland, first by boat tour and then on foot up to the viewing point, accompanied by Tammy, Tyler, and Mazie. Jamie notes the cliffs are over three times higher than the Cliffs of Moher, though less sheer, with a more mountainous look and multiple vertical drops.

4165732.abstract: Jamie outlines a Summer Challenge task asking kids to spec out a Gaming PC, listing all needed components with links and explanations of why each part is chosen and how it fits the build's goal. The post notes the challenge as completed, linking to Tyler's write-up on building a Towertech PC.

4165739.abstract: This post outlines a Summer Challenge Collection task asking kids to embed a chess game played on lichess.org into a blog post, complete with commentary on critical points and, ideally, the PGN with referenced moves. Jamie notes the challenge as completed, linking to Tyler's blog post fulfilling it.

4166427.abstract: Jamie compiles a Harper's Index-style summary of an Ireland trip, tallying 1,907 kilometers driven, 16 pints of Guinness, 18 fish & chips orders, five Airbnbs, two hotels, three museums, four boat trips, two islands, seven wool sweaters, and 1,648 photos, with links to daily logs.

4167214.abstract: Jamie describes flooding at Cannon Lake that submerged the dock and caused a pontoon boat, kept on Sealegs, to float away across the lake. After an attempt to reach it on foot through muddy terrain failed, Jamie and others retrieve it by kayak and drive it back to shore.

4167223.abstract: Jamie describes severe flooding at Cannon Lake in 2024, worse than a 2016 flood also mentioned. Jamie drives to check the pontoon boat, wades through waist-high water to lower the bimini and canopy poles, and ties the boat securely, while noting nearby homes and roads, including Shager Beach and Cannon Lake Trail, suffered significant flood damage.

4168945.abstract: After repositioning a UniFi G4 Instant camera to watch the boat during Cannon Lake flooding, Jamie finds raccoons tampered with it overnight, but lawn care workers later put the camera back in place unprompted.

4170509.abstract: Jamie outlines a Summer Challenge task asking kids to pick a topic or theme, like flowers, water, movement or wind, then take a phone photo walk capturing five to ten images and share them on their blog, redeemable up to three times. Completed entries link to work by Tyler and Mazie.

4170510.abstract: Jamie outlines a Summer Challenge Collection task for kids: write about a video game they've played, which doesn't have to be a review but should include screenshots, with the challenge redeemable up to three times.

4170511.abstract: Jamie outlines a Summer Challenge task asking kids to write about a book they've read, suggesting a book report style post that includes the cover image and, preferably, a quoted excerpt. The challenge can be redeemed up to five times.

4170513.abstract: Jamie outlines a Summer Challenge task asking kids to build a simple counter using Apple's Shortcuts app and Data Jar, with functions to increment, decrement, create, and remove a counter, then write a post sharing the shortcut. Jamie links to a completed example by Tyler.

4170523.abstract: Jamie describes receiving a Ledger Stax crypto wallet, pre-ordered in December 2022 after hearing how former iPod designer Tony Fadell approached its book-like design. Jamie unboxes the device, notes the recyclable cardboard packaging, and plans to configure it alongside an existing Ledger Nano X.

4180447.abstract: Jamie provides an update on flooding at Cannon Lake, noting water levels dropped slightly but remain high, with the lake association warning of possible contamination from upriver flooding.

4180449.abstract: Jamie describes remounting a UniFi G4 camera at Cannon Lake using a yard stake and scrap wood after raccoons interfered with an earlier ground-level setup on a 2x4. The new position raises the camera closer to eye height and also captures floating algae collecting near the dock where the pontoon is moored.

4180476.abstract: Jamie describes helping cousin Josh Ellis launch Rambling Josh, a website collecting columns Josh has written twice-monthly for the Burke County Tribune for nearly 20 years, totaling over 450 pieces. Jamie imported 240 columns, including the first, "Shadow Puppets," with plans to add more, some requiring OCR from saved clippings.

4180550.abstract: Jamie describes helping cousin Josh launch Rambling Josh, a Micro.blog site hosting 20 years of newspaper columns originally written as 240 Word documents.

4208620.abstract: Fiber internet from Bevcomm is installed and activated at Jamie's cabin, one year after the initial go-ahead given on July 1, 2023. Jamie describes upgrading the cabin's network beforehand to UniFi equipment, using MoCa adapters over existing coax wiring as a backbone, plus WiFi 6 LR access points and an outdoor U6 Mesh access point.

4214485.abstract: Jamie outlines a Summer Challenge Collection task for the kids: use Playdate's web-based Pulp game editor to build an open-ended experience for the Playdate handheld, whether a game, an educational tool, or something silly, as long as it has a clear goal.
