4216014.abstract: Jamie describes a visit to High Wheel Confectionary in Ironton, praising generous ice cream scoops and a soda cellar with unusual flavors. Jamie buys Moxie soda and a Goo Goo Cluster, and notes an upstairs toy store and lounge.

4216617.abstract: Jamie shares photos from an afternoon spent paddling on Pennington Mine.

4216860.abstract: Jamie introduces "Blog Pensieve," a practice of backdating blog posts to fill historical gaps left when busy or offline, named after the Harry Potter memory-storage device.

4217062.abstract: Jamie recounts a family weekend in Crosby, Minnesota exploring the Cuyuna area with Tammy, Mazie, and Tyler, staying at Crosby Lofts and detailing meals, shops, and stops like Red Raven, Mac Daddy's Donut Garage, and High Wheel Confectionary.

4226975.abstract: Jamie tries terminal.shop, a coffee store accessible via ssh, after cousin Quinn Chrest (who built a terminal-based task tracker) mentions it. Jamie tests the curses-based interface, browses products and the FAQ, and places an order, receiving confirmation email #000 signed by Terminal Products Inc.

4234453.abstract: Jamie shares a seven-minute video walking through the gardens at Canoe Bay, calling them a highlight of the stay there.

4236424.abstract: Jamie describes attending a Foo Fighters concert at Target Field with Mazie, who has become a fan, highlighting singing along to "My Hero." The post includes the full setlist, covering songs like "Everlong," "Best of You," and a partial acoustic "Stairway to Heaven," plus photos of the crowd and stage.

4237190.abstract: Jamie shares a video of cousin Josh performing the original song "Drinkin' Hat," a piece brother Gabe started and the two "worked out" together, noting it includes a callout to their Grandpa and Grandma.

4239283.abstract: Jamie reflects on sending Weekly Thing 291, a special issue about Ireland that broke from the usual format and required about two hours of manual assembly for sections, links, headers, and images.

4239302.abstract: Jamie recaps a League Cup match between Club Necaxa and Minnesota United FC at Allianz Field, featuring an early penalty for United, a red card leaving United down a man for 69 minutes, and goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair's dozen second-half saves securing a scoreless-for-Necaxa win. Jamie attended with friends Jim and Tom.

4239305.abstract: Jamie describes the launch of DD Lounge by Kai Brach of Dense Discovery, a feature for Friends of DD subscribers that Jamie has followed since 2020.

4239358.abstract: Jamie describes Gmail marking issue 291 of the Weekly Thing newsletter as spam despite the sender being in contacts, and notes Google's own Search Console, Cloud, and Account emails were also flagged as junk.

4257423.abstract: Jamie notes 2024 Minneapolis rainfall totals 28.26 inches through August 11, just short of the 1892 record of 31.23 inches, and 38% above normal. Jamie cites Minnesota DNR data and a chart, and mentions the sump system running overtime all summer.

4305354.abstract: Jamie recounts seeing Steve Earle perform a nearly two-hour solo acoustic show at the Dakota with Tammy, following previous shows in 2017, 2018, and 2023.

4308472.abstract: Jamie shares photos from an evening at the Minnesota State Fair, spent with Tiffany and Andrew.

4308690.abstract: Jamie describes gathering with family at Northwood Park in New Hope, Minnesota, to mark the 86th birthday of Tammy's Dad, Don Olson, who died in January.

4310522.abstract: Jamie describes floating down Minnehaha Creek on tubes with visiting Tiffany and Andrew, starting at Utley Park in Edina and taking out at Minnehaha Creek Park, covering 3.7 miles in just over two hours.

4317132.abstract: Jamie describes the folder structure used in OmniFocus to manage a GTD system, prompted by follow-up questions after the Omni Show appearance.

4334961.abstract: Jamie describes Tyler's completion of a Summer Challenge to build a Playdate game using Pulp, resulting in "The 5 Piece Sword," and links to Tyler's posts on its enemies, heart-based health system, and spikes and spike balls, noting a final boss stage is still in progress.

4340254.abstract: Jamie describes Tyler reaching a savings goal and buying a PURE AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT 16GB GPU at Microcenter for a gaming PC build. Tyler installs it and drivers largely independently, reaching frame rates over 300 fps in test games, prompting Jamie's reflection on how much PC building has changed in 20+ years.

4345605.abstract: Jamie describes ordering a sauna from NorthUp Sauna after encountering the company's translucent-walled models at the Minnesota State Fair's Dairy Building. Conversations with owner Darin, of Urban Wing, led to a custom configuration for Jamie's cabin, with delivery expected in November or December.

4355925.abstract: Jamie describes attending the Fall CIO Wine Tasting event hosted by Dee Thibodeau of Charter Solutions and Terri Naughtin of Naughtin Group, held on the downtown Minneapolis rooftop venue of Tony Peleska's Kraus Anderson, with Chuck Kanski of Solo Vino presenting a range of wines and grape backgrounds.

4355929.abstract: Jamie recaps Minnedemo 40, noting attendance at the first Holiday Minnedemo in 2006, then summarizes seven demos: HabitAware's app/bracelet for body-focused repetitive behaviors, OmegaVR's accessible VR, tinkl's gender-neutral bathroom finder, Attentio's LLM training platform, Abe's DIY video-help service, HLRBO's hunting-lease marketplace, and…

4355931.abstract: Jamie highlights progress from ENS DAO Newsletter #70 (Sept 24, 2024), noting ENS integration with PayPal and Venmo for simplified crypto transfers, the revived eth.link gateway powered by eth.limo, and POAP's new free ENS subname feature. Jamie also cites August 2024 DAO financials showing $1.9M revenue and $113M in reserves.

4355991.abstract: Jamie experiments with Google's Notebook LM after seeing Garrick Van Buren's post "Two AI Bots Discussing My Work," feeding it issues of the Weekly Thing newsletter (292, 287, 276, and a batch of 14 issues) to generate AI-bot podcast discussions.

4356145.abstract: Jamie's child Tyler attends the Minnesota Debate Teachers Association Jamboree, a first tournament, while Jamie judges rounds after 35 years away from debate. Jamie notes the 2024-2025 policy topic on strengthening U.S.

4363320.abstract: Jamie lists the Thingelstad family's favorite cheeseburger spots: Lion's Tap, Tap Society, Lake & Irving, and The Dakota, plus a homemade smash burger cooked on a flat top at the cabin, which Jamie considers the only true smash burger among them.

4377885.abstract: Jamie explores FIFA Collect, an NFT platform built on the Algorand blockchain, drawn by "Right to Buy" collectibles tied to 2026 World Cup tickets. Jamie sets up a Pera wallet, buys ALGO on Coinbase, swaps for USDC-a, and purchases a World Cup 1994 USA poster collectible, noting "right to buy" items resell for around $300.

4380550.abstract: Jamie logs a weekend trip along Minnesota's North Shore, driving to Duluth and Grand Marais with stops at Ursa Minor Brewery, World's Best Donuts, Artist Point, Grand Marais Light, and shops like Drury Lane Books and Sivertson Art Gallery.

4391502.abstract: Jamie and Tyler fly a Boeing 737 simulator at Extreme Flight Simulation, with Tyler as pilot and Jamie as co-pilot. They run a full pre-flight routine and choose four airports to take off, fly, and land at—MSP, CDG, HHX, and LGA—noting HHX's difficult landing approach and LGA producing their best landing, before completing a full shutdown.

4398225.abstract: Jamie references the 2010 Citizens United Supreme Court ruling, which allows unrestricted independent campaign expenditures by corporations and unions, and contrasts it with an Economist report from October 21, 2024 describing Elon Musk's $1m daily lottery for swing-state voters signing a petition.

4403960.abstract: Jamie logs a family trip log to Chicago for MEA weekend, tracking a day-by-day itinerary with Tammy and Tyler covering stops in Arlington Heights, Gurnee, and downtown Chicago.

4428835.abstract: Jamie reports the results of the annual Things 4 Good candle sale, which raised $7,010 from 78 buyers, a 21.8% increase over 2023, plus $260.25 donated from Mount Olivet Holiday Boutique sales.

4428961.abstract: Jamie analyzes data from the 4th annual Things 4 Good Fall Fundraiser, which raised $7,010 selling candles at the Mt. Olivet Holiday Boutique. Jamie reviews inventory of 252 candles across eight scents, sales trends by transaction, and payment methods, noting Venmo's dominance and that Winter Wonderland and True North sold out first.

4428963.abstract: Jamie reports that the Things 4 Good Fall Fundraiser has run for four years, raising $22,739 for non-profits, with 2024 reaching $7,010 and 78 transactions after opening sales to the public via the Mt. Olivet Holiday Boutique boosted candle sales nearly 50%.

4435946.abstract: Jamie attends the MISRC Digital Leadership Conference on AI and speaks on a panel with Jean Machart and Elwin Loomis about AI strategy. Cris Ross of Mayo Clinic outlines seven technological challenges for AI in healthcare, while Jake Krings and Melissa Ludack of Target describe AI use in stores and their app.

4439549.abstract: Jamie describes handling build errors on thingelstad.com caused by embedded Twitter/X posts whose original accounts have been deleted. Jamie explains the migration from Twitter archives using Hugo shortcodes and the decision to delete affected blog posts, honoring authors' intent, since most contained no original content from Jamie.

4439850.abstract: Jamie recounts leaving Twitter/X in stages since 2016, including deleting tweet history, removing connections, and finally deleting the @thingles profile in November 2024. Jamie argues no social media platform is healthy, comparing them to cigarettes and gambling, and shares an AI-generated gravestone image marking the account's end.

4466758.abstract: Jamie reflects on sending the 300th issue of the Weekly Thing newsletter, started May 13, 2017, and shares lessons learned, including the value of automation, summer and winter breaks (inspired by James Whatley's Five Things on Friday), embracing experimentation like the Weekly Thing Forum and new Supporting Memberships, and deliberately not…

4466787.abstract: Jamie announces a Supporting Membership for the Weekly Thing newsletter, previewed earlier in issue 299 and on the Weekly Thing Forum. Membership funds accrue and go annually to a chosen non-profit, starting with Creative Commons, founded by Larry Lessig, whose 2017 TED Talk Jamie links to; members receive a gold star mention in each issue.

4466816.abstract: Jamie breaks down the material cost of producing a single Things 4 Good candle, itemizing vessels, soy wax, scent, wooden wick, wick clip, label, and warning sticker, totaling $10.35–$13.40 (or $8.28–$10.72 with discounts). Since candles sell for $25 with costs covered separately, Jamie notes the full donation goes to charity.

4472466.abstract: Jamie describes switching from Apple's discontinued Leather cases to the Mujjo Leather Case for iPhone 16 Pro, after disliking Apple's Silicone and Clear cases and finding the bare phone too slippery.

4477542.abstract: Jamie compares two packaged lefse brands ahead of Thanksgiving: Freddy's Lefse, made in Fargo since 1946, thin and round with an optional cinnamon-sugar shaker, versus Laura's Lefse, a rectangular, thicker variety Jamie traces to Mrs. Olson's Lefse of Gonvick, Minnesota.

4482273.abstract: Jamie watches The Matrix with Tyler, prompted by wanting to share the film after being surprised it's 25 years old. Jamie checks Common Sense Media reviews before deciding the R-rating is acceptable, then streams a 4K version via iTunes rather than the Plex DVD rip, noting the AI storyline feels newly relevant, the cell phones look dated, and…

4482285.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy attend a Justin Willman performance at The Fitzgerald Theater, filmed as a taping for a new Netflix comedy and magic special.

4500290.abstract: Jamie describes attending the Vikings v Cardinals game with Tammy from club-level seats at the 50 yard line. Jamie recounts a slow first three quarters of field goals before the Vikings rallied from 19-6 down to win 23-22 on a late touchdown and a Cardinals interception.

4504593.abstract: Jamie describes BlogFlock, a new service by Raphael Kabo that lets users build shareable "river of news" style lists from open RSS feeds, and creates a BlogFlock list covering all 66 blogs featured in Manuel Moreale's People & Blogs project, excluding Ray Thomas and Steyn Viljoen (no RSS feeds) and Devastatia (adult content).

4518898.abstract: Jamie describes attending a cookie decorating class hosted by Tammy's sister Corinne and Corinne's husband Denny, who prepared a hundred cookies, Royal Icing, and printed patterns for guidance. Jamie decorates a gnome, a sweater, and a snowman, calling the snowman frightening enough to eat.

4519720.abstract: Jamie tracks YouTube TV's price history since first subscribing in 2019, from $43.01 to a January 2025 bill of $90.48, a 13.58% annual growth rate that outpaces inflation. Jamie notes YouTube TV is the least-used but most expensive of all subscribed streaming services, has paused the subscription, and considers returning to over-the-air HDTV.

4519748.abstract: Jamie describes designing a logo for the Weekly Thing newsletter, published for over seven years at weekly.thingelstad.com, using ChatGPT for exploration and OmniGraffle to refine the design.

4519801.abstract: Jamie links to a W3C Statement on Ethical Web Principles, quoting its call for the web to be non-harmful, secure, private, transparent, environmentally sustainable and multi-platform, and finds the list worth striving for.

4542946.abstract: Jamie announces the five randomly selected winners of the Weekly Thing Christmas Blog gift giveaway, using a Python script with random.shuffle to pick names: Marcos, Claudia, Jesse, Phil, and David.

4563205.abstract: Jamie describes a shortcut called Collection Creator built to work with Micro.blog's photo collections feature, which lets users group photos and reference them via shortcode.

4569301.abstract: Jamie shares 2024 blogging statistics using Amit Gawande's Post Stats Plugin: 701 posts and 51,905 words, with June's spike tied to a trip to Ireland.

4569530.abstract: Jamie tracks POAP event creation trends by comparing the sequential event numbers from birthday POAPs created annually since turning 50, now up to the 53rd.

4573259.abstract: Jamie describes attending a Shabby Road Orchestra performance of Beatles classics at The Dakota with Tammy, Jamie's Mom, and Kurt, as a Christmas gift for Jamie's Mom, a Beatles fan.

4573939.abstract: Jamie proposes combining POAP with RSS, noting the two currently don't connect, and outlines use cases like tracking new token claims for events, automating actions via IFTTT, and following friends' POAP collections.

4573957.abstract: Jamie highlights Open RSS, a non-profit that advocates for RSS and helps discover or bridge feeds for sites lacking them, discovered via a Lifehacker article. Jamie corresponds with co-founder Mark, donates, and suggests Open RSS as a future beneficiary of Weekly Thing Supporting Memberships.

4581997.abstract: Jamie responds to Mark Zuckerberg's Threads announcement changing moderation policies, noting the six changes: replacing fact-checkers with Community Notes, simplifying content policies, easing enforcement, restoring civic content, relocating moderation teams to Texas, and pushing back on foreign censorship.

4589500.abstract: Jamie shares three Shortcuts built for Micro.blog's photo collections feature, having created 64 collections so far: Collection Creator (updated from an earlier version to build collections from clipboard URLs, with improved logging and API failure checks), Collection Copier (adds all photos from one collection into another, useful for…

4589531.abstract: Jamie marks 24 years since Dave Winer introduced Payloads for RSS, the enclosure element that became the technical foundation of podcasting, and quotes Winer's original description of the url, length, and type attributes. Jamie notes Winer initially disagreed but was persuaded by Adam Curry, calling it an example of the power of open protocols.

4589608.abstract: Jamie congratulates Manton on launching micro.one, a simplified $10-a-year blogging service, praising it as an easy, affordable way to own a domain rather than rely on social media platforms.

4592253.abstract: Jamie responds to Jatan Mehta's question about whether one would blog if raised in the social media era, concluding "yes, I would absolutely blog." Jamie recounts a timeline starting with a blog in June 2004, joining Twitter in December 2006, leaving in 2017, and never primarily writing on Facebook.

4593004.abstract: Jamie shares a new Shortcut, following up on the Micro.blog Collections Shortcuts post, that exports all Micro.blog collections into a JSON object listing each collection name with its photo URLs, addressing gaps in Micro.blog's built-in export for large blogs.

4812693.abstract: Jamie describes trying the Deep Woods Cabin room at Copper Cat Escape Games in Brainerd, recommended by staff member Allon as a favorite, after visiting the venue the previous day. Jamie's group completed the room with no clues in 13 minutes 8 seconds, calling it one of the best rooms attempted in Minnesota, room 61 overall.

494221.abstract: Jamie starts watching the new Twin Peaks (2017 TV series), having been a fan of the original 90's series and watched it multiple times. After the first episode, Jamie finds it weird but is eager to continue.

5119482.abstract: Jamie recounts a neighborhood teen twice offering to shovel snow after snowfalls, initially declining since the shoveling was nearly done. Reflecting on valuing kids' entrepreneurial efforts, like neighborhood lemonade stands, Jamie reconsiders and hires the teen, who does a great job.

5120821.abstract: Jamie, Tyler, and Tammy complete The Istanbul Gambit at Enigma Adventures in Bloomington with 1m 39s remaining, marking their 64th escape room. Jamie praises the room's pacing, laser-based solve, and multiple objectives, including a completed bonus mission.

5120822.abstract: Jamie and Tammy Thingelstad attend a Valentine's Concert by The New Standards at The Woman's Club of Minneapolis, held in the dining room rather than the usual theater. Jamie notes the sound felt underpowered for the room with no visible sound engineer, and that performer Chan seemed off compared to typical shows.

5121348.abstract: Jamie describes dinner at Gus Gus in St. Paul, where the family orders cheeseburgers after hearing they were excellent. Jamie's wife Tammy thinks the burger may top Lake and Irving's, while Jamie calls it a tie, but rates Gus Gus's fries and airy brioche bun as the deciding win.

5121827.abstract: Jamie recounts attending a David Francey concert at the Celtic Junction in Minneapolis with cousin Josh, Dawn, Paul, Jodi, and Tammy. Terra Spencer opens, then Francey performs with Chris Murphy, with standout songs "This Morning" (written for John Prine) and "The Breath Between"; Jamie compares Francey's cadence to Shane MacGowan's.

5121830.abstract: Jamie describes trying Collector Crypt's Elite Pokémon Gacha Machine after Tyler investigates an announcement, paying tokens for a random graded card via a Solana blockchain transaction. Jamie and Tyler pull a 1996 Japanese Venusaur Holo card with a PSA NM-MT 8 rating and plan to "burn" the NFT so Collector Crypt ships the physical card.

5121839.abstract: Jamie highlights favorite Super Bowl LIX commercials, naming Nike's "So Win" (set to Led Zeppelin) as the best, noting Gruber's agreement, followed by Rocket's "Take Me Home," WeatherTech's "Whatever Comes Your Way," Jeep's Harrison Ford spot, and ChatGPT's "The Intelligence Age."

5122716.abstract: Jamie shares a table listing Bitcoin books alongside the price of BTC at each book's release date, sourced from a Nostr post reshared from stacker.news, spanning titles from "Bitcoin: Beginner's Guide" (2014, $258) through "The Big Print" (2025, $101,405).

5122797.abstract: Jamie links to Simon Willison's blog post sharing an excerpt from a 1979 IBM training manual stating a computer can never be held accountable. Jamie reflects on how this holds up in the AI era and questions whether efforts to make AI appear accountable actually sidestep real accountability.

5126264.abstract: Jamie describes a first-time ice fishing trip on Piersons Lake, invited by Andy to Andy's ice house along with Liam and Mike, who was also fishing for the first time. Jamie notes augering holes for fun, using sonar to spot fish, and that everyone caught some.

5131575.abstract: Jamie describes a first visit to Berlin in Minneapolis to see the Tina Schlieske Sextet, featuring Tina Schlieske with Cody McKinney, Pete Hennig, Bryan Nichols, Zacc Harris, and Brandon Wozniak, playing two jazz sets highlighted by Frank Sinatra covers.

5132837.abstract: Jamie describes seeing Mason Jennings perform at the Dakota, calling the show wonderful and praising the wide selection of songs, the stories shared about them, and Jennings's unique voice. A black and white photo shows the performance.

5149122.abstract: Jamie creates a custom GPT for the Weekly Thing newsletter, loaded with all 310 published issues, accessible via ChatGPT to anyone with an account. Jamie suggests sample queries, like comparing views on Facebook versus TikTok or summarizing specific issues.

5149164.abstract: Jamie describes turning a personal Shortcut, previously used to calculate a "version number" based on age, into a SuperWidget phone widget that updates automatically each day at 5:00 AM. Jamie places it beside the Four Thousand Weeks widget and reflects that the version number feels more personally meaningful than the weeks-remaining rings.

5149169.abstract: Jamie describes trying homemade marshmallows made by brother-in-law Denny, in vanilla and chocolate flavors, roasted over a fire pit. Jamie notes the cube-shaped marshmallows are larger and heavier than store-bought ones, with a crunchy exterior and gooey interior, though too gooey for S'mores.

5202669.abstract: Jamie describes a third performance by The High Kings, this time at The Fitzgerald Theater, calling it the best of the three after earlier shows in March 2024 and August 2024. The crowd sings along to "Red is the Rose," and the band announces a return for the Irish Fair of Minnesota this summer.

5203720.abstract: Jamie joins Shivani Stumpf, Amy Patton, Teddy Bekele, and Jadee Hanson for a September 15, 2020 panel on managing technology teams through the shift to fully remote work, covering hiring, onboarding, training, promotion, and predictions for lasting changes.

5203760.abstract: Jamie describes a new "Sync OmniFocus" Shortcuts action added in OmniFocus 4.5.2, connecting it to a mention by Ken Case in Omni Group's 2025 Roadmap podcast.

5222413.abstract: Jamie notes a price drop for Wegovy, quoting an Economist report that Novo Nordisk cut the monthly cost from over $1,300 to $499 for uninsured US patients via its online pharmacy, amid competition with Eli Lilly's Zepbound.

5227165.abstract: Jamie details how AI, via a ChatGPT subscription with Shortcuts automation, assists in producing the Weekly Thing newsletter—generating subject line options, content-relevant fortunes, byline drafts, Supporting Members messaging using Buttondown and Stripe data, and final grammar edits—while emphasizing that AI never writes the actual commentary…

5236903.abstract: Jamie recounts completing "The Hospital" escape room at Puzzleworks in Minnesota, the 65th escape room attempt, finishing in 54 minutes 47 seconds. Jamie's wife Tammy ranks it among a personal "top 10," and Jamie praises the room's elevator mechanic and well-balanced puzzle difficulty.

5237302.abstract: Jamie describes reconciling the family's list of completed escape rooms by cross-referencing blog posts, photos, YNAB financial records, and Apple iCloud calendars, raising the count from 43 to 65 rooms, and links to the updated list on thingelstad.com.

5237569.abstract: While doing blog gardening, Jamie notices it has been 16 years since appearing as a guest on MPR's Midmorning show discussing Twitter, and revisits the original post after running the audio through Whisper Transcription to add a transcript.

5246560.abstract: Jamie attends an Anselm House lecture titled "Are We Merely Machines?" featuring Rosalind W. Picard of the MIT Media Lab, covering materialism, scientism, and ontology.

5267025.abstract: Jamie announces hosting the April IndieWeb Carnival with the theme "Renewal," suggested by Tammy over a family dinner after struggling to settle on a topic.

5285728.abstract: Jamie recounts the travel day launching a Florida spring break trip: a ride to MSP, dinner at Settebello Pizzeria, greeting Kim and Tony, and a Delta flight delayed by storms before arriving in Orlando near 1am to a nearby Holiday Inn.

5286088.abstract: Jamie recounts day one of a Florida spring break trip: donuts at Peachey's, botanical gardens, a drive to Anna Maria Island, a beach walk at sunset, and card games (Sevens, Blackjack, BS) suggested by Tyler.

5286096.abstract: Jamie recounts first trying Peachey's Donuts, based in Sarasota, Florida, at the Minnesota State Fair with the family. During a Spring Break trip, Jamie's wife Tammy arranged a stop at Peachey's for breakfast, where they also tried the pretzel.

5286260.abstract: Jamie recounts day two of a Florida spring break: Tammy and Mazie run in the morning, breakfast at Mademoiselle Paris, beach gear rental from Fun & More, beach time, dinner at The Porch, a bike ride, and a sunset beach visit followed by an evening walk with Tammy, Mazie, and Tyler.

5287938.abstract: Jamie recounts day three of a Florida spring break: donuts, horse riding for Tammy, Mazie, and Tyler, a shoreline walk, lunch at The Waterfront, shopping stops, beach time, ice cream from a boat, and biking to dinner at The Porch.

5287945.abstract: Jamie describes encountering an ice cream boat at Anna Maria Beach, run by Project 11:11, a charity started by Erin Gallivan from Bradenton that raises money for veterans through ice cream sales, and shares links to the organization's profiles and GoFundMe page.

5290841.abstract: Jamie recounts day four of a Florida spring break trip with Tammy, Mazie, and Tyler, including breakfast at Ginny and Jane E's, a boat tour with Jeremy featuring snorkeling, manatees, and dolphins, dinner at SMOQEHOUSE, a final beach sunset, and late-night ice cream at Dips.

5290843.abstract: Jamie recounts day five of a Florida spring break trip, starting at Turner's donuts before spending the day at Kennedy Space Center, visiting the Rocket Garden, Astronaut Hall of Fame, a VIP bus tour, and the Atlantis building, then driving 281 miles to St. Augustine.

5291180.abstract: Jamie contrasts blogging with social media's engagement-driven feedback loops, citing Manton Reece's post "no one cares (for now)" and an email from Manuel Moreale as a rare exception to blogging's typical silence.

5292093.abstract: Jamie recounts day six of a Florida spring break in St. Augustine, including a run by Jamie's wife Tammy and Mazie, breakfast at Blue Hen Cafe, a chocolate tour at Whetstone Chocolates, downtown shopping, a fort visit, and dinner at Saint.

5293528.abstract: Jamie recounts the final day of a Florida spring break trip: driving from St. Augustine to Orlando, visiting Discovery Cove, revisiting the Crazy Train Escape Room, then flying home and finally getting to sleep at 2:00 am.

5293537.abstract: Jamie describes visiting Doldrick's Escape Room in Florida to play "Crazy Train: The Ballad Of Skeemin' Plotz," ranked 61st in the world by the 2024 Top Escape Rooms Project. Jamie's wife Tammy found the ranking, and the group completes the 75-minute room, their 66th escape room overall, using no clues.

5293737.abstract: Jamie recounts visiting Smoqehouse's Anna Maria Island location, recalling the original Faribault, MN spot near the family cabin (opened 2016, later closed) and the Northfield location destroyed by a kitchen fire.

5294048.abstract: Jamie shares photos and a brief account of a boat tour with Crysten's AMI on the bay side of Anna Maria Island, guided by Jeremy, featuring snorkeling for sand dollars, crabs, and shells, plus manatee and dolphin sightings.

5294174.abstract: Jamie watches Into the Wild with Mazie, having first seen it in 2008 and read the book soon after. They discuss the film and revisit the Chris McCandless Wikipedia article, noting updates, and Jamie still finds the Eddie Vedder soundtrack amazing.

5294363.abstract: Jamie plans to distribute a POAP for Minnebar 19 using three IYK POAP Discs at the venue, an approach simpler than the method used for Minnebar 17. Jamie also plans a special POAP Card for a newsletter session and a personal "You've met me POAP" IYK Card, and suggests attendees install the POAP Home App beforehand.

5294378.abstract: Jamie reflects on maps as storytelling tools, recalling a Canadian fishing trip where the group swapped stories over a map each evening, and argues blogs should better connect posts by location.

5294683.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a day spent at Discovery Cove in Orlando, presented as an embedded photo collection titled "Discovery Cove 2003."

5304035.abstract: Jamie links to a series of daily trip recaps by fellow blogger Barry Hess, who traveled to Florence and Cortona with family to visit a daughter studying there. Jamie compares the posts to Jamie's own 2023 family trip to Florence and lists all twelve posts spanning March 27 to April 7.

5313662.abstract: Jamie quotes The Economist's report that Gary Shapley, installed as acting IRS boss reportedly at Elon Musk's behest, will be replaced after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent complained to Trump, marking the fifth person in the role this year. Jamie argues this reflects chaos and dysfunction, not efficient governance.

5321288.abstract: Jamie describes escaping "The Dungeon" room at Puzzleworks, calling the puzzles challenging and the mechanics impressive, with a well-constructed story that starts players in separate rooms. Jamie notes the game master granted a few extra minutes, marking this as escape Room 67, and shares photos of the completion time of 59:34.

5323626.abstract: Jamie recounts completing "The Anomaly," a new escape room at Puzzleworks, divided into three 20-minute segments with heavy parallel puzzles, only one lock, and computer-based interaction, scoring 63,550 points for 17th place on the leaderboard—room 68 overall.

5327943.abstract: Jamie invites readers attending Minnebar 19 to say hello in person and receive a "You Met Jamie Thingelstad at Minnebar 19" POAP token, redeemable via tap from an IYK card, linking to the token's page on POAP Gallery.

5327948.abstract: Jamie announces a special POAP created for attendees of the "How to Newsletter" session at Minnebar 19, with an NFC card available in the room for tapping to add the badge to a collection.

5327952.abstract: Jamie creates a Minnebar 19 POAP token to commemorate the event, following a similar POAP made for Minnebar 17 two years earlier. Meg Steuer at Minnestar shared the t-shirt graphics used for the animated design, and Jamie loads tokens onto POAP NFC discs placed around the event, recommending attendees download the POAP Home app.

5333349.abstract: Jamie reflects on research suggesting people listen to less new music as they age, and describes wanting to avoid that stagnation, citing Brandi Carlile as an artist discovered later in life alongside earlier favorites like Violent Femmes, Run-DMC, Hüsker Dü, The Replacements, and Uncle Tupelo.

5333393.abstract: Jamie rounds up submissions to the IndieWeb Carnival on the theme of Renewal, hosted for the first time this month, listing roughly 26 contributors including Lou Plummer, Sacha Chua, Frank Meeuwsen, Manu Moreale, and Jamie's own "Musical Renewal" post. Jamie also creates a commemorative POAP token to send to each participant.

5337196.abstract: Jamie recounts transporting the SPS Growth Cup trophy to the new Warsaw office, describing checking it as oversized luggage through Delta ($400 fee) and KLM (free but returned with a damaged wheel), meeting team members including Yuri and Eugene, and a tense security screening in Warsaw where a guard questions the trophy's purpose.

5337667.abstract: Jamie recounts watching Fighting With My Family, describing it as a good story about sibling rivalry set against professional wrestling, though not the comedy it was billed as. Jamie notes Dwayne Johnson appears in only four scenes, writer-director Stephen Merchant's humor is largely absent, and Vince Vaughn delivers the funniest moments.

5341641.abstract: Jamie adapts a Minnebar 19 presentation into an article detailing eight years of publishing The Weekly Thing newsletter, covering content curation via RSS and Pinboard, automation through Shortcuts and Data Jar, the Buttondown/OmniFocus toolchain, limited AI use, and sustainability practices like scheduled breaks and avoiding analytics.

5341996.abstract: Jamie sees comedian Nate Bargatze in Duluth for the first time, catching the opening night of the sold-out Big Dumb Eyes tour. Julian McCollough hosts, with opening bits from Steven Rogers, Keith Alberstadt, and Aaron Weber before Bargatze's set.

5341999.abstract: Jamie recaps sessions attended at Minnebar 19, covering talks by AnnMarie Thomas on play, Paul Cantrell on technology and authoritarianism, Joe Meyer on beekeeping tech, Greg and Jenny Swan on deepfakes, Jim Bernard on accordion and goal-setting, Cameron MacDonald on 3D printing basics, and Bill Gintz and David Quinn on product discovery…

5342290.abstract: Jamie traces the origin of the name Minnebar, starting with Tim O'Reilly's "Friends of O'Reilly" (FOO) events and Foo Camp, which led to the 2005 creation of BarCamp unconferences.

5342524.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a 1.63-mile hike at Jay Cooke State Park, completed in 51.6 minutes, describing the scenery and the day as delightful.

5346099.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a visit to Gooseberry Falls, describing a walk to the lake shore and back.

5368178.abstract: Jamie describes visiting Enigma Adventures in Maple Grove on Mother's Day to try the Pirates of the Spanish Main escape room, recommended by Copper Cat Escape Games.

5406528.abstract: Jamie describes acquiring a Traeger Grill from a brother-in-law who switched to a Blackstone Flat Top and wasn't using it. Jamie hopes the Traeger will produce better brisket than the Big Green Egg has managed, noting how simple it is to start.

5422279.abstract: Jamie announces the 612 POAP Challenge, combining location-based POAPs with the 612 Series NFT collection created by Erik Halaas, whom Jamie previously interviewed. The Minneapolis-based challenge runs until Labor Day, inviting participants to visit locations and collect POAPs; Jamie completed the first one via a walk.

5448037.abstract: Jamie celebrates Mazie's birthday by attending the Stone Arch Bridge Festival, noting its size and Minnesota-inspired art. Jamie lists favorite vendors including H. Ward Miles, where Mazie made a first art purchase, plus local artists considered for a future 612 POAP Challenge, and switchel from Hobby Farmer.

5449719.abstract: Jamie recounts a car ride with Mazie listening to Green Day, Screeching Weasel, Minor Threat and other punk bands, then draws a parallel between Punk Rock's DIY, anti-commercial, community-driven ethos and the IndieWeb movement.

5453399.abstract: Jamie follows up on the earlier post "IndieWeb is Punk" after Jim Mitchell created a matching t-shirt, linking to Jim's post announcing it. Jamie also made a POAP badge using Jim's artwork, had ChatGPT write its description in the voice of Henry Rollins, and offers claim codes to anyone who reaches out.

5468439.abstract: Jamie describes building POAP2RSS, a service providing RSS feeds for POAP token claims, using AI "vibe coding" tools including Claude, ChatGPT o-3 Deep Research, and OpenAI Codex.

5482508.abstract: Jamie tries an AI image prompt asking GPT-4o to turn a home kitchen photo into a black-and-white cinematic portrait with water droplets, as if the subject just emerged from water. Jamie finds the result intense but thinks it resembles a grandfather more than Jamie, and links to cousin Quinn Chrest's version of the same prompt.

5485185.abstract: Jamie describes solving the Gold Rush escape room at Escape in Time in Madison, rated hard, finishing with 13m 15s remaining despite needing clues at a few points. Jamie praises the location and the candy shop puzzle entrance, noting it as escape room number 73.

5489530.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy attend a Lord Huron concert at the Armory, marking their first time seeing the band live. Jamie describes enjoying the show despite limited familiarity with the music, comparing the sound to David Lynch's style and the complex song storylines to The Decemberists.

5492890.abstract: Jamie recounts day one of a trip to Burlington, Vermont with Tammy, Mazie, and Tyler, including a delayed, oversold Delta flight, checking into Hotel Vermont, and exploring Church Street Marketplace shops like Phoenix Books and Outdoor Gear Exchange before dinner at Veritá Pizzeria.

5492902.abstract: Jamie explains the acronym QMSB, naming the four segments of a summer vacation: Quebec, Montreal, Stowe, and Bismarck. Montreal includes the first Olson Family Vacation with Tammy's side of the family, Stowe continues that trip, and Bismarck involves a cousin's wedding in North Dakota.

5493827.abstract: Jamie recounts a 23rd wedding anniversary marked by a rained-out Island Line Trail bike plan in Burlington, a drive into Quebec through the Highgate Springs border crossing, and exploring Old Quebec with stops at Cow's Ice Cream and Chocolats Favoris, followed by an anniversary dinner at Le Clan while the kids dine at Le Chic Shack.

5494866.abstract: Jamie recounts day three of a Quebec City trip: breakfast at La Buche, exploring Old Quebec's stairways and Parc Montmorency, and visiting Beauchamp Art Gallery. Jamie later visits Strøm Nordic Spa while Tammy, Mazie, and Tyler go horseback riding, before everyone reunites for pizza at Nina and escape rooms at Cabinet Mysteriis.

5495800.abstract: Jamie recounts day four of a Quebec trip, hiking at Mont Sainte-Anne while Tammy, Mazie, and Tyler go canyoning, then visiting Montmorency Falls, Ile d'Orleans farms and cafes, Basilica of Sainte-Anne-de-Beaupré, and an escape room at Cabinet Mysteriis.

5498545.abstract: Jamie recounts leaving Quebec for Laval, completing two escape rooms at Escaparium, and lunch at Birdhouse Wings, before driving into Montreal to begin Olson Family Vacation 2025 with a Notre Dame Basilica lightshow, Bevo Pizza, and a walk to the Grande roue de Montréal.

5502246.abstract: Jamie recounts a Montreal vacation day including coffee at Structure Coffee, a guided bike tour with Montreal on Wheels, tea at Papermane Tea Room, card shop visits, a construction update call with Quartersawn, Men's dinner at Vieux-Port Steakhouse, and Old Port evening activities including ziplining and Taylor Swift themed fireworks.

5503110.abstract: Jamie recounts day 7 of the Montreal family vacation, including coffee at Structure Coffee, jet boating with Jet Boating Montreal, a bagel-making class at The Bagel Class, a stop at a Mount Royal lookout, and an evening performance of Cirque du Soleil's Luzia.

5503495.abstract: Jamie describes visiting Magnifico at Escaparium, ranked the World's #1 Escape Room by TERPECA 2024, calling it unlike any escape room experienced before. Jamie's family, Tammy, Mazie, and Tyler, share reactions describing it as private interactive theater blending puzzles, actors, rides, and magic tricks within a circus-themed story.

5503530.abstract: Jamie recounts day 8 of the QMSB trip, visiting Columbuse Cafe and Structure Coffee, then driving to Laval for the Magnifico escape room at Escaparium, lunch at Birdhouse, and ice cream before crossing back into the United States.

5504557.abstract: Jamie recounts day 9 of the QMSB trip, also Olson Family Vacation day 5, including watching the Hungarian Grand Prix, visiting Stowe Farmer's Market and Stowe Bee Bakery, pool time, shopping in Stowe, the Ben & Jerry's Experience, and dinner at Doc Ponds.

5506989.abstract: Jamie recounts day 10 of the QMSB trip, also day 6 of the Olson Family Vacation, covering a Burlington bike ride via Local Motion and the Island Line Trail, snacks at August First and NU Chocolat, pool time, dinner at Doc Ponds and The Bistro at Ten Acres, and creemees at Red Barn Ice Cream.

5508594.abstract: Jamie links to a Nature article, "Writing is Thinking," which argues that writing forces structured thought rather than reporting results alone, and quotes its point about sorting research into a coherent story.

5508649.abstract: Jamie recounts the final day of a Vermont trip, including a coffee run to Vermont Artisanal Coffee, a history tour and hike to the chapel at Von Trapp Family Resort, a bike ride in Stowe with Tammy, and a farewell dinner at Idletyme Brewing Company.

5509450.abstract: Jamie describes visiting Cabinet Mysteriis in Quebec for an immersive escape room called Dreamwalkers, featuring no visible timer or screens, confiscated watches, knit slippers, and a game master named Mr Fox appearing through an old TV cabinet. Jamie's group did not solve the room within 75 minutes but enjoyed the experience.

5509451.abstract: Jamie recounts playing "2002: A Bovine Odyssey," the second escape room of a double header at Cabinet Mysteriis following Dreamwalkers. Jamie describes challenging puzzles requiring AI game master help and a puzzle malfunction resolved through an in-character "space pizza delivery man" fix, praising the immersive design.

5509452.abstract: Jamie describes returning to Cabinet Mysteriis for a third escape room, Screaming Metal, set in a post-apocalyptic hostage scenario with actors, including one carrying a baseball bat. The group escapes within the hour, and Jamie praises the authentic ending and immersive story.

5509453.abstract: Jamie recounts the final day of the Olson Family Vacation 2025, covering Stowe: breakfast at Stowe Bee Cafe, shopping, a last Maple Creemee at Red Barn Ice Cream, then driving to Burlington, returning the rental car, and flying Delta 4901 to Minneapolis before a one-night stop home ahead of the trip's next segment.

5509454.abstract: Jamie describes playing Lost Island of the Voodoo Queen at Escaparium, an escape room styled like a movie set featuring a dock, a moving ship, and an island where players save lost souls. Jamie's group completes the experience, breaking the Voodoo Queen's spell, and looks forward to other Escaparium rooms.

5509456.abstract: Jamie describes an escape room adventure at Escaparium following a morning session defeating the Voodoo Queen. A wardrobe in a hallway transports the group to another world guided by a character named Moss, involving hidden secrets and a raft trip down a river to a hidden cave to save Moss and friends before returning through another wardrobe.

5512821.abstract: Jamie recounts completing "The Experiment" at Escape Room Alexandria, escaping with 6 minutes 46 seconds remaining, noting puzzles that shifted from parallel solving to coordinated teamwork. Jamie also mentions chatting with owner Lindsay, who has done over 200 rooms, marking this as room 80 on Jamie's escape room list.

5512824.abstract: Jamie logs day 13 of the QMSB trip, driving to Alexandria, Minnesota for ice cream at Up North Ice Cream and the Mad Scientist room at Escape Room Alexandria, then continuing to Fergus Falls to check into the newly opened Mill Boutique Hotel and dine at Union Avenue.

5514404.abstract: Jamie describes visiting Puzzled Escape Rooms in Fargo to complete the Time Machine room, calling it fun but an older-style room heavy on codes and locks, with the beginning proving hardest. This marks Room 81 on Jamie's escape room list, and a photo shows four people posing with wooden signs at the venue.

5514409.abstract: Jamie recounts day 14 of the QMSB trip, covering breakfast in Fergus Falls, a walk at Prairie Wetlands Learning Center, shopping downtown, then crossing into North Dakota for an escape room, shops, and food stops around Fargo, including Ferguson Books and Silver Lining Creamery.

5516315.abstract: Jamie, Jamie's wife Tammy, Mazie and Tyler visit Breakout ND in Bismarck to play the Gemini Quantum Quest escape room, splitting into two starting groups before joining forces and completing the game with 11 minutes 15 seconds remaining.

5516318.abstract: Jamie recounts leaving Fargo for Bismarck, North Dakota, with stops at Youngblood Coffee Roasters, Prairie Kitchen, Fireflour Pizza, and downtown spots including Anima Cucina and Brick Oven Bakery, plus an escape room at Breakout ND and Amanda & Reid's wedding reception at Baymont in Mandan with relatives.

5516991.abstract: Jamie recounts the final leg of the QMSB trip: checking out of Baymont in Mandan, coffee at Joyhouse, gas and Culver's in Fargo, entering Minnesota, ice cream at Cocoa Maas in Monticello, then arriving home in Minneapolis.

5523624.abstract: Jamie describes seeing Ruthie Foster perform a solo set with a guitar named Pearl at the Dakota jazz club. Jamie notes this was a first time seeing Foster play, praises the songs and accompanying stories, and calls the performance great.

5523635.abstract: Jamie describes using GPT-5 to generate short introduction texts for blog categories, referencing Manton Reece's post on category improvements and noting a dependency on Tiny Theme to display them.

5525902.abstract: Jamie describes using GPT-5 in Agent mode to analyze over 9,800 blog posts spanning 20+ years at thingelstad.com/archive/ and recommend a new category structure. The AI spent 31 minutes researching and proposed 32 categories, from Travel & Adventure to Weekly Thing (Newsletter), each with descriptions and example posts.

5525915.abstract: Jamie describes a conversation with Matt about adding a Tiny Theme feature for blogging dialogs, like Messages exchanges or AI chats, with left/right sides and author names. Jamie shares custom CSS for this, posting chat.css for others to use.

5566832.abstract: Jamie describes a supplement program developed with a wellness-focused doctor after comprehensive blood testing, similar in spirit to Peter Attia's approach. The regimen includes Premium Insurance Caps, Elite EPA Gems (soon switching to O.N.E. Omega), Vitamin D3, and DHEA, with Curcumin likely added; retesting is planned in 2-3 months.

5574183.abstract: Jamie quotes two Economist briefs describing ABC's indefinite suspension of Jimmy Kimmel's late-night show after comments about Charlie Kirk's killer, following FCC chairman Brendan Carr's warning about broadcast licenses and Trump's praise of Disney's action.

5575014.abstract: Jamie recaps the 10th anniversary of SPS TechJam 2025, an internal "unconference" featuring talks from volunteer team members and an AI-focused Hackathon, describing the presentations and learning as incredible.

5575694.abstract: Jamie describes a first visit to the Lakeville Art Festival, praising the grass setup and separated food and music area with picnic tables, plus lunch from Pizzeria 201, HomeTown Creamery ice cream, and Groveland Confections chocolate.

5584204.abstract: Jamie checks in on a Dappnode running 32 validators for the Gnosis blockchain and finds it has been running for over a year without updates. Jamie applies pending updates to Core, Dms, Nethermind Xdai, and Teku Gnosis packages, requiring a couple of reboots, and gets everything synced and current using only a web browser.

5584213.abstract: Jamie describes a focused Pokémon card collection tracked on a Collectr profile, built with help from Tyler. Jamie collects every Perrserker card (feeling a Nordic kinship with its Viking helmet), Alakazam cards (tied to a past love of playing Wizards in Dungeons & Dragons), and graded cards that simply look cool, totaling 31 cards so far.

5584217.abstract: Jamie joins Pokémon TCG Pocket after noticing a special event and seeing that Tyler has collected on the app for a long time, sharing a friend code for connecting. Jamie observes that the app resembles what Pokémon might build if pursuing digital collectibles like NFTs, training users on collectible behaviors in a new digital ecosystem.

5584227.abstract: Jamie compares using OpenAI API calls versus Apple Intelligence models directly in Shortcuts on OS 26, noting the OpenAI approach requires fussy JSON handling and API keys while being brittle and error-prone.

5585334.abstract: Jamie reflects on never seeing John Prine perform live before Prine's death in 2020, recalling discovering the songwriter through the CD set Great Days: The John Prine Anthology. Jamie describes a Dakota show by former Prine bandmates Jason Wilber and Dave Jacques, who performed Prine's catalog and raised funds for the Hello in There Foundation.

5594932.abstract: Jamie forks Lukas Ros's outdated Plausible Analytics plug-in for micro.blog, creating Plausible Analytics 2, available on GitHub, which uses the current embed code snippet and adds a Plausible icon, and recommends micro.blog users switch to it.

5603466.abstract: Jamie's friend Lee Zukor plays in the band The Long Honeymoon, whose debut album "The World is Waiting" is now out. Jamie buys a copy on Bandcamp and, after listening twice during a North Shore drive with Tammy, describes it as having a distinctly Minneapolis sound reminiscent of the Jayhawks, Gear Daddies and Honeydogs.

5610505.abstract: Jamie and Tammy attend the Twin Cities Film Fest screening of Good Fortune at the Edina 4 theatre, marking Jamie's first Film Fest event with an audience vote. The movie, starring Keanu Reeves, Aziz Ansari, Seth Rogen, Keke Palmer, and Sandra Oh, follows Arj and Jeff swapping lives via Gabriel the Angel; Jamie and Tammy both rate it four stars.

5610512.abstract: Jamie, Tammy, and Tyler see Tron: Ares at Emagine Willow Creek, continuing Jamie's Tron fandom since watching the original at age 10 in Jamestown, ND.

561648.abstract: Jamie describes spilling a full cup of Dunn Bros coffee across the desk, then dropping an iPad and knocking the cup again, spraying coffee onto the wall, before accidentally hanging up on a conference call while trying to mute it.

5627714.abstract: Jamie describes hiking at Lebanon Hills Regional Park with Tammy, letting Tammy lead without a planned route. Random turns take them to a parking lot on the opposite side of the park near Valleywood Golf Course, stretching the outing to 6–7 miles, and Jamie shares photos of the lake, trails, and autumn foliage along the way.

5629880.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy suggests watching Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure (1989) after a conversation with Tyler about movies from their youth. Jamie finds it hasn't aged that well, notes how young Keanu Reeves looks, and describes Tyler picking apart the time-travel plot and questioning the era's lack of smartphones.

5633382.abstract: Jamie describes picking up new progressive lens glasses after relying on readers as eyesight worsened. Jamie notes the lenses feature 400 specific positions and expects a couple weeks of adjustment, hoping for less eye fatigue by day's end.

5643883.abstract: Jamie reports the annual candle fundraiser raised $9,048 from 73 buyers, a 29.1% increase over 2024, split among four chosen organizations: Animal Welfare Institute, Border Angels, The Food Group, and Sandy Hook Promise.

5643906.abstract: Jamie reviews the 5th annual Things 4 Good Candle Fundraiser, which raised $9,048, up 29.1% from last year, selling 321 candles across eleven scents including new addition Charcoal Rose. Jamie highlights new offerings like T4G Labs, Rekindled candles, XL 24oz candles, and lids, plus supply challenges and checkout improvements planned for next year.

5643909.abstract: Jamie reviews five years of the Things 4 Good Candle Fundraiser, noting a total of $31,787 raised for non-profits, with 2025 bringing $9,048 and 73 unique transactions after selling 321 candles.

5644026.abstract: Jamie references The Omni Show episode "How Jorge Arango Uses OmniFocus," where Arango cites Gall's Law: complex working systems evolve from simple ones, while complex systems designed from scratch fail.

5644907.abstract: Jamie announces the end of the Weekly Thing Forum, hosted on Ponder, following Good Enough's decision to shut down Ponder.

5654312.abstract: Jamie and Tyler tour four Twin Cities Pokémon card shops: Viral Card Games in Fridley, praised for organization and its TCG Player-based bulk search kiosks; Ultimate Collectibles' warehouse sale at the Hopkins VFW, tipped by brother-in-law Max; MN Poke Pulls in Plymouth, tied to Whatnot live-auction box breaks; and Lost Zone Cards in Bloomington…

5654318.abstract: Jamie notes that the Things 4 Good Candle Fundraiser has surpassed 1,125 candles sold since 2021, with yearly totals of 134, 180, 226, 264 and 321. Jamie calculates the 1,000th candle sold was the 196th candle of the 2025 sale, in the 40th transaction.

5664838.abstract: Jamie describes using OmniFocus "Idea Lists" to track books, shows, restaurants and gift ideas as a specific form of "someday, maybe" lists. Jamie shares a custom Shortcut called "Add to List" that integrates with the share sheet to quickly capture items into the right list, and links to download it.

5672361.abstract: Jamie shares observations from MnTech Outlook 2026, where panelists including Eric Pratt, Kristin Bahner, and Tarek Tomes discuss AI and transformation as top priorities.

5686188.abstract: Jamie describes POAP's new Airport POAP Rally 2026 collection, featuring location-based POAPs at 100 airports worldwide, and compares its scope to the earlier 612 POAP Challenge covering 31 Minneapolis locations.

5696699.abstract: Jamie recaps 100 days of collecting in Pokémon TCG Pocket, begun in September around the First Anniversary celebration after Tyler had been playing since launch. Jamie made in-app purchases for Poke Gold, subscribed to the Premium Pass, and shares a chart showing near-complete Dex coverage across promo sets.

5704827.abstract: Jamie recounts a visit to the Legend of the Yeti escape room at The Escape Game Nashville, describing a slow start caused by an unexplored puzzle the game master missed, though the group ultimately solves the room, marking room 84 on Jamie's escape room list.

5705323.abstract: Jamie recaps 2025's escape room adventures, completing 25 rooms total, a personal high compared to previous years back to 2016.

5705369.abstract: Jamie attends Opry Country Christmas at the Grand Ole Opry, describing an evening featuring The Gatlin Brothers, RaeLynn, Mandy Barnett, Tasha Layton, Riders in the Sky, Charlie McCoy, John Berry, and spotlight artist The War and Treaty. Jamie shares photos of the decorated stage, performers, and audience.

5724927.abstract: Jamie describes visiting the World Snow Celebration on a cold morning to see teams finishing snow sculptures ahead of a deadline and participating in the People's Choice vote, selecting Team Falcon of Mongolia while Jamie's wife Tammy chose Team Warm Your Cold Brits.

5725065.abstract: Jamie announces the Yearly Thing 2025: Agents, Attention, Artifacts, a book compiling all 324 links commented on across 31 issues of the Weekly Thing in 2025, organized into 10 topic chapters covering AI, software, privacy, cryptocurrency, Apple, blogging, attention, leadership, health and productivity.

5725150.abstract: Jamie links to Peter Rukavina's graph of Amazon spending and creates a similar chart using personal purchase data requested from Amazon's Privacy Center. The resulting graph, shown without scale, reveals a sharp jump in 2015 that continues into the 2020s, a pattern Jamie finds surprising given family comments about frequent Amazon purchases.

5737487.abstract: Jamie describes a trip to Northfield with Tyler, stopping at Content Bookstore, Games n' Geek, and Little Joy Coffee for a Flat White. At Games n' Geek, Jamie buys a 1-of-1 miscut Galarian Perrserker V card previously seen for sale, adding it to a complete Perrserker collection, and considers sending it to PSA for grading.

5737909.abstract: Jamie orders Orka Bar, a high-protein ice cream treat, after seeing it featured on Shark Tank, and finally receives it months later after a backlog of orders. Jamie finds the egg white, cream, and whey protein bars tasty despite a messy, thin chocolate shell, and would buy them regularly if sold in grocery stores.

5776605.abstract: Jamie describes ringing the Nasdaq closing bell in New York with SPS Commerce, a third such experience after the 2014 opening bell and 2023 closing bell (marking CEO Archie Black's retirement). This visit celebrates SPS Commerce reaching 100 quarters of consistent growth, with 100 customers attending the reception and ceremony.

5781632.abstract: Jamie describes improving Elixir's intelligence by refactoring its data and tools with Codex using GPT-5.4. Steps include an ERD analysis of shortcomings, Clash Royale API reconnaissance, tool redesign, and testing with 50 questions developed with Claude, all completed in 45 minutes.

5789430.abstract: Jamie describes shipping three new features in Elixir, a Clash Royale bot, during morning coffee: stronger memory for clan continuity, tracking of ladder and Path of Legend momentum (a Codex-suggested feature from cr-api-docs), and an upcoming weekly clan recap, with links to GitHub diffs and commits.

5792949.abstract: Jamie recounts the days surrounding a cancelled flight to Europe, including having to reschedule an escape room and give up plans to see the Anne Frank museum.

5794783.abstract: Jamie logs a long travel day in the Netherlands: arriving at AMS airport, storing luggage, then train trips to Delft for breakfast at Kek and sightseeing, followed by Den Haag, where the Escher museum is closed but Madurodam is visited.

5794785.abstract: Jamie recounts a day trip from Amsterdam to Utrecht, including two escape rooms, fresh stroopwaffels, exploring the city, a stop at Keen Coffee, a music box museum, and dinner at Casa Damstraat, while Jamie's wife Tammy secures Brandi Carlile tickets.

5796516.abstract: Jamie recounts a day trip from Amsterdam to Brussels, traveling by metro and Eurocity train. Highlights include waffles at Maison Dandoy, visiting Mok Studio, an escape room at Botanist Manor, a chocolate-making workshop, and dinner at Wolf Food Hall with Tyler and Jamie's wife Tammy before returning by train and taxi to Hendricks Hotel.

5798199.abstract: Jamie recounts day five of a European trip in Amsterdam with Tammy and Tyler, including the Alchemist escape room, a canal cruise, and multiple visits to Tony's Chocolonely Super Store. The group also trains to Hilversum for dinner at Mout Food Hall and the Zoltar Speaks escape room before returning to Amsterdam.

5799248.abstract: Jamie recounts day 6 of a European trip: Tammy runs, then coffee at Sango and pancakes at Pat's Poffertjes in Amsterdam before checking out of Hendrick's Hotel and taking a Eurostar train to Paris.

5804381.abstract: Jamie recounts day seven of a European trip, spent at Disneyland Paris with Tammy, Mazie and Tyler. Highlights include Hyperspace Mountain, Nautilus, Pirates of the Caribbean, Phantom Manor, dinner at Bistrot Chez Rémy, and the Disney Cascade of Lights show before checking into the Disneyland Hotel.

5804382.abstract: Jamie logs a day-long visit to Disneyland Paris, tracking ride times and wait strategies for Peter Pan, Big Thunder Mountain, Indiana Jones, Crush's Coaster and Avengers (including single rider line tips), plus seeing TOGETHER: a Pixar Musical Adventure and the Magic Mickey show, shopping for Disneyland Paris gear, Mazie's evening departure to…

5807257.abstract: Jamie recounts day nine of a Europe trip, covering a Metro ride to Parc des Princes for a Paris Saint-Germain stadium tour and shopping, lunch at Specimen burgers, a visit to Notre Dame, an escape room called Galactic Mission, and stops at a Pokémon shop and Ben's Cookies before returning to the Airbnb.

5807287.abstract: Jamie recounts day 10 of a Europe trip, spent in Paris, including an escape room called The Taxidermist, lunch at Ladurée, a walk to the Arc de Triomphe, and an evening Bateaux Parisiens dinner cruise on the Seine past the illuminated Eiffel Tower.

5808256.abstract: Jamie describes traveling by train from Paris to Barcelona via Gare de Lyon, arriving in the afternoon and settling into an Airbnb near Sant Pau.

5810121.abstract: Jamie recounts day 12 of a European trip in Barcelona, including brunch at Billy Brunch, exploring Park Güell, visiting Arte Vistas Gallery and the Picasso Museum, and pastries at Brunells Patisserie.

5811707.abstract: Jamie recounts day 13 of a European trip in Barcelona, including a paella cooking class with a market visit, coffee at Nomad Coffee Bar, and Pokémon card shopping at Arco TCG after Gameria proves disappointing.

5812600.abstract: Jamie shares an itinerary called "Mazie's Barcelona Finale," a self-guided tour through Barcelona with 18 stops, including the Arc de Triomf, Parc de la Ciutadella, El Born Centre de Cultura, Barrio Gótico, Casa Batlló, Gràcia, and dinner at La Alcobita, plus recommended food stops like Boldú, 99 Cheesecake, and El Desván Bakery.

5813291.abstract: Jamie recounts the final travel day of a European trip: Daylight Savings begins in Spain, and Tammy and Mazie fly Vueling to Split, Croatia while Jamie and Tyler fly Delta from Barcelona through Amsterdam to Minneapolis, including a tight connection, a running dash to the gate, and a 40-minute delay for a medical deplaning.

5834094.abstract: Jamie describes a rapid onset of facial cellulitis and sepsis, starting with chills and ear pain that worsened quickly, forcing missed plans to see Bruce Springsteen in concert.

5835666.abstract: Jamie adapts an internal talk into a blog post arguing that AI and agentic development are transforming software from a costly, rigid "solid" into something malleable, or "liquid," fundamentally changing how discovery, proof of concept, and team roles work.

5840025.abstract: Jamie quotes Om Malik's "Software Eats Its Own" on Anthropic's Claude Code revenue hitting a $2.5 billion run-rate, doubling since January, with company ARR reaching roughly $30 billion. Jamie calls the scaling remarkable and hard to comprehend.

5863188.abstract: Jamie describes building a new website for the Weekly Thing newsletter using Claude Code, Claude Design, and Codex, calling it a project previously too costly to attempt.

5863195.abstract: Jamie describes building Your Version Number, a website expanding on Jamie's 2018 blog post applying software versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) to age, storing data in the URL with over 20 visual themes, plus a Work Edition using YEARS.QUARTERS.BUSINESS_DAYS versioning and workplace-themed layouts, built with Claude Code.

5867140.abstract: Jamie describes seeing "The Sheep Detectives" at Willow Creek with Tyler, Tammy, and Tammy's Mom near Mother's Day, after Tyler noticed the preview and thought Tammy would enjoy it. Jamie finds the film a touching "whodunnit" story that works well with sheep as principal characters.

5872375.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy attend a Suburbs show at the Parkway Theater in Minneapolis, having never previously seen the band despite regularly seeing Chan Poling perform with The New Standards. Jamie notes many audience members wore black Suburbs t-shirts, suggesting a crowd of dedicated fans.

5872650.abstract: Jamie describes creating a four-agent AI support team, built on Discord and the Weekly Thing archive, to assist with publishing the newsletter after nine years of manual workflows.

5881438.abstract: Jamie describes attending the first meeting of Minnesota's Technology Advisory Council after an official appointment by Governor Walz to advise Minnesota IT Services (MNIT), which is preparing for a CIO and gubernatorial transition.

5904586.abstract: Jamie describes rebuilding Thingy, an archive chat agent originally built for the Weekly Thing newsletter, into a full agent covering thingelstad.com's 12,000+ blog posts and the Another Thing podcast too.

5924180.abstract: Jamie describes building six autonomous agent automations for Elixir, the bot running the Clash Royale clan at poapkings.com: Data Analyst, Product Manager, Build Manager, Quality Manager, Operations Manager, and Evaluator.

5939193.abstract: Jamie recounts arriving in Seattle for World Cup travel, flying Delta flight 881, collecting an airport POAP, and taking a Lyft to an Airbnb. Jamie visits a FIFA store and a Macron store, eats smash burgers at Secret Burger Kitchen, and walks past The Spheres and Serious Pie while exploring downtown Seattle.

5939194.abstract: Jamie recounts day two of the Seattle World Cup trip, starting with Mochi Waffles at Mr Waffle, coffee at Fonte, and Bill Speidel's Underground Tour, followed by lunch at Serious Pie and pastries at La Panier.

5939195.abstract: Jamie recounts day three of a Seattle trip, including a Boeing Future of Flight factory tour led by Val, coffee at Gloom Coffee, lunch at Mr Waffle, and an escape room at Locurio's The Storykeeper. The day ends with a Lime scooter ride through Fremont and dinner at Aerlume with Tyler.

5939196.abstract: Jamie recounts the last day of a Seattle World Cup trip: checking out of an Airbnb, breakfast at 5 Spot in Queen Anne, a stop at Kerry Park for views, a scooter ride with luggage, and the flight home on Delta 941.

5967543.abstract: Jamie logs travel details for the start of a trip to Porto, including a Lyft ride to the airport, dinner at Shake Shack in MSP Airport, and a delayed Delta flight (DL 162) departing MSP for Amsterdam at 8:55 p.m.

5967546.abstract: Jamie outlines a travel itinerary for the first day in Porto, covering a layover in Amsterdam, a flight to Porto on DL 9338, and settling into an Airbnb via metro.

5967547.abstract: Jamie's family spends a day in Porto that includes coffee at C'alma Coffee Room, brunch at CA Downtown, and escaping the Alice Escape Room at Cubus Escape in 48:31 without clues.

5992562.abstract: Jamie's cousin Josh Ellis has written the Rambling Josh column for over 20 years, roughly matching the age of Jamie's own blog. Jamie recalls helping Josh get the column's writing online in 2024 and now shares that Josh has published a signed book collecting the columns, linking to where to buy it and to Josh's post "Six and A Lot" about it.

6023599.abstract: Jamie reflects on AI's disruption of software development, building on Laurie Voss's essay "We are all product engineers now" and Jamie's own earlier "Software is Liquid" post.

6023610.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy attend a screening of "Out There: A National Parks Story" at the Parkway Theatre, followed by a panel with filmmaker Brendan Hall and supporting organizations.

6028654.abstract: Jamie describes a session with Claude in WT Builder to improve the generated audio for Weekly Thing podcast issues, including natural pauses, better section handoffs, spoken blockquotes and lists, embedded images, better pronunciation, and links now included in descriptions, making the podcast version a viable way to engage with Weekly Thing.

673051.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the Green Lake Triathlon, where Jamie's wife Tammy completes a first triathlon alongside Hector and Michelle. Jamie expresses pride in Tammy's new triathlete status.

673399.abstract: Jamie attends Push Conference 2007, listening to a talk by the director of the National Institute of Play and to Clyde Prestowitz, author of Rogue Nation and leader of the Economic Strategy Institute.

673524.abstract: Jamie compiles a series of tweets recounting a stranded night in New York after a flight home is delayed then cancelled. The tweets describe frustration over lack of WiFi at LaGuardia, seeing Frost/Nixon, staying at friends Hadar and Lois's, and finally boarding a flight the next morning.

71839.abstract: Jamie shares photos from Maker Faire, including a TARDIS replica, a Lego USS Missouri from Brickmania, and R2-D2. Jamie also congratulates Paul Boswell in person on the successful Turing Tumble Kickstarter and looks forward to receiving one.

729115.abstract: Jamie describes a Michael Franti & Spearhead concert at Music in the Zoo, calling the show inspiring for how the band engaged the audience, including bringing children on stage to sing and dance. Photos capture the band performing under colorful stage lighting.

778854.abstract: Jamie and Mazie walk the length of the High Line in Manhattan, from 30th Street south to the end, sharing photos of sculptures, murals, grasses, wildflowers and old railroad tracks captured with an iPhone XS camera. Jamie links to earlier visits to the High Line from 2012 and 2023.

778858.abstract: Jamie shares photos of a Birthday Cake from Milk Bar, brought home after a Daddy/Daughter trip to NYC with Mazie, showing a three-layer funfetti cake with white frosting, rainbow sprinkles, and cookie crumble topping.

781650.abstract: Jamie shares photos from Minnedemo 30, noting excitement for the event and pride in SPS Commerce sponsoring as a Terabyte-level supporter, alongside images of the venue marquee and an SPS Commerce projection screen.

782458.abstract: Jamie describes a visit to the Minnesota Zoo's Jack-o-Lantern Spectacular, an event created by Passion for Pumpkins using 5,000 pumpkins, and praises the artistry, including large photo-style pumpkin displays.

783957.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a morning spent exploring Franconia Sculpture Park, noting the Twin Cities' access to great public art.

788322.abstract: Jamie shares photos of the newly opened 16th floor of SPS Tower, highlighting the growing team's new space, a Library area, bright colors and fun references throughout.

803052.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the 89th annual Mt. Olivet Lutefisk Dinner, describing a meal of Swedish meatballs, rice pudding with lingonberries, and lefse, alongside photos of the crowd, nephew Garrett, and family selfies.

805263.abstract: Jamie logs a day of road travel titled "Summer of Love," tracking a trip from loading the van through stops in Alexandria, Bismarck, and Dickinson, into a North Dakota wind storm, ending at a Days Inn in Glendive, Montana with surprisingly strong free WiFi.

805273.abstract: Jamie logs a day of driving through Montana, with timestamped stops including Circle, Lewistown, and Great Falls, a mention of Barack Obama campaigning nearby, and arrival at Glacier National Park by evening; links to the full Summer of Love photo collection.

805282.abstract: Jamie logs a day of driving from Kalispell, Montana toward Seattle, Washington, with stops in Coeur d'Alene, Idaho and Ellensburg, Washington, noting rain, $4.06-per-gallon gas, and arrival in Seattle by 7:20 pm, linking to the full Summer of Love Collection.

805296.abstract: Jamie logs day six of the "Summer of Love" trip, noting the F5 Networks office across from the Seattle hotel, unexpectedly sunny weather despite a rain forecast, and discovering the band The Blair St. Mugwumps, buying two of their albums.

805363.abstract: Jamie logs day 15 of the Summer of Love trip: a bakery and haircut stop, a visit to the Children's Museum in Portland, OR, falafel at Karams, gas at $4.16/gallon, an impromptu drive to Eugene, OR, and dinner at Mezza Luna Pizzeria.

805378.abstract: Jamie logs a day of travel: a Cafe Borgia at Full City Coffee in Eugene, a pit stop en route to the Redwood Forest, and arrival in Crescent City after what Jamie calls an awesome drive, with video to follow.

805384.abstract: Jamie logs day 17 of the Summer of Love trip: Mexican food at Torero's and breakfast at Good Harvest, both in Crescent City, CA, followed by a visit to see the Giant Redwoods, which Jamie calls awe inspiring and majestic.

805389.abstract: Jamie logs day 18 of the Summer of Love trip: a stop at Ramone's Bakery and Old Town in Eureka, CA, playing with pigeons with Mazie, then driving down Highway 101 toward San Francisco and eating at In-N-Out Burger for the first time.

805395.abstract: Jamie logs a day in San Francisco: seeking sourdough bakery recommendations, eating breakfast at Savor, finding parking difficult, replacing a bricked Linksys router with an AirPort Express, and preferring not staying in a hotel for this trip stop.

805409.abstract: Jamie logs travel updates from day 22 of the Summer of Love trip, departing San Francisco at 12:03 pm and arriving in Monterey, California by 2:08 pm, with a link to the full collection.

805420.abstract: Jamie logs a day 24 road trip down CA-1 toward Big Sur while listening to Jack Johnson, including a lunch stop at Nepenthe with an "unbelievable view" and a note calling it possibly the trip's best day so far.

805425.abstract: Jamie logs day 25 of the "Summer of Love" trip, including a morning visit to Carmel and the Blue Dog gallery, then an afternoon at the rental house with Mazie during nap time while Tammy stays in Carmel, interrupted by a carpenter drilling nearby.

805431.abstract: Jamie logs a road trip day from Monterey to Las Vegas, noting gas prices reaching $5.50/gallon and desert temperatures hitting 107°F while crossing the Mojave, then settling into a room at Mandalay Bay. Jamie links to the full Summer of Love Collection.

805441.abstract: Jamie logs day 27 of the Summer of Love series in Las Vegas, noting a pool visit, weighing Fathers Day plans like a Hoover Dam trip, and a walk to The Four Seasons to get Mazie macaroni and cheese.

805446.abstract: Jamie logs day 28 of the Summer of Love series with short notes: a pool visit, Fathers Day cake, mojitos in Black Cherry, Watermelon and Apple flavors, a dislike of Comic Sans MS, and a walk from Mandalay Bay down the Las Vegas strip that Jamie calls a mistake.

805452.abstract: Jamie logs a day in Las Vegas as part of the Summer of Love series: struggling to sleep, spending time at the pool lazy river, having lunch at Bobby Flay's Mesa Grill with a Cactus Pear Margarita, and a quote from Mazie about blogging.

805458.abstract: Jamie logs day 30 of the Summer of Love trip: leaving Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas, stopping at Hoover Dam, lunch in Flagstaff at Beaver Street Brewery, and arriving in Sedona, AZ, where Tammy reads about local snakes and dangerous creatures.

805470.abstract: Jamie logs day 32 of the Summer of Love road trip: heading to the Grand Canyon, waiting for Tammy and Mazie at a Flagstaff Target, getting the car's oil changed at a Honda dealer, and dinner at the New Jersey Pizza Company in Flagstaff.

805475.abstract: Jamie logs day 33 of the Summer of Love trip, visiting Montezuma Castle National Monument, having lunch at Judi's in Sedona, and noting a 104°F temperature. Jamie also reflects on discomfort using a video camera compared to photography, and links to the full Summer of Love Collection.

805479.abstract: Jamie logs a day of travel from Sedona, Arizona to Moab, Utah, with a brief stop to explore downtown Moab, dinner at Miguel's Baja Grill, and an effort to adjust Mazie to the time change. The post links to the full Summer of Love Collection.

805483.abstract: Jamie logs day 35 of the Summer of Love trip, moving from breakfast at Cali Cochitta B&B in Moab and Arches National Park to Colorado, passing through Glenwood Springs and Winter Park en route to C-Lazy-U Ranch near Granby, with a mention of Mazie's mosquito bite.

805492.abstract: Jamie logs day 36 of the Summer of Love, describing a first horseback ride at a dude ranch on a horse named Buster and noting that internet access there is hard to find. Jamie links to the full Summer of Love Collection.

805500.abstract: Jamie logs day 42 of a road trip, tracking mileage while heading home through Ogallala and Lincoln, Nebraska, with a Dairy Queen stop and a hotel check-in delayed by 50 basketball camp teens. Jamie expresses mixed feelings about the trip ending and links to the full Summer of Love Collection.

805509.abstract: Jamie logs the final leg of a road trip, tracking progress on I-35 through Culver's country and into Minnesota before arriving home, ending the journey with plans to catch up and sleep at home. The post links to the full Summer of Love Collection.

806498.abstract: Jamie describes a book club discussion of Maggie Mahar's "Money-Driven Medicine: The Real Reason Health Care Costs So Much," calling the meeting awesome and recommending the book, with the discussion described as great.

806507.abstract: Jamie and Jamie's wife Tammy see the movie The Soloist and Jamie finds it a great film, hoping movies like it continue to be made.

807314.abstract: Jamie shares a MediaWiki template snippet using ParserFunctions syntax to calculate a time delta between two dates, offering it as an example of why MediaWiki needs Lua scripting support.

807385.abstract: Jamie shares updates and photos from Minnebar 7, covering the event's shirt, earrings, a Mophie Juice Pack Air, sessions on Color Theory by John Mindiola III and Varnish by Mike Willbanks, and Jamie's own presentation, Running VPS with Confidence.

807451.abstract: Jamie shares updates from The Collaborative Technology Summit 2012, appearing on panel 2 to discuss 8thBridge and the evolution of technology in Minnesota alongside Erin Newkirk of Red Stamp.

807608.abstract: Jamie attends and presents at Twin Cities Agile Day 2012, held at the Minneapolis Institute of Art. Jamie notes a session by Jeff Sussna on continuous delivery, links to Andon on Wikipedia, and shares a line from David Hussman: (Value) = (Why) / (How).

807881.abstract: Jamie documents smoking five full racks of ribs and a pork shoulder on two Big Green Egg grills for Mothers Day, using dry rubs and a sauce recipe credited to Mike Rock, with photos tracking prep through the finished, cut ribs.

810220.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the #TeamSPS TechJam event showing a SumoLogic branded sumo wrestler stress toy figurine balanced on a Kubb king piece and lying among Surly Brewing beer cans in a cooler.

810341.abstract: Jamie attends the premiere of DocuMNtary, a project by Nick Roseth documenting the story of tech in Minnesota, and helps kick off the event by speaking at the podium.

810452.abstract: Jamie's wife Tammy and Jamie see the movie La La Land, and Jamie enjoys it. The post includes a photo of the film's poster showing a couple dancing near a street lamp under a starry night sky above a city skyline.

816610.abstract: Jamie surprises the kids with a Home Free concert, the last stop on the group's Christmas Tour, at Treasure Island. Photos show the five singers performing under colored stage lights and posing with someone dressed as Santa Claus.

831283.abstract: Jamie reflects on struggling to find a satisfying blog platform, having left WordPress for Markdown and Jekyll, hosted first on GitHub Pages then Netlify for SSL, but finds static sites too much friction for regular publishing. Inspired by Manton Reece's consolidated site, Jamie considers using micro.blog for longer posts too.

835540.abstract: Jamie shares reactions to seeing Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, praising the story, the comic-book-style visuals, and the soundtrack, and includes the movie's poster showing Miles Morales swinging above New York City.

870267.abstract: Jamie shares photos and impressions from a Bob Mould concert at The Mohawk venue in Austin, TX, describing the show as great and the venue as cool.

871176.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a San Antonio FC versus Las Vegas Lights soccer match at Toyota Field, noting San Antonio leading 1-0, with images showing gameplay, the pitch, and a goal celebration with red smoke on the scoreboard.

924054.abstract: Jamie describes an amazing coffee experience at the new Little Joy Coffee in Downtown Northfield, praising the shop, coffee, and barista, and noting owner Tim's deep knowledge of coffee. Photos show a cortado with latte art, Groundwire Coffee Roasters bags, and a La Marzocco espresso machine.

924060.abstract: Jamie shares photos from Northfield Shares a Dinner, a community dinner held on a closed downtown street with long rows of tables and hundreds of attendees. Jamie thanks the organizations behind the event and includes a menu featuring Carolina Smoked Pork, Mesquite Turkey Breast, and roasted sweet corn.

947873.abstract: Jamie shares photos from Stockholm Pie Company, showing slices of chocolate cream, blueberry, and nut-topped pie eaten for breakfast, along with an exterior shot of the shop's signage on a small-town street.

947926.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a visit to Together Farms with cheeseburgers, Wisconsin cheese curds, and beer, including images of a directional sign, a food stand, a red barn, and a pond on the farm property.

947995.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a farm food tour stop at The Nelson Stone Barn, describing crazy good pizza despite a long wait, followed by Spotted Cow Ice Cream for dessert. Photos show the stone barn, a wood-fired oven, the ordering line, and finished pizzas.

949155.abstract: Jamie shares photos of two Infratech WD-Series heating units installed on a porch, intended to make watching Fall baseball and Premier League soccer more comfortable on cold mornings.

954645.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a barbecue outing at Black Market StP with old neighbors, noting October snow kept the beers cold. Images show the Jim Manns Struttin With Some BBQ trailer's chalkboard menu, takeout containers of food, and a sliced rack of smoked pork ribs.

954646.abstract: Jamie visits Bad Weather Brewing for the first time due to bad weather, describing the tap room as great despite the busy crowd, and shares a photo of the bar area with fermentation tanks and two glasses of beer.

978543.abstract: Jamie watches Avengers: Endgame during a flight, noting that most Avengers movies have been seen this way. Jamie finds the movie enjoyable overall but considers the time travel angle a recurring problem in sci-fi.

986797.abstract: Jamie shares photos from a first visit to the Gingerbread Wonderland at Norway House, featuring gingerbread replicas of Glensheen Mansion, Dayton's Downtown Minneapolis store, and Bergen's Bryggen. Jamie picks Glensheen Mansion as the best entry.

986902.abstract: Jamie shares photos from the 13th Annual New Standards Holiday Show, describing a stage lit in blue and purple with confetti cannons, a Santa-costumed guitarist, and a packed ornate theater audience, calling it a Christmas tradition with new and returning guests.
